The terroir forms beautiful notes apple and pear, with a crisp and saline finish. This is a sparkling wine from a lesser known region that is a real game changer - it's elegant, clean and effortlessly drinkable.

It's got fine bubbles carrying a firm chalky spine and brisk, mouth-watering acidity. There’s a subtle textural breadth from time on lees and oak, but the overall impression remains composed. The finish is long, dry, and mineral, leaving a clean, slightly saline impression with excellent persistence.

A benchmark expression of Silvaner from old vines rooted in limestone, the Grauer Stein is a wine of striking precision and depth. Aromas of fresh herbs, flint, and subtle reduction lead into a palate that is taut yet concentrated, with vibrant citrus, savoury texture and a pronounced saline edge. Aged on lees for extended complexity, it delivers a layered, mineral-driven profile with remarkable energy and finesse. The finish is long and salty, marking this as a serious, age-worthy white.

A wine that represents far more than what's in the bottle. This is a wine of culture and legacy — a wine that (metaphorically) got up on the dining room table and took a stand for Teroldego, having since become one of the world's most hyped red wines. And the taste? Spicy, fresh plum, herbal deliciousness with a graphite undertone. Packed full of flavour and freshness — you can sip this away at Sunday lunch without falling asleep mid-mouthful.

It's rich colour stems from the skins of Pinot Gris, which lend the wine intense, umami-like flavours. Red thai curry meets ice-cold capirinhas. Open this bottle the next time you want to trick and treat your friends, and share with them a true discovery. Made from Pinot Gris from one of Michael Wenzel's organically grown limestone vineyards around his home town of Rust.

On the north shore of Lake Balaton in Hungary you find Kolonia 52 - a winery with a wealth of knowledge thanks to time spent with Gernot and Heike Heinrich, as well as Stephanie and Edi Tscheppe of Gut Oggau. This Furmint is a testament to that knowledge. A clean and elegant expression of the grape, with a fine mineral structure coming from the volcanic soil.

This is an extra special skin-contact. No seriously. It's one of those bottles that make such an impression that you can easily recall the first time you ever tasted it. Vermentino macerated on the skins and then aged in barriques for 22 months. The grapes come from a small plot planted in 1970 on the Ligurian coast. And when you taste this wine, that's where you go. Dried apricots, wild herbs and a light sprinkle of crunchy sea salt flakes.

A delightful blend of Pinot Blanc and Chardonnay from the beautiful hills of Styria. Strohmeier is the embodiment of biodynamics and his forward thinking approach that champions harmony with nature is very apparent in TLZ Weiss No.14. This wine balances acidity and structure with punchy freshness.

producer: Domaine de l'Ecu | Fred & Claire Niger
notes: Domaine de L'Ecu are known in the Loire for being forward thinkers and questioning everything. With such depth to their winemaking knowledge, Terra is a perfectly place to start when exploring their plethora of excellent wines. Terra, which is 100% Melon de Bourgogne, is a clean and precise wine. It's rounded and easy drinking, with a striking citrus note accompanied by white flowers and a lovely minerality.

From rich granite soils, a blend of Muscat Moravian and Müller-Thurgau make up this traditional method brut nature. The wine has a playful side, with structure but delicate bubbles and a fun acidity, but can also show off it's serious side; it's an elegant sparkling wine that proves just how great Bratislava is as a wine region.

An energetic and alive wine from Bratislava. This sparkling rosé is full of character. A blend of Blaufränkish, Cabernet Sauvignon and Riesling, the bottle is expresses ripe berries and a lovely integrated acidity. It's playful and fun, but also serious and elegant. This traditional method is certainly a crowdpleaser.

Spolu means together, which is a name that works perfectly for a wine made from both white and red varieties. A blend of Grüner Veltliner, Blaufränkisch, Pinot Noir, this a not-quite-red, not-quite-rosé, and manages to marry juicy fruit with serious structure in the glass. Mysterious and delicious.

Summer in a glass! This 100% Solaris cuvée – a PIWI cultivated in the Niedermayr vineyards by Thomas's father at the turn of the last century, designed to thrive in the specific conditions of their vineyard, eliminating the need for artificial chemicals and pesticides – is bursting with tropical and herbaceous aromas. Drinking this feels like sitting in a the garden of an Italian masseria. Saluti!

A Grüner Veltliner that tells you exactly why Martin is one of the top producers in the Wachau. Expressive, structured and layered with apple and quince. It's an elegant and fresh, a wine that will impress.

An expressive and elegant Spätburgunder from the Rheinhessen. Layered with texture from limestone-rich soils, this Burgundian style Spätburgunder is brooding with notes of berries and dark cherry, complimented by a slight forest and earthiness. The structure comes in the form of black pepper and great, integrated tannins.

Savigny-lès-Beaune Rouge is a Pinot Noir that captures the lighter, more lifted side of the Côte de Beaune. It has a supple and fine palate where fresh red cherry and raspberry fruit sit with a vibrant, mouth-watering acidity. The structure is gentle but defined, with fine tannins and a subtle earthy undertone adding depth. The finish is elegant and precise, with a bright, energetic feel that makes it highly drinkable yet characterful.

Poiré Comment! is a traditional Normandy perry made from carefully selected old pear varieties, giving it a pure and artisanal expression of fruit. The palate is light and gently sparkling, with crisp pear and citrus notes carried by bright, refreshing acidity. There’s a subtle natural depth that adds texture without heaviness, keeping it very easy to drink yet strikingly characterful. The finish is clean, zesty, and lightly saline, making it a refreshing and highly drinkable.

A beautiful Vermentino from the Ligurian coast. It impresses with a deeply savoury and mineral driven palette, with a sea salt touch, orange blossom and ripe citrus fruits. Rebosso is a cuvée to come back to time and time again.

The level of care that Aris of Selvadolce puts into his wines is very apparent in Rucantu. All hand picked and spontaneous fermented with wild yeasts, Rucantu really shows of Selvadolce. It's rich with a maritime minerality, with rich texture coming from a short maceration.

This is a wine that's absolutely alive with energy. It's a great introduction to the incredible wines from Martin. It's a thoughtful and precise Grüner Veltliner that remains remarkably clean despite it's layers of complexity. This will certainly win over anyone new to the world of natural wines.

This Zweigelt ticks serious boxes; it's a crowd pleaser, it's fun and approachable, it's chillable, and it suits all occasions. A deliciously light wine, it's ideal for chilling down a bit and pairing with that easy mid-week dinner. It's packed with juicy red fruits, with wild cherry and fresh blackberry giving depth, a cutting minerality and a nice structured finish from its 12 months spent on the lees.

Rosso is a bold blend of Rossese and Granaccia from vines in Liguria overlooking the Mediterranean sea. The impact of the warm breeze is notable in these wines - think big tastes of red forest fruits, raspberries and blackberries, all backed up by a solid structure and a light freshness.

We're excited to have Turbolento back with us! This is a pet-nat to shout about. Turbolento is made from only Pigato and carries a bright and fun Ligurian energy. It's got a beautiful saline touch, backed by crisp citrus and stone fruit. It's a complex and high energy pet-nat that'd be a treat to kick off any party, or pair with fresh shellfish, like crab or lobster!

High above the Kamptal valley, where steep vineyards meet shimmering mica schist soils, this wine captures the essence of its place. Fresh, mineral-driven and layered with cool spice, it reveals vibrant citrus, subtle stone fruit and a taut, lively finish. Its remarkable energy, precision and complexity make it an expressive reflection of the region, where the character of the vineyard takes centre stage. Equally suited to enjoy on its own or alongside seafood and aromatic, spice-driven cuisine.

This all-natural grape juice is a real summer pleaser. A refreshing expression of Zweigelt and St. Laurent, Traubensaft is a high acid, high energy grape juice. It's packed with notes of rhubarb, and the early harvest preserves its radiant freshness and unique pik colour. This is one for the people that appreciate bright freshness and huge character.

A bright and energetic alcoholic sparkling option! The sunshine soaked vineyards really shine in this rosé. It's high energy makes it the perfect party wine, but also works great as an aperitif or to pair with a light and fresh salad.

An incredibly delicious Chardonnay (Morillon) from chalky soils and insanely steep vineyards! F ermented in large oak casks and aged for 2 years on its lees, there's a delectable balance of acidity with a toasty creaminess to this wine. Like the Vom Opok Sauvignon Blanc, the minerality from the soil adds that undercurrent of wet stone complexity. One sip and it's easy to see why the Werlitsch wines have such a cult-like following!

This 0% grape juice from Renner is a through-and-through thirst quencher. It's vibrant and bright. Delightful intense fruit aromas and exotic pineapple on the nose which fully awakens the senses. The palate has a vibrant freshness thanks to the early harvest of the Gruner Veltliner grapes. Natural sweetness and a refreshing acidity balance together harmoniously. Enjoy neat, or as a spritz with some sparkling water.

The texture is light yet structured, supported by bright acidity that keeps the wine lively throughout. The finish is clean and precise, leaving a sense of focus and elegance.

A precise and elegant wine showing off what Grolleau can be capable of in the Loire. The wine has energy, but focuses on clean fruit and drinkability. Harvested at peak ripeness, L'Envolée is fresh, with fine tannins and structure and a body of spice, dark fruits and a hint of liquorice.

Aged in amphorae for 8 months, this wine is all about depth of flavour and a remarkable amount of fresh acidity. Think crushed red berries, wild flowers and a pinch of cool spice. It's a wine for lovers of a light chillable red but with a bit more elegance.

Picture it: you're holidaying in the French alps, and you step outside your chalet to fresh snowfall on a crisp winter's day. The cold bites your cheeks as you inhale the scent of fresh pine mingles with wet stone, but your various layers of winter gear offer a comforting weightiness to keep the cold at bay. That's what it feels like to drink this cuvée from Les Mangeux d'Pierre – a beautifully crisp and fresh Altesse from the Bugey region of Savoie, full of beautiful herbal aromatics and a stringent acidity without the sacrifice on texture or body. We'll cheers to that!

We're so excited to introduce Icy Liu to the Newcomer Portfolio, and her incredibly promising first vintage. This 100% Gamay is all crunchy red fruits alongside pretty, spicy aromatics and a delicate earthy quality. Perfect for fans of serious Cru Beaujolais, Pinot Noir or young Syrah – these bottles are moving very quickly in our bar, so don't sleep on this drop.

A Bordeaux blend but not as you know it! A consistent standout rosé in our wine range. Slightly lighter in colour to its previous vintage yet very vibrant in it's flavour, this Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt blend is perfect if you're looking for something in-between a rosé and chillable red. It reminds us of a lemon and red berry tart - zesty and fruity, but with an uplifting tang. From biodynamically farmed parcels of Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch in the Burgenland region of Austria. Direct pressed, the wine was aged on the lees in old barrels before being bottled unfined and unfiltered.

A wine that spans the legacy of 3 generations of the Tscheppe family. Vines planted by the grandfather, nurtured by Andreas Sen. Tscheppe and brought to full potential by Ewald who calls this very old field blend a personal favourite year after year. Contrary to most of his Sauvignon and Chardonnay blends this hosts a set of varieties including old-vines of the native Styrian grape Welschriesling. Situated in the steep Styrian hills a few minutes away from the border with Slovenia. The vineyards are some of the oldest in the family, grown on the signature limestone-rich Opok soils.

Purellus is a sparkling Riesling made in a pétillant-naturel style, capturing the energy of the Mosel with gentle bubbles and a bright, zippy characteristic. Citrus, green apple and subtle orchard fruit lead, backed by a lightly savoury edge. The wine is crisp, refreshing, and fun, making it a vibrant and characterful sparkling wine.

This Riesling leans into clarity and balance, offering a precise yet approachable expression of a grape native to the Mosel. Citrus and green apple notes sit at the forefront supported by a lively line of acidity that keeps everything lifted. The texture is fine and slightly rounded, with a distinct mineral streak adding definition and tension. It comes across as focused and energetic.

Pyramide is a Riesling with a more concentrated and structured profile, drawing depth from older vines from its steep Mosel sites. The palate is tightly knit, with vibrant acidity shaping layers of citrus, stone fruit and a herbal edge. There’s a pronounced mineral core that gives the wine tension and direction. It shows both intensity and precision, offering a more serious and age-worthy expression of Riesling.

Côte du Württemberg is definitely a fun and easy going wine. It's fresh with bright red and dark berry that's carried with a lively acidity. A subtle peppery spice and gentle herbalness gives this wine beautiful detail, and the fine tannins carry the structure with not too much heaviness. A clear, juicy and energetic wine that's fun to drink.

A wine that is the equivalent of a long novel. It will capture your imagination and just for a moment, allow you to delve out of this world. Freude means Joy in German, and opening a bottle of this skin contact giant always brings a big smile to our faces. Ewald infuses the skins with the juice for almost a year in some vintages, allowing the wine to take on layers upon layers of flavour. Ewald makes two skin-fermented white wines from the Werlitsch vineyards. 'Freude' is one of them and it is macerated with whole bunches: 100% in a good year, or 50-70% in a tough year, for much longer periods

Le Bois des Ormes 2023 by Hunter McKirdy is a fresh, elegant Pinot Noir from Alsace with bright notes of strawberry and cherry. It has a smooth texture, gentle acidity, and a clean, balanced finish that keeps it lively. Light yet refined, it’s an easy-drinking wine that still feels thoughtfully made.

Les Champs des Fleurs is a fresh, mineral-driven Riesling from Alsace with bright citrus and green apple notes. It’s crisp and dry, with lively acidity and a clean, refreshing finish that keeps it sharp and easy to enjoy.

A focused, terroir-driven Blaufränkisch from Austria’s Eisenberg, shaped by cool slate soils and old vines. It shows layered dark and red fruit with herbal, spicy notes and a clear mineral edge, supported by fresh acidity and fine tannins. Structured yet elegant, it’s a refined wine with depth and ageing potential.

TLZ Lysegron No.9 is a textured, natural Pinot Blanc from Styria, made with minimal intervention and no added sulphur. It shows floral, herbal notes with hints of stone fruit and a lively freshness on the palate. Deeply expressive, it’s a distinctive, characterful wine with depth and a slightly wild edge.

This is everything you want in a deeply macerated Styrian skin-contact. Think orange rind, nutmeg, a twist of cinnamon and a sprinkling of white pepper. And there's something intangible here, something we simply cannot put into words... something that gives us goosebumps (the good kind). And for us, that's the sign of a truly great wine.

This wine is a distinctive, amphora-aged Teroldego with a fresh yet structured style shaped by its ageing process. It shows layered dark berry fruit with floral and earthy notes, supported by bright acidity and fine tannins. Focused and expressive, it’s a refined red with depth and a clean mineral edge.

Morei Cilindrica is a precise, amphora-aged Teroldego with deep and structured profile. It shows dark cherry and wild berry fruit layered with spice, herbs and a clear mineral edge, lifted by fresh acidity and fine tannins. Focused and expressive, it’s a refined, terroir-driven wine with depth and a long, clean finish.

Rosso Per Tutti is a vibrant, easygoing red blend made for pure drinking pleasure. It bursts with juicy red berries, soft spice, and a touch of earthiness, carried by bright freshness and a smooth, relaxed feel. Lively and approachable, it’s a fun, unfussy wine that still shows plenty of personality.
Ripe fruit but with minerality and depth - if you have yet to get into Sauvignon Blanc from Austria, this will be your gateway bottle.
Named after the Ureki beach in Georgia, this Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot blend is wild and delicious. There's body for sure but somehow remains reminiscent of the coastline that inspired its name

producer: Domaine de l'Ecu | Fred & Claire Niger
notes: Fresh, saline and just so pretty on the nose – citrus zest, white flowers and a lean mineral edge make for an incredibly more-ish wine. Pair it with oysters, lemon pasta or a big hunk of goats cheese and thank us later!

Whether you've watched the movie Sideways or have had a bad experience with the grape, merlot may not be your vibe. And we totally get it! But THIS bottle, this Austrian merlot right here: absolute game-changer. Full of plush and cozy dark fruits with a delicate finish that won't weigh you down, it's a weeknight wine staple. A merlot moment if you will. Paired with dinner, dessert or a netflix and chill situation, we promise you won't be disappointed.

Coming from the South African term for 'hungover', Babelas is the kind of wine that you'll certainly want to put away enough of to warrant one. A fun and fruity pink pet nat, this is a bottle that screams a good time. Strawberry and pomegranate, creamy and fresh – drink it until the word "bubbles" starts to sound more like "babelas", and then take yourself off to bed with a pint of water and a paracetamol for the morning.

producer: Les Vignes d' Oliver | Olivier Cohen
notes: Déferlante Blanc 2024 comes from old-vine Clairette Blanc grown in the sun-drenched hills of the Languedoc. Olivier Cohen works with a light touch in the cellar, allowing the grape’s naturally fresh, textural character to shine through. The wine is full of bright notes of citrus, pear and white flowers, carried by a gentle herbal lift. On the palate it feels lively with a soft, saline edge that keeps everything balanced and refreshing. A vibrant, easygoing cuvée that captures the sunny energy of the south.

This is a dry Riesling from Rheinhessen, grown on limestone-rich soils that give it a clear, stony character. The palate moves between lime zest, orchard fruit with a hint of white peach, backed by a mouthwatering line of acidity. It finishes with a cool, chalky grip that lingers.

Pettenthal is a single-site Riesling from the steep red slate slopes of the Rhine, giving it a deeper, more powerful expression. It opens with ripe citrus, peach and a touch of smoky spice, underpinned by firm acidity and a distinct salty, mineral core. Structured and concentrated, it has real drive and a long, focused finish.

Orbel is a Riesling from the cool, exposed Orbel site, showing a more restrained and high-tension style. It leans into citrus peel, green plum and a faint herbal edge, with acidity and a firm, stony backbone. Sleek and precise, it feels linear and energetic with a long, mouthwatering finish.

Hipping is a Riesling from the steep Roter Hang in Rheinhessen, defined by red slate soils. It opens with ripe lime, white peach, and a hint of red fruit, layered over a smoky, mineral undertone. Broad yet focused, it balances depth and tension perfectly.

It's a Gamay party! A bright and sumptuous rosé made from Gamay, Muscaris and Souvignier Gris, coming together to make a wonderfully aromatic and herbal rosé for all seasons. So good we want to swim in it.

This is a Loire Chenin Blanc is very reflective of Menards winemaking. From schist soils that brings together ripeness and freshness in a very natural way, it opens with flavours of pear, quince and citrus, with a soft honeyed touch and a hint of herbs. The wine feels full but easygoing, finishing with a long, fresh, slightly saline edge.

Orion Alpha from Pierre Menard comes from carefully managed parcels in the Loire. On the palate, red and black berries combine with subtle notes of dried herbs and a touch of pepper, while fine-grained tannins provide structure without heaviness. The wine is bright and focused, with lively acidity that carries the flavors through each sip. Layers of dark cherry, plum, and gentle spice emerge gradually, giving depth and complexity. The finish is precise and lingering, leaving a sense of the vineyard’s character long after the glass is empty.

Fresh and precise, with complex aromas, herbal depth, and vibrant acidity. Crafted in Steiermark from organically grown Sauvignon Blanc on steep slopes, hand-harvested in small batches and refined with herbs from Mama Anna Neumeister’s garden delivering unmistakable regional character with 0% alcohol.

Aromatic and expressive, with ripe fruit, gentle spice, and vibrant acidity. Crafted in Steiermark from organically grown Gelber Muskateller on steep slopes, hand-harvested in small batches and refined with herbs from Mama Anna Neumeister’s garden delivering unmistakable regional character with 0% alcohol.

Whilst spraying their vines for Demeter preparations, Julie thought to herself, if the natural ingredients and teas she was spraying on the vines were good for them, then maybe they're good for us. A curious seed was planted, and this is the result. From their wild and luscious herbs growing across the vineyard, Julie started co fermenting them with her grapes. A blend of Gruner Veltliner and mint, this is perfectly refreshing on a warm day. It's bone dry and structured, low in ABV, and the perfect alternative for a digestif or desert.

This elegant cuvée from Le Grappin comes from carefully tended Chardonnay vines planted on the limestone-rich slopes of the Côte d’Or . Made with minimal intervention and gentle aging in old barrels, the wine highlights purity and freshness. Bright citrus, green apple, and white stone fruit unfold with a delicate texture and vibrant energy. A subtle mineral edge with a balanced finish reflects the hillside terroir and Burgundian character of this wine.

Fruktinger is a delicious blend of Saison brewed in Malmö with head brewer Kim from Rocket Brewing, blended with wine and lees made by Claus Preisinger. This is then topped up with fresh fermenting rhubarb juice that Karl, Mikael and their team harvested earlier in the year. Basically a beer, wine, fruit juice hybrid that will rock your world! Our go-to on a Friday afternoon in the Newcomer Wines garden.

Wine flavoured with hops! Wild hops began growing around the perimeter of one of Weninger's orchards, and since none of their beer brewer friends wanted to work with the hops, Weninger took them for himself and made something magical. The fresh, uncooked hops were added to the wine during fermentation and remained in contact for several weeks in amphora. Since the wine was directly pressed Blaufränkisch, tannin and fruit on the palate of the Glimmer of Hops are attributed to the hops. Drink it straight up or mixed with tonic for a gorgeous little aperitif – prost!

aromas: Green Apple, White Peach, Peach, Lime, Slate
notes: Reiler Mullay-Hofberg is an elegant Riesling from the Mosel with a very focused style. Think lime zest, green apple, and white peach, layered with smoky slate and a clear mineral edge from the steep vineyard. It's very crisp and precise and finishes dry, lively and long with a refreshing, stony lift.

producer: Domaine de l'Ecu | Fred & Claire Niger
notes: If you want an easy drinking and thirst quenching rosé, you've got it. From the warmth of the Loire Valley, Muse is lively and mineral and definitely thirst quenching. It's crisp and clean with a vibrant acidity, mouthwatering texture and a hint of a saline tension. Thoughtfully made with low-intervention techniques, Muse is a must for a warm summer day.

It tastes like the lightest of Beaujolais Crus with its smashable raspberry fruit, but still has the undergrowth seriousness of grand cru Burgundy. It's a wine that will stay on your mind long after the bottle has gone.

A vibrant and charismatic wine that's perfect for entertaining. Bright freshness and an abundance of fruit finishes with a dry edge, perfect for a light dinner or chill night with friends. Well worth chilling it down for extra joy.

Weinland is made mostly from young, disease-resistant PIWI varieties like Souvignier Gris, grown across different vineyard sites. It shows a very pure, understated fruit profile - green apple, citrus, and white peach - with a faint floral lift and a gentle herbal edge that comes from the long lees ageing. The wine feels crisp and linear, driven by a bright, almost racy acidity and a subtle, chalky texture.

Steiner Kékfrankos comes from the historic Steiner vineyard in Sopron, where old Blaufränkisch vines grow on gneiss and mica schist soils that give the wine its firm, stony character. The wine is layered with dark cherry, blackberry and plum, layered with cracked pepper, dried herbs, and a subtle smoky, mineral depth that reflects the rocky site. An elegant and terrior expressive wine.

A cross of Riesling with Pinot Bianco, Manzoni Bianco is all white flowers and dried apricots on the nose but with a lean and mineral finish on the palate. A balanced and serious wine that will continue to develop with age – perfect with a fresh salad while sitting in the sun.

Not your average skin contact! Vitovska is a rare and ancient grape varietal primarily found in Northern Italy and Slovenia. It's known for its sage and stone fruit qualities, as well as some floral and spice notes. Yet give it a week on the skins like this bad boy here, and you'll also find incredible structure and depth. Amber in colour and bold in flavour, this is a perfect addition to a smokey eggplant dip, lamb kebobs, roasted mushrooms, or anything with a bit of herbs and spice.

This is a pure expression of Jacquère grown on clay‑limestone soils in the foothills of the French Alps in the Savoie region. Matthieu Goury works organically and with minimal intervention, pressing whole bunches and fermenting on indigenous yeasts before aging gently in neutral barrels for extended texture and complexity. The palate is lively and light, with a taut mineral thread and bright acidity that carries juicy green apple and citrus through to the finish. There’s a refreshing energy and clean, alpine clarity that makes each sip feel crisp and vibrant.

This is a vibrant Chardonnay from organically farmed vines planted on clay‑limestone soils in the foothills of the French Alps in the Savoie region, where cool mountain breezes and bright sun help give the grape both freshness and ripeness. Matthieu Goury works with minimal intervention, letting the varietal purity and site expression develop naturally with gentle aging before release. The wine balances bright acidity with a rich, textured core of ripe orchard fruit and a hint of stone, carrying through to a long, clean finish. A pretty and playful skin contact for anyone who likes their wine with a fun backstory! When Weninger planted his Frettner vineyard back in 1999, he thought he had planted Pinot Noir for the chalky higher part of the vineyard. But three years later, he discovered that they had actually received Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris vines. In 2018, he decided to ferment the Pinot Gris and Pinot Blanc together on the skins, and since 2021, it's been a Pinot party: the skins of the Blanc and the whole berries of the Gris ferment in the direct pressed juice of the Noir. A perfect ending to a happy accident!

A wonderfully layered and complex dry cherry juice, made from wild bird cherries from trees planted around 100 years ago. These cherries are considerably smaller than other cherries, with large stones in the middle, meaning that the juice they can produce is limited, but incredibly concentrated. A real show stopper for drinkers and non-drinkers alike. These natural juices are unfiltered, cold-pressed, and bottled without any additives.

A truly unique 0% option that will delight drinkers and non-drinkers alike. 60-year old bio-dynamically planted Conference Pear trees, planted in very specific locations on account of their pH value and soil compositions. Fruit is harvested when it's at its ripest, before being cold-pressed and bottled without any filtering or additives – resulting in a layered, refreshing and complex non-alcoholic drink with a profile that would rival some serious, terroir-driven wines.

An ode to the tradition of off-dry Rieslings in the Mosel. Rudolf and Rita blend two vineyards mainly for the 'Silbermond' and in their own words "love its lightness and pronounced mineral spiciness reminiscent of citrus fruits."

Roughly translating to 'slate flower', on account of the blend of grey slate and blue slate vineyards, both surrounded by forest, meadows and the river. There's so much going on in the glass for such a young wine – on first impressions, cooking apple and wet pebble, before opening up to dried herbs, floral quality, and the kind of salty lick you get from the rim of a good margarita.

producer: Domaine de la Touraize | André-Jean & Heleana Morin
notes: This Vin Jaune is a remarkable oxidative white wine from the Jura, crafted with exceptional patience and tradition. It reveals complex aromas of walnut, dried citrus peel and savory umami depth, developing through extended ageing under voile. The palate is bone-dry, intensely structured, and layered, with a distinctive saline and nutty character that lingers long on the finish.

This terroir driven Riesling from father and son duo Clemens and Lukas, made in the Wagram region of Austria, is a storytelling wine. This is a wine that will change over time in the glass – allow it to open up and let the story unfold. Fresh stone fruit turns into juicy pineapple, before unveiling a more complex richness from its time spent in oak. Sublime!

Coming from Liguria, the Selvadolce wines are always reminiscent of the sea. While the Rosso Se is a powerful red with dark berry fruits and a good bit of tannins, there's an underlying freshness and elegance that brings you right back to the coast. Pair it with pizza and any tomato-based stews and sauces, or gift it to a Nebbiolo lover in your life who's looking to try something new!

Zagersdorf is a finely tuned, terroir-focused red that captures the depth and precision of this historic Burgenland site. It has aromas of ripe black cherry, plum and redcurrant, layered with dark spice and a stony mineral undertone. The palate is structured and energetic, driven by fine-grained tannins and vibrant acidity that give the wine tension and length. This is a poised, age-worthy wine.

This cuvée comes from organically farmed parcels of Sankt Laurent — Austria’s own red grape with close genetic ties to Pinot Noir — in the varied soils around Burgenland’s village. With gentle, low‑intervention winemaking and a focus on freshness, the wine lets the pure fruit expression and site energy come through naturally. Juicy cherry and red‑berry flavours mingle with supple, fine tannins and lively acidity, giving the wine a vibrant yet elegant texture. Bright acidity and a subtle mineral thread carry through to a long, precise finish that reflects the vineyards’ character.

Handled gently in the cellar, the wine focuses on purity, and freshness. Bright notes of blackberry, sour cherry, and plum lead the way, lifted by hints of black pepper and wild herbs. The palate is lively and finely structured, with crisp acidity and a subtle mineral edge. An energetic expression of Blaufränkisch that captures the character of Burgenland beautifully.

From organically farmed vineyards in Burgenland this Furmint from Hannes Schuster is lively and fun. There's incredible tension and clarity from the limestone and slate soils. Fermented with native yeasts and handled with a light and considerate touch in the cellar, the focus of this Furmint is purity and freshness. Crisp apple, citrus and a subtle herbal note is complimented with bright acidity and a mineral core. It's lively and balanced and a vibrant expression of Furmint.

Aus den Dörfern is a big and expressive field blend of local varieties from several villages across Burgenland. This is an easy going wine that is so reflective of the every day character of Burgenland. Bright green apple and citrus unfolds with lively acidity and a gentle mineral lift. The texture is soft but vibrant, and the finish is clean and deeply refreshing. Aus den Dörfern is a bright and approachable white wine that defines the spirit of the region.

‘R’ 2022 is a finely detailed Pinot Noir that emphasizes precision and vineyard expression. Aromas of red cherry, wild strawberry, and raspberry, layered with rose petals, subtle spice, and a hint of earthy minerality. The palate is silky yet structured, with fine tannins and vibrant acidity giving it tension and clarity. This is an elegant, age-worthy Spätburgunder that balances purity of fruit with finesse and a long, focused finish.

This Silvaner is a focused, site-driven white that showcases the purity and precision of this classic German variety, but with a distinct Burgundy-esque touch. It's got energy and high acidity driven by minerality. This 2022 vintage offers plenty of crunchy orchard fruit with a touch of herbaceous-ness. It's long aging on the lees offers a silky but firm texture and would be great aged.

An elegant and expressive Pinot Noir offering a finely tuned balance between ripe fruit and savoury complexity. Aromas of red cherry, raspberry and a little bit of spice lead into a silky palate layered with hints of dried herbs and gentle oak. Fine-grained tannins and fresh acidity provide structure while maintaining a supple, approachable texture. The finish is smooth and lingering, with notes of dark berries and a touch of earthy minerality.

A vivid, alpine expression of Pinot Noir, Steingut from Christof Ruof showcases the purity and precision of Graubünden fruit. Wild cherry, cranberry and subtle herbal notes lead into a bright, finely structured palate with crunchy red berries and lifted acidity. Gentle tannins and a light, mineral-driven texture give the wine both energy and finesse, reflecting its minimal-intervention approach.

A characterful and expressive white, the Santenay Blanc Saint Jean 2023 balances richness with precision. Yellow orchard fruit, white flowers, and a faint smoky-mineral note lead into a palate that is vibrant. The wine shows a creamy palate, lifted by fresh acidity and a distinct limestone-driven energy. The finish is long, refined and gently saline, reflecting both its biodynamic origins and the finesse of the Côte de Beaune.

Vibrant citrus and green apple unfold with a crisp, energetic texture and a saline‑tinged minerality that keeps the wine bright and focused. The vines are farmed carefully and vinified with minimal intervention, letting the vineyard express itself naturally. Red cherry and raspberry dominate the palate, joined by subtle wild herb and earthy notes. Fine tannins and balanced acidity give the wine structure while keeping it light and approachable. The finish is clean and focuse. It’s a Burgundy that delivers charm and clarity.

A bright and refined expression of Lemberger, otherwise known as Blaufränkisch outside of Germany. Blueberry and black cherry on the nose, with a subtle spicy characteristic and a clean mineral finish.

Zotzenberg is a Grand Cru Riesling from the historic Zotzenberg vineyards around Mittelbergheim , where marl‑calcareous and sandy‑gravel soils on steep slopes give the grape bright energy and mineral drive. The wine is made with careful, low‑intervention winemaking that lets the vineyard speak for themselves. Vibrant citrus and stone fruit unfold alongside a piercing mineral thread and lively acidity that keeps the wine focused and precise. The finish is long and clean, carrying a subtle saline tension that reflects the unique Grand Cru terroir.

What do you get if you cross everyone's favourite red Austrian varietal with everyone's favourite method of making light, juicy red wines? You get Bottlefish! This carbonically macerated Blaufränkisch is fruity, juicy and bursting with notes of tart red fruits and violet, with a delicate structure and oodles of charm. Stick it in the fridge and get ready for a good time.

Expressive yet easy-going, the five different varietals in this blend were all macerated for different lengths of time, resulting in a super approachable yet layered skin-contact wine. Like the name suggests, this wine makes us think of stargazing on a clear night – bright, sparkly, and the longer you pay attention, the more is revealed to you. Also like stargazing, this wine can be appreciated regardless of your experience – a great entry-level bottle of orange wine, and one that's sure to make you want to explore further.

This is what we like to call a gateway orange wine. The kind of skin-contact wine that will solidify your love for the stuff. Made from Gewürztraminer and Pinot Gris, it's floral, ripe, and a tiny bit spicy, with notes of rose and lychee that give it a Turkish Delight twist. Real 'how was this made from grapes?!' wine.

Elysion is an expressive wine from the hills above Bolzano in Alto Adige. It's structure is made up of citrus peel and orchard fruit, with wild herbs and a tea note. It's textured and gently tannic on the palate with a layered complexity.

Caroline is a vibrant wine from Alto Adige that captures both clarity and textural depth. Orange peel, apricot, camomile, and wild herbs lead into a finely structured palate with gentle tannins and bright, energetic acidity.

Damien is a deeply coloured, expressive dark rosé from Alto Adige made from Lagrein. It's got aromas of black cherry and wild berries layered with dark fruits and herbal notes. The palate is textured and structured, with fine tannins and bright acidity giving it the shape of a light red rather than a conventional rosé. The finish is savoury, mineral, and persistent, with a cool alpine freshness running through it.

Art Terre is a precise, elegant mineral-driven Brut Nature Champagne from Premier Cru Chamery. Crafted from a blend of Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier, and Chardonnay, it opens with aromas of citrus, green apple and white flowers. The palate is energetic, showing vibrant acidity and a distinctly chalky, limestone tension. The finish is long, dry and saline, with a focused, linear mineral drive.

A delightful champagne from 100% Chardonnay grown in the village of Vandières in the beautiful Vallée de La Marne. Full of minerality and energy, this is a Champagne perfect for all occaions.

One of the young stars of the grower Champagne movement, Flavien is making his mark in the region with cuvees sought out by collectors around the world. His non-vintage cuvée is the hallmark of his work — think fresh stone fruits, that ever-desired minerality, a touch of rock salt and the most enticing brioche finish. Put simply — yum. A bottle to sip slowly with your nearest and dearest.

This is a structured, terroir-focused Pinot Gris from the steep volcanic slopes of Styria. The palate is shaped by tension and precision, with a firm mineral backbone, vivid acidity, and a fine grip. It shows a layered, savoury depth rather than overt fruit expression, building complexity through texture and site-driven character. The finish is long, dry, and sharply defined, with a persistent saline, stony edge and clear ageing potential.

Alte Reben is a vibrant Sauvignon Blanc crafted from old vines, delivering impressive depth and character. It opens with crisp green apple and fresh citrus, lifted by subtle herbal notes. On the palate it is bright and well-structured, balancing lively acidity with a gentle texture and a refined mineral edge.

Klausen is a refined Sauvignon Blanc from old vines, showing depth and precision. The focus here is on structure, with a firm backbone of acidity balanced by a subtle, rounded texture. Mineral notes run through the palate, giving it clarity without relying heavily on overt aromatics. The finish is long and composed, making it a sophisticated and food-friendly choice.

Ried Klausen comes from a south‑facing parcel of Sauvignon Blanc in the Steiermark, where gneiss and loess soils lend the wine a powerful mineral energy and clarity. Made with minimal intervention and a focus on expressing the site, the wine shows vibrant fruit purity and tension. The finish is clean and persistent, with a subtle saline thread that carries the vineyard’s character through to the last sip.

Finito is a distinctive skin-contact Sylvaner, crafted in a zero-zero style that highlights both character and individuality. Extended time on the skins gives the wine a gentle tannic grip and a textured, layered palate. It is driven more by structure and savoury complexity than overt fruit, with a natural freshness keeping everything in balance. The finish is long and evolving, making it an intriguing choice for those seeking something unconventional and expressive.

One sip of this will make you understand why Mythopia's wines have such a cult status. Pinot Noir but not as you know it – there's a stewed strawberry and black cherry quality, along with a balsamic note and a herbaceous edge and a rich finish. The oxidative style of winemaking used by Mythopia gives their wines an incredible depth and complex character – these wines are truly in a league of their own.

Rosé Vom Opok is a distinctive rosé with real depth and character, shaped by limestone-rich Opok soils. It shows a structured palate with fine grip, balanced by fresh acidity that keeps it lively and precise. Subtle red fruit and savoury notes sit alongside a pronounced mineral edge. The finish is dry, focused, and persistent, making it a versatile and very interesting rosé.

Graf Sauvignon is a structured Sauvignon Blanc with notable depth and precision, shaped by biodynamic farming and careful élevage. It shows a focused palate with firm acidity and a layered, textural feel that gives it presence and drive. Subtle herbal and savoury notes sit alongside a strong mineral backbone. The finish is long, dry, and composed, making it a serious and food-friendly expression of the variety.

With its zingy acidity and bright lemon zest goodness, this wine overflows with life. We poured it at our bar a couple weeks ago and we couldn't believe how quickly it flew! There's just something electric about this wine. The perfect crowd charming, dinner party bottle of white.

Omnia comes from biodynamically farmed vineyards in Styria , where opok soils and steep slopes give the wines their vibrant energy. The cuvée blends Sauvignon Blanc with Muskateller, bringing together the structure of Sauvignon with the aromatic lift of Muskateller. Made with a low-intervention approach and spontaneous fermentation, the wine highlights the bright, expressive character of the fruit and the tension of the Styrian terroir. On the palate, lively citrus and orchard fruit mingle with subtle floral notes and a fresh, textured core. This is distinctly Styrian.

Pierre Ménard makes precise and refined wines in the Loire. The slopes of the Coteaux du Layon are schist-rich, and Cosmos is an excellent expression of Chenin in sweet form. There's a classic balance of richness and acidity that is captured in this cuvée with beautiful harmony. Crafter with late harvest grapes, the wine builds layers of honeyed fruit, dried apricot and a gentle spice. Despite its natural sweetness, a bright line of acidity keeps the palate lifted and vibrant. A balanced sweet wine that feels both generous and precise, with plenty of life ahead.

Pluton is a precise and textured Chenin Blanc that reflects a careful, low-intervention approach in the vineyard and cellar. It shows a structured palate with taut acidity and a fine phenolic grip that gives shape and energy. Notes of orchard fruit sit alongside a pronounced mineral backbone, adding depth and definition. The finish is long, dry, and focused, making it a compelling and age-worthy expression of the Loire.

Chaos is a distinctive Chenin Blanc that balances precision with natural complexity. It shows a structured, textured palate driven by firm acidity and a subtle phenolic grip. Layers of orchard fruit are interwoven with savoury and mineral nuances, giving the wine depth and tension. The finish is long, dry and persistent, making it a compelling and characterful Loire expression.

A truly tropical Chenin Blanc! Think Mango Soleros on a hot day – tangy, fruity and a little bit creamy. We also get a bit of quince and baked apple pie filling from it – the kind of wine you just want to keep swirling and sniffing all day to see what else you can uncover.

Orion Alpha from Pierre Menard comes from carefully tended vineyards in the hills of the Loire. On the palate, crisp apple and pear mingle with soft citrus and a touch of white flowers, while a light stony minerality runs underneath. The wine’s texture is focused and very present, with balanced acidity that keeps it lively without overpowering. Each sip reveals subtle layers of orchard fruit unfolding steadily across the palate. The finish lingers with a fresh, clean brightness that makes you want more and more.

Thorsten's special cellar below his house has somewhat a unique micro-climate. Most of his Rieslings would ferment dry within the first 12 months but then there are barrels that keep fermenting (slowly) for many more months, sometimes years! The aptly named 'Lentum' is one of them and it is astonishing to see how this evolution gives the wine a character that is far away from Mosel Riesling. To us it is like drinking energetic Chablis with the perfume of slate grown Riesling. A wine with lots of attitude and panache.

Schäf Reiler Mullay-Hofberg Spätlese is a finely balanced Riesling with natural richness and tension from a steep, slate-driven Mosel site. It combines delicate sweetness with bright, mouth-watering acidity that keeps the wine focused and lifted. Layers of ripe stone fruit and citrus are underpinned by a pronounced mineral core. The finish is long, precise, and elegant, making it a classic off-dry expression with great ageing potential.

Mullay-Hofberg Kabinett is a delicate Riesling that balances light sweetness with vibrant acidity from a steep slate vineyard. The finish is long, crisp and refreshing, making it an elegant and highly drinkable Mosel expression.

Trepail Blanc 1er Cru is a refined Blanc de Blancs Champagne that highlights the purity and tension of Chardonnay from a Premier Cru site. It shows a precise, structured palate with fine mousse and vibrant acidity that gives it drive and lift. Subtle citrus and orchard fruit sit alongside chalky, mineral undertones. The finish is long, clean and focused, making it an elegant and highly expressive Champagne.

Trepail Rouge 1er Cru is a still Pinot Noir from Champagne, showing finesse and structure from a Premier Cru vineyard. It offers a supple yet focused palate with fine tannins and vibrant acidity that gives it lift and precision. Red berry fruit is complemented by subtle spice and a distinct chalky minerality. The finish is long, fresh and elegant. A poised expression of still Pinot Noir from the region.

Klettgau is a Gemischter Satz from a region nestled in the Randen mountains. Here, limestone-heavy terroir is key to understanding these wines - it imparts a sharp and nervy mineral edge. Spontaneous fermentation and a short period of skin contact helps this lean, mineral wine carry some weight and texture, with energy shining bright and notes of wild herbs.

Romorantin comes from young vines planted on flinty clay soils in the Loire Valley . Made with a gentle, low-intervention approach and aged patiently in old barrels, the wine captures the rare, distinctive character of the Romorantin grape. Vibrant citrus and orchard fruit unfold alongside notes of beeswax and warm stone, carried by a lively, mineral tension. A subtle saline thread brings freshness and length to the finish. A beautifully textured, small-production white that shows the depth and individuality of this Loire variety.

La Cabane is made from Sauvignon Blanc grown on fertile sandy-loam soils in the Loire Valley . Made with a gentle, low-intervention approach, which includes whole-cluster fermentation, native yeasts, and aging in old barrels, the wine highlights the natural energy of the fruit and the Loire. Bright citrus and orchard fruit unfold alongside a subtle herbal lift and a soft, rounded texture. A delicate mineral note keeps everything fresh and balanced through the finish.

Extra is a structured but easy drinking Côt (Malbec). It's got depth and vibrancy, with dark and savoury red fruits but still a light and bright body. It's got lively acidity and complexity, and whilst being very thirst quenching still interesting and nuanced.
Aged in barrel for a year before bottling, this Chenin is depth meets energy. Delightfully balanced and an absolute crowd charmer.

This blend of Groslot and Cabernet Franc from the Loire focuses on purity and drinkability. It has a light, juicy palate with bright citrus and orchard fruit carried by crisp and very lively acidity. The texture is soft yet energetic, with a subtle mineral thread that keeps it focused. The finish is clean, easygoing, and deeply refreshing. It's a versatile everyday white that retains interesting characteristics.

"Boucherottes” is a Pinot Noir from a south-facing Premier Cru site near the Pommard border. This wine is full of both depth and finesse. The palate is supple and finely structured, with ripe red cherry and berry fruit carried by fresh, well-integrated acidity. Layers of subtle spice, earthy nuance and a stony mineral thread add complexity and detail. The finish is long, elegant, and poised.

Beaujolais-Villages 2023 from Le Grappin comes from carefully selected vineyards across the granite soils of Beaujolais . Made with a low-intervention approach, the wine highlights the bright, expressive and fun character of Gamay . On the palate it’s fresh and lively, with soft spice and a subtle mineral edge adding depth. Full of vibrant cherry and raspberries. A joyful, easy-drinking Beaujolais that shows the energy and charm of the vintage.

“Les Toisières” is a Chardonnay from a small hillside parcel on the Meursault border, shaped by a cool, precise style. Bright citrus and orchard fruit lead, carried on a line of fresh, driving acidity. The texture is fine and slightly creamy, with a distinct stony, saline minerality adding tension underneath.

"Les Grèves” is a Chardonnay from one of Beaune’s most esteemed premier cru sites, known for producing wines with both richness and precision. The palate is layered and finely textured, with ripe citrus and orchard fruit supported by vibrant acidity and a gentle, creamy depth. A pronounced mineral core adds tension and definition, keeping the wine focused and lifted. This is an elegant wine full of clarity and finesse.

An elegant and carefully created Chardonnay from vines planted on limestone slope in Montagny. Made with minimal intervention and aged in old barrels, the wine develops a silky texture and a bright, focused energy. Flavors of ripe white fruit and subtle citrus unfold with a natural, refreshing minerality. The finish is long and precise, balancing weight and tension.

This Kékfrankos (Blaufrankish) comes from volcanic soil in Hungary's Balaton region. A very expressive but drinkable red, it leads with black current and a juicy body followed by a touch of sour cherry, with a precise minerality and slight flinty note. 11 months in oak barrel makes this wine rounded, fruit forward and easy drinking.

Blanc de Blancs is a traditional-method sparkling made entirely from Chardonnay, focused on a structured and pure wine. It shows a finely structured palate with vibrant acidity and a very fine, persistent sparkle. Citrus and green apple notes are layered with a distinct chalky minerality and subtle reduction that adds tension and depth. The finish is long, precise, and energetic, giving it a focused and elegant Champagne-style expression.

A truly special expression of Chardonnay! The kind of wine that simultaneously could have you believing it's come out of a classic Burgundian estate, while still reflecting the specific magic that Moritz Kissinger is making in the Rheinhessen. A future classic in the making!

Zöbinger Heiligenstein Steinwand Erste Lage is a Riesling from one of Kamptal’s most distinctive terraced sites, shaped by ancient Permian sandstone and volcanic soils. It shows a tightly coiled, highly structured palate driven by vibrant acidity and a noticeable mineral backbone. Citrus and stone fruit notes are present, but framed by a firm, stony precision rather than overt fruitiness. The finish is long, linear, and intensely focused, with clear ageing potential.

It shows a tightly coiled, highly structured palate driven by vibrant acidity and a noticeable mineral backbone. Amphibolit is a precise and deeply textured white wine from old mixed plantings rooted in the crystalline amphibolite soils of Kamptal. It is built on structure rather than overt fruit, with a firm, linear palate driven by vibrant acidity and a subtle grip. Layers of citrus, orchard fruit, and faint herbal notes are entwined with a striking stony, almost smoky mineral core. The finish is long and highly focused, giving the wine a sense of clarity, depth and intensity.

Glimmerschiefer is a field blend wine from old vines rooted in mica schist soils in Kamptal, made primarily from Grüner Veltliner, Riesling and small amounts of other traditional local varieties. It is built around a linear, mineral-driven structure with vibrant acidity and a fine, stony tension throughout the palate. Subtle citrus, orchard fruit, and herbal notes sit in the background rather than taking the lead, giving the wine a restrained, savoury profile. The finish is long, precise, and deeply expressive.

Shining Blanc is a Chenin made from a biodynamic approach, grown on mica schist soils in Kamptal. It shows a precise, tightly structured palate driven by vibrant acidity and a fine, chalky mineral tension. Citrus and orchard fruit notes are present but restrained, supported by subtle savoury depth and a lightly textured feel. The finish is long, focused, and energetic, giving the wine a pure and highly detailed expression.

A wine that is as modern and old school as it gets - how’s that possible? Well, Alwin and Stefanie always had vineyards on their best sites in Kamptal planted with the lesser-known varieties of the area such as Weissburgunder and Muskateller however it never felt as if it was the wine they felt connected with - that changed when they decided to pick the vineyard as a whole - so meaning picking all their grapes including the classic Grüner and Riesling and co-ferment them and press them as a traditional field-blend as Alwin's grandfather would have done. To give some more flavour and character

“Doudou Tu Viens” is a Pinot Noir that is full of purity and charm. The palate is supple and fluid, with bright red berry fruit leading the way and a gentle, juicy texture underneath. Fresh acidity keeps it lifted, while a subtle spicy, floral edge adds nuance. This is a highly approachable and joyful expression of Burgundy.

San Sou Si is a Gamay from old vines rooted in pink granite soils in Fleurie, showing a pure and vibrant expression of Beaujolais. The palate is silky and lifted, with juicy red berry fruit carried by bright, energetic acidity. There’s a gentle floral and spice edge that adds detail. The finish is long, fresh, and precise, giving it both charm and structure.

Sous les Coudriers is a Chardonnay that combines precision with a vibrant, energetic style. The palate is finely structured, driven by bright acidity and a mineral backbone that gives it real drive. Citrus and orchard fruit are layered with subtle savoury and lightly creamy notes, adding depth and definition. The finish is long, focused, and dynamic, leaving a clear and expressive impression of its cool-climate origin.

Les Champs des Roches is a precise and clean Riesling from Zellenberg, nestled in the Alsace. It's an aromatic wine with notes of ripe apple with a clean mineral core. There's vibrant acidity in this wine which gives it depth and structure, but remains fresh and thirst-quenching. A lovely Riesling that is more than simply Alsace.

Les Pentes Sèches is a Pinot Gris from the declassified Schoenenbourg Grand Cru in Alsace. This is an elegant and clean wine suitable for all wine drinkers. Crisp apple, lemon and dried herbs shine through, and the palate is clean with a sharp minerality running through.

A classic expression of Jacquere from the Savoie – fresh with a bracing acidity, notes of ripe apple, a flinty, smokey quality, and a clean and elegant finish. Grapes are pressed very gently using an old Coquard press (widely used in Champagne for the quality of extraction) and fermented directly in oak – Mathieu Goury makes wines made using an old-school approach and a 'no-compromise' approach to quality, which is immediately evident as soon as you taste them.

Maluseaux is an expressive Gamay from old vines grown on clay‑silt soils in the Loire Valley around Noizay in Vouvray, where limestone‑rich tuffeau gives the fruit vibrancy and freshness. Alexandre farms biodynamically and tends his vineyards with horses, and this Gamay is vinified with minimal intervention to let the site speak clearly. The palate unfolds with juicy red‑berry and raspberry fruit, framed by supple tannins and lively acidity, giving the wine a bright, energetic structure. There’s a hint of herbal nuance and fine mineral tension that carries through to a clean, focused finish.

A beautifully light Vouvray that doesn't sacrifice on depth. Honey, lemon and butter on the nose, with an almost tropical finish and a delightful salty edge. A touch of residual sugar gives this wine incredible depth and character, without straying into sweet wine territory – the perfect wine for a little every day luxury.

One of our favourite crisp, clean and aromatic whites – this Grüner Veltliner is full of crisp apple, bursting citrus and a very subtle touch of smokey minerality. Fruit forward enough to make it immensely quaffable, but with enough layered complexity to make you pause for thought. Delicious!

Mic Drop Fact: Italy has over 2,000 native grape varieties in the country! And with that many grapes, there's always a new one to discover. Speaking of, meet Nosiola. An ancient Trentino grape variety that is elegance meets concentration with a lasting kiss of skin-contact. A goose-bump worthy bottle.

So seductive! This take on 'glou-glou' from Domaine Inebriati saw Carignan grapes which Victor Beau would usually make into a fuller-bodied red, undergo fermentation by carbonic maceration, resulting in a super juicy, super comforting light red – blueberries, plums and a dusting of cocoa, all underlined by a savoury earthiness. We can't get enough of it!

notes: A dream with seafood but refreshing on its own, this wine shows the impact of different soils on the grape, Melon de Bourgogne, and the true potential of how great muscadet can be. Poiré Le Closevin is a traditional Normandy perry made from carefully selected old pear varieties, giving it a pure and artisanal expression of fruit. The palate is light and gently sparkling, with crisp pear and citrus notes carried by bright, refreshing acidity. There’s a subtle natural depth that adds texture without heaviness, keeping it very easy to drink yet strikingly characterful. The finish is clean, zesty, and lightly saline, making it a refreshing and highly drinkable.

Poiré La Prémoudière is a traditional Normandy pear cider made from a blend of old pear varieties, giving it both finesse and character. The palate is bright and lightly sparkling, with crisp pear and green orchard fruit supported by vibrant, mouth-watering acidity. Subtle floral and almond notes add a gentle aromatic depth without heaviness.
A delicious and bright Cider from Normandie made up of Apple, Pear and Quince.

The 2021 cuvée of Selves from Nicolas Carmarans comes from old-vine Chenin Blanc planted on limestone and clay soils in Cahors . Made with minimal intervention and native yeast fermentation, the wine captures the purity and minerality of the site. Bright citrus, green apple, and hints of white flowers unfold with fine, racy acidity and a subtle mineral touch. Gentle weight and a smooth texture carry through to a long, precise finish. Delicate layers of honeyed fruit and soft orchard notes emerge, adding depth without heaviness.

producer: Ça Boit Libre | Damien Bastian Goddard
notes: The Mon Blanc series from Bastian Goddard are a true testament to how Goddard can make a fun, engaging and very serious wines all in one. The 2023 vintage of the Mon Blanc Marignan delivers both freshness and depth, with pure fruit and a lovely balance. From it's limestone-rich soil in Savoie this wine is seriously crips and lovely. Smooth and layered texture, a herbaceous tone and a fine mineral notes. Dangerously easy drinking but very sophisticated.

A slight earthiness is present, but it's minerality runs through to the finish keeping this wine precise and balanced.

On the palate, subtle citrus and orchard fruit unfold with vibrant acidity and a soft, lightly tannic grip. The finish is clean and persistent, reflecting the wild, expressive spirit of Strohmeier’s Styrian vineyards.

Lucas Rieffel is farming and making wines of the future. His wines are not your typical charming-but-old-school Alsatian wines; rather they are emotive, jolting wines that show an entirely new face of Alsace. This crémant is zingy yet luxurious, like a hefty squeeze of lemon on a fresh crepe. If you're looking for a delicious traditional method sparkling wine without the Champagne price tag, you've come to the right place.

Fleurie 'Poncie' is a delightful and fun expression of Gamay from old vines planted in the historic Poncié lieu-dit in Fleurie. The sandy granite soils here give the wines a lift and a unmistakable finesse. Made with whole clusters and a gentle, low intervention approach, the cuvée captures the vibrant and floral cluster known in these wines. Bright red berries and cherry are accompanied by soft spice and silky tannins. A subtle mineral edge adds length and precision all the way to the finish.

wine: Blanc de Noirs Reserve Brut Nature 2013
notes: A sparkling wine that's almost more Champagne-esque in style than some Champagnes we've tried! What's more, if you bought Champagne that had spent the same amount of time ageing on lees that this wine has – 10 years! – you'd end up paying super mega bucks for it. A beautifully classic sparkling Blanc de Noirs with mind-blowing depth, the perfect bottle for a celebration, or to stow away for a few more years for a real treat that's worth waiting for.

Anita and Hans are working on the limestone slops of the Leithaberg. This is a region where Blaufränkisch and Furmint thrives. It's both deep and incredibly fresh. Minimal intervention and a gentle approach is key for developing these wines. The character of the vineyard shows clearly in Tannenberg. There's crisp apple and citrus shining through with a subtle herbal note. Bright acidity held together with a firm mineral backbone. The texture is structured and balanced, leading to a long, focused finish. A distinctive expression of Furmint that shows both precision and depth.

This Blaufränkisch comes from south-facing vineyards in Burgenland , where slate and loam soils give the grape structure and energy. Made with gentle handling and minimal intervention, the wine lets the vineyard speak clearly through the fruit. On the palate juicy dark berries and tart cherry are supported by fine tannins and a touch of spice, leading to a vibrant, mineral-driven finish.

Nittnaus' Gritschenberg vineyard produces some seriously good wines. Limestone and slate soils are key to giving the Blaufränkisch here both structure and freshness. Restraint and low-intervention is key in Anita and Hans' approach. On the palate dark cherry and blackberry are supported by fine tannins and a gentle touch of spice. The acidity is bright but remarkably balanced and focused, and a subtle minerality carries straight to the finish. Precise, expressive and elegant.

Made with careful, low-intervention winemaking, the wine highlights the purity and precision of the site. Juicy dark berries and tart cherry are complemented by fine tannins and a touch of spice, all backed up by vibrant acidity. The finish is long, mineral-driven and balanced, revealing the vineyard’s character in every sip.

With a little effervescence on opening, this is a wine for those who aren't afraid to try something new or different.

Crunchy red fruit, pink peppercorn and gentle but present tannins make for a real crowd-pleasing wine.

producer: Domaine de l'Ecu | Fred & Claire Niger
notes: From Domaine de l'Ecu , this wine is made entirely from Folle Blanche grown on sandy, well-drained soils in the Loire Valley. Fermented and aged with minimal intervention in neutral vessels, it showcases the purity and delicacy of the grape. On the palate, bright citrus, green apple, and gentle floral hints are balanced by lively acidity and a subtle mineral touch. The texture is light and precise, carrying through to a clean, focused finish. A very expressive wine, it perfectly reflects the elegance and individuality of Folle Blanche.

Coming from the steep slopes of the Saybritz vineyard in south Burgenland, this single vineyard expression of Blaufränkisch is electric. Dark fruited and spicy, all while remaining seriously terroir driven – this pure expression of one of our favourite varieties is about as good as it gets.

Ofen comes from Blaufränkisch vines planted on the gravelly, limestone slopes of Burgenland. The wine highlights the purity of the fruit and the character of its site. Ripe dark cherry and blackberry are supported by fine tannins and vibrant acidity. There's focus through the finish, and it's precise and engaging. This is a Blaufränkisch that offers energy and complexity while remaining approachable from the first sip.

Mammutquite is back! And the 2025 vintage of Wachstum König's quince juice is tasting better than ever. Much like wine made from old vine wines, there is outstanding depth and concentration to this cuvée, with the mammoth quinces harvested to make the juice coming from exceptionally old trees – more than 100 years old, in fact. A game changer for the low- and no-alcohol landscape. These natural juices are unfiltered, cold-pressed, and bottled without any additives.

Bright, refreshing and linear, this is everything you could want from a Trocken (or dry) Riesling. On the nose, this is almost reminiscent of a whiskey sour, with a tart lemon quality and a subtle refined smokiness. A wine with a prominent mineral quality, this would pair well with almost anything but particularly with delicately spiced Thai food.

Off-dry with a touch of residual sugar that gives the wine a sumptuous round quality, along with a green apple quality, reminiscent of cloudy apple juice. This is first and foremost, though, a terroir-driven wine, with pertinent notes of slate and a touch of campfire smoke, like the kind that lingers on your clothes after a bonfire. Enjoy this with a goats cheese salad on a sunny day and transport yourself to the rolling green hills of the Mosel valley.

With its deep golden colour, oily texture and notes of bruised apple, wet stone and flakey sea salt, this is Riesling that will delight fans of something more classical in style as well as those who are yet to be convinced of the joy of a good Riesling. This is a bottle that will only improve with age too, so drink it now or hold onto it for a few years and reap the rewards.

If you're only familiar with Tokaji as a sweet wine, prepare to have your world rocked. With just a touch of residual sugar to balance out the naturally high acidity of Tokaji wine, the Birtok Válogatás 2020 is full of depth, sophistication and energy. Lemon drops, green apple and just a hint of spice make this a perfect thirst quencher and contemplative wine at the same time.

notes: From Alwin & Stefanie Jurtschitsch , this 2022 Grüner Veltliner comes from the steep, south-facing terraces of Ried Loiserberg in Kamptal . Fermented naturally with minimal intervention, it showcases bright orchard fruit and crisp citrus, lifted by subtle herbal notes. The texture is precise yet supple, carrying through to a long, focused finish. Perfectly balanced energy, clarity, and elegance.

Stone fruit, citrus peel, and subtle floral notes unfold with bright freshness and a silky texture. A soft mineral undertone carries through to a long, precise finish, reflecting the character of the hillside vines.

A rich, ripe and round white wine coming from the north of Italy in Alto Adige. While you might not be familiar with Souvignier Gris as a variety – a hybrid specifically developed to withstand different diseases – this is the perfect bottle to get acquainted with it. Fresh and fruity, with notes of honey and melon, the perfect summer time wine.

This Cabernet Sauvignon comes from vineyards on the rocky Karst plateau near the Adriatic, where the grape develops a distinctive balance of power and freshness. Farmed organically and made with a traditional approach, the wine is aged slowly in barrel to allow its structure to soften and its character to develop. There's deep notes of blackcurrant, dried plum and dark cherry, layered with spice and leather. With time in the glass, earthy tones and a subtle smokiness add further depth.
