Here we have Grenache, both noir and gris, harvested in Villeneuve de Berg to the south of the Ardèche. The red grapes sit in the juice of the gris to bleed their pigment and gently draw out tannin over an entire month. It was then bottled straight after, in November the same year, meaning all of the ageing has taken place in the bottle. The wine feels somewhere between a fruit punch and a herbal tea - juicy red strawberry melds with spicy Grenac

A multi-dimensional maceration of equal parts Viognier and Grenache Blanc. The former come from organically farmed vines planed over limestone and clay near Sardan in the Gard, the latter from St Remeze in the south of the Ardèche, both of which benefit from the influence of the mistral wind, moderating temperatures. Made in the infusion style, whole bunches of Viognier sit for 25 days in the direct-pressed juice of the Grenache, for a gentle extraction. The wine was then slowly pressed off by hand and left to rest for one year in an old 400-litre barrel before bottling with no additions. The

Some serious Doubs Chardonnay with a lot to interest fans of the crystalline Jura style associated with the likes of Ganevat, Labet, Overnoy, et al, or similarly a top Côte de Beaune Burgundy . From the warmest vintage in recent memory, it is quite remarkable how the old vines have harnessed its qualities whilst avoiding any of the trappings one might associate with such a year. Displaying great density, power and length, this is already compelling and will reward drinkers for many years to come. *Please note this is the 2018 vintage, not the vintage displayed in the example photograph*

The second vintage of a new cuvée from the young vines of Grenache Blanc that Meryl and Geraldine have been experimenting with for the last couple of years. Belying the youth of the vineyard, here we see some impressive concentration and some lovely light-footed citrus peel zip. Reminiscent of camomile flowers and bay on the nose, this golden wine has a lovely, full mouthfeel, long, limestone-esque acids and a pleasant harmony of ripe yellow citrus, stone fruits and savoury herbs. Grapes were directly-pressed and aged on the fine lees for six months in steel tank before bottling with no additi

aromas: Green Apple, Pear, Lemon, Elderflower, Limestone
notes: 100% Sauvignon Blanc from the youngest vines planted over the mineral-rich limestone gravel, direct-pressed into steel, preserving immaculate freshness, then bottled in early 2026 with no additions. Less steely and with softer edges than his more classical staple ' La Pente de Chavigny ', this feels open and inviting, but still with that lovely laser-beam of mouthwatering acidity. Crunchy green apple, elderflower and ripe pear come together in a salivating meld, with a line of raw lemon citrus cutting it all through - without intervention, none of Mikaël’s whites complete malolactic, giving th

Vivid ruby Carignan and another delightfully bright, luminous vintage, already drinking superbly in its youth. Fruit is freshly crushed black and red cherry with a herbal lilt of wild fennel garrigue and light balsamic twang, towards a lovely sense of limestone minerals in the finish. Of all the Mazel cuvées, Raoul feels to shift in appearance more noticeably from year to year - 2024 is what we'd describe as a classic vintage; dry, fruit-driven and with an unmistakable energy. From 50 year-old vines planted over limestone and clay, the grapes undergo a ten-day carbonic maceration before being

A magnum bottling of the second vintage of the Oustric’s latest cuvée to the ranks, which is sure to delight just as much as it did upon its debut. From vines much younger than the other long-established reds of the domaine, it is a recent planting of Cinsault that transmits vigour and youthful energy. Put through the usual carbo treatment for 10 days as whole bunches, it shows an attractive vivid ruby in the glass and aromas give off those dusty dry spices so typical of the grape. Crackling with a bright, nervy energy, the fruits have a pleasing balance of tart raspberry and plum. There is so

Magnum bottling! A perfectly nourishing, Ardéchoise expression of Grenache that we'd happily drink day after day. In keeping with the vintage, 2023 sees an abundance of blackcurrant fruit right upfront, giving way to those typically herb-flecked liquorice notes, fennel and clove. It continues the run of form of wines from the last couple of vintages with their propensity for youthful drinking. To us, it is in many ways the perfect bistro wine – affordable enough to put on the table without to much fanfare, yet quietly overperforming and drinking well with just about anything you care to pair i

Characteristically vibrant, intensely fruit-driven Syrah, that dials the deep, glossy blackcurrant and toasted black peppercorn spice to 11. There are aromas of flint and gunsmoke around the juicy fruit, with the herbal notes of rosemary and thyme. It's a front-loaded, rippling wine of immediacy. Best enjoyed with a group of friends in one sitting. Bunches were de-stemmed, crushed and macerated for one week in fibreglass tank, a neutral but porous vessel that the wine rested in until the following spring, before bottling with no additions.

Late harvested for full ripeness, this is bold, classic Cabernet Sauvignon that calls out to be opened up on cool autumn and winter nights. Plenty of smoky blackcurrant fruit, with an umami quality and powdery graphite tannins, this is a wine to stand up to the bolder dishes you might be turning to this month. A bottle to enjoy with friends in one sitting. The bunches were picked in late September, de-stemmed, crushed and macerated for one week before being moved to concrete tanks to complete fermentation. After this, the wine was transferred to clay tinaja to rest for 6 months before bottling

The fruit is picked nice and early to keep it fresh and prevent those OTT baked flavours you might associate with this style. Intense, scorched fruit and just a hint of vanilla from judicious use of oak. Affordable New World pleasures.

Chenin Blanc from less than a hectare of old vines planted over clay, limestone and silex, spread out amongst tiny parcels. From a powerful vintage, the grapes were pressed directly to old barrels for three years of élevage and the wine was bottled with a touch of sugar remaining. This has now dissolved into the wine, leaving a vin de garde of staggering depth and complexity which will reward drinkers for many years to come. Please note that this vintage differs from the photograph and is bottled under crown cap rather than cork.

*Please note that this is a zero-alcohol sparkling soft drink* An ingenious multi-purpose beverage which has quickly become one of our favourite wine alternatives. L’Antidote is made using sparkling Gamay juice which is infused with 15 wild herbs, apple, lemon & ginger; sweetness, fruit and herbs balanced in harmony. Wildly popular for good reason, L’Antidote is the ideal bottle if you are abstaining, but equally the necessary tonic when the morning after requires restorative properties. Romain has recently experimented with a white version of the beverage, Antilope, which is less sweet and a

aromas: Fig, Lemon, Saline, Almond, Walnut, Honey
notes: The intense, Comté-loving, oxidative sous voile style of Chardonnay. Here, over the slow course of 28 months, the wine aged in old oak barrels with no topping-up to form its flor. Highly savoury, the primary fruit has given way to saline flavours of toasted almond and walnut, honey and woody spices. That said, there is fruit to be found too - lemon rinds with a waxy quality and stewed fig provide the counterpoint. With incredible poise and complexity, this special wine has a finish that seems to last for days. A beautiful foil to an after-dinner cheese course, or even as an aperitif alongside

Another of Didier's wines from hybrid vines, here using the white Seyve Villard in a co-fermentation with the red Léon Millot and Plantet varietals. It is amazing to see how it takes on the characteristics of a more familiar Jura red regardless. It has the translucent appearance, ethereal quality and exotic aromatics one might associate with the more expressive examples of Trousseau or Poulsard. As the name would suggest, the vivid purple pigment comes from the Léon Millot, creating an inviting shade in the glass. An intriguing pull of aromatics, from blueberry and watermelon, through blackcur

A wild rosato that bursts with tropical fruit, fresh strawberries and crunchy apples. The volcanic soils on which the grapes are grown give the wine a salty, fresh minerality and a good lick of acidity. Rosarella is made using the same white grape varieties as Tierra! Grapes including Drupeggio, Procanico, Trebbiano & Malvasia. During the last stages of fermentation, the white juice is passed over the skins of Sangiovese grapes from Osarella, where it spends a few days macerating. This technique leads to a wine full of fruit but with very low, fine tannins. A delicious, unique rosato with a wi

100% Grolleau that at a featherweight 9 degrees of alcohol falls very much into that that 'vin de soif' category we so love here at Wayward. Lots of the earthy brambly black fruit and dark cherry notes that we associate with this lesser-sung grape. The oh so delicate and slightly wild 2023 vintage boasts a soaring violet perfume and a slight spritz upon opening. Serve chilled for the best results. Babass is often complimented on his meticulous attention to detail when it comes to his soils. This in turn is credited to the texture, poise and delicacy to be found in the finished wine.

Since Didier declassified to VDF he can no longer write 'Savagnin' on the label, but that is what we have here, coming from both the Champs Rouges and Longefin plots. He has chosen to name the wine using the historical name of the varietal, Traminer. A delightfully lifted expression of the grape, lower gravity gives a fluid, lightweight body that equally doesn't lack the texture, attack or length you'd hope for. Pure, mineral, almost cleansing in character, it marries honey, smoke and spice to beautiful effect. A difficult 2024 wrought with low yields from frost has produced something very spe

A beautiful, deep-fruited Syrah - something Val himself admitted he didn't quite think would turn out this way! Serious is perhaps the wrong word, but this is so very much a Rhone Syrah in its blackcurrant fruit, olive and peppercorn character that both leaps from the glass and explodes on the palate. Soft, silken tannins, fragrant aromas of charred capsicum and coffee and a salty bite of tapenade in the finish. A fantastic take on the grape that shows off Val's more finessed side. A mixture of whole bunches and de-stemmed grapes macerated for 14 days, lifted further by some directly-pressed j

Bouju's iconic Festejar fizz, here in its blanc iteration and geographically scattered, made using grapes from four distinct regions in France. For the lovers of the finer details: Chardonnay comes from both at home in the Auvergne as well as a little further south in Limoux. Sylvaner & Pinot Blanc from the Alsace and even a little Anjou Chenin, Loire, for good measure. The results? A feelgood, party-punch of a wine. All of the grapes are brought together to press, bottled and then left for a year on lees in the bottle. There is texture, there is aromatics, there is a long, cleansing line of a

From young vines of Pinot Noir planted over pure limestone in Uchizy, facing east, some three hundred metres above sea level. The grapes were fermented as whole bunches for a month in cuve, left to infuse without pigeage or remontage, before being pressed off to large foudres for one year of élevage. A warmer year has produced a wine that is a little darker and deeper than previous vintages, where firm tannins frame woodsy notes of berries, earth and spice. Bottled by hand directly from the casks.

La Vrille's entry white, made from younger vines of Ugni Blanc, that lesser-sung French sibling of Trebbiano. Much the same as that Italian grape, it offers yellow fruits with something a little saline and mineral. There is also a lovely oily citrus quality and the softness of ripe pears that ensures a bottle of this wine doesn't hang around for long. The grapes are direct-pressed in whole bunches and left on the fine lees in cuve for 8 months before bottling with no additions. Despite the modest price, this is actually one of their smallest production cuvées - only 700 bottles were made this

Viura from some big, Northern Spanish declassified vineyards farmed with biodynamic practises. An unconventional helping of grapes like Riesling, Petit Manseng and Macabeo are added to the blend, and makes it super-tasty. Fruity, easy-going and a great price.

Mikaël's classic Touraine Sauvignon Blanc from a mixture of five different parcels, each planted over gravelly limestone. The grapes are direct-pressed, then fermented for a month in fibreglass before being raised in steel for a pristine, bone-dry and whistle-clean style. The fruit is harvested once it has shed those clichéd, underripe grassy green characteristics, and its sharp line of acidity is emphasised by the wine naturally not completing malolactic fermentation. 2024 was a warm vintage which shows itself in the generous fruit profile, but as always the wine is angular and mineral too. The same quartet of grapes that makes up the Tinto blend, here given a direct-press into old oak barrels to ferment and age. It follows that this is a deeper, more complex style of rosé, an intriguing mixture of fresh red berry fruit, dessicated coconut and rich, gently oxidative notes from the wood, all rounded of with a piquant lick of raspberry balsamic. An intriguing, highly original wine.

Spry, light-footed blend of Touriga Nacional, Castelão, Tinta Barroca and Syrah planted over the region's calcareous clay soils. The cool Atlantic influence brings out the aromatic side of the grapes - a dusty, powdery perfume with delicate violet florals. A well-executed balance of oceanic freshness in harmony with a charming, old-school rusticity, this understated tinto quietly overdelivers. The grapes were destemmed and crushed, then fermented with eight days of skin contact. The wine was then racked into 225-litre oak barrels, where it aged for twelve months before bottling with no additio

A gorgeous expression of Pinot Noir from thirty five year old vines planted over volcanic sandstone. It macerated as a mix of whole bunches and destemmed grapes for ten days, before being pressed to a combination of old barrels and vats for a year of rest. Light, bright, pretty and perfumed with red berries, earth and spice, it sums up everything we love about Pinot from Alsace.

Ancestral-method Chenin made using the earliest harvest selection for its abundance of mouthwatering acidity. The two years sur lattes before disgorgement has taken the wine from quenching pet-nat into altogether more refined territory. Open aromas of ripe orchard fruits take on a zing of sherbet as perlant pinprick bubbles dance on the tongue. A hairline wire of lingering acid pulls through ripe flesh and chalky minerals, into an extended saline finish, the brioche and spice of the lees an assured counterpoint to the clean, linear fruit. From the first passes of the vineyards in early to mid

A robust, deeply-coloured rosé made mainly from a press of Côt, with a little Gamay in the mix too . Clean and on-point, reflecting a warmer vintage but retaining a fresh line of acidity that cuts the heady raspberry and black cherry fruits with a saline finish. Noëlla joked it's almost reminiscent of an old school Claret, back in the days before those wines became heavy and extracted. A simple vinification - both varietals were pressed off the skins directly into steel, where the wine rested until spring 2026 before bottling.

Noëlla's unconventional red blend that makes so much sense. The wine shows the glossy, herbaceous hallmarks of Cabernet Franc with a dark-fruited, sanguine undertone from the Côt. Think charred green bell peppers, freshly picked forest berries and stony minerals, given depth and supple texture from the time in old oak. As ever, it shows her signature elegance and concentration of fruit. Two separate vinifications of Cabernet Franc and Côt, the former de-stemmed and the latter as whole bunches, both macerated for 10 days before being pressed into 500-litre barrels and steel tanks respectively f

Pretty coral pink pet-nat, this year using a red and white blend of Romorantin, Chardonnay and Côt from her own domaine. Delicate aromas that meld forest berries with stony minerals lead into a fine rush of elegant, needlepoint bubbles. The lean fruits sit in harmony with a gentle creaminess and saline influence from the lees contact, with long, coiling acidity. A little more delicacy and complexity to this blend than the vintage that preceded it, the addition of the white grapes brings a peach quality to the red berry fruits. The grapes were pressed directly together after harvest and bottled

Another beautiful cuvée from Laurent’s Roche Blanche estate. La Pause is made from 100% Gamay from 50-year-old vines. 2024 was cooler vintage for the Roche Blanche estate, with all of Laurent’s wines showing fantastic balance and structure. The grapes underwent a two-week whole bunch maceration before being pressed into 500l barrel and 40hl wood vat for 8 months élevage. La Pause is wonderfully silky, with a featherweight lightness, but still with quite beautiful fruit. A very elegant, fresh and juicy style.

wine: Le Temps des Cerises 'La Peur du Rouge' 2024
notes: Axel made multiple passes through the vines over two weeks, ensuring that he had grapes that provided freshness as well as aromatic complexity. The fruit saw a short maceration for 5 days before pressing and élevage in cuve. An excellent year for this cuvée, it pours a hazy golden hue in the glass and shows a panoply of exuberant tropical fruits balanced by a refreshing acidity.

wine: Le Temps des Cerises 'La Capitulation Ne Paie Pas!' 2024
notes: A wine that began its life as his ‘Brutal’ cuvée years ago. Made with hand-harvested Cinsault, picked during the first passage through the vines. the grapes saw 5 days of whole-bunch maceration before a short élevage in fibreglass tanks. The lightest, and probably the most sought-after of Axel’s wines, this pale, crimson pink offers freshness in abundance with plenty of soft red fruits and vibrant acidity. One to chill down and enjoy in a single sitting.

A new vintage of Metisse, another refinement of the method. In a slight twist to last year, we still have Syrah, direct-pressed to give some fleshy pink juice, but this time we have whole bunches of Viognier in dropped into it for just over a week, to gently macerate and infuse. The grapes come from the Gard, Southern Rhône. The wine is then raised for 8 months in a big, old foudre barrel before bottling with no additions at all. The darker juice from the Syrah pulling more towards a rosé in appearance, but with a peachy sunset tint from the macerated Viognier, it remains a hard wine to catego

Beautifully-coloured rosé pet nat from monsieur Cousin made from a direct-press of the Chenin that becomes Au-delà and this year the other half is Gamay. Completing fermentation in the bottle, the wine was disgorged by hand in November 2025. The split, or partage of red and white grapes gives an enticing blush of hazy pink peach in the glass. There is a tartness to the early-picked fruit giving an impression of green strawberry, blood orange, spiced red apples and orchard blossom. A wire of acid coils around it all providing both tension and refreshment. A delightful celebration fizz.

Immensely popular recent new Mazel cuvée, now on its third vinatge. From vines much younger than the other long-established reds of the domaine, it is a recent planting of Cinsault that transmits vitality and youthful energy. Put through the usual carbo treatment for 10 days as whole bunches, it shows an attractive vivid ruby in the glass and aromas give off those dusty dry spices so typical of the grape. Crackling with a bright, nervy energy, the fruits have a pleasing balance of tart raspberry and plum. There is something iron-rich and bloody at its core and the mineral imprint of the limest

One of those rare beasts, a completely sans soufre Champagne from Romain & Thomas Henin's uncompromising La Bulle Libre project. In a region dominated by big-name Champagne houses and prestige, it is refreshing to find something like this. Grower-led, from start to finish, and a wine that reflects a sense of place over a generic 'house style'. A Champagne of terroir that truly fits with the ethos of the other wines we list. 100% Pinot Meunier. A very pretty blanc de noir, with bright, berry-tinged fruit, lovely aromatics and a delicious texture. The grapes were pressed, spontaneously fermented

The 2025 ‘Lucky You!’ is here, The welcome return of Laurent's most iconic wine, a blend of around 70% Sauvignon Blanc with 30% Chardonnay, all from the historic Clos Roche Blanche estate. 2025 was a warm dry vintage and the wine is bursting with fruit, with,as usual, a wonderfully lush texture and balance. The two grapes work together effortlessly, the Sauvignon Blanc bringing beautiful bright fruits while the Chardonnay adds minerality and soft creamy texture.

Delicate new sparkler from Thomas and the first non-Chenin wine we have tasted from him. Made using Gamay, Cabernet Franc and Côt from a small quarter-hectare parcel that he has recently taken on. A luminous salmon pink in the glass from just 24hrs with the crushed grapes sitting in the press, it was then transferred to bottle to complete fermentation and disgorged after one year sur lattes . Soft, mousse-y bubbles cushion a pretty watercolour wash of little bramble fruits and crisp Russett apple, with some unexpected notes of blood orange and clementine citrus. Richly scented with savoury herbs aplenty- think rosemary, thyme and freshly cut grass underpinned with a smoky minerality. The outsized litre-bottle here going some way to describe the wine's drinkabilty. Light influence of skins lends subtle grip and golden tones rather than mouth-puckering tannin. The bitter herbal notes sit beside punchy stone fruit flavours making this wine a dream combination with aromatic spices. You don't need to worry about sipping it either.

Whilst his new love is hybrids, Didier still has more than enough time for the classics - here we have an opulent style of topped-up ouillé Chardonnay. The barrel notes are balanced, but can be picked up on immediately - that rich butterscotch, coconut sort of character that feels to intensify the fruit. Lemon is oily, or like a dense lemon curd; bruised orchard pears, a marmalade-y pithiness and concentration, and a deep-set, struck-match reduction that coils off and melds into the electric acids. Power and purity in great harmony. A mixture of Chardonnay from all three of the Grappe parcels

An atypical Jura white made using a direct-press of the Seyve Villard hybrid - a disease-resistant varietal that requires no herbicide or pesticide vineyard treatments. It flourishes over the red and grey marls and fossil-rich Jurassic limestone of the region, producing a wine that lacks none of the tension and edge you'd hope for from its native Chardonnay or Savagnin. With pristine clarity it shows crisp green apple and preserved lemon, moving through into something more soft and lactic. Fresh and lifted, there are some aromatic herbals and florals above a flinty reduction at the wine's core

aromas: Pear, Melon, Chamomile, Limestone, Oyster Shell
notes: Magnum bottling! Ripe and textural with layers of stone fruits, savoury herbs and a bright mineral backbone from the limestone. Honeyed and nectar-like, with rich aromatics of bay, chamomile, melon and pear. There is an oily, mouth-coating quality with some great attack and verve as the wine passes through into a lovely electric oyster shell salinity in the finish. A nourishing country wine with plenty of Mazel soul. A perfectly nourishing, Ardéchoise expression of Grenache that we'd happily drink day after day. 2024 sees an abundance of blackcurrant fruit right upfront, giving way to those typically herb-flecked notes of liquorice root, fennel and clove. The acidity gives some welcome, angular attack, and as the generous fruits fall back it reveals a mineral undertow of charcoal and stone, something we've found to become more pronounced in recent years. It continues the run of form of wines from the last couple of vintages with their propensity for youthful drinking. To us, it is in many ways the perfect

La Vrille's entry white, made from younger vines of Ugni Blanc, that lesser-sung French sibling of Trebbiano. Lithe and lean this year and heavy on the yellow citrus, there is the raw attack of freshly squeezed lemon with something more oily and pithy to soften the edges. As ever, this is infused with their trademark herbal bay laurel character and the low finished alcohol lends a tonic quality. The grapes are direct-pressed in whole bunches and left on the fine lees in fibreglass cuve for 8 months before bottling with no additions. Despite the modest price, this is actually one of their small

Mikaël's smallest cuvée of which only around 1000 or so bottles are made each year, depending on the yield of the vintage. 100% Côt from 35 year-old vines in a small parcel of silex and clay at around one third of a hectare. These flinty soils are also dotted with unusual black stones, the eponymous and charmingly-named 'Couilles d'Anes' - donkey balls, as the local vigneron colloquially refer to them. No-one can really explain their presence, but it is most likely an ancient alluvial spread from the historic path of the river Cher. The grapes are destemmed, foot-crushed and then macerate for

A beautiful single-vineyard cuvée, using the forgotten Sauvignon Gris varietal - know locally as Fié. It's a historical grape of the region that was largely abandoned because of its low yields in favour of the ubiquitous Sauvignon Blanc. Fié has a much broader, more textural profile and ripens with striking light purple skins. The vineyard is situated on the slopes down to the river Cher, here with particularly deep, well-draining limestone gravel and just a small percentage of clay. Immediately, the aromatics are open and draw you in - white peach, lemongrass, something a little golden and ho

A dark, brooding Spanish natural red wine made with the lesser-known Tintilla, a grape native to the province of Cádiz. Expect ripe, brambly fruit with juicy red cherries and kirsch sitting against a background of Mediterranean herbs. Full and structured but not lacking balance with a welcome line of acidity keeping everything in check, a rare feat amongst wines grown in the scorching heat of Southern Spain. The vineyards here are part of a large 500ha estate in the San Jose del Valle, inland, 35km south east of Jerez, in beautiful countryside close to the Sierra de Cadiz. The estate is made u

Albert’s “Tot” wines are from a single day of harvest, where he passes through each of his plots and selects the ripest grapes – giving a great snapshot of both the producer and growing season. The Tot Blanc is made from white grapes from all of Albert’s plots, which are very lightly macerated on the skins for a week, lending the wine the lightest of tannin alongside sunny stone fruits and Mediterranean herbs. A wine which lies somewhere in between the orange and white wine world. Tot Blanc is is fresh, light, tonic and herbaceous, with a delicately aromatic nose with some aniseed-like underto

Aromatic, juicy rosé of Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier, Johanniter & Pinot Gris, a blend of two vintages both with the same varietals, macerated whole bunch for ten days. In 2024 the barrel wasn't topped up, giving a slight oxidative quality which perfectly balanced with the fruit. The wine immediately impressed with lots of juicy fresh fruit sitting alongside a subtle herbaceous edge. Both delicate and thirst-quenching, this is one to throw in an ice-bucket and knock back with abandon. It’s still early days for this exciting new UK based project, we look forward to see what happens next.

A textured, hazy blend of Parellada and Trepat which glows bright in the glass - a true sunshine wine! The Parellada provides a tonic, citrus quality to the wine, whilst the Trepat provides a hint of bloody-iron minerality alongside bursts of tropical fruit. Pouring a peachy-pink sunset in the glass, this red/white blend gives us everything we need for those long sunny afternoons, with herbs, fruit and minerals sitting in perfect balance. Is it an orange? Is it a rosé? Call it what you like, one thing is for sure, a bottle won’t last long. Made using hand-harvested grapes, the Parrellada and T

The latest from Hannah’s ABRACADABRA project! Here we have a curious cuvée made using Muscat which has been passed over the skins of Auvergnat Gamay for 7 days, resulting in bright, pinky-hued juice. The wine is gently fruit-forward with notes of forced rhubarb sitting beside a bloody mineral edge. An experimental, category-defying cuvée falling somewhere in between the rosé and orange wine world. The grapes here come from two organic growers, the Muscat from Mattia Carfagna (Pouzolles, Hérault) and Gamay d’Auvergne from Nicolas Lebleu (Blanzat, Puy-de-Dôme). Tiny production as always, with ju

The latest from Hannah's ABRACADABRA project! An intriguing red/white blend of Viognier and Cinsault, this is a category defying natural wine which feels somewhere in between the rosé and orange wine world. It’s all tart vibrant fruit with a salty backbone reminiscent of pickles and brine which sit alongside a soft creamy edge and the lightest pearlescent tingle on the palate. A vital and expressive which is one-of-a-kind. Arriving with us just in time for those long, Summer afternoons. Made with a blend of Viognier from Mattia Carfagna’s parcels in Hérault, Southern France, and Cinsault from

A fascinating micro-cuvée of a meagre 300-bottle production, all coming from one single vineyard planted with the Roter Traminer varietal. It's a tiny parcel that Martin has essentially let grow wild, with no ploughing and minimal pruning. It's an experiment in helping the vines to develop their own natural resilience in this setting of biodiversity. Much like its sibling Gewurztraminer, the Roter strain gives off beautiful floral aromatics, but in a far more delicate, detailed and nuanced way. The scent of rose petals but with nothing cloying or overdone. This sense of restraint follows in to

The grape most synonymous with Franken, this is one of Martin's more serious terroir wines made with 100% Silvaner. The vineyard parcel (one of Martin's oldest planted in the late 80s) sits over a particular type of limestone the region knows as Muschelkalk. Rich in fossilised shells and century old marine deposits, it is highly calcareous and imprints precision acid and minerality to the finished wine. To start the grapes were foot-trodden as whole bunches and macerated over the course of a day. After pressing, the first year was spend in old German oak barrels before a transfer to steel for

From the warmer 2023 vintage, this blend of direct-press Dornfelder and Domina draws you in with fragrant, red berry fruits and florals. A vibrant cherry red in the glass, it is a light-bodied Rotwein that demands to be served chilled. Lifted, open and fresh, the fruits meld damson and redcurrant with herbal notes of hibiscus flowers. A wine that very much gives you a feel for the deceptively long, hot summers that can be found in this lesser-sung Bavarian wine region. A spring/summer essential. After pressing the juice was transferred to steel tanks to complete fermentation and rest for 11 mo

Another excellent one-off Crozier cuvée made using a blend of wine that has had time to age a while in the cellar - as its name suggests, a blend of Syrah from 2021 and Merlot from 2019. With a gentle flash of tawny to the edge of the rim, here we have a fine balance of development and freshness. Deep, concentrated red and black fruits meld with rustic tannin, cracked pepper spice and those trademark herbal notes: fennel, burdock root and coltsfoot rock can be picked out amongst the leather, rolling tobacco and richer barrel notes. An electric red/white blend from Lucie and Jules of Ham Street Wines in Kent. Nimble and detailed with pure, juicy red fruits, violets and herbs sitting against a subtle smokiness. A wine which lands in that special intersection between light red and dark rosé, its best served chilled (preferably on a sunny day!). A co-fermentation of 80% Pinot Meunier and 20% Chardonnay, the whole bunches macerate for 25 days before going through the basket press into stainless steel and aging for 8 months. The clue is in the name with this one, Limonada is all about freshness and zip. This is the second iteration of this wine, made using vines planted in 2020. This year Joachim and Caroline chose to press the grapes directly and age the wine in amphora, giving an earthy undertone to that clean, fresh Xarel-lo profile we know and love. A drought-resistant white grape variety which is native to Catalonia, Xarel-lo has been planted in recent years in the Roussillon as a grape that is able to withstand the unforgiving heat and minimal rainfall in the region. The latest iteration of Love Streams! This time made using negocé fruit primarily sourced vineyards in London, Wiltshire and East Sussex. Made with a blend of Bacchus and Reichensteiner, this high energy pet-nat is heady with citrus, elderflower and wild hedgerows. Think Spring in a glass! One to throw in the ice bucket and drink with abandon. The grapes are pressed directly and initially fermented separately before bottling together to finish as a pet-nat. Bottled with no additions. Magnum bottling! Another delightful new experimental La Vrille cuvée that is sure to pique the interest of those who fell for the bright, juicy charms of Canon d'Achille. Similarly, this is a fluid, weightless red that ripples with pure fruit and works best served from the ice bucket. A blend of Grenache and Syrah, it is big on the red fruits - fresh cherries as well as that soapy, confected quality of sweet shop cherry lips. Magnum bottling. Full of delicious, dark blackcurrant fruit, this is 100% Syrah given a twelve-day, whole-bunch carbonic maceration before being pressed back into tank. This had completed fermentation 7 months later and was bottled with no additions in spring 2023. Another lifted and vibrant expression of the varietal. Nicely fruit-forward this vintage, the palate is all salty black olive and blackcurrant, with some saline, savoury bitters and the line of acidity is taut with energetic vim. An utterly thrilling wine and the epitome of the beguiling, almost unfathomable potential that these humble-in-youth wines have to age. 100% Carignan, now with over two decades in the bottle, it has slowly transformed into something quite astonishing. A good friend of ours once remarked "It's like Mazel wines are meant to be old" - it makes a lot of sense when you get the chance to see how they evolve. A briny, sharp wine of refreshment that bursts with salty lemon and grapefruit citrus and textured, peachy flesh. The vines in this particular parcel reach down to a layer of volcanic bedrock which binds all these fruits with an unmistakable aroma of bonfire smoke and lends some good tension to the acidity. A 50/50 mix of Malvasia di Candia and Falanghina from vines planted over rocky limestone and clay at some 400 metres altitude in the hills of Cerreto Sannita . The only white Antonio makes as a direct-press, it shows a rounded, textural mouthfeel that is typical of the grape. Sherbert-y lemon, Galia melon, a savoury, hay-like quality and a saline undertone, leading to green almond bitters in the finish. Following a more challenging 2023, it's great to see Fontana back on this broad, fleshy, well-balanced sort of form. A direct-press of 100% Falanghina planted over rocky limestone at 550 metres of elevation. Fermented and raised in steel, the wine is bottled the following spring with no additions.

A brand new Gismondi wine from 2024, based around a new parcel of Moscato Bianco he recently acquired. This aromatic varietal seems to fare well at the altitude Antonio works, here planted at 550 meters over rocky limestone in the vineyard where the 2024 harvest commenced, in late August. It keeps the florals in check whilst providing some delicious, nectar-like body. The rest is Malvasia from one of the higher 700-meter parcels and the very end of the harvest, at the end of September - so here we have the wine as a perfect book-end of the vintage. Using the Sérine varietal, a lesser-known sibling of Syrah principally associated with some of the finest Côte-Rôtie, and riffing on the tradition in that fabled AOC of blending a little Viognier with the red grapes, Paulette has created a striking wine full of seductive perfume and elegant, soft edges. The split is in fact 50% of Sérine to 30% of the white grape, but the deep colour of the wine goes some way to show how much pigment is contained within these thick-skinned, tightly-clustered berries. At once airy and lifted, but with an unmistakable depth and concentration, for us this is Gamay at its best. The diurnal temperature fluctuations at this altitude draw a diffused perfume, and the granite keeps the acidity tightly-wound. Beautifully supple and fluid in texture, with powdery tannins and deep, dark maraschino cherry fruit. The longer maceration brings a multilayered complexity alongside the higher-register aromatics and salty minerals and dry spices. Pure, fruit-forward Cinsault giving an ultimate red-fruit bomb of raspberries, pomegranate, crunchy cranberries, cherries, wild strawberries and a touch of sour wine gums. This is about as fruity, fresh and zingy as it gets! The 2024 iteration is even lighter than previous vintages, with a minerality, a touch of herbs and the gentlest of spritz giving the wine even further lift. Another shining example of a bright, vibrant natural wine that goes against the big, broad-shouldered-wine expectations that people associate with the region. A totally delicious, bouncing ball of a wine. Made with 100

100% Viognier from two different parcels on either side of the valley, one facing east to catch the morning sun and one facing west, soaking up the afternoon rays, providing overall ripeness in the finished blend. From a cooler vintage, the wine is nevertheless broad and textural, showing oily citrus, grassy elderflower and fleshy yellow stone fruits. There are verdant green herbs, bay laurel and the time the wine has had in contact with the lees can be felt in the savoury spice of the long finish. Intriguing Sauvignon Blanc with a degree of opulence that pulls off a fine balance between rich, barrel-y influence and fresh, invigorating citrus fruits. Big aromas that meld some of those buttery notes with lemon and lime leap from the glass and on the palate the wine is impressively soft, rounded and concentrated. Pithy white grapefruit and a certain creaminess entwine with the racy acids in its very long finish. In short, not your typical Loire Sauvignon; in some ways there are elements you could liken to a Bourgogne Aligoté. A fascinating wine of contrast and balance. Magnum bottling! Fro

A great introduction to the world of natural orange wine here with Sicilian skin-contact Catarratto. Expect a rich, pithy fruit character with ripe melon, grapefruit, sage and white flowers sitting beside saline freshness with ease. Totally moreish. Great bang for buck here! Made with 100% Catarratto, 30% of the grapes macerate on skins for just 3 days, making the wine incredibly approachable and a great place to start if you’re new to orange wine. Fermentation with native yeasts in stainless steel tanks, no filtration, no fining and just a touch of sulphur.

From the prized 80 year-old vines of the domaine, this is an incredibly scarce micro-cuvée variant on Les Doyennes, and the product of a single 180-litre clay amphora. As such, the wine particularly stands out from the others in the currently release – where they are tense and angular, this wine possesses a completely different character, the sharper notes filed down, soft-edged and diffused. It’s fascinating to see how this small vessel has taken the wine in such a different direction. Rayon is tense, multilayered Chenin, with concentrated ripeness, textural depth and a judicious opulence. The nose shows luscious orchard fruits with a softness of apple blossom, honey and the faintest touch of walnut. Perfectly balancing buttery broad-shoulders with a lucid clarity, this finely-tuned wine is bound with a sinew-y coil of acidity that cuts with phenomenal length – the titular white ray. Blending grapes from different altitudes - the obscure pink-skinned Trebbiano Rosa varietal planted over clay at the bottom of the valley alongside Malvasia di Candia from the volcanic soils at around 600m. This year Antonio has taken on a new parcel of Trebbiano which joins the mix. Co-fermented on the skins over 2 weeks in open topped tanks before being pressed off to steel for a short rest, then bottled in the spring with no additions. Feeling that the 2024 harvest from the prized Le Franc vineyard was not suited to the usual barrel treatment, Olivier decided to vinify this fruit in a similar way to Pur Breton - the results are superb and possess the vibrant energy of a primeur. A little reduced on opening, this quickly gives way to a rapidly-evolving list of aromatics - little red fruits, floral lift, the dusty spice of peppercorns toasting in a pan. Fluid and light on the palate, this nimble, bracing wine is a revelation. Best served lightly chilled.

Great value wine for the table that ticks all the boxes in terms of viticulture and vinification - an expressive blend of white grapes that mutes the overtly 'Sauvignon-y' characteristics by not picking too early. It's an interesting, unusual wine that doesn't correspond with its mixture of varietals in the traditional sense. There is a lightly oxidative note and a bready, lees-y back palate that bounces off the fruit which is at once fresh and zesty and creamy and opulent. It's always great to find wine like this at this sort of price. Easy, fun and just a little bit wild.

From Olivier's prized old vines of massale selection Cabernet Franc, grafted by his grandfather in the late 40s. As you'd expect, Le Franc demonstrates vin de garde qualities that suggest a long life ahead in the cellar - we're happy to offer some with a little cellar time, from the 2022 vintage. De-stemmed, foot-crushed and fermented in an open-topped wooden vat, it was then pressed and run by gravity into old demi-muid barrels to rest for 18 months before bottling with no additions. Pur Breton is in many ways Olivier's emblematic cuvée. Side-stepping the more vegetal, herbaceous side of the grape, here we have something a little more savoury, spicy and perfumed. Sangiovese full of ripe plummy fruits, spice and Mediterranean herbs, underpinned by a distinct olive-briney note and bloody minerality that ties the wine together. Super versatile, the 2023 Osarella succeeds is a touch lighter than previous vintages, without compromising on depth of flavour. ‘Osarella’ is the name of the hamlet in the municipality of Orvieto where the vineyard is located. The vineyard is south-facing and characterised by clayey soils rich in fossil shells. Made using 100% Sangiovese, the grapes are a blend of both destemmed and whole bunches. As you're more likely to find a pet nat from the Loire, or a cremant from Limoux listed here at Wayward, it follows that Champagne isn't really an area we specialise in. Show-stopping biodynamic grower Champagne that will have the hairs on your arms standing on end. Truly sublime and unforgettable wine. We don't say that lightly! This comes from low-yielding vines in the lieu-dit 'Biaune', a cool parcel planted alongside the forest on Kimmeridgian soil. The Chardonnay vines are massal selections from Selosse’s 'Avize' and Dauvissat's Chablis Grand Cru vineyards. Miranius, named after the friendly fox who roams the vineyards enticed by the sweet aromas of the grapes. Made with 100% Xarel-lo, a fairly neutral grape which is most commonly used in Cava production. When grown with care, it acts as the perfect vehicle for terroir expression. Here we see the brisk, agile side of the grape, mineral driven from the limestone rich soils from which it is grown. Crisp as a fresh green apple with citrus aplenty and a satisfying salty finish. Bold and ripe with a balanced creaminess that doesn't knock your head off with oak. Tropical fruit, those banana foam sweets and pears that collapse with ripeness. Affordable New World pleasures.

A wine that easily disproves the notion that Cava can only be cheaply produced, everyday fizz. This is mature, complex Cava produced with a patience that we have not seen elsewhere! A hazy, pale gold wine with discreet tannins and lifted aromas of yellow citrus and salty grapefruit pith. An earthy smokiness and tense, cleansing acids gives a thoroughly volcanic feel. 'Cerreto' is the local name for Malvasia di Candia, here given a 9-day skin fermentation in open-topped tanks, before being pressed off to steel to rest before bottling in the spring with no additions. A new pet nat of supreme refreshment, made with 70% Gros Vert, an obscure grape not often cultivated for winemaking that Val purchases from a neighbouring organic grower in Luberon. A huge field blend from a single plot of old vines planted all the way back in 1912. Filled with fresh raspberry fruit intwined with a deep minerality and gentle spritz upon opening, giving the wine an irresistible thirst-quenching quality. An incredible multi-faceted natural wine that changes and grows in complexity as you drink it. Try it chilled. The grapes undergo a two-day infusion before aging in a mixture of concrete tank and wood, emphasising freshness and fruit with just a touch of spice in the background. A light-footed new counterpart to Mikaël's crowd-pleasing French Clara , and much like that wine, it is incredibly easy get on with - perfect fare for the table or a bottle to open when nothing too demanding is required. A special cuvée made only in exceptional years, of which 2023 was deemed to be in this part of Beaujolais. One of our top picks for the colder months at that sweet-spot, mid-range price point - Rossore is dark, brooding Piedmontese Barbera that sees a maturation in old barrels, adding many layers of complex cedar spice to wrap around the smoky red fruits. The barrels are not topped up which adds another, gently oxidative complexity. The wine is also aged in the bottle for a year before bottling, meaning it is really hitting its stride right now and provides incredible value at the price point. A thirst-quenching sparkling rosé that never seems to last long once the bottle is popped open. Aromas of apricot and acacia blossom are met with a hint of grapefruit alongside a zippy acidity. The 2023 feels even lighter than the previous vintage – with hints of gentle blackcurrant-like fruit notes and subtle spice. As the name suggests, this one is full of summery berry fruits and is best enjoyed outdoors when le ciel est bleu (the sky is blue). A joyful and immediately satisfying Malbec/Merlot blend, this is the juiciest of La Calmette’s wines. Immediate and enticing, bursting with ripe red fruits and spice underpinned with a satisfying edge of graphite and intense minerality. 2023 was an exceptional vintage for Maya and Nicholas, the resulting wine is beautifully silky and ripe. In a region otherwise known for muscular, tannic, over-baked reds, ‘Serpent A Plumes’ goes against the grain, showing Malbec’s brighter, lighter side without compromising on substance and depth of flavour. Huge solera-style red that blends 6 different vintages of Grenache and Syrah in old barrels, making for the most muscular, powerfully-structured and complex wine we have tried from this grower. Going back as far as 2018, it shows an interesting mix of developed notes from age, with the fruit-driven character of the more youthful wine from recent years - such is the intrigue of this type of assemblage. Bright, fluid Grenache, with lifted aromatics of dusty redcurrant, capsicum spice and strawberry liquorice. Slick, glossy texture with compact tannins that become more prominent as they move into the finish. There is something distinctly Gamay-esque at play here; fruit-forward, flora, but with those dusty dry spices and herbal tones that make it so very Ardèche. The grapes went through carbonic maceration as whole bunches and were pressed off after four days to mature in steel tanks for ten months before bottling with no additions.

Alakazam is a direct-press Chardonnay made with from Ardèchois grower Thierry Doulmet in Alba la Romaine. The wine is aged for 2 years in old barrels from Andrea Calek, and not topped up. An Americano is a traditional apéritif from Piedmont. A play on the French amér, it is similar to a Vermouth, but usually contains extra bitter components. Mauro’s is based on Grignolino from his niece-in-law, Nadia of Cascina Tavijn. This is blended with raw alcohol steeped in sugar, wormwood, savoury, orange skin, gentiana root and a host of dry Italian pantry herbs. Served on the rocks with a glug of soda and a slice of orange, it is a cult classic that never disappoints.

Muscular Northern Rhône -style Syrah from the Bonneton’s prized vineyard, where vines planted as far back as the 1940s cling to steep, south-facing terraces that look down to the river Doux, one of the Rhône ’s western tributaries. The very oldest vines here are specifically Sérine, a thick-skinned, tightly-clustered clone of Syrah that is principally associated with nearby Côte-Rôtie. Pin-prick bubbled natural pet-nat of Moscatel d'Alexandria from Albert’s Clot del Tuets plot. The 2022 vintage was a ripe one, Natürlich manages to be both fresh and juicy. Peachy pink-hued, zippy and thirst quenching, the 2022 is a blend of Folle Blanche 70%, Gamay 20%, Pinot Noir 10%. Great value, everyday drinking bone-dry white. The character is lean; fruit is saline lemon, with a zesty, prickly acidity. Smoky and bread-y on the nose with added texture from extended time on the lees - the classic technique in this area to give this ordinarily neutral grape varietal. Very easy to get on with.

Another year means another exciting new cuvée from Jérôme. Made using a blend of many local grape varietals; Barbera, Sangiovese, Ancellotta, Merlot and Lambrusco Grasparossa from old vines planted over limestone, over 400 metres above sea level. The grapes were destemmed and fermented on the skins for ten days, before being pressed to cement vats until the following spring. Samodia Rosso is rustic, layered and a little bit wild. A huge blend of local varietals which have had just a touch of skin contact. Pouring a hazy shade of gold in the glass, it is a little more compact and elegant than last vintage, with stone fruits, almonds and minerals at the fore. Vino da tavola of the highest order! Made with a blend of local grapes including Pignoletto, Albana, Montuni, Trebbiano Modenese, Trebbiano Romagnolo and Moscato from old vines planted over limestone, over 400 metres above sea level. A third of the grapes were fermented on the skins for four days, whilst the rest were pressed directly to concrete, where the wine res

Very tasty, very youthful, very nicely priced natural Rioja from El Mozo, an organic grower in Rioja Alavesa. If you prefer your Rioja in the 'joven' style - that means fresher, fruit-driven and kept away from the oak barrels; this is the one. It's made in the maceratión carbónica style in open concrete tanks. A method used to to yield maximum juice and dial back the tannic structure. There's also a splash of Viura and Malvasia in there too (white grapes) to lighten things further. Such a little sweet-spot bargain.

Magnum Bottling! A micro-Jura gem coming care of the talented young grower Thomas Jacquin. Thomas is part of the next generation of growers making a name for themselves in the Jura, and here we have his first vintage of Savagnin that has been aged in barrels. The result is fantastically complex with yellow citrus, nutty spice and minerals aplenty, with just the right amount of grip that indicates it will evolve beautifully over time. A wine very much built for the long haul. Fromenteau is made with 100% Savagnin from a 25-year-old parcel planted over clay and marl in Arbois. The majority of th

France and Spain meet in this unique blend of Grenache Noir and Graciano harvested from vines just outside of Estella in Navarra, planted on clay soils. The fruit saw 3 weeks of maceration with élevage for one year in a mix of large and small old barrels. A deep and finely structured wine that offers a refined take on the region through Imanol’s unique lens. Spicy with notes of cracked black pepper and salt sitting against blackberries and a touch of liquorice. The perfect accompaniment to Spanish tapas. Originally from San Sebastián, Imanol Garay’s project draws on inspiration from his experi

A sunkissed blend of young vines of Callet, Manto Negro and Fogoneu from Felantix along with a handful of other local varieties, planted over the island’s characteristic red clay soils. The grapes were mostly destemmed, with a small quantity of whole bunches in the mix, and macerated from anywhere between a week and a month before being pressed off to vats for six months of rest. The result is a delicate wine with a complex perfume of blackberries, red earth, brine and wildflowers that marries wonderfully with the silky tannins and cascade of bitter herbs that follow. A litre of Mallorcan suns

A sure-fire banger natural wine here in in Schödl's entry-level wine. As with most of their whites, an element of skin-contact provides texture and aromatics and has the wine dancing in the middle of the white wine/orange wine venn diagram. A miscellany of local grapes - Grüner, Welschriesling, Muscat & Weissburgunder - marry together, each contributing a little of their character in harmonious balance. Ripe stone fruits, floaty perfume and some sharp, zingy acid.

Ça Se Discute, a prime red chiller arriving just in time for the sunshine. Made using two different varieties of Pineau d'Aunis, regular Aunis and Aunis Tenturier, bought in from outside of Laurent's Clos Roche Blanche domaine. The grapes here coming from Domaine de Cambalu in neigbouring Francueil- just 15 minutes from Laurent. For the 2024 iteration of this cuvée Laurent de-stemmed the fruit as usual and aged in fibreglass tank keep the fruit impeccably fresh. The wine is vibrant and bright and feels featherweight on the palate, clocking in at just 10.5%. Alongside beautiful aromatics you’ll

A tea-like maceration of Pinot Gris (known here as Ruländer) that brings together white flowers, lychee and apricot from the top end to meet more earthy, savoury depth coming from below. A gorgeous sunset crush in the glass, the inclusion of the skins placing this wine somewhere between pink and orange in both appearance and character. All peaches and cream, citrus peels and spice, the tannins are delicately extracted and this grippy texture persists well into the finish. The grapes were manually de-stemmed and then crushed and macerated on the skins for 5 days in steel. After a very gentle pr

A big blend of different Mallorcan varietals from all over the island go into this iteration of Fato (previously known as Chateau Pacquita). The fruit here is dark, luminous and sun-kissed without being weighty. Balancing the fruit is a gentle layer of earth, herbs, spice sitting against a salty sea breezy quality. Few wines transport us to their origin in the same way as Elio's, this is Mallorca in a glass. Fato 2022 is made with old vines of Callet, Manto Negro, Garnatxa Peluda, Fogoneu Mallorqui, Fogoneu Frances and more from 8 small plots in Felanitx and Porreres over the island’s emblemat

If you're after a simple, satisfying, thirst quenching fizz, this is a go-to. A pink-pet nat made with Catalonian staples Xarel-lo, Macabeo & Parellada and just a splash of red grape Mandó (an almost extinct varietal). The name means 'I am thirsty', so you can imagine what you're going to get - a moreish and cleansing fizz, brisk and generous with lemon and apple notes aplenty from the white grapes while the Mandó supplies all the tart red berry & sour cherry notes. Youthful, vibrant and one to not take too seriously. Pop it in the ice bucket, it’s the ultimate thirst-quencher.

The first sparkling wine ever from Gismondi - it's a party indeed! A traditional method fizz that takes as a base wine the directly-pressed Falanghina of Fontana from the 2022 vintage, which is then re-fermented in the bottle with the must of 2023 without disgorgement, col fondo style. A fine-beaded frizzante that pours a hazy gold in the glass, this very much takes the fleshy, textural peachiness of the varietal and sets it against the saltiness of both the lees contact and the limestone rock of the vineyard soils. Mousse-y and soft, it has a pleasingly rounded front end that goes through orc

Fantastically pure single-vineyard Pinot Noir that is bottled each year under a different name. Reflecting the burst of sun that came just before the 2023 harvest, Chamade binds pretty red fruits, perfume and spice with a sumptuous ripeness and underlying muscularity. Growing over cooling limestone marl helped to preserve the acid core of the wine and there are fragrant, aromatic elements floating above deep red and black fruits. A beautifully expressive wine that shows both power and freshness and reflects one of the many unique terroirs of the region. The grapes went through carbonic macerat

Dark fruited Merlot from 50-year-old vines situated some 500m above sea level (some of the highest vines in the Ardèche) on the edge of the wild and mountainous Cevennes forest. Sota Mon Soleu (Under my Sun) is a beautifully pure expression of Merlot which balances lush ripe fruit with just a touch of spice against silky tannins and fresh streak of acidity. The 2023 vintage was warm, much like 2022 but with more rain just before harvest, providing some much-needed balance to the wines. As Laurent says 'it's a bottle of sunshine!'. Fantastic value to be found here.

Never ones to stop experimenting, Petit Prince is a stunning new La Tangente cuvée that pushes the idea of multiple terroirs further, here taking grapes from the Gard, Vaucluse and the southern Ardèche and bringing them together to combine their delicate infusion style with the structure of whole-bunch. Cinsault & Carignan see the latter treatment, macerated for ten days and then blended into a separate vinification where an uncommon combination of Grenache, Syrah and Tempranillo has been gently extracted by dropping a selection of complete bunches into their directly-pressed juice. After 7 mo

A one-off cuvée from the cellar that harks back to the more structured style of their earlier reds. A mix of grapes from two regions, it blends Cinsault from the Gard with Gamay from Beaujolais. Both were co-fermented, macerated together as whole bunches for ten days before being transferred to a mixture of clay amphora and old oak foudre barrel to rest for 8 months. The wine was then bottled with no additions and has been rested in the cellar for three years before release. With a bit of time to age, the dusty perfume of the wine has developed into something akin to a savoury Jura Pinot, inte

100% Chardonnay from the tiny growing region of Bugey, a region that sits between Savoie and Jura. This one hits immediately jumping from the glass with all things citrus, peaches and cream. On the palate the wine is first all textured and mouth-coating before a welcome lick of acidity zips into the finish. Hazy, textured and just a little bit wild. Made with grapes from many different micro-parcels planted over 5 hectares. Each parcel with it's own soil type and exposure gives a real snapshot of the growing region – a Patchwork cuvée! After hand-harvesting, the grapes are brought to the cella

The most boldly-structured of the Grange du Nord wines, Mitan introduces a wild-edged nose of Carignan to the Grenache and Cinsault, and brings a lightly vegetal, stemmy character from the whole bunches. Giving the most textbook notes of the varietals in its expression, there are forest fruits, blackcurrants and spice, with a tannic structure that feels woven into the wine. At once more classical, but at the same time that rugged, ever-so-funky Carignan character is still at the door, gently nudging its way in to those crowd-pleaser qualities. A fine balance of structure and freshness, and an

Wine from this remote Sicilian satellite island is always something to get excited about, offering a distinct sense of place with little to compare to. Here we have some real nectar; 100% Zibibbo from 60 year-old bush vines fermented on the skins in amphora buried in the sandy volcanic soils of the vineyard to harness the heat of the earth to trigger fermentation. The grapes are de-stemmed and macerate for between 8 and 15 days in these vessels before being gently pressed and then fed back in with a portion of the skins to rest for 6 to 8 months before bottling. In recent years one of the big challenges in this part of France has been slow or stuck fermentations. Whilst different methods can be employed to combat this, like maybe blending in freshly pressed juice from a more recent vintage to kick-start movement again. In cases such as this things have been left just as they are and bottled as a medium-sweet wine with its own unique character. A super-fun and totally wild one off rosado with the lightest little spritz. Made in collaboration with Viña Niebla. A high-energy, totally unique pink with tropical, aromatic notes coming from the Moscatel, bursts of red fruit from the Tempranillo and concentrated, raisin-like fruits coming from the Pedro Ximénez. A little bit of everything going on here with the finest, lightest little spritz to help it slip down - delicious. Coche Discoteca ‘Car Disco’, a wine born after a night of music, fun, wine and a police fine for having little party out of their car in a parking lot. The wine was cre

Broad, textural Chenin from a single half-hectare plot. With a prickly, perlant energy on opening, the wine shows a wonderful balance of soft edges and angular tension. Vinous orchard fruits, sherbert-y lemon rind, with a zing of passion fruit and its invigorating acidity carrying later notes of ginger spice and stony minerals into the long finish. Taut, electric and lush, this is a wonderful way with the varietal. Bunches are de-stemmed and macerated on the skins for 9 days before being gently pressed off to steel to complete fermentation and rest until the spring. As with all of Olivier's wi

A rare planting makes for a unique expression of Syrah, it's potential to display dark, charry fruit here feels enhanced with the volcanic influence. A wide-open perfume floats above a slick, glossy body that is dense with juicy black olives and blackcurrant. Less granular in texture than the other wines using indigenous grapes, it shimmers long into the profoundly mineral finish. Younger at 20 years of age, the vines sit at 600 meters. The grapes were de-stemmed and macerated in steel for 8 days before 9 months ageing in old oak barrels. No additions were used at any stage in the process and

Go-to Rhone blend at a price that makes having real, natural wine on your table an everyday option. Syrah and Grenache, meaning spicy aromas and lots of juicy red fruit. Estézargues Is a cooperative of winemakers working around the Gard, the difference being that each member is working organically, thus creating an affordable wine that is made with no industrial methods.

An intensely mineral driven Georgian wine, made in the most traditional way possible. Expect lashings of all things salty, savory, and herbal. Balanced out by a good amount of spice and stone fruits. Fermented and aged in traditional terracotta qvevri, this wine reflects the deep Georgian history of winemaking, this is how it would have tasted all those years ago. Textured, mineral driven and well balanced. Made with 100% Chinuri (a variety indigenous to Georgia), the grapes are lightly crushed before being poured into 2000l terracotta qvevri which buried are in the floor of the cellar- skins,

A light and lively red which balances purity of fruit with an earthy, spicy, black pepper undertone. Though light in body, this wine delivers intense black fruit flavours with some lovely little tart red fruits sitting in the background. A real, honest and unfussy natural wine with a wild edge. Ideal when lightly chilled, you’ll find a welcoming little spritz on opening – wine for any day of the week. Mauricio Gonzalez Carraro is part of the Asociación de Productores de Vino Campesino de Chile, who are committed to low intervention wine making and revitalising the local heritage of the pipeño,

'Sfuso' is the type of wine that you'll find at the trattoria on your trips to Italy - simple wine for the table that is poured into carafes from a tank rather than being bottled. Yes, this wine does come in a bottle, but it gives you an idea of the style of the wine. Simple 'vino da tavola' at its finest. Something that despite its ubiquity on Italian soils is something that you don't find so easily once you're home again. grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Cabernet Franc, Gamay
notes: Another year means another exciting new cuvée from Jérôme. Once again, this wine is different from its predecessors and is made up of a wild blend of Grolleau, Gamay, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chenin Blanc and Sauvignon Blanc – a category defying red/white blend giving us the best of both worlds. Biclir is light and fragrant, showing touch more tannin and green fruit than previous cuvées, though still lithe and bloody with some pretty floral aromatics floating from the glass. As always with Jérôme’s wines, this is positively bursting with character and energy. Unconventional, unique,

Mauro is the only person who makes a white Chinato, based on Moscato d’Asti. Like all Chinato, the dominant ingredient here is bark from quinine trees, though there is plenty of lemon, vanilla, cloves and cinnamon in the mix. Mauro suggests a glass of this with some torrone, or nougat, ideally from his friends the Barberos just a short walk from his laboratory.

Light as a feather pét-nat of Grolleau Noir, bursting with all things fresh pink fruit. Think cranberries, tart strawberries and under-ripe cherries, all bound together with fresh coil of acidity and thirst-quenching bubbles. One that offers freshness, poise and elegance in abundance, the perfect aperitif. Working in the hamlet of Beaulieu-Sur-Layon, in the vibrant wine region of Anjou, Cedric crafts vibrant and compelling wines which truly speak to the health of the vines and the hard work undertaken in the vineyard. For the 2023 iteration of Somnambulles Rose, the grapes were direct-pressed,

Made using 100% Grenache Noir from 80 year old vines - the estate’s oldest vines which yield wonderfully concentrated fruit. The grapes are de-stemmed and undergo a 6-day fermentation with indigenous yeasts in stainless steel vats. The wine is muted (fortified) halfway through fermentation before being left to rest for 10 months in stainless steel, retaining as much fruit character as possible. On the nose this sweet red wine bursts with clear cut cherry, raspberry blackberries with just a hint of menthol and spice adding a layer of complexity. Luscious but light on its feet with a digeste qua

Delicate with pin-prick bubbles, ripe red fruit, fresh acidity and clocking in at very inviting 10% ABV - a no-brainer fizz for the season! Previous vintages of this fizz were much more pink, the current 2023 looking almost ‘blanc-de-noir’ in style, but with all the warming, ripe fruit of previous vintages. We always find that Albert’s wines offer incredible value for money, offering complexity, ripe fruit and freshness in equal measures. His Ancestral Trepat is, of course, no exception. It's a grape we don’t see too often here - native to Catalonia and primarily grown in the Conca del Barbera

A welcome return for this forest fruit Gamay that brims with tart black berries and sanguine minerals. It reminded us, in a somewhat protracted way, of something like a Lambrusco minus the bubbles - it has that crush of dark fruit, bright acidity and iron-like streak, softened with some creamy, lactic notes then deliciously smooth on the way down. Savoury charcoal bitters tail in the finish - a great vintage that sheds the carbo style of last year. Sauvignon Blanc from two small parcels of old vines averaging out at around 65 years in age from the old Les Bois Lucas domaine that in a former life Noëlla used to manage for its previous owner, Junko Ara. As you'd expect from vines of this age the fruit has exceptional complexity and concentration resulting in a wine of impressive texture and multi-layered depth. Reflecting the warm vintage, the 2022 has more power and attack than those that preceded it. The wine is a pale gold in the glass with all manner of rich aromas to take in. Brioche and frangipane alongside white flowers, candied lim

The latest from Benoit Killian, an experimental musician and winemaker in the outer reaches of Burgundy, the Saône valley. Meligoté comes from a single parcel of 2/3 Aligote & 1/3 Melon de Bourgogne, of which the majority are ungrafted. The grapes are pressed directly and aged in barrel. The Aligoté brings tension and focus, the Melon de Bourgogne bringing roundness and aromatics. Showing plenty of flesh, texture and rounded fruit at the moment, the wine feels fun in its youthful years, but only gain complexity with time. We would recommend laying this one down for a least 6 months.

A delightful introductory Riesling from Staffelter Hof which takes a more classical approach to the grape than some of Jan’s more experimental cuvées. Pure, mineral, zesty Mosel Riesling with soaring acidity sitting nicely with green apple, lime zest, salinity and that unmistakable waft of kerosene lifting from the glass. A clean, easy-drinking, versatile Riesling - great bang for buck! Produced using grapes from slate soils, fermented and aged on the lees in stainless steel tanks, with a touch of sulpher added at bottling. This is one from Jan's 'classic' range, it is more familiar as Mosel R

Those who have had the experience know that, whilst humbly priced, Mazel wines age with aplomb. We're happy to offer a small quantity of the above Syrah cuvee with well over a decade under its belt. Here we start to see the youthful fruit fall away into something more chiseled and defined. As with more recent vintages Larmande is 100% Syrah, fermented in carbonic maceration as whole bunches. The main point of intrigue here is that 2011 marks the final vintage that the wine would be transferred from steel tanks with a portion left to rest in old oak for a couple of years. Impeccably on-point Grüner with the added intrigue of its style leaning from the steely and linear to the more openly fragrant. The briefest of skin macerations dials up all of those hallmark aromas of the grape - white peppercorn, lime, green herbs - with aplomb. Of course there is that trademark mouth-watering acidity to cut it all through and time resting in a mixture of wooden, concrete and clay vessels ruffles up some welcome texture. A brilliant take on this varietal.

A bright, aromatic blend of Grolleau and Chenin Blanc with just a touch of Cabernet Franc in the mix. Coming from Mariette & Albéric’s modest 2.5 hectares of vines dotted around the villages of Rablay-sur-Layon, Beaulieu-sur-Layon and Faye D'Anjou. The vines here are aged up to 75 years old and are planted on varying mixes of clay, schist and gravelly soils on sites surrounding the nearby Layon river. The 2022 vintage of L’Abiizze sees the addition of Chenin Blanc in the blend, adding tension and energy to the wine. The vintage is a touch lighter than previous, with bright aromatic fruit, vivi

A terroir driven Riesling which balances opulence and minerality with ease. Made from vines that Jean-Pierre planted with his father 30 years ago, the Leu dit Stein is grown on grey marl and limestone. A blend of two different vintages. Two-thirds 2020 juice aged in old barrel for 3 years, and one-third of 2023 aged in barrel for 8 months. The resulting wine offers deep complexity which evolves dynamically once opened. Pouring with a beautiful oxidative shading, this Riesling is rounded and offers a perfect balance of salinity, citrus and concentrated golden fruit all wrapped up with a chisell

The colour of a brick-tinged Nebbiolo in the glass, this singular red/white blend of Catarratto and Pignatello really captures the essence of this far-flung volcanic island. Packed full of dusty black fruit, floral cherry blossom, exotic spices and the twang of salinity that the Sirocco wind brings in on the breeze, it's a fine balance between detailed layers of structure and seductive drinkability.
