100% Riesling from the Grand Cru site of Kastelberg, planted over a mix of Schist and sandstone. The grapes are pressed very slowly into wooden barrels to ferment, giving the wine a distinct texture and a full, rounded feel on the palate. The 2022 shows great balance, picked early to retain freshness. Chiseled, mineral and persistently salty with great length and complexity. Of course, this being Durrmann, there is a wire of taught acidity cutting through it all.

The Gran Cerdo natural wines have become ubiquitous staples over the years. Providing such great value and easy drinking it's not hard to see why. We've now added the rosado to the range! It's mainly Tempranillo with a little Garnacha and a splash of some of the grapes that end up in the Blanco. Refreshing red strawberry fruits, with a candied quality, make this one a no-brainer for thirsty party drinkers.

Unrivaled value to be found here in this bottle-fermented fizz out of Catalonia's Cava country. It uses a familiar grape, Xarel-lo, but takes it well away from the style of Spain's most famous sparkling wine by adding plenty of aromatic Muscat and doing it all a la pet-nat. This is an altogether more laid-back style; bubbles that fizz but don't impede your consumption in the slightest, light body, peachy texture and that lovely orange blossom perfume. Hazy, glowing, good-time material.

Simple, straight-up Xarel-lo delivering huge bang-for-buck. Clean, fresh and mineral with little of that peppery aroma and a salty twang in the finish, this is a wine you'll want to stock up on and come back to again and again.

Notte is everything we love about Italian skin-contact wines; the Malvasia & Moscato providing an almost never-ending list of complex aromatics: elderflower, jasmine, lime pith, ginger, tinned peaches, clementine zest and more. The Spergola adding an integrated tannic structure that only improves and becomes further embedded with time. So much going on with this fantastic wine and it really stands up to the heavy Emilia cuisine. Put it on the table with formaggio-laden pasta dishes, salumi and porcetta. Sublime stuff!

Proper Lambrusco-style sparkling red that we describe as being like a summer pudding in liquid form. Lots of little inky black berries, a tart lick of acid and something a bit creamy and lactic, with a nicely upfront, grippy tannic structure and frothy bubble. There’s a real savoury, slightly vegetal character here that makes it a must with salumi and the rich, meat-heavy cuisine of Emilia-Romagna. It's in this context that sparkling red wine truly makes sense! For us, this is one of the best out there.

An entry-level selection that immediately claims the plaudit of best-priced orange wine in the house. This is Falanghina with a mixture of the grapes direct-pressed (like a regular white) and some left to macerate on the skins (a la orange) leaving a golden glow and just a modest mouthful of grippy tannins. Ripe, quince-y stone fruits and smoky/nutty flavours jostle together in loose harmony. Very tasty stuff and such bang for buck.

This is his direct-press Aligoté, given a slow 24-48 hour press in his antique basket press, which gives texture and body to the wine. It has electric acidity and incredibly pure fruit. Drinking well already but this one will only benefit from some cellar time if you have the patience to lay it down.

The Crème de Tête 2012 was made from grapes harvested the third week of December "when the moon was in the constellation of Leo, a fire constellation that brings power and plenitude". Alain sprays some mineral (silica based) biodynamic preparations to help the shrivelled grapes hold onto the vines so late into the season – reaching extreme concentration (the unicorn Crème de Tête 2005 was harvested during the last days of December!). Aged for eight years in both oak and acacia barrels, this is fuller and richer than the 2011 and 2013, viscous on the palate and slightly hidden at opening, it de

A fantastic new Cabernet Franc cuvée made using grapes from Mikael Bouges and his more limestone-heavy terroir in Faverolles. The fruit is destemmed and sees a long, three-month maceration before being aged in barrel for 18 months. Aromatically this is a textbook example of the grape; plush, brightly-toned notes of red berries, charred capsicum and ground coffee are vibrant and upfront. On the palate the wine is glossy, with deep, sumptuous fruit and gentle bitters leading into detailed granular tannins and a stony, mineral backbone. A superb new addition to Noëlla's repertoire that stands apa

Peppercorn spice and deep fruits leap from the glass, the texture of the wine is beautifully soft and silky, with integrated, lightly gripping tannic structure. There is a rusty, iron-like mineral quality beneath it all, that really shows itself in the long, stony finish. A truly elegant wine that demonstrates the complexity of its old-vine origin. Reflecting the heat of a scorching vintage, with little rain, the structure is bolder and more concentrated than previous vintages. 100% Gamay from the Guerin’s prized plot of 50 year-old, massal selection vines, planted over sandy, decomposed grani

Another négociant wine, this time using Bergeron, a highly obscure strain of Roussanne that is found in the alpine region of Savoie. Macerated on the skins and aged in barrel, it is is ripe and exotic on the nose, with dry tea-like tannins. Incredibly delicate, alluring and one of Bouju's harder to track down cuvées. Plus a little bit of trivia: the label was designed by non other than elusive winemaker Aurélien Lefort.

Chinato is perhaps Piemonte’s most famous digestif. Traditionally made with aged Barolo, it takes its name from the bark of quinine (or “China”) tree, which is the chief botanical here. Vergano prefers to use a younger wine from Barbaresco, the tannins not as firm, the perfume a little more lifted. The china bark lends the wine tea-like tannins, while herbs and spices like cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, coriander, bay, ginseng and rhubarb provide warmth and real interest. There is no better way to end a meal.

Place: Colli Eugane, Italy Grape: Glera Vibe: Frothy Another iconic label from Alberto. Glera but with actual flavour and personality. Not so much this becomes an intellectual exercise as it's mainly about good time drinking. It's fizzy and fun, with lots of lemon and pear fruit leading the charge before a nice chalky finish. Its bubbles are fine and refreshing and it should be enjoyed cold, with plenty of company and not a care in the world. Sharp stuff.

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Toasty A collab between Alanna and 4 winemakin' pals (Alicia Serres, Sierra Echegaray, Kara Fowler, and Jenna Florio) across Europe. They have started up a shared label project! Cool. This is Flonheim Chardonnay from Alanna. Older vines on limestone, aged in old large-format oak. Lovely reductive nose that opens into a ripe-fruited, floral and saline number. It's direct and delicious. Quite serious, but still so drinkable. So into German Chardo. ABV: 13%

wine: Vin de LaGamba, Frauen Power Blanc 2024
notes: Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Fresh as Frauen Power Blanc! Direct-press Riesling given a LaGamba makeover. This is, as per the red, incredibly fun to drink. All whilst having a quiet confidence about it. It's long and persistent, grounded by a salinity and mineral edge. It's broad-fruited upfront thanks to time in barrel before the fizz carries you into that persistent and tingling finish. Stock the fridges. ABV: 11%

Place: Etna, Sicily, Italy Grape: Nerello Mascalese + Carricante + Catarratto Vibe: Mineral Nerello with small amounts of white as per the ways of old, from a tiny plot planted in 1940 on the volcanic sands of Monte Ilice, on the southeastern slope. Short maceration before ageing in glass demijohn. This always leaves me speechless, such a powerful wine yet still so effortless when in the glass. Savoury, with dried herbs, but lifted by an almost alpine freshness. The tannins are firm and the acidity off the charts, all good signs that this will age wonderfully over the coming years. Place: Etna, Sicily, Italy Grape: Nerello Mascalese + Alicante Vibe: Mineral Older vines on the southwest slopes of Etna. Featherweight and floral, this is a delightfully crunchy wine, with the most gorgeous colour. Just so fluid, red wine flavour but white wine structure. It’s destined for a chill and to be deleted in record time. Not short on complexity with a little varietal white pepper cracked throughout. If this is négoce, I can’t wait to see their domaine gear in a few years. ABV: 12%

This allows for gradual, slower ripening that has become a blessing in the warming world we live in. Handles the warm vintage so well, elegant and restrained, with time things have gone all honeyed and smoky. ABV: 13%

At once both classic yet wild, plenty of black fruit cut up with lavender and fresh herbs. Immediately captivating, with heady aromas of bruised and wild fruit. The palate is long, and as with all his wines, incredibly salty due to an élevage that saw him avoid topping up the barrels. The palate is so fluid and juicy, there's lots of wild fruit, dried herb and spice. The vines are at 450m altitude, so this is fresh AF, with crazy acid and salty minerality and a finish that you'll dream about for years to come. The fairest way to share the A&B love. From their plot Vigne au Daim in Gizia, taken over from a local elder in 2011. They’ve kept traditions alive by continuing to co-plant many different varieties here. This is roughly 35% Petit Béclan, 25% Gamay, 20% Poulsard, 10% Trousseau and 10% Pinot Noir. Jura wine of old. Petit Béclan is practically extinct, and here it brings a brooding rusticity with its small, tight bunches and thick skins. This, as per all their reds, is fully destemmed, then co-fermented and aged in 300L barrels for 12 months. Their grippiest and most structured red, with ripe blackberry fruit, but still with their mi

Alive and wildly alluring. The fairest way to share the A&B love. This bottling is intensely savoury, with a touch of integrated VA, some lovely florals and a smidge of almond. Don't mind if I do. * Note there are two labels of this wine, one with the man and one with the woman. wine: Allante & Boulanger, Trousseau Patarate 2023 - Mystery Pack

Place: Wagram, Austria Grape: Cabernet Franc Vibe: Unbelievable I didn’t think Cab Franc from Austria would be in pole position for one of my wines of the year, but the world is full of surprises. From the first sniff, I knew I was in trouble. Big trouble. Instantly reminding me of the wines of Clos Rouegard. I’ve tasted in the legendary cellar, sorry not sorry, and this would not have looked out of place in the slightest. Picked from just four rows of recultivated, old Cabernet Franc vines in the Mordthal site in Rupperstal, on poorer loess but with very sunny exposure. Only 24 bottles in the

Place: Wagram, Austria Grape: Sankt Laurent Vibe: Bright + Fun Lukas’s little range of extremely fun, extremely drinkable wines. This big blend is much more than the sum of its parts. Something so compelling about these cooler climate reds. They have really nice aromatics, plenty of fresh fruit on show here running the gamut from red apple skin through to plum. A little spice too. Actually a pretty serious wine despite the lightweight frame. Uncomplicated doesn’t mean boring, this is plenty complex, it just so happens to be dangerously drinkable too. Chuck this in the fridge and go on a journe

Place: Wagram, Austria Grape: Grüner Veltliner, Roter Veltliner, Riesling, Weißburgunder and Müller-Thurgau Vibe: Natural, textural Vibe: Bright + Fun Lukas’s little range of extremely fun, extremely drinkable wines. This big blend is much more than the sum of its parts. The fruit is plenty juicy, there’s a nice chalky texture and a very pleasing mineral finish. Uncomplicated doesn’t mean boring, this is plenty complex, it just so happens to be dangerously drinkable too. Seriously, watch the bottle change from first sip to last... Yeah, told you. Instantly into my go-to rotation.

grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot
notes: Place: South Australia Grape: Cabernet Sauvignon (65%), Merlot (14%), Petit Verdot (12%) + Cabernet Franc (9%) Vibe: Oppulent Bordeaux blend but out of Beechworth. Yea, the classics are back, just with a lil' modern twist. An assault of purple and red fruit, violets and herb. Tannins are velvet-like, and drinkability has not been an afterthought. It’s midweight and majestic in the glass. Find me some one dones't like this. ABV: 13%

Place: South Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Oppulent The broader of the pair of Beechworth Chardy’s. Things get whole bunch pressed and ferment straight into oak, without temperature control. As soon as the ferment wraps up, the wine is sulphured to stop malo and retain all that raspy, fresh acidity, before going back to barrel to soften once more. We’ve got texture and opulence, but there’s real complexity woven throughout here. Nutmeg spice and a mealy texture you only find in the grape at its most seductive. ABV: 13%

Place: South Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Flinty + Fine The coolest single site Chardo, sitting at 560 to 620 metres. Fruit ripens nice and slow here, all whilst retaining plenty of acid. Tightly coiled and tense, but give this a moment to flesh out and you’ll get everything you want in your Chardonnay. Sea spray, nutty, and plenty of pristine green fruit. All I'm saying is, you don't get value like this in France... ABV: 13%

Place: Pyrenees , Basque Country Grape: Gros + Petit Manseng, Tannat (Direct Press) + Chenin Vibe: Beguiling Objectively one of the weirder and more wacky wines we sell, also one of the most delicious. Barrel aged and bottled with a small 18g of residual. Slightly spritzy, slighty sweet, super acidic + super tasty. I can't say I've had anything like this before and doubt I ever will. Kaledoscopic with a myriad of orchard fruit on show, it's at once generous and ripe but cutting and fresh. Pretty wild and adventourous but just imagine the food pairings... It's pretty bonkers, but seriously wort

Place: Loire, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Natural, textural Ooof, 2023 is shaping up to be some year in the Loire if you like things freshhh and lean. The cool vintage brining plenty of acid and nervy drive. Typical Sauvignon aromatics up front: all pretty elderflower and lime, but given time this takes on a pithy, savoury character from the maceration. Very nice. ABV: 12.5%

grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Cabernet Franc, Gamay
notes: Place: Loire, France Grape: 40% Sauvignon Blanc, 20% Chenin Blanc, 20% Grolleau, 20% Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Gamay Vibe: Juicy Exceptional drinking achieved through a hectic blend. Half direct press, half macerated in whole bunches. Bursting with fruity aromatics, bloody mineral depth, and just the faintest grip. It’s light on its feet yet full of character and complexity. Jérome’s wines have an infectious energy. ABV: 12%

Place: Trás-os-Montes, Portugal Grape: Tinta Gorda + Local Varieties Vibe: Light and bright From the same parcel as her maceration, just this time a local grape, Tinta Gorda, with a dash of the other varieties. Again, simple winemaking where things are gently foot-trodden to extract a bit of colour and phenolics. Wonderfully red fruited, all cranberries and redcurrant, with this lovely herbal quality woven throughout. A soft, almost waxy texture too, as here she experimented with ageing in old barrel. Technically a rosé, but to me this drinks like a light red of the highest order.

wine: Menina d'Uva, Ciste Branco de Maceração 2024
notes: Place: Trás-os-Montes, Portugal Grape: Malvasia, Bastardo Branco, Formosa, Verdelho Vibe: Adv Skinsy Another intriguing blend, this time from a single old parcel west of the village at 550m of altitude on clay soils. Aline opted to macerate things for 11 days, before a year of ageing. This is more intense, ginger spiced and full of wild herbs. The texture is cut through by some lovely crunchy acid. Again, there's quite a lot going on here but there is such an ethereal, fragrant quality that makes this so irresistible. Grill some fish. Drink this. Be happy. ABV: 13%

Place: Trás-os-Montes, Portugal Grape: Malvasia, Bastardo Branco, Formosa, Poilta Vibe: Moreish Portugal is the place to be RN. I absolutely fell for this producer from the first sip. Everything is gently foot-trodden before fermenting in fibreglass, matured for over a year before being bottled unfined and unfiltered. Really golden, hinting at something tropical and floral on the nose before being grounded by a really saline and mineral back palate. This is so versatile and utterly delicious. Feel good wine. ABV: 12%

Place: Colli Eugane, Italy Grape: Tai Rosso Vibe: Earthen Old school Italian. Tocai Rosso is the Venetian slang for Grenache. This is grown on volcanic soils and made totally without input from a pioneer of the natural wine movement in Italy. Zero zero liquid history. This has gone all earthen and savoury, that plush fruit peeling away to reveal so much tertiary charm and allowing its volcanic terroir to show clearly. Soy-like umami and savouriness. I was recently in the region, where horse is a local delicacy, and this would be a nice match, but back here in the UK I think I'll stick to regul

Place: Ardeche, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Vibrant Challenging times call for creativity, and in this rough vintage Pierre decided to blend his older vine parcels with a tiny splash of younger vine fruit. In the cellar he opted for a one week infusion of 10% whole bunches in pressed juice. The result is a pristine and pale red that falls somewhere between rosé and light red. It's full of delicate and detailed red berries and herbs. It's hard not to instantly reach for another glass. Behind the modest labels is some of the most exciting wine coming out of France at the moment.

Place: Ardeche, France Grape: Blend Vibe: Charming A terraced plot consisting mostly of Pinot Noir and Gamay, with a few rows each of Pineau d'Aunis, Ploussard, and Muscat. Picked and vinified together with a week of whole bunch maceration before destemming for another week of maceration, then a 9 month élevage. Fresh fruit kissed by a gentle earthen note, acidity is perky and bright and things are framed by soft tannin. It's so charming in the glass, an utter joy from first sip to last.

wine: Pierre Bourlier, La Viticulture est un Sport de Combat 2024
notes: Place: Ardeche, France Grape: Merlot Vibe: Vibrant Not always a fan of Merlot, but when handled gently and in the right hands it can really swoon me. Biodynamically grown and utterly captivating. Lifted on the nose, and incredibly fresh on the palate despite the darker cherry leaning fruit. Bit of spice, bit of grip but all in the most pleasing sense. A delightfully good bottle, that takes you vicariously to the Bistro's of France. ABV: 14.2%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Aligoté Vibe: Natural, textural Ahhh. I love Bouzeron. Aligoté at the pinnacle. Spicier and deeper than his Bourgogne, this has the material to go quite a bit further in the cellar. Brand new wine for us too, and I think it's the only proper Bouzeron on the shelves atm. Stupidly good drinkin' as per the Skyaasen way. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Natural , textural Soupois is a lieu-dit getting some serious love in the Jurassien south at the moment. Situated between Rotalier and Gizia, sitting at roughly 250–450 metres altitude, with south and west-facing slopes that consist solely of Triassic and Jurassic marl soils on Bajocian limestone. This is a thumping expression, vinified 'Ouille' style in old barrel for 30+ months. The fruit has shed its skin, revealing a taut wine full of candied peel, spice and minerals. It's a real surprise to me why these wines don't command the same feverish hype a

Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Oxy + Salty The crown jewel of the Buronfosse range. I tasted some yellow wine in their cellars, and that mouthful still haunts me to this very day. Really one of the better examples of the style you can find. L'Attente, as in "the wait". Trust me, the wait has been very much worth it. Vivid and almost incomprehensibly complex, all tied together by a piercing salinity. Maldon level salty. ABV: 14.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Tart and Tingling I love Cider, I love the Jura, I love Buronfosse. This was a no brainer. Comprised from their 300 tree orchard, with 15 different varieties they've preserved a wonderful essence of the fruit lifted by a gentle little spritz. Tart and crunchy this is a wildy delicous bottle and a perfect way to either start a meal, or even better finish it off alongside the cheeseboard, when the Vin Jaune is just a bit too much. ABV: 4.5%

Place: Veneto, Italy Grape: Vespaiola Vibe: Serious An older vine selection of Vespaiola from iron-rich basalt soils. Concentration is dialled up, yet without sacrificing drinkability. This grape has stolen my heart. Its aromatics and tropical tinged fruit are addictive, and this is the most serious example money can buy. It doesn't get better. Don't let the playful label fool you, this is a serious wine. Layered and laser like in its precision, the finish is wickedly mineral and salty with classic Italian bitters dotted throughout. Please please taste this; I promise it won't disappoint.

Place: Veneto, Italy Grape: Malvasia, Vespaiola, Garganega, Nebbiolo Vibe: Legendary Affectionately named after Marco's dad, Sevelino. After a long lunch with the big man himself at the family home, I can safely say this wine is equally as vibrant as Seve himself. The fruit here comes from the vineyard planted in their backyard to ensure there would always be wine on hand. Legend. Thankfully, Marco is now sharing the family's personal supply. A field blend in the truest sense. Picked together, destemmed, before a gentle maceration lasting over 40 days. Bottled the following spring with the add

Place: Colli Eugane, Italy Grape: Corbinello Vibe: Crazy but classy A more experimental sparkling from Alberto, combining techniques of both ancestral and traditional methods. The 2023 Corbinello was directly pressed into tonneaux, where it fermented and matured for a year. In 2024, more Corbinello fermenting in fibreglass was blended with the aged wine from the previous year before being bottled, allowing a natural second fermentation to kick off. It rested here for over a year, without any additions of sugar, yeast or sulphur before its disgorgement. It's labour-intensive and kinda mad scien

Place: Colli Eugane, Italy Grape: Pinot Noir + Corbinello Vibe: Vibrant Mainly Pinot with a splash of the late ripening Corbinello, from young vines on clay heavy soil. Everything is directly pressed for a super pale Rosato. This is tingling in the mouth, all blood orange and grapefruit like. It' really unqiue, but plenty vibrant, lifted by some gorgeously integrated VA before the finish is grounded in salt and smoke. This is a wild ride, not for the faint of heart but utterly mind blowing for those who prize vitality in the glass.

Place: Colli Eugane, Italy Grape: Caberent Sauvignon Vibe: Crunchy Cab Sav from Veneto is rarely inspired drinking, yet let me please introduce you to this. The Faedesfa effect on full show, showing the grape at its savoury and wild best. The fruit is typically dark but still crunchy and fresh, lifted by sharp aromatics. Things go all earthen and cocoa like on the palate and it's a wine I found myself coming back to time and time again. It's both immediate in its deliciousness, but has lots of complexity woven throughout. Drinking well now but I'm personally squirreling one away for a rainy da

wine: Georges Comte, Le Moutherot Les Pelerins
notes: Place: Doubs, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Life changing About as old school as they come. IYKYK. These wines are always unforgettable. Georges is based in Émagny, an area between Burgundy and Jura, and his old vines grow on firm clay and limestone soils. He ages in old barrels for two years, always bottled without filtration, fining, or any added sulphur. He only releases the wines when deemed they are at their best. 2018 was an incredibly warm year, yet it's remarkable how Georges' old vines have managed to still produce a wine of such finesse. Going all savoury and golden. 2013 might be h

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Unreal Chardonnay from forty year old vines in Orbagna on pure limestone. Again, pressed to barrels for three years of élevage. This is immediate in its deliciousness, there is power but still nicely poised. Stone fruited and ripe, before things turn mineral and chalky. Insanely good. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Pulsating Chardo on blue marl, from a cool shaded site in Grusse. 50 year old fruit is pressed straight to barrel where the wine rested for three years undisturbed. Heady and layered, this is a Jurassien white at the pinnacle. It's spiced and meditative, seemingly revealing new layers with each sip. Ex Labet Alumni coming in clutch. ABV: 13%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Fiano Vibe: Exotic Orchard like aromatics open up into a highly refreshing wine full of citrus and sea spray. Mostly seeing steel, although we do have a little leesy, textural component woven throughout through the addition of a single three year old barrel. Another cracking example of how these Southern Italian varieties are so suited to the coastal McLaren Vale. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Fratelli Badini, Il Bianco Trebbiano Toscana 2025
notes: Place: Tuscany, Italy Grape: Trebbiano Vibe: Natural Trebbiano Toscano given some TLC with a lovely one week maceration to coax out lovely orchard fruit, a bit of colour and plenty of refreshment. It's such a delicious drinking wine, marmalade-like yet dry and racy. We had this sitting in their old cellar, surrounded by more cheese and salumi than you could imagine. It cut through with ease. The perfect apéro orange does exist. It's right here. ABV: 13%

wine: Timothee Stroebel, Coteaux Champenois 'Le Vin Tranquille Blanc' 2022
notes: Place: Champagne, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Rares Old vines dating back to the 1960s, from the Les Cumines lieu-dit. Crystalline and cutting, candied citrus meets a touch of iodine. A triumphant still wine, where the warmth of the vintage has softened the shrieking acidity into something layered and meditative. Undoubtedly one of the best expressions of the grape I've ever tasted. Vin d'Émotion! Cute label too. ABV: 12%

wine: Timothee Stroebel, Brut Nature 'Heraclie' Pinot Noir 2019
notes: Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Rares Pinot Noir from the following vintage, again from old vines near Villers-Allerand. Even more red fruited, screams Blanc de Noirs of the highest order. Strawberry shortcake, lots of herbs. Powerful and bracing. 3 bottles only. ABV:12.5%

Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Meunier Vibe: Rares All Meunier, from two parcels of old vines near Villers-Allerand. Beautifully handled, leaning slightly oxidative with a blush of rose from ripe fruit. Morello cherry, red apple skin, plenty of umami. Heraclie never misses. Rare. ABV: 12.5%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Nero D'Avola Vibe: Easy to Like Biodynamically picked Nero from McLaren Vale that is handpicked and given a bit of whole bunch TLC. So smooth and juicy, with a lovely lick of signature spice atop all that dark brambly fruit. Breezy. ABV: 12.9%

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: 60% Grillo + Zibbibo + Inzolia + Catarratto: Vibe: Salty Two of my favourite wine reigons meet in this curious and contemplative bottle. Sicilian fruit given some Jurassien TLC. A gentle kiss of oxidative character meets us first, with just the right amount of smoked nuts and salt before we open into a wine that really feels rooted in the Island. It's only 11% and has real zip and drive too. A must taste!

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: 60% Nero D'Avola + 20% Trebbiano + 20% Inzolia Vibe: Refreshing Probably shouldn't be buying Rosato as summer draws to a close, but after tasting this I couldn't resist. This is such a great example of why pink wine doesn't need to be watery and thin. There's complexity without losing its quite frankly astonishingly high levels of refreshment. Sherbety, with a blood orange-like acidity before all the herbal stuff, then watermelon both flesh and rind. The finish is smoky and salty too. A pitch perfect wine, and one that you can happily drink all year round. 11.5%

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: 80% Nero D'Avola + 15% Syrah + Inzolia Vibe: Rustic Yea, how good's a nice comforting Sicilian Red. A well put together blend, with Nero's natural acidity brightening up the tannic Inzolia and peppery Syrah. There's some rustic tannin and deep fruit, but it remains bright and drinkable. It's a wine made for a takeaway pizza or a home cooked ragu. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot Noir + Pinot Gris Vibe: Natural An equal split of the Two Pinots! An infusion using Yann's custom-designed immersion grids in stainless steel fermenting bins that can be tipped directly into the press. Geeky bits aside, this is just so fun. A chilled red of unrivalled digestibility. Wild strawberry and cherries galore again with a tingly spritz that makes this pretty much addictive. Drink chilled and you'll be chilled. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Riesling Vibe: Natural Yann makes Alsatian Grand Cru that actually tastes like one, wish I could say the same for all the 50+ GCs of the region. From the slopes of Wiebelsberg, close to the Crax hill and the edge of Kastelberg. The soil here is sandstone and schist. On release, this was so nervy and tense, but after 5 years things are slowly softening. The acidity is still racy and refreshing, lots of lime bitters and again an almost endless finish. A food wine, that would perfectly cut through the rich, local fare. A steal considering both the age and the quality.

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Riesling Vibe: Natural Yann makes Alsatian Grand Cru that actually tastes like one, wish I could say the same for all the 50+ GCs of the region... The length of this is quite frankly frightening. This is from a steep south facing parcel where the vines are planted on terraced hills. Soil is 'recooked' schist which is essentially extra hard and dense, making those roots dig deep. So spiced and smoky and salty. Drinking great atm but gonna live a long, long time. ABV:12.5%

grapes: Pinot Noir, Syrah, Riesling, Cabernet Franc
notes: Place: Transylvania, Romania Grape: Syrah, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Noir Vibe: Juicy One whole litre of natural red wine for just over £20? Maybe miracles do exist after all. This is a really juicy blend from Transylvania! Worthing branching out from your usual drinking habbits and giving this a go . Flavour wise, think crunchy cherries and perky plums. It's easygoing and all the better for it. Pop and pour kind of wine for when 750ml is just not enough.

Place: Transylvania, Romania Grape: 25% Riesling, 25% Chardonnay, 25% Furmint + 25% indigenous varieties Vibe: Easy One whole litre of natural white wine for just over £20? Maybe miracles do exist after all. There is a lot to like here and not just the price and 1L format. Citric and almost a little tropical with texture built in through short skin contact. Still firmly a hazy hued white, this is easy going and effortless. Well made and so well priced. Get out your comfort zone and give it a go, you won't be disappointed.

Place: Loire, France Grape: Côt AKA Malbec Vibe: Savoury Yeah, Malbec doesn't tend to be something I usually reach for. However when it's in the hands of a legendary producer, and especially with a little bottle age, I too can be partial to a splash. This is a really great example, with its brambly nature and sweet spice profile. There's some signature Paradis earthen stuff and a rustic tannin structure that is just starting to soften. A trip to the butchers for a good steak, and that is your evening sorted.

Place: Loire, France Grape: Cabernet Franc Vibe: Savoury Naysayers often remark about how natural wines are mere exercises in short extraction for simple 'glou glou' styles. I say, drink a bottle of this! Deep and brooding, this is Cab Franc in its most unadulterated form. Long maceration before a long élevage before a long snooze in the bottle. Time is key and we have now been greatly rewarded. This is a big wine, spiced plummy fruit giving way to seriously tasty notes of undergrowth and forest floor. There is so much going on, words don't do it justice. ABV: 12%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Gamay, Côt, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Noir + Gascon Noir and more Vibe: Herbal Unreal juice! After a decade things have now gone all savoury and earthen whilst the acidity remains present and cutting. You can thank us again for dealing with the whole aging thing for you. Ready to go after plenty of rest. Such a curious wine, all fig leaves and plums before things take a turn into something mineral and iron rich. Layered and multidimensional, a wine for reflection. ABV: 12%

Place: Grapes from the Pyrénées but vinified up in Jura, France Grape: Muscat Vibe: Tropical + tart I really enjoy when Alice gets her hands on Muscat. She has a wonderful way of taming its usually flamboyant self. This iteration sees just a light maceration. We've still got all the good stuff. Tropics, floral and grapey, but as per the house style this is grounded in a saline minerality and freshness. So zesty and tart, it's a real joy to drink. A delightful wine that you'll never be bored of.

Place: Grapes from Minervois but vinified in the Auvergne, France Grape: Macabeo, Viognier + Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Pét-Nat + Friends A tough vintage meant Catherine had to buy in some grapes. Everything was directly pressed before the fermentation finished up in bottle. It had 9 months to rest before being disgorged. Now after a little snooze in the cellar this has found its feet. The sun kissed fruit of the south has now gone all golden whilst still retaining some nice acidity. Fine bubbles and a salty finish are an added bonus. Drink cold and fast! ABV: 12.5%

wine: Mas Guineu Vinyaters, Dos Mons Roig 2024
notes: Place: Penedes, Spain Grape: Monastrell + Parellada Vibe: Juicy Blouge Monastrell, often a bit of a brute, that here is softened by being co-fermented with the refreshing Parellada. Violet in both colour and flavour, supported by lots of mulberries and blackberries too. Nothing jammy though, this a blouge of inherent drinkability and digestibility. It will also pair perfectly with quite literally anything. Tapas time, I think... ABV: 11%

wine: Mas Guineu Vinyaters, Dos Mons Brisat 2024
notes: Place: Penedes, Spain Grape: Chardonnay + Muscat Vibe: Easy Skinsy, Natural My latest obsession after tasting a bottle of it earlier in the year on a little trip to España. Just like that it suddenly began being imported to the UK. Just my luck. Pithy but still so fresh and drinkable. A little golden and nutty too but just the right amount. Very good. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot Gris Vibe: Serious Probably didn't need another macerated Pinot Gris from Alsace on the shelves, but I had a bottle of this blind recently and it was easily WOTN. I also went to visit a few years back and tasted this before it had reached its current final form. It's best in class for both region and style, no two ways about it. Makes total sense once you understand the uncompromising, almost unheard of approach in the vineyards. They don't plough or mow, essentially they've adopted a radical form of Fukuoka inspired farming. Things are growing pretty much wi

Place: Barossa Valley, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Luscious Wow. When I heard these wines had finally relanded in London after a long hiatus, I made the long pilgrimage across the river just to get a taste, something I'd usually avoid at all costs as a born-and-bred North Londoner. This bottle was the pick of the bunch. Chenin in its orchard fruited best. Slightly reductive and very mineral, you'd think this came from one of Anjou's finest. You see Tom applies some old-world sensibilities to new world fruit. There's wax and lanolin, and whilst things feel golden and sun kissed, the acidity

Place: Barossa Valley, Australia Grape: Riesling Vibe: Crispy Tom has absolutely knocked it for six with this trio of whites. I love Riesling, but often it's so stripped back. Copious amounts of excess SO2 before being fined and filtered to within an inch of it's life. Tom's taken the opposite approach, unafraid to let the fruit do what it wants. We still have plenty of citric drive and pretty florals but instead of water weight this has layers and substance. It unfurls wonderfully given some time to breathe too. Zero adds again, showing that wines down under need not be subjected to vinous cr

Place: Barossa Valley, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Textured Another belter, Aussie chardo handled more like it's new wave Burgs. There's no lashing of new wood to hide behind, and no sulphur either. Just old vine, free run juice that sees 18 months in old oak. Remarkable to taste! All custard creams and lemon curd. If you're scared of the new world, please let this change your mind. It feels 'frencher' than lots of recent chardo from the ever warming Europe. Yes, there's texture but also plenty of drive. Things are picked perfectly to ensure something that is crisp but not short on flavo

Place: Barossa Valley, Australia Grape: Syrah Vibe: Light and bright Apparently if you say "Poolside" in an Aussie accent it sounds like Poulsard. Hence, Tom has taken Barossa Shiraz and tried to handle it as gently as possible to try and achieve something Jurassien. He's done a very good job. The flavour spectrum might be a little different but drinkability and texture have been achieved. Colour too. It's rosé or light red depending on your mood. Bright and rhubarb led, there are wisps of pepper and herbs galore. Would make for very good poolside drinking too. Drink cold!

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Classic The lesser spotted rouge from the famed domaine! Coming from a teeny tiny 0.6 hectare plot in Irancy, this doesn't pop up often. Buy on sight when it does. Still young but my god is it beautiful right now. Spiced and with plenty of floral red fruits. Juicy but framed by some lovely soft tannin. Most Irancy could only dream of tasting like this, reminds me a lot of Pataille's work in Marsannay. Unreal. ABV: 13%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Collector's Item The result of a shocking vintage that was under intense threat from botrytis, the XXI is a blend of the fruit normally destined for Pur Sang, Silex, Buisson and Blanc etc., and it's a stunner. Hovering between the pronounced florals of Buisson and the laser-like precision of Silex, this is a bottling with its own distinct personality. If you're a Dagueneau fan, and I know u are, you're gonna want one of these. ABV: 12%

Place: Serbia Grape: Welschriesling , Bakator, Piros Magyarka, Riesling Vibe: Adv Skinsy Something skinsy from Serbia! Didn't really know what to expect going into this, came out feeling energized. Really tasty. One of those macerations that ticks all the boxes. The fruit is marmalade-y but fresh, there's a bit of tea-like spice, some savoury herbs. There's just enough grip but things aren't astringent. Very well balanced and immensely drinkable. Come for the curiosity, stay for the complexity. ABV: 13.5% Please note the bottle is sealed with a natural layer of clay, sourced directly from the

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Crisp Wickedly mineral and crispy Chardo from the relatively unknown Vézelay. Still in Burgundy but quite a way off from the Côte de Beaune, this little outpost sits somewhere west of Dijon but below Chablis. There is something so crystalline and cooling about Chardo grown here. All minty fresh and herbal. This is electrifying, drives down the palate and leaves us on a salty high note. If you like Chablis, you'll want to take a look here.

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural, lighter About as northerly as Red Burgundy gets, which in the past might have been a problem. Not sure if you've seen the weather recently, but cool sites are now very much prized parcels. This is still ripe, but that freshness is doubled down on with some whole bunch lift. Really bright and breezy. Not lacking in flavour though: sour cherry and whiffs of five-spice. This producer is one to watch. ABV: 11.8%

Place: Chablis, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural I am a sucker for some serious, aged Chablis, and Vaillons is a little 1er I happen to be fond of too. Everything has integrated, all golden, nutty, savoury. Quite something. If you've never had an aged Chablis, this is a pretty good place to start. Pretty keen pricing for something that's only just passed the legal drinking age. Sold as seen*

wine: Good Intentions, 'Lake of Fire' Estate White 2023
grapes: Chardonnay, Riesling, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Gris
notes: Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Cabernet Franc, Riesling, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay Vibe: Texture + Tasty This is the first taste of Andrew's high density home vineyard, a blend of directly pressed Cabernet Franc (65%), Riesling (20%), Pinot Gris (5%), Chardonnay (10%). his special vineyard is right at the base on the south side of the volcanic crater that erupted approximately 4200 years ago. COOL. Only 300 bottles produced. Don't snooze. ABV: 13%

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Grüner Veltliner Vibe: Texture + Tasty Gutsy take on Grüner! Ripe fruit and richer than its European relatives. Still with some nice orchard freshness plus we've got lots of green herbs and plenty of that signature white pepper spice too. Steal! ABV: 13%

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Gewurztraminer Vibe: Floral Skinsy Gewürz dials up on aromatics. Don't be fooled by that deep amber colour, this is super pretty. Lychee, Turkish delight, and tropics all on show. So perfumed, you can smell it a mile off. ABV: 13%

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Fiano Vibe: Textured Fiano! What a grape. Does well on its home turf of the Italian South but that also means it's suited to the hot and sunkissed lands of Aus. It retains acidity despite the soaring temps. Here, texture is built in through a barrel ferment and we get an almost creamy and nutty palate before finishing all mineral. ABV: 13%

Place: Tuscany, Italy Grape: Sangiovese Vibe: Frothy Oi Oi! Strawberries n cream - but the expensive stuff that one only really buys in a moment of weakness or panic in the supermarket of dreamz... Full of life and vitality. ABV: 10.5%

wine: Maison Meyer, Bourgogne Aligoté 'Aux Belles Roses' 2024
notes: Place: Burgundy, Frane Grape: Aligote Vibe: Allocated A properly serious Aligoté from a vineyard in Meursault. It is charming and very fresh, but should be savoured for its depth, structure and complexity - a finely tuned mix of bright lemony flavours and a very fine stony salty finish. ABV: 12.0% Due to scarcity this wine is not subject to any discounts

wine: Maison Meyer, Bourgogne Chardonnay 'Les Jardins du Ciel' 2024
notes: Place: Burgundy, Frane Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Allocated Cool, precise and complex, a little reductive with considerable length - this punches very hard. ABV: 12.0% Due to scarcity this wine is not subject to any discounts

Place: Burgundy, Frane Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Allocated Rully is the vanguard for quality Chardonnay in the Côte Chalonnaise and Meyer is working with their very best. A fine mineral driven style with a delicate citrus blossom and pear profile, subtly fattened out by a little spice from the wood. ABV: 11.0% Due to scarcity this wine is not subject to any discounts

wine: Maison Meyer, Savigny lès Beaune 'Blanc Crayeux' 2024
notes: Place: Burgundy, Frane Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Allocated True to the character of the vintage, this is cool and tautly structured with a real crackle of energy. Bright acidity creates momentum straight as an arrow through the length of the wine which goes on and on. ABV: 12.0% Due to scarcity this wine is not subject to any discounts

wine: Maison Meyer, Savigny lès Beaune 'Les Planchots de la Champagne' 2024
notes: Place: Burgundy, Frane Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Allocated Les Planchots is in southern part of the commune, close to the Dijon road, consisting of denser soils. All in the fruit here – fresh, red-berry flavours with a typical hint of hedgerow, an extraordinary delicacy backed by smooth, fine tannins, and a long satisfying finish. ABV: 12.0% Due to scarcity this wine is not subject to any discounts

wine: Maison Meyer, Côte de Nuits Villages Rouge 'En Chantemerle' 2024
notes: Place: Burgundy, Frane Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Allocated Located a little further south in the Corgoloin part of the Côte de Nuits Villages, Chantemerle has heavier soils than Les Platières, and the wine is correspondingly rounder and richer. Smooth, juicy red fruit and vibrant acidity are balanced by dense, elegant tannins driving to a long fresh finish. ABV: 12.5% Due to scarcity this wine is not subject to any discounts

Place: Penedes, Spain Grape: Grenache Vibe: Juicy Old vine Garnatxa given a juicy face lift. Light in body but not on flavour. This is so easy and fresh, it needs an ice bucket and all your mates. To make wine this vibrant in Spain is not easy, especially without additions! Lucy got creative here. Half the fruit is destemmed and lightly crushed before being transferred to tank, the remaining whole bunches layered on top. A quick four days of maceration, with very low extraction follows. The Free-run is separated before the remaining skins are pressed very gently, before being blended back toge

Place: Tuscany, Italy Grape: Trebbiano Vibe: Frothy Pet Nat alla Badini, sounds good. The ferment was restarted in bottle with a bit of Vin Santo must as is the family tradition in this neck of the woods. Gentle effervescence partnered with elite levels of refreshment make this a no brainer. On my visit the table was laden with home produced cheese and charcuterie yet I left feeling lighter than upon entry, I think this wine is the reason.

wine: Pierre-Yves Colin-Morey, Hautes Cotes de Beaune 'Bout du Monde' 2023
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Zingy I love these hefty bots, with all their coiled up energy. That smokey signature reduction often means these are built for the long haul, yet I find their work in the Hautes Cotes to be more than accomplished and approachable. Alluring even. ABV: 13%

wine: Aristotelis Ke Anthoula, Namina Road Riesling 2025
notes: Place: Gundagai, NSW Grape: Riesling Vibe: Zippy and a bit Spritzy Maddy and Tony head to the granitic hills of Murrumbateman for some primo fruit with the Namina Road range. Rizza here, in all its thirst quenching glory. The crown seal is your gateway to this lightly pétillant beauty, a bit of RS left post ferment having done its work in bottle. This balances out any sharpness and caresses the liquid down ones gullet. The fruit leans citric and apricoty and the acidity is nicely saline. A banger. ABV 11%

wine: Aristotelis Ke Anthoula, Namina Road Pinot Noir 2025
notes: Place: Gundagai, NSW Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Juicy Maddy and Tony head to the granitic hills of Murrumbateman for some primo fruit with the Namina Road range. Pinot on show here, not made in every vintage, only when the fruit allows. I've been sampling a fair bit of Jura Rouge of late, and this is giving similar vibes - aka tasty and very, very fluid. There's that twiggy, decaying forest floor stuff on the nose, then a tonne of red and orange fruit flowing through once it hits the tastebuds. Effortless, serve lightly chilled. ABV: 13%

wine: Aristotelis Ke Anthoula, Namina Road Chardonnay 2025
notes: Place: Gundagai, NSW Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Bright Maddy and Tony head to the granitic hills of Murrumbateman for some primo fruit with the Namina Road range. Chardonnay this time, and best left out of the fridge for a while to maximise expression. This gets better and better with air and patience. Whole bunch pressed to old oak, it's a wine of freshness and vitality with underlying depth and composure. Grown up stuff! ABV: 11%

Place: Gundagai, NSW Grape: 50% Fiano, 30% Vermentino, and 20% Nero d’Avola Vibe: Frisky An extended maceration co-ferment. A bath of red and orange wine, aka Blood Orange. If the name has you tasting fruit, you aren't wrong. It's citric and tonic like in the best way possible. The fruit is hand destemmed and left in tank for 6 months, before being basket pressed at the end of winter after it naturally settles. Definitely one to be served straight from the fridge. Definitely one where you needn't bother keep the cork. ABV: 12.2%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Intoxicating + Oxy Yikes. My favourite oxy wine. It's so well balanced, kissed by flor but still with plenty of verve underneath. You could say I'm biased, as I first drank this alongside a huge chunk of Comté at Maylis and JF Ganevat's cabin just above Rotalier. Sorry, you had to be there. Bragging aside, everyone who I've drunk this with subsequently has fallen just as hard. A surefire winner. Fruit from L'Étoile, two years topped up, four years sous voile. Not enough characters to capture how beautifully complex this is. Poached pears, golden nuts,

Place: Piedmont, Italy Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Stunner Erm, what the hell. Piedmont has been putting out some decent Chardo for a while now, but nothing this tasty at this price point has crossed my lips until now. It's such a unique, lime-laden expression of grape and place. It's really limey. Then it goes all salty. Bit like a margarita. But a wine. From northern Italy. One of the most instantly pleasurable bottles I've had in a very long time. Utterly refreshing, both in the literal sense and because it's great to see young winemakers making wines that are made to be drunk young and with ab

Place: Piedmont, Italy Grape: Dolcetto + Nebbiolo Vibe: Juicy Another belter, so pretty and fresh. It's about time young winemakers started having some real FUN in these parts. Fun, yes, but not mere novelty. This comes from La Morra, after all. 80% Dolcetto brings plenty of wild fruit, while a little splash of Nebbiolo bolsters the floral aromatics and spice. This is light on its feet, begging for the ice bucket and large pours for an apero. Impossible not to like. ABV: 12%

wine: Domaine de Montbourgeau, 'Les Budes' Savagnin Ouillé 2022
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Natural, textural Single vineyard Savagnin on grey marl and limestone. This sees a longer élevage of 18 months but remains topped up throughout. It's gone all salty and spine-tingling. Starts with a lovely reduction before fleshing out into nectarines and nuts. Powerful and persistent on the palate. Never disappoints. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Veneto, Italy Grape: Tai Rosso (Grenache) + Garganega Vibe: Pét Nat + Friends Pink and fizzy. It's all I want to drink in the summer. It's rejuvenating. All the red berries, grapefruit-like bitters and pretty colour, with just enough fizz to keep you ticking over. You'll see why the label is an accurate reflection of mood after your first sip. ABV: 12%

wine: Domaine Lajibe, Campsou Bengueres 2023 Party Pack
notes: Place: Jurançon, France Grape: Gros Manseng Vibe: Future Unicorn Tasting notes for this are long and varied. A friend and I wrote down the following: candied citrus, nashi pear, wild herbs, anise, salt, sesame, unripe pineapple, honey, and I could go on and on. Seriously, this is one of the more complex and compelling things I've had in a long time. You'd think it'd be too much, but it's grounded by a persistent minerality that's like drinking liquid rock. It's a beast of a wine, one that will live for a very, very long time in the cellar. I don't know how I'll keep my hands off it... ABV: 13.

Place: Jurançon, France Grape: Gros Manseng Vibe: Vibey Mansengs et Compagnie is Jean-Baptiste's negociant line. Here, grapes are sourced from a relatively high-altitude parcel (350m), fairly unique for Jurançon. Dry, dense and cutting Jurançon in the house style. A parcel of small sedimentary pebbles left by Pyrenean glaciers. Complexity built in through the blending of vintages. Powerful but pretty. Lajibe is so good. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Etna, Sicily, Italy Grape: Nerello Mascalese Vibe: Pretty Unreal pink. Fifty-year-old vines planted over volcanic sand and basalt in Milo. Watermelon-like in both colour and flavour. Backed up by Amaro, cherries and herbs. A volcanic minerality persistent right throughout. This is so serious yet so drinkable. Wish all Etna Rosato tasted like this. Tiny amounts. ABV: 13%

Place: Etna, Sicily, Italy Grape: Carricante Vibe: Pretty A very small run, where the grapes were pressed directly into fibreglass. 9 months in the purest vessel, glass, before a further year to relax in the bottle. Elegant and vibrant at the same time. This feels like a stark contrast to the 2023. Pomelo and almonds with a waxy, honeyed thing reminiscent of some serious Chenin. Etna Bianco of the highest order. ABV: 13%

Place: Etna, Sicily, Italy Grape: Carricante Vibe: Heady Carricante at 800m of altitude, a particularly unique site where soil is composed of volcanic sand and stratification of lapilli, small rock fragments deposited after volcanic eruptions. Cool. Lo-fi winemaking, hi-fi flavour. Destemmed and soaked in plastic for 36 hours before off to rest in steel for 9 months. Bright but with an incredibly smooth and soothing texture. This is one heck of a wine. Acacia honey, spiced and bruised but golden fruit. Lots going on, tiny amounts made. ABV: 12%

Place: Badacsony, Hungary Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Toasty Blanc de Noir of this quality would be eye-watering if we were in that little wine region next to Reims. Things don't get that silly round in this neck of the woods. Just don't tell too many people about this secret. Two-thirds fermented in stainless steel, one-third in amphora, before 10 long years on the lees, disgorged in 2025. We've got creaminess and texture, biscuity and brine. The volcanic minerality, after 10 years, is now right at the fore. An absolute steal considering just how long it's taken to get here.

wine: Bencze Birtok, Aries 'Dancing on the Flor' 2021
notes: Place: Badacsony, Hungary Grape: Riesling Vibe: Mineral Harvested a little later than normal in the 'Aries' phase of the lunar calendar. Whole bunch pressed, long and slow it then spends four and a half years in amphora developing a layer of flor. Classic Riesling aromatics up front, all jasmine and citrus blossom before we see a savoury, herbal side of the grape. The palate feels almost soft and creamy but is cut through by lashings of acid. It leaves you salivating with a salty, persistent finish. I can't say I've had anything else like it. I didn't think Riesling could taste like this, and

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay + Savagnin Vibe: Mineral A really tough year for Yves, losing the large majority of his fruit. A real shame, especially when the work in the vineyards is so painstaking and thoughtful. We get a nice mix of Savagnin's salted yellow fruit and the white floral thing Chardonnay sometimes brings. Starts all flinty, finishes all chalky. Mineral. ABV: 13%

wine: Domaine de Montbourgeau, L'Etoile Chardonnay Ouillé 2023
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural Such a slept on producer. Built in a more classic style but one that overdelivers consistently. This is their house blend of their Chardo from plots around L'Etoile. It's a textbook example of what to expect from topped-up whites. White florals and fruit with things showings just a little hazelnut. Racy and ready to go. ABV: 13.2%

wine: Domaine de Montbourgeau, Crémant du Jura NV
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic fizz Brut Zero, bone dry and bubbling. A timeless, tried and tested classic from a producer that will never let you down. Labelled as NV but always from a single vintage and the youngest Chardo vines. This is sizzling, and you'd be hard pressed to find a better way to kick off an evening.
