Things are lo-fi but well thought out, sourcing fruit from sustainable and organic growers. The winery itself is low impact too, using solar energy and rainwater to keep things ticking. Jordan is very, very good at what he does, with creative and unusual blends that end up in wines with ridiculous drinkability. These wines taste like they cost double. Probably should too tbh. We've put together a little 6-pack to get you fully acquainted. Tw

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural + Vibey Dialled in and dialled up. A step up in both concentration and flavour. Ample texture but still invigorating in its innate drinkability. We're leaning into a honeyed, stone fruit-y palate that finishes on pure salt. No adds but incredible precision. Decant if drinking young, cellar potential here looks great.

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural + Vibey Just the second vintage from Simon, and boy is it good. Mâcon is finally having its moment. Wasn't much of a surprise when I found out he's married to Jessica Litaud. The style here is a little different, cutting and fresher. Still ripe and orchard-y but with mineral tension for days. Unbelievably easy to delete a bottle. If you require hydration, look no further.

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Chardonnay + Riesling + Pinot Meunier 10% Vibe: Refreshing Clever and creative blends resulting in pure deliciousness is the calling card of Jordan Hein. Here, Pinot Meunier brings the blush hue and some savoury depth, barrel-fermented Chardonnay builds in texture, and Riesling's acid washes it all away. Dry, bright, endlessly chuggable, but also a lot more than the sum of its parts. Summer has never looked so good. 12.5% Abv

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Fresh + Fizzy Volcanic Pinot all spruced up with a little sparkle. Fermented in steel and then matured on full solids building in character and leesy richness. That volcanic limestone providing an essential backbone of divine freshness. This is all wild strawberry and rhubarb before we delve into petrichor and gravelly minerality. If this the first attempt at Blanc de Noir, I think the future is looking rather bright indeed. Stock up whilst you can. ABV: 12%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Fresh + Fizzy Not a typo. MV = Multi Vintage. Sounds nicer than Non-Vintage, right? This is 20% 2023, 40% 2024 and 40% 2025, all seeing individual love and care in the cellar. A very nice house style on show, there's some autolytic savouriness, lots of citrus zing. A truly harmonious sparkler that offers serious value. Fans of fizz, I'm telling you it doesn't get better at this price point. ABV: 12%

Place: Blewitt Springs, McLaren Vale Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Generous This is the grape at its best. Generous on ripe fruit and flavour but without losing its puckering vein of acid. Barrel ferment and time on lees bring us texture that complements the pithy, savoury side of the grape very nicely. More serious than the price tag suggests, in Europe Chenin that looks this good will be costing you double. Blewitt Springs, the gift that keeps on giving. 12.5% ABV

Place: Brittany, France Vibe: All-Rounder IYKYK. The ultimate 1 litre of fun. Hazy, rustic, with such a balanced level of sweetness. Cidrerie Kerisac are master blenders, and drinking this transports you immediately to sitting under a warm Brittany skyline. Glug glug. ABV: 5.5%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Elite This special plot sits high in the hills of Fleurie, bordering both Chénas and woodland. The vines here are pushing a century old and grow on pink granite and quartz. This is a cool vintage, and it has to be one of the most moving bottles of Beaujolais I've had in some time. It tastes of the region of old, before it got HOT. Feather-weight and nimble, gorgeously pale and vibrant, this wine is at once effortless and complex. Stony minerality, florals and herbs sit atop the crunchiest red fruit imaginable. Purity is the name of the game. I'm not

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Elite Also from En Remont, but this section of vines is a little younger, still around 50 years old mind, and sitting over basalt. The same whole bunch ferment, before a year of élevage in Julie's old cellar under the farmhouse. Immediate and ethereal, the cool vintage has rendered the grape at its most pretty and perfumed. Another gorgeous wine that will reward for many years to come. Wish there was more...

wine: Julie & Toby Bainbridge, Champ de la Croix 2024
notes: Place: Loire, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Chillable, lighter Very little Loire Pinot tastes this good. There is plenty of spice that makes this feel quite grown up and serious. Yet, at the same time we still have the fruit forward and smashable nature of the Bainbridges' winemaking philosophy on full show. People pleasing.

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Sharp First Chenin from 2025! What a belter it is too. It was a hot and dry year, and when the rains came around mid-August, they decided to harvest early. As such we get chenin in its most razor-sharp and cutting, the energy of the younger vines further contributing to this wonderfully citric and salty wine. Very hydrating...

Place: Loire, France Grape: Grolleau Vibe: Fun Fizz Become a bit of a cult fizz. Good reason to. Pet-Nat at its most unpretentious and enjoyable best. Grolleau gives lots of juicy strawberries and a bit of herb. A little creamy too. Wimbledon wine. ABV: 10%

Place: Aragon, Spain Grape: Grenache + Tempranillo Vibe: Natural, easy Juicy, biodynamic, unoaked Spanish Red. Pair with literally anything and you're rolling. This is so damn tasty! So damn pretty. A perfect midweek drop. ABV: 13%

Place: Aragon, Spain Grape: Grenache Blanc Vibe: Crisp and Dry They've managed to put out an enviably crisp and refreshing Spanish white. Everything's aged in stainless, and we get lots of pure citrus with just a little stonefruit mingling in the backdrop. Truly fresh, and that's no easy feat given the warming world we're living in atm. Grapes are farmed biodynamically too, on top of an aesthetically pleasing label and a price that's practically impossible to come across these days. Summer fridge essential. No brainer. ABV: 13%

wine: Domaine de l'Octavin, Corvée de Trou Trou 2022/23
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Trousseau Vibe: Yum I see Les Corvées, I buy Les Corvées. Wines from this vineyard are always so special, but I really like how Alice has brought her own unique take to this famed site. 2022 was warm giving depth and concentration, 2023 was cooler enhancing freshness and drinkability. A marriage made in heaven. This has plenty of savoury, almost mushroom-y, meaty notes yet wrapped up in a really lithe, and crunchy frame. It's unique, and hard to put down.

wine: Domaine de l'Octavin, Hip Hip J… Chardonnay 2023
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Yum Fruit from around Arbois, mainly direct press but with some fruit that is destemmed and macerated for a month. 18 month élevage helps everything harmonise. This is ripe fruited, almost quince like with some smoke and salt thrown in for good measure. It should come as no secret, that I really rate Jura in 2023. I remember this being a highlight from one of the dimly lit caves of the Loire, and I'm so glad I now have direct access without having to cross the channel. Tasting even better than my hazy memories too.

Place: Jura, France Grape: Grenache Vibe: Vibrant + Wild Only Alice could take Grenache from Vaucluse and turn it into a vibrant Red/Rosé hybrid that is buzzing with both life and acidity. Pale and hazy, with plenty of crunchy raspberries and wild herbs. It's got a real nice bitterness too, and at this price point offers a nice entry into the brilliant and bonkers wines from Ms Bouvot. ABV: 11%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin + Gewürztraminer. Vibe: Vibrant + Wild Betty Bulles is constantly changing from vintage to vintage. Previous iterations had Chenin and Vermentino. In 2025 we see the unlikely marriage of Savagnin and Gewürztraminer. Well, perhaps not that unusual as the latter is actually a direct, pink-skinned, and highly aromatic mutation of the former. They do also work really well together. We get subtle florals but with plenty of drive. Limey, zesty and salty, this creative blend is about as refreshing as wine gets. You'd be hard pressed to find anything better to drink

Place: Rhône, France Grape: Cinsault + Grenache Noir Vibe: Silly Silly Good Very much in the L’Anglore mold. It dances between delicate florals, lipsmacking fruit and zesty citrus, all pulled off with serious finesse. If you don’t know, now’s the time to get acquainted. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Rhône, France Grape: Mourvèdre Vibe: Pure + Pretty Nicolas Renaud, the man behind these Grillion wines, is in my eyes one of the most underrated winemakers out there. A good pal of the Pfifferlings, there is an evident similarity in these bistro-bound bottles. Southern fruit married with an undeniable freshness. Mourvèdre has never looked so pretty. Half direct press, half given the carbo treatment. Full of fruit, florals and spice. Light redor deep rose, call this what you want, just save me a glass. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Aligoté Vibe: Classic, textural The Aligoté revolution is in full swing! Centenary vines located within Puligny-Montrachet. We'd be adding a 0 to the price if it were Chardy. Elevated acidity penetrating some suitably deep fruit. Pretty clear why so many quality-conscious producers are refocussing on Aligoté. ABV: 12%

Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Grenache Vibe: Fun, Natural Ultra light this vintage, combined with Mataburro's usual insane levels of refreshment. 2023 was again drought-ridden, but thanks to some last minute rain at the time of harvest we get real, real freshness. One of those bottles where if you blink, you'll miss it. A bit like the South of France trying to emulate Jura Poulsard. Unbeatable in the heat. Serve chilled, drink fast. ABV: 11%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Natural, textural SHEESH! Yellow Wine from the King of Jura. 2012 too. Could live longer than you and I... If you can resist that it is. *Please note that due to the limited quantity of this wine available it is not subject to further discount.

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay + Savagnin Vibe: Adv Skinsy A first for me in that we have a maceration from the Maestro. Seven weeks on skins, then whacked off to barrel for years and years. Experimental and edgy, but also just really tasty. No reference point here. All almond skin, spice, bitters, dried fruit etc etc. A lot going on, and all of it delicious. ABV: 14.5% *Please note that due to the limited quantity of this wine available it is not subject to further discount.

wine: Jean-François Ganevat, Crémant de Jura 'La Combe' NV
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural 24 months on lees, zero dosage. A driving style, full of citrus fruit that shreds the yeasty/brioche stuff to pieces. Ganevat seemingly can do it all, fizz included. ABV: 12%

wine: Jean-François Ganevat, 'Victor de la Combe' Blanc NV
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural We thumped a bottle of this on a recent trip to the Jura. I say thumped in the most literal sense. It was gone in nanoseconds. Tingling in all the right places. Negoce as per the fun labels, with fruit sourced down in the Macon and also closer to home in their native Jura. ABV: 13.5% *Please note that due to the limited quantity of this wine available it is not subject to further discount.

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural Spring frost did not play nice in 2021. Here we have a blend of all his Chardo parcels. Aptly named, then aged for four years in large 600-litre barrels. Whilst a sad reminder of the cruel of nature, atleast we get to enjoy one of the better liquids money can buy. Every cloud and all that... This pack includes 1 x Chardonnay 'Blanc Survivants' 2021 and 1 x Mystery White Jura Please note due to scarcity this is not subject to further discount.

wine: Jean-François Ganevat, Grands Teppes VV 84 Months 2018 PARTY PACK
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural Old vine fruit given the usual deft touch, and isn't it lovely? Grand Teppes is always my personal favourite bottle too, I remember bringing a magnum to a staff party once. Had one glass, and it got lost on the table. Never again. Probably does mean it was pretty good though. This version sees a whopping 84 months of long and peaceful élevage. RARES *This pack includes 1 x Chardonnay 'Grands Teppes VV 84 months' 2018 and 1 x Mystery White Jura Please note due to scarcity this is not subject to further discount.

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot Noir + Pinot Gris Vibe: Mineral Pinot Noir and Gris that are both directly pressed, albeit slowly and gently, so we get a little blushed hue yet no tannin. I'm still calling this a white wine. You call it what you like, but you can't argue this doesn't absolutely slap. Aromatically we've got florals and raspberries whilst the palate feels all taut and mineral, dry and chalky but with an honeyed note going on too. A killer bistro wine. Who's cooking me a choucroute?

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Riesling Vibe: Mineral A true winemaker's winemaker. You ask any half decent Alsatian vigneron who is making some of the best wine of the modern era, it's this guy. Vineyard was previously owned by Marc Tempé and has been worked lovingly for years now, biodynamic for 25+. This first release is a belter. The long, slow press brings both strength through oxygenation and draws out some complexity from the skins. Smoky and mineral, this has both texture and drive in spades. How good is new wave Alsace? Easily one of the most exciting corners of France atm. ABV: 12%

wine: Lukas Hammelmann, Riesling Trocken Solera NV
notes: Place: Pfalz, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Classic Sh*t hot. The house style leans heavily into a more textural style of Riesling. There's richness on show but lifted by a wonderfully fine reduction. This is a blend of vintages from '19 to '23. Barrels are topped up but without any sulphur, so we get a smidge of flor-derived oxidative character. Originally started as an experiment, I hope this is a permanent fixture in the line-up. There's freshness and drinkability in spades, yet real complexity built in too. On top of that, the fruit comes from the Grand Cru Klostergarten, yet due to bureau

wine: Lukas Hammelmann, Riesling Trocken Roter Berg 2022
notes: Place: Pfalz, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Classic, lighter Oh my god. This is very very tasty. Fruit off a limestone-rich parcel, before two years' élevage and then a year in bottle before release. The climate here is cooler than the more famed parcels of the Pfalz., and I'm here for this insanely detailed wine. Classy and refined Riesling, the acidity is there but not so tear-jerking. The fruit here is fleshy and very herbal, with so much clarity on show. Pfalz on fire.

Place: Pfalz, Germany Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Classic, lighter Could be one of the better wines I've tasted in recent memory. And yes, this is Spätburgunder. Long gone are the days when Germany's attempts at Pinot would be laughed out of a line-up of Burgundy. We're at the very pinnacle of wine here. Seriously, it's that good. Facing north and harvested relatively early, 60% of the fruit is de-stemmed and fermented in wood for 14 days. Things then move to barriques for another two years of élevage. Light bodied and delicate but with so much going for it. Mineral driven and stony, with a whiff

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Serious Phew, this is a proper, proper orange wine, crying out for dinner. Citrus peel and bitters come raring out the gate, with a chewy, solid tannic structure and sweet fruit on the palate. It's deep and broody, but with an enviable freshness keeping it eminently drinkable. Not for novices, but that's not u anyway, is it? ABV: 12.5%

wine: Rouges Queues, Hautes Côtes de Beaune 2018
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Vibe: Perfumed Such a slept on producer, and I really hope you're still not sleeping on the Hautes Côtes. Even in warmer vintages like this we get actual freshness, and things don't command such a silly price tag either. Throw that into 2018 pricing and we have a true bargain. Farming is truly exceptional and with 8 years off the vine this is really peaking. Full of savoury spice and tea-like spice I can't believe no one has pulled the trigger yet. Just 2 left.

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Energetic Grusse might ring a bell or two if you like highly allocated Jura. Home to Kenjiro Kagami and also home to a plot behind one of my favourite bottles from Mr Ganevat, who happens to be the mentor to Mr Guadagnolo. Small world. Anyway, this feels the broader of the pair, the fruit a little riper but still with plenty of vitality. Orchard fruits aplenty, a healthy lick of salinity, so much energy on show. Can't wait to see this in a few years. Will be hard to keep my hands off.

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Lively Jura Chardonnay from the region's rising star. The more vertical and taut of the pair. High toned and heavenly, heavy on the citrus, and wildly captivating with a salty mineral finish. Just a touch of a skinsy thing here too, adding texture and bitters. One for the cellar.

wine: Bastien Pointillart, Champagne Blanc de Blancs 2014
notes: Place: Champagne, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Cult Stupid. You can't really find these, so I don't really know how we've been so blessed to end up with a tiny tranche here in the UK. They always spend a long long time on lees, they often have just a small dosage, but with such searing acid, it never registers. Finish never seems to end. '14 was the first vintage too. Sheesh.

wine: Bastien Pointillart, Champagne Blanc de Blancs 2015
notes: Place: Champagne, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Cult Stupid. You can't really find these, so I don't really know how we've been so blessed to end up with a tiny tranche here in the UK. They always spend a long long time on lees, they often have just a small dosage, but with such searing acid, it never registers. Finish never seems to end. IYKYK. Unicorns.

wine: Icy Liu, Bourgogne Rouge Doudou Tu Viens 2023
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural, lighter A cuvée produced in tiny amounts from Icy's first forays into winemaking. I just love this. Ethereal and fine-boned as per the house style, yet so far from lacking complexity. This dances effortlessly between crunchy blue and red fruit with just a kiss of earthy charm. Obsessed. Just 591 bottles in 2023.

grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Riesling, Pinot Gris
notes: Place: Pfalz , Germany Grape: Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Auxerrois, Scheurebe, Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir Vibe: Classic, textural Big German blend given a nice soak on skins. The maceration of SS26. No two ways about it. Peach iced tea levels of refreshment, in a fun and fruity bottle with the colour and texture to match. Priced to pour. Fill those fridges. ABV: 10%

Place: Kent, England Grape: Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir, Bacchus, Seyval Blanc, Reichensteiner Vibe: Energetic Just the second release since her first vintage. A big blend from her home site, with exceptional farming at the edge of the Romney Marshes, vines sitting atop a little chalk seam. 2024 was a tough year in England, cool and pretty wet, but Sophie has once again produced something with real energy and character. Everything de-stemmed, crushed by foot before fermenting in steel. Things then rest for a year in tank and demijohn before bottling with a teeny tiny bit of sulphur. Pretty elderflo

wine: Domaine Hubert Lamy, Bourgogne Blanc 'Les Chataigners' 2023
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural An elite producer doing elite things. Richness yet precision has become the calling card. Whilst the others in the range are built for the long haul, this Bourgogne Blanc gives us access to these fine elixirs a little earlier. Still from a prime site, on the slopes as Saint Aubin bends over into Meursault. This is truly excellent drinking. ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Crunchy Lovely little Côte de Nuits. I really like that Antoine's wines still have a bit of structure despite the newer generation trending towards things more ethereal. I like both, but I like variety more. Pinot in a darker hue, plum leaning with plenty of five spice. Those limestone soils keeping things nice and direct too. Going to age great. ABV: 13%

wine: Antoine Lienhardt, Les Plantes au Bois 2023
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Classic, textural Lovely little Côte de Nuits. I really like that Antoine's wines still have a bit of structure despite the newer generation trending towards things more ethereal. I like both, but I like variety more. His largest parcel, where the vines are between 50 and 70 years old. Bit of a calling card, and an ultimate crowd pleaser. Find me someone who doesn't like this. Impossible. ABV: 13%

Place: Dorset, England Grape: 64% Chardonnay + 36% Pinot Noir Vibe: Unicorn Don't want to make bold claims, but this is about as Selosse-like as UK fizz gets. Incredibly limited, just 1000 bottles. 002 sees an extra year on lees than the first release. Extra vinous, from a single vineyard on chalk. True to the house style, a very long and slow oxidative pressing, wild ferment, full malo, bottled at 4.5 bars of pressure and left to get real toasty for four years. No sulphur, no dosage either. Yikes. Benchmark. Tiny amounts.

Place: Friuli Venezia Giulia, Italy Grape: Merlot, Schioppettino, Ribolla Gialla Vibe: Natural + Unique Nikolas's first ever red. Harvested late September at full ripeness before a short maceration, and this is so unlike any red I've had from the region. Fine boned and with some structure, but lifted by around 30% white juice. A real medley of red fruit and plenty of florals. There's a distinct green peppercorn thing going on that I imagine comes from the Schioppettino, whilst the Merlot brings something herbal. Hard to categorise. Utterly delicious. Like a combination of all my favourite wine

Place: Friuli Venezia Giulia, Italy Grape: Tocai Friulano Vibe: Natural + Unique Tocai Friulano with a tiny percentage of Picolit and Malvasia Istriana from the cru Montona, located on the windy Quarin hill overlooking the Slovenian Brda. Surrounded by forest on rich, fossil-filled limestone soil. A cool vintage rendering something so herbal and unique. Gin and tonic levels of refreshment. Soothing chamomile and cooling acidity with a nutty, almond like finish. Breathtaking.

Place: Friuli Venezia Giulia, Italy Grape: Tocai Friulano + Malvasia + Ribolla Vibe: Natural + Unique The wine that made me fall in love with the producer. South facing on the warmest side of the region, some vines dating back to 1910. A week of maceration in concrete for a golden hued masterpiece. Candied fruit, dried herbs, so much citrus pith. Nothing chewy or astringent either. Lifted by a healthy amount of acidity and with a so much depth of flavour but just so effortless. The most immediate of the range, and a must taste for anyone who enjoys macerated wine that transcends. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Friuli Venezia Giulia, Italy Grape: Pinot Grigio + Malvasia + Chardonnay Vibe: Natural + Unique Mind bending. A week on skins before being split across an assortment of vessels. Steel, concrete, barrel. Outrageous for a first attempt. It doesn't taste of this world. That slightly pinkish hue followed up with a grapefruit-like palate. Tangy and beautiful phenolic bitters. Spice and salt. Honey and caramel. A kaleidoscope of flavour I can't stop thinking about. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Muscat Vibe: Natural Only 800 bottles of this. Shame, as I'd gladly take them all. Macerated Muscat is one of life's great pleasures. All bergamot and candied fruit, with time to breathe dried citrus and sweet spices come to the fore. Food-friendly and a perfect foil for those particularly tricky dishes to pair, like asparagus and artichokes that are just coming into season right now. ABV: 10.5%

Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Macabeu Vibe: Natural What a lovely wine. I'd usually not be too fussed about Macabeu, but we're not dealing with normal vignerons here. From a parcel called Les Terres Rouges, whole bunch pressed before heading into a big old foudre. Starts all smoky before diving into pineapple, nostalgic boiled sweets, fennel, and positive bitters. A lovely wild edge but still so classy.

Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Grenache + Carignan + Vibe: Natural My personal favourite bottling from the brothers, a lovely vineyard on schist with a bed of limestone underneath. Again, effortless but not lacking backbone. This is so seductively savoury I can only imagine things going up from here. Hard to keep your hands off it though.

Place: Roussillon, France Grape: 60% Mourvèdre + 40% Grenache Vibe: Soulful I don't know how they manage it. Richness and concentration, but equally revitalising and fresh. A fruit bomb but still dark and garrigue-y. Pretty crazy to think how they've channelled so much 'Pinosity' into something that has no right being this fine boned and elegant. ABV : 12%

This pack includes La Liberté 2023 + 14 Watts. Double Trouble is no bad thing, IMO. La Liberté 2023 Grape: Carignan + Mouvèdre Vibe: Heady Sourcing some fruit from the south after Benoit decided to blend all his plots of Gamay in the warmth of 2023. Some is directly pressed, some is macerated. Signature Benoit vibrancy with a fruit profile that feels pleasingly southern. Harmounious after 1 year of elevage. This is wild and beautiful. 14 Watts 2023 Grape; Gamay Vibe: Dreamy 3 weeks whole bunch maceration and 1 year elévage who a typically Auvergnat expression of the grape. Smokey and seductive

Place: Loire, France Grape: Cabernet Franc Vibe: Natural + Fresher From prime Franc territory between Chinon and Saumur. Two south-facing sites on clay, limestone, and a healthy chunk of silex. Whole bunch pressed, and from a cool vintage the grape sits in a lighter frame. Full of spice and crunchy wild fruit. BBQ vibes. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Cabernet Franc Vibe: Natural + Fresher A blend of four tiny parcels, soils are more sand and limestone heavy here too. Similar vinification but quite a different expression. Ever so vegetal, in a really pleasing way, with fine sandy tannins to boot. The fruit still shines bright, all compelling and stony. I could drink and drink and drink this. I plan on it too. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc + Cab Franc Vibe: Natural Icons IYKYK. Chenin from less than a hectare of tiny plots, stupidly old vines planted over clay, limestone, and silex. A powerful, solar vintage given three years of elevage, bottled with a tiny bit of residual hence the crown cap. That has now fully dissolved, leaving a wine of immense power but also poise. Bit of a unicorn, and will live a long time in the cellar. If you can be patient enough, that is. Due to the limited nature of this wine, purchases will also include a bottle of Bejon, Saint Germain 2024.

Place: Catalunya, Spain Grape: Sumoll Vibe: Natural, Lighter Centurion vines, harvested in multiple tries to ensure everything is perfectly ripe. Destemmed and put through a rigorous sorting by Glòria. Short maceration then off to beeswax lined amphora. No adds. From that geeky bit alone you should know this is something very special. Minimalist label, maximal flavour. One of the world's best pinks. ABV:12.5%

Place: Monmouthshire, Wales Grape: Albarino Vibe: Adv Skinsy Don't ask me how Albariño ended up in Wales. Don't ask me why they macerated it. All I know is this is very tasty. Unexpectedly good. Tangerine and a bit of bruised orchard fruit, some hay and chamomile too. Low ABV a bonus, the actual orange colour another pleasant surprise. Well worth a look. ABV:9%

Place: England Grape: Ortega + Auxerrois Vibe: Crispy An approachable and easy-going English blend that is actually priced to pour. Get in. Walgate makes some pretty serious wine but has now turned his hand to something a little friendlier on the wallet. Quintessentially English. Elderflowers and orchards. The acidity a little softer, with a bit of time in older oak building in some texture too. ABV: 11%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Sylvaner Vibe: Hedonistic One of my favourite grapes, one of my favourite producers. You just know this is gonna be good. Then you find out, it's a 6-month gentle maceration, before being given 36 months of ageing. Jeez. This is a fairly intense maceration; with lots of texture and tannin but at the same time, things feel so energetic. Plenty of dried citrus, woodsy herb, but what really comes through is a crystalline minerality. Unreal. Vincent, we <3 u. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Lazio, Italy Grape: Sangiovese Vibe: Yummy Simply stunning for the price. Cherry fruited, a little of that tomato leaf thing, tannins already nicely integrated. The grape's inherent acidity keeping everything bright and fresh. Lovely label too. An absolute must have. ABV: 13%

Place: Piemonte, Italy Grape: Nebbiolo Vibe: Yummy Nebbiolo's eye-popping prices had me on the hunt for something a bit more wallet-friendly, and here she is. Juicy cherry compote flavours sit happily next to some earthy, woody notes. A great intro to Nebb if you're a first-timer, although be warned, the prices are all up from here... ABV: 12.5%

Place: Itata Valley, Chile Grape: Semillion Vibe: Natural, crisp Something skinsy for under £15? No, you haven't gone back in time. But you have gone to Chile. One of the last few places where real value is still to be found. A fresher style of maceration with very light grip. More citrus and floral than anything, with just a little hint of spice. ABV: 12%

Place: Itata Valley, Chile Grape: Cinsault Vibe: Natural, crisp Provençal-inspired pink from all the way over in Chile. Not only really tasty but an absolute bargain too. Granitic soils bringing typical crunchy red fruit and florals. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Loire Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, crisp I've been looking for a tasty sub-£20 Chardonnay for quite some time. No easy task in the current climate. This ticks all the boxes. Organically certified, bit of citrus, bit of stonefruit. Uncomplicated and immediate, a lovely crisp midweek white. Always a good idea to have a bottle or two on hand, just in case. ABV:13.5%

Place: France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Rares The Ex-Labet boys are working wonders as per. Gamay, given a Jurassien makeover. Almost featherweight and so vibrant. Want to know what I mean when I talk about 'Energy'? Then see here. Rare as. ABV: 12%
Place: France Grape: Pinot D'Aunis Vibe: Rares. The Ex-Labet boys are working wonders with some Pinot D'Aunis. The grape at it's most lifted and vibrant. Rares.

Place: Abruzzo, Italy Grape: Trebbiano D'Abruzzo Vibe: Soulful In case you didn't know, the local Trebbiano is vastly different from what you'll find scattered across Italy. Lower yielding, and capable of making some of the finest, most long-lived wines in the world. A mix of young vines bringing freshness and older vine material bringing complexity. We're at 200 metres above sea level on limestone and clay too. There's a reductive touch here that I really like before everything fleshes out into an array of nuts, hay, and golden fruit. Taut and mineral, chalky texture, and an unmistakable sali

Place: Abruzzo, Italy Grape: Montepulciano Vibe: Soulful I really like summer. It means I'm finally allowed to give the rosé shelf a refresh, though personally I drink the stuff year round. You should too. It's no secret this region produces some of the world's greatest pink wines. Emidio Pepe, sadly, doesn't leave Italy, and Valentini, will cost you an arm and a leg. This is here to scratch a similar itch, one you can not only afford but buy year-round. Emotional drinking. Reductive at first but give it time and you'll find herbs, minerals, and earthen charm in abundance, all sitting atop gor

Place: Modena, Emilia Romagna, Italy Grape: Uva Tosca Vibe: Pét Nat + Friends Uva Tosca, another ancient local variety given the spotlight. Blushing on both the vine and in the glass. Gently pressed and so delicate but with plenty of detail. This is so ethereal. Pink grapefruit and blood orange citrus, a bit more stonefruit and lots of salt. The acidity zippy and vertical. About as hydrating as fizz gets. Ultimate thirst quencher. ABV: 11%

Place: New Zealand Grape: Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling Vibe: Easy Skinsy Suitably named blushing orange from Nelson. Refreshing rather than grippy. All tropical and salty fruit, the structure faint and pleasing. Drink chilled to be chilled. ABV: 12.5%

Place: New Zealand Grape: Pinot Noir, Gamay + Pinot Girs Vibe: Lithe + Lifted Pinot and Gamay brightened up further with a bit of Pinot Gris. Creative blends are clearly a calling card for Mr Craighead. Plenty of red fruit here, but this is far from mere glou glou. Small berry Pinot spice, a herbal note too. Another clean and curious zero zero bottling that is quite frankly far too cheap. Not complaining. Go go.

Place: New Zealand Grape: Chardonnay + Vermentino Vibe: Salty The home line from Alex, as you'd expect, comes from domaine fruit. Mainly direct press Chardonnay with a fifth Vermentino. A dreamy interplay between salinity and subtle fruit. Texture, but a thread of tension running right throughout. Pure and pretty, no additions at any stage. Zero zero wine doesn't get any cleaner.

Place: New Zealand Grape: Muscat, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris, + Riesling Vibe: Easy An aromatic blend that on paper would make more sense in Alsace than from Nelson on the northern tip of the South Island. But I learnt the French were some of the first to plant vines here, so makes sense total sense, and these grapes do well in this sun-kissed part of the island too. Here things are restrained, the florals kept in check, the fruit heavily citrus leaning, with some bite and plenty of freshness. A wine you could think deeply about or pour carelessly. Either way, you'll feel more nourished once t

Place: New Zealand Grape: Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Easy A bright blend from one very clever winemaker. Equal parts fruit and florals, cleaned up by a pleasing pinch of acidity. Like taking a stroll through a spring meadow, just without the hayfever. Originally, only meant for the market in Japan but when the importer tasted they simply couldn't refuse bringing a few bottle back to the UK. That good.

Place: Côtes-du-Rhône, France Grape: Grenache + Syrah + Mourvedre Vibe: New Wave Rhone Stupidly good CDR, named after Wil's late grandfather who would heroically open a bottle most mornings before midday. King. Pure and instantly pleasurable, I can see this fitting dangerously into my go-to rotation. Plenty of cherry fruit, a lick of herb, and a faint crack of pepper. I'll be drinking this en masse, just as Wil's grandfather would have done. You should too. ABV: 14%

Place: Coteaux du Lyonnais, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: New Wave Rhone Another thumping bottle from Will. The 2024 feels fresher than the previous vintage, no bad thing at all. Still a core of lovely fruit but a little crisper and breezier with it. Yet to be disappointed by anything from this producer, and the future is looking very bright. How good are those labels too. Chardo at this price point doesn't get much better. ABV: 12%

Place: Terra Alta, Catalunya, Spain Grape: Garnacha Vibe: Crunchy A little collab with Eloi of Sistema Vinari, whose wines I'm also obsessed with. This Garnacha clone gives lower tannin, lighter colour and more modest levels of alcohol, so a French-style carbonic treatment was the order of the day. More lifted than you'd expect, but still with that signature fruit. There's a kiss of bitter brine to cut through. This is at once fun and fascinating. A wine to ponder on, but also pound on the porch. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Terra Alta, Catalunya, Spain Grape: Tempranillo, Morenillo, Garnacha + Carinyena Vibe: Juicy Òscar calls this simply a vi de taula, but it offers much more refreshment than many local table wines. A blend of plots, some direct press, some whole bunch, vines young and old, with limestone the common thread linking them all. There is a lot to like aromatically, and the palate follows suit. Juicy, with a nice splattering of earthy spice. Far too easy. Proper BBQ bottle. ABV: 14%

Place: Aragón, Spain Grape: Macabeo Vibe: Saline Things get taken up a notch here. A single vineyard of gnarly old bush vines planted in the 1930s at 600m altitude, with limestone soils pushing the freshness even further. I can't remember a Spanish white with such veracity and verticality. The cool vintage feels very much reflected when tasting Oscar's whites side by side. Lean but not mean, saline and citrus-driven. This and some fried fish would be very, very tasty. ABV: 12%

Place: Aragón, Spain Grape: Garnacha Blanca + Macabeo Vibe: Sunkissed A stunning wine from Oscar. Unafraid of the natural ripeness that Cataluña has to offer, this is picked perfectly to capture a heady expression of this sun-kissed corner of Spain. There's still plenty of freshness to offset the texture, with lots of energy to boot. Chalky and saline at first, then an assault of raw almonds and honeyed tones. A wine calling out for sunshine and smoke from a nearby grill. ABV: 14.5%

wine: Giuseppe Mascarello e Figlio, Barolo Perno Vigna San Stefano 2020
notes: Place: Piemonte, Italy Grape: Nebbiolo Vibe: Cuddly Mascarello is a name that might be familiar if you're of the Piemonte persuasion. Sweetly spiced and succulent. This will likely live longer than you and I. A cool, iron-rich cru that always hits the spot. The fruit is always so juicy, with tannin to die for. ABV: 15%

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Merlot, Blaufrankisch, Portugieser, Sankt Laurent, Pinot Noir Vibe: Serious Skins This wine has come on leaps and bounds in recent years. Grown up, got a new label, but still plenty of youthful energy and personality. This big blend is much more than the sum of its parts. Really juicy and vibrant, works a treat chilled. Go looking and there's plenty of herbal, earthen stuff mingling in the background too. Weeknight winner.

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Riesling, Weissburgunder, Gelber Muskateller, Silvaner Vibe: Serious Skins Hectic in the best sense. Extended time on skins plus a bit of time in barrel under flor leads to a very multidimensional bottle. At once tropical and tangy before diving straight into savoury and salty, courtesy of that oxidative kiss. Somehow keeps everything nicely balanced and remains insanely refreshing.

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Sylvaner Vibe: Serious Skins How good is Sylvaner? Everyone gushes over Riesling, but this is also a grape that can do it all. Like Riesling, but with more focus on herbs and spice. Especially here, where subtle skin contact and plenty of time in bottle has pushed the primary fruit back to reveal something really interesting. White pepper, bay, and botanicals, then comes that drying citrus fruit and apple skin grip. Serious stuff.

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Grauburgunder, Riesling, Sylvaner Vibe: Juicy This wine has come on leaps and bounds in recent years. Grown up, got a new label, but still plenty of youthful energy and personality. Flirting between orange and white, skin contact adding texture and flavour rather than overt grip and tannin. Clean and fresh but with enough exotic florals to keep you entertained. Unreal value.

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural , textural Boyer! Simply the best zero-zero Burgs money can buy. This is the place to wet your toes if you like things tense and tantalising. Don't be fooled by the humble Côteaux Bourguignons appellation; this is Boyer after all. Punches well above. Limited.

wine: Parched + Les Caves de Pyrene Present: Back Vintage Banditos
notes: We've been huge fans of Testalonga for a long time here at Parched. When we received some back vintage stuff from them, we knew what we had to do. Fionn and J are gonna be taking you through a journey of Testalonga's best vintages of their top wines; starting at 2012, then a few vintages til 2024. Only 15 tickets avaliable, so get em while they last. In 2008, after many years making wine all over the globe, Craig and Carla Hawkins started Testalonga in Swartland, South Africa. All of the fruit comes from dry-farmed, organic sites. The wines are made with as little manipulation as possible – in

Place: Jurançon, France Grape: Petit and Gros Manseng Vibe: Off The Charts Jeeez. What a wine. Young, this is full of flinty, sesame-laced reduction that gives way to a hectic array of fruit and flower. Saline and spine-tingling, I can imagine this is gonna age so well. There is a LOT going on here, and all of it is delicious. The acidity slices through it all like a warm knife through butter. Desert island drinking. Also featured in Fresh Foillard and Limited Lajibe: The Latest Biweekly Bottle Drop .

wine: Labet Party Pack ft. Chardonnay Sous Voile 'Cuvée du Hasard' 2018

wine: Les Jardins de la Martiniere, Akane No Oka 2019
notes: Place: Loire, France Grape: Cab Franc Vibe: UNICORN 30-year-old Cab Franc, from the bottom of a south-east facing slope on clay soils. A beautiful place, and the name translates to "the sun setting over the hill." Fruit was macerated in whole bunches for 10 days with daily pigéage, then raised in barrique for a year before moving to cuve for another four. Bottled late 2024. This is a lithe, fragrant expression of the grape. Earthen and floral at the same time, bright fruit and with a really sapid, savoury finish that lingers long in the mind and palate. . Due to scarcity this comes in a pack .

Place: Colli Eugane, Italy Grape: Riesling + Pinot Vibe: Fun Genre-defining, mind-bending, and insanely delicious. All things I like in my wine. Yes, the blend is correct. Riesling with a dash of Pinot Noir, from the volcanic hills of the Colli Euganei. Whole bunch pressed, into a ten-hectolitre cask, bottled without additions. Not something you see every day, but we're very much here for it. Blushing in the glass, the nose is intoxicating. Bergamot and an assortment of berries, with spice and bite on the long finish. Hard to put into a category other than very, very good.

Place: Colli Eugane, Italy Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Vibrant Sauvignon Blanc is not inherently evil, despite what you might think. This is a case-in-point example of the lofty heights the grape can reach when given a bit of TLC. De-stemmed before a short maceration, then into cask, bottled without additions. Golden fruited and in no way green, almost rich before a cleansing vein of acid and a tea-like grip. Just a hint of something floral and herbal too. Wow. I could, and plan to, drink this all year long. Crown cap is merely for our convenience.

Place: Colli Eugane, Italy Grape: Caberent Franc Vibe: Vibrant I've always had a soft spot for Italian Cab Franc. It feels almost wrong, given Italy has so many native varieties, but I can't lie, it absolutely slaps here. Two plots blended, one on red clay, the other marl. A carbonic ferment and time in steel brings out a pure, instantly pleasurable side of the grape. Crunchy cherry fruit, plenty of Mediterranean herb, and a splash of pepper. A tiny spritz adds even more energy to this incredibly fun-loving bottle. One of those wines you'll delete in seconds. How good is the label too?

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: Grenache Vibe: Electric Etna and Grenache. Two of my favourite things. You just know this is going to hit the spot. Four different plots, harvested together and macerated for two weeks before heading to chestnut barrel. Signature Etna smoke meets plush ripe cherries, nuts and spice and all things nice. A delicious snapshot of place.

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: Grecanico Dorato + Others Vibe: Electric Ungrafted, pre-phylloxeric vines from a very special vineyard on their doorstep. Grapes macerate gently for six days in open vats before heading to steel for 11 months. Insanely energetic yet powerful and present on the palate. Fruit runs the gamut. Citrus and orchard-y, a faint grip and a cleansing saline finish. Have a look, you won't regret it.

Place: Veneto, Italy Grape: Vespaiola Vibe: Fizzy Worth it for the label alone. How good is a bottle of Col Fondo in the sun? Vespaiola, a local Venetian grape, brings a heady combination of underripe Mango, citrus, stone fruit and smoke to the party. Fine fizz carries it all, with a little herbal business lurking underneath if you go looking. This vintage is so so good. Incredibly clean and crispy, I can think of no better Apero. ABV: 12%

Place: Veneto, Italy Grape: Cab Sav, Merlot + Vespaiola Vibe: Fun A devilish blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Vespaiola. Is this an Italian Bordeaux Blend? Far from it. Not something you'd think would be this delicious. Trust me, this is a must-taste. The fruit profile is astonishing. Blueberry, pomegranate and an almost beetroot-like earthen note. That little splash of white cleans everything up, keeping things drinkable and mineral. Little chill wouldn't go amiss. Also featured in Ciao Bella: New-Wave Veneto, Labet and Spring Events .

Place: Veneto, Italy Grape: Vespaiola Vibe: Fun Vespaiola, a new one to me, but a grape with such personality. It used to be prized for sweet stuff due to its ability to hold its acid for seemingly forever. Now, Marco is leading the charge in vinifying things totally bone dry. This is a combination of three hillside plots on volcanic soil, in cellar purity is preserved by hanging out in a mix of fibreglass and concrete. Golden both appearance and flavour. Lush and tropical-fruited with subtle spice and just enough phenolic bite on the finish. Delicious!

Place: Tarragona, Spain Grape: Macabeo + Xarel-lo + Parellada Vibe: Summery Proper 'cava'. This fizz is guaranteed to be a fridge staple all summer. Citrus-heavy, a little toasty and with plenty of that Spanish salt on the finish. Clean and delicious. Naturally made too. Go on, chuck another in the basket. ABV: 12%

wine: Parched + Side Piece Present: Bianka Schmitt (DB Schmitt)
notes: How good is May? There are few better things in life than racy German wine, so we're stoked to have Bianka Schmitt in the house for a night of pure bliss. The Schmitt winery has been in the family for over 230 years with Bianka and Daniel working their 16 hectares for the last decade. They work in full biodynamics which they learned from legendary Alsace vigneron Patrick Meyer and are one of only 80 producers in Germany to be certified by Demeter. Bianka is from Hungary, Daniel is German. They met in 2012 when she was cellar hand in his parent’s winery. Together they have taken over the family

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Riesling Vibe: Smoking hot A short soak on the skins helps coax out the aromatics before pressing off to rest in barrel on full lees. My new reference point for Alsatian Riesling. Texture but little weight, taut and mineral. Dry and diesel-led from the warm vintage. All that energy coiled up waiting to unfurl. Going to age like a dream, don't think I'll be able to keep my hands off. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc, Sylvaner, Riesling, Gewürztraminer Vibe: Mineral A blend of all the whites Pierre tends. A proper snapshot of what Alsace can taste like in the hands of a skilled vigneron. Fruit saw a 3 day maceration before 11 months élevage sur lies in barrique. Perhaps the more approachable of the pair. Citrus forward with slate-like minerals running through it. Beautiful bitterness woven in too. Obsessed. ABV: 12%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Grolleau Vibe: Pretty Picked early to preserve freshness. Things aren't green though, this sits firmly on the jolly, red-fruited side of the spectrum. Bright, bone dry and crisp. A wild berry and citrus sensation. Crown cap is purely for convenience rather than to keep in any bubbles. Picnic pls? ABV: 9.5%

Place: Rioja, Spain Grape: Tempranillo Vibe: Classic Jade's first estate-bottled Tempranillo. The grapes come from her La Cantera plot in Labastida, 36-year-old bush vines planted in clay–limestone soils at around 600m elevation. Cherry, tobacco spice, fine tannin washed out by a cleansing acidity. Drinking like a dream atm but ready for a short snooze too. Dealers choice. ABV: 13%

Place: Rioja, Spain Grape: Tempranillo Blanco, Garnacha Blanco Vibe: Classic White Rioja has never looked so fresh, so fine-tuned. Yellow plums and apricots up front, a creamy midpalate, and a super saline finish. Altitude again lending freshness and finesse. Unreal. ABV: 13%

Place: Rioja, Spain Grape: Garnacha Vibe: Classic A single parcel of old vines at 600m altitude on red clay and limestone. Serious terroir. 30% whole bunch brings lift and savoury freshness. About as refined and refreshing as Garnacha gets. Absolutely breathtaking. 🛒ABV: 13%

Place: Poland Grape: Gewürztraminer Vibe: Natural, textural From the top of the hill, where the soil is more clay and sand. Really elegant considering we're dealing with Gewurz. Grapey aromatics, but restraint is shown before a little rose petal and lychee come out. Far from flabby, this makes for a compelling expression. ABV: 12.5 %

Place: Poland Grape: Riesling Vibe: Natural, textural The pick of the Polish bunch. Riesling on limestone. Music to my ears. Vertical and direct, this drives down the palate. Blossom and citrus part ways for a finish of pure steel. Spine tingling. ABV: 12 %

Place: Poland Grape: Pinot Blanc Vibe: Natural, textural Pretty serious Polish gear. Aged in concrete on fine lees for texture. Plenty of fruit here but far from the star of the show. Texture and salty minerality take centre stage. More than a curiosity, this will make you pay full attention. ABV: 12 %

wine: Tony Bornard, Ploussard 'Au Fil des Générations' 2021
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Ploussard Vibe: Iconic A response to a couple of horrendous vintages lost largely to frost. Very limited. Absolutely delicious but hopefully never again. ABV: 12%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Auxerrois Vibe: Mineral Am I the only one who loves Auxerrois? It's often way back in the Alsatian pecking order, but I think that's because historically no one has given it the care and attention it deserves. The parcel is 50 years old, on alluvial and granitic soils, and Anaïs ferments on skins for a couple of days before pressing off to rest in vats. This is fragrant and subtly smoky, with pithy citrus, tingling minerals and a nice saline bite. It instantly made me crave Tarte Flambée. ABV: 13%

wine: De Moor, Vendangeur Masqué ‘Le Meme Azimut’ 2024
notes: Place: Alsatian fruit vinified in Chablis, France Grape: Riesling + Gewürztraminer + Muscat + Pinot Blanc Vibe: Tasty, Natural 50% Alsatian Riesling, 50% whole cluster fruit. Balance. Aromatic and stone-fruited for sure, but there is precision and drive too, as per the De Moor way. Light on its feet but not lacking personality. At this price you'd be mad not to. ABV: 12%

Place: Marlborough, New Zealand Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Insane Maceration not just for trend's sake, but here it earns its place, adding phenolics and flavour you simply wouldn't get from a direct press. Like a stone fruit salad with plenty of citrus and tea-like spice. The acidity is cleansing, the bitters almost negroni-like. ABV: 12%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Poulsard + Pinot Noir + Trousseau + Gamay + Chardonnay + Savagnin Vibe: Eclectic Méli Mélo means 'hodgepodge' en francais, which makes sense given this is a field blend in the truest sense. Aromatic, lifted, perfumed and delicate, this one has red berries and earthiness in spades, with a slight underlying funk, which I for one am not mad at. This is from a cracking vintage too. ABV: 12%

wine: Domaine de la Petite Empreinte, Persévérance 2022
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Mineral I can only really describe this in expletives. One of the most mind-bending and beautiful things I've tasted this year. 36 months of undisturbed élevage in large format barrel renders the grape at its most taut and mineral. Time has allowed the Sauvignon to shed its fruity skin, leaving us with an expression of liquid rock. Reductive and flinty, it fans out into a kaleidoscopic array of pure, unadulterated deliciousness. Holy sh*t. ABV: 14.5%

Place: Vinho Verde, Portugal Grape: Loureiro + Alvarinho Vibe: Natural, crisp I've been looking for a Vinho Verde that is actually from healthy grapes, made without the usual artificial interference for quite some time. Finding one has proved rather difficult, until now. Spritzy, saline and citrus-heavy as you'd expect, but biodynamic fruit has added further energy to an already sprightly style. Lip-smackingly delicious! ABV: 11%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Poulsard + Pinot Noir + Trousseau Vibe: Eclectic A warm, hot year has given us a dark and brooding expression of the Jura. This is a wild ride and not for the faint of heart. It will reward time in the cellar, or being shared ferociously with friends. Morgane's wines are always a thrill. ABV: 12%

wine: Domaine de la Petite Empreinte, Mas a Tierra 2023
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Silky This is one estate to watch. Pure fruited and juicy, a whisper of structure and an addictive grip. Morello Cherry comes to mind, mint too. Nice vein of acid suggesting this one is ready to go the distance, if you're more patient than I am. ABV: 13%

Place: Styria, Austria Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, Textural Classic Styrian Chardo done extremely well. Starts with that smoky, flinty reduction we all love, then opens into layers of apple, pear, and white flowers. Rich and textured on the palate with plenty of density. Food wine at it best. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Styria, Austria Grape: Weissburgunder Vibe: Natural, Saline Benchmark Styrian Weissburgunder. Fruit is grown on Opok soils, which bring out a super saline and mineral palate + an acid line that'll make you pucker. Tonnes of ripe fruit both on the nose and the palate, adding an amazing lift to the wine. As always, no additives. Banger. ABV: 12%

Place: Styria, Austria Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Natural Sauvignon with a tiny bit of maceration to extract some texture. As always with these wines, the palate is super dense and full of life. On the nose, we get a hint of grass along with tonnes of herbs. Less fruit on this one, but we like that. Sauvignon done just right. ABV: 12%

Place: Stajerska, Slovenia Grape: Mainly Blaüfrankisch Vibe: Natural, Juicy A Blaufränkisch-heavy blend from Slovenia. Bouncy and blue-fruited, this is the perfect midweight wine. Nicely rounded, yet never heavy or jammy. High on flavour, low on price, and made sustainably without unnecessary faff. Works equally well if you're into reds with a little chill. On that note, I'd be very happy to have this at a BBQ straight from the esky. ABV: 12%

Place: Stajerska, Slovenia Grape: Furmint + Welschriesling + Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Natural, textural Slovenian wine? Push the boat out and try something new. At this price, you'd be mad not to. Super crisp and crunchy orchard fruit, backed up by lemon and lime acidity. A little herbal, a lot refreshing. My new favourite bottle under £20. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Leicestershire fruit, Vinified in Somerset, England Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Energetic Pink-y, orange-y, very tasty! Fruit from up North at Matt Gregory's place. Hand-destemmed and split into two batches. Two thirds macerated for 4 days, the remainder for 11, then basket pressed to barrel. Here it spent 9 months ageing under flor. Bottled with no additions. Geeky bits aside, this is actually very approachable. Crunchy berry fruit, a citrus lift and a little savoury salt. So much going on for such a modest ABV, not complaining though, means I can probably take the whole bottle for a solo

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural, lighter Love Chiroubles! Sick of drinking Beaujolais that's overripe and alcoholic? Me too. Thank god for Jules Metras, who just like his dad, has a magic touch. This is firmly in the style of Beaujolais of old. Sitting at decent altitude for the region means we're still on the lithe and agile side. A crunchy fruit profile, a whisper of florals and a satisfying kiss of something wild. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Refreshing Younger-vine Chardonnay from Alice's prized plot in Arbois. A small portion is macerated as whole bunches, while the rest is directly pressed. The result is invigorating, as all of Alice's wines are. The maceration lends texture, while the plot's limestone soils bring plenty of nervy tension. Quite unique, even by Jura standards! It's lean, almost razor-sharp, and bracingly refreshing. Perfect if you're not afraid of things that are both sharp and salty.

Place: Tuscany, Italy Grape: Malvasia Toscana + Canaiolo Vibe: Sweet Can't believe we haven't stocked any Vin Santo before. Known locally as Holy Wine for its succulent flavour and deep amber colour. Sun-kissed, really ripe grapes are left to concentrate further by drying out on straw mats. So tasty, all golden and raisined, but still effortless and moreish. Bring out the biscotti.

Place: Tuscany, Italy Grape: Trebbiano + Malvasia Vibe: Natural Vino Bianco as you'd find it in one of Tuscany's many trattorias. Uncomplicated but uncompromising in its deliciousness. Stone fruit, a little herbal, a little texture too. You could pair this with literally anything and you'll be more than satisfied, though it's easy enough to take for a solo spin. The only downside is that 750ml isn't enough, but at this price you can always grab two. Trust me.

Place: Tuscany, Italy Grape: Petit Manseng Vibe: Skinsy The Badini family were clearly ahead of their time, planting the increasingly popular Petit Manseng in Tuscany just over 30 years ago. Kinda niche but this also makes for some very nice drinking. A long maceration draws out some phenolics, but the grape's natural acidity keeps things lip-smackingly fresh. Into it.

Place: Tuscany, Italy Grape: Sangiovese, Canaiolo, + Colorino Vibe: Trattoria Booze A third each of Tuscany's native reds. Savoury and seductive, this is trattoria wine at its finest. It'll glide effortlessly alongside charcuterie all the way through to ragù. An absolute steal, your midweek Italian just got a serious upgrade.

Place: Tuscany, Italy Grape: Trebbiano + Sangiovese + Canaiolo. Vibe: Chiller Vino Rosso has never looked so good. The region's native reds are brightened up with a healthy splash of Trebbiano, making for something fun and unpretentious. But there's some complexity if you want to go looking, thanks to ungrafted vines planted in the 1950s. You'll be needing a plate of pasta pronto!

wine: Parched + Side Piece Present: Curro Barreño (Vitícola Mentridana & Fedellos)
notes: It's been a minute between events, and we could think of few better ways to kick off the 2026 Wine Calendar down on the Dalston Riviera. We're extremely excited to be joined by Curro from Vitícola Mentridana & Fedellos over in Spain. We are long time fans of both projects, as are you by the looks, so it is a pleasure to cordially invite 14 lucky guests for an evening of elite wine and somehow better vibes. Mentridana is his project in the Gredos Mountains near Madrid, focussing on Grenache grown on other worldly granitic terroir. For Fedellos we head north into the rugged Ribeira Sacra where t

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Chardonnay + Sylvaner + Pinot Blanc + Chenin Vibe: Elegant Who says Pet-Nat can't be classy? Mainly Aurvergnat Chardo, supplemented by grapes from friends. Direct press, one year on lees, no additions as ever. Full of buoyant bubbles, brioche and lemon rind. About as elegant as the category gets. ABV: 13%

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Gewürztraminer + Pinot Gris (Alsace), Muscat d’Alexandrie (Roussillon), Chardonnay (Auvergne), Ugni Blanc + Grenache Blanc (Pinet) Vibe: Perfumed Again, showing this couple's skilled hands when they get access to fruit from all over France. A real regional blend, the aromatic varieties bring fragrance and florals, balanced out texturally by their more neutral counterparts. The colour is as gorgeous as it tastes. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Pineau D'Aunis Vibe: Perfumed The couple also have a deft touch when it comes to their négociant work. This is the grape in its lithest, most fragrant form. Pale, almost pink, with bright red fruit and just a whisper of that signature spice. A short spell in the fridge will do wonders, nothing too frosty though!

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Gamay D'Auvergne Vibe: Mineral One of the domaine's oldest plots, on the basalt slopes around Corent. Aged for around a year in old barrels and stoneware jars, this has become a reference point for the region. Spicy aromatics on the nose, crunchy and rustic fruit, that signature Auvergne mineral streak. It's almost bloody, but bloody delicious. In this vintage, things have never looked so good. Stable and singing with air too. ABV: 13%

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Textural and tense What a wine. Fruit from their own vines, a perfect blend of two vintages and with a small portion macerated for texture rather than colour. This is firmly a white wine, and one of extraordinary heights. Dense and rich, yet with an inherent freshness. The finest Auvergne Chardonnay I've tasted to date. Drink one now, squirrel one away. ABV: 13%

Place: Aragón, Spain Grape: Syrah Vibe: Rares Usually I'd run a mile if you threw a Spanish Syrah at me, but this has changed my mind. Feeling more like a really, really good Northern Rhone, dare I say maybe even better. Gorgeously purple fruit, but the varietal signature olive tapenade and floral thing is on full display. A bit of bacon fat and a cooling, rocky element mingling about too. I'm obsessed. ABV: 12%

wine: Jorge Olivera, O Baile do Gurrión 2023
notes: Place: Aragón, Spain Grape: Garnacha, + Macabeo + Garnacha Blanca Vibe: Rare as hen's teeth , The prettiest looking wine I've seen all year, and just as pretty on the palate. One of the better Blouges I've tasted. Featherweight and fresh, with blood orange, rhubarb, wild strawberry and cranberry all doing their thing. Delicate but detailed and expressive. I really wish we had more than just a couple of bottles. ABV: 13%

Place: Aragón, Spain Grape: Garnacha, Tempranillo + Syrah Vibe: Rares Just the Syrah left as whole bunches, the rest destemmed. A gentle two week maceration before peaceful ageing in barrel. This feels like the darkest, most intoxicating of the range. There's quite a lot to unpack, but thankfully with a texture so silky you'll have no issue heading back for glass after glass. ABV: 12%

Place: Aragón, Spain Grape: Moristel + Garnacha Vibe: WOW The flagship wine from Spain's most hyped new grower. Sitting at 600m altitude, the fruit is destemmed before spending a couple of weeks fermenting on skins, then sent to barrel to come together before being bottled with zero additions. Glowing a pretty ruby, this is full of maximum flavour with no heaviness. Boysenberry, a hectic array of florals and a dusting of peppered spice. Worth the hype, and then some. Tiny allocation so get acquainted fast. ABV: 12%

Place: Aragón, Spain Grape: Macabeo + Chardonnay Vibe: Rare as hen's teeth I've heard and seen a lot about these wines on Insta. The hype is pretty crazy in Spain, but seemingly worldwide too. Hard to know if that is just fluff or if it carries any weight. Thankfully, upon tasting, I can confirm this is truly it. Spanish wine at it's pinnacle. Easily the best maceration I've had in this style, all made with zero additions to boot. Squeaky clean, ripe citrus, lots and lots of salt. Looks like a sunset, kinda tastes like one. We got just a single bottle. GO! ABV: 13%

Place: Mallorca, Spain Grape: Mostly Callet + Manto Negro, Fogoneu Frances, Fogoneu Mallorqui, Garnacha Peluda Vibe: Fragrant New year, new label but as ever, a real snapshot of Mallorca. The blend comes from individually picked parcels, where time on skins and whole bunch usage vary across the lot. The fruit is dark and luminous without being heavy, with herbs and spice woven throughout. If you've been to the island, you'll know it from the glass. Magic. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Mallorca, Spain Grape: Blend Vibe: Juicy Young vines of Callet, Manto Negro and Fogoneu from Felanitx, planted over the island's characteristic red clay soils. Always bottled young and made for the table. Even in the litre format, it disappears quickly. Light and bright, with red berries, herbs and the island's signature briny imprint. Delicious. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Mallorca, Spain Grape: Premsal + Callet Vibe: Saline + lifted A collaboration with Cati Ribot, in whose cellar Eloi vinifies. A co-ferment of red and white varieties produces a rosado with real personality. Grapefruit and salt make it as refreshing as a cocktail, lifted further by a tiny but well-judged smidge of VA. The colour is as cute as the label. Ice bucket and the beach, please. One of the rare occasions where I'll forgive you for using a tumbler lol. ABV: 12%

Place: Mallorca, Spain Grape: Mainly Macabeo + Premsal, Parellada and Vinater Vibe: Salty A Mallorcan white so salty and citrus-heavy it's hard not to salivate from the first sniff. We've got a nice chalky minerality on the mid-palate before a finish that screams of the coast. If you're dreaming about your next holiday, let this convince you to book the flight. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural, lighter I really, really wanted to taste Icy's wines for some time. When I did they didn't disappoint. Fluid yet flavoursome. These are featherweight in structure but defo not on flavour. Vines planted in 2001 from "Roc Blanc" in Mercurey, a parcel that is southeast-facing with calcareous sandy marl. Lots of pink peppercorn and a little forest floor. Vibrant and effortless. Just the 591 bottles on the entire planet. Rare as.

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural, lighter I really, really wanted to taste Icy's wines for some time. When I did, they didn't disappoint. Fluid yet flavoursome. These are featherweight in structure but defo not on flavour. This is Beauregard 1er cru fruit declassified due to the younger vines. Mineral and cherry-leaning, a delicate, fine boned expression, that is everything I want to drink atm. A measly 532 bottles produced... ABV: 12.5%

Place: Champagne, France Grape: Meunier Vibe: Spicy All Meunier from their top vineyard at 180 metres on fossilised limestone soils. Very tasty, leaning into a more citric profile. Lots of sea spray and oyster shells. Looks like it’s time to get shuckin’. ABV: 12%

Place: Champagne, France Grape: Meunier Vibe: Spicy All Meunier from a one-hectare single parcel on sandy marl soils. 55-year-old vines. No dosage, three years under cork. So gastronomic, strawberry shortcake and spice. Flavien can do no wrong. ABV: 12%

wine: Flavien Nowack, 'La Tuilerie' Blanc de Blancs 2012
notes: Place: Champagne, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Elite 100% Chardo from Flavien’s first vintage at the helm. White sand and limestone with marine subsoil about 1.5 to 2 metres under the surface, south-facing at 100 to 120 metres above sea level. A late release, only disgorged in April 2023. It blew my mind. The colour was still so fresh and clear, showing no sign of age or fatigue. Yet the palate was full of nougat and umami savouriness from the extended time on lees under cork. Very very limited. Disgorged 2025. ABV: 12%

wine: Hunter McKirdy, Le Bois des Ormes 2024
notes: Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Herbaceous All about concentration. Red fruited, herbaceous and packed with real intensity, even on the nose. On the palate there’s a bit more structure than you might expect but it still keeps things herbal and fresh. You could easily lay it down for a few years before opening it, or just drink it now... I won't judge. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Blend (Sauvignon Blanc, Menu Pineau, Romorantin, Chardonnay) Vibe: Herbal I’ve seen some wines described as herbal and often been left wondering. Not here. This is so fragrant and pleasantly green in all the best ways. Lime-laced, crunchy apple, then all the herbs: basil, mint, thyme. Beautiful balance between fruit and bitters, which makes it as refreshing as an ice-cold G&T on a warm day. From experience, these only get better with age, but it’s hard to keep your hands off. ABV: 12%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Pinot Vibe: Fresh Good Pinot made by good people has no right being priced like this. Two plots at decent altitude keep things in the fresh and fragrant camp, so if you want something overly ripe and jammy, look elsewhere. If you want something tasty and ethereal, you're in the right place. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Delish Chardo from the hills. Dreamy combo. You can taste the winemaking pedigree here, with a perfect balance of riper fruit, citrus, and a gentle hint of old barrels to keep things soft and silky. New World fruit with Old World attitude. Burgundy this good will cost ya 3x. Do your wallet a favour. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Labet Party Pack ft. Savagnin Elevage Long Ouillé 'En Chalasse' 2019

notes: The fairest way to share the Labet love. How to stop our tiny allocation of Labet disappearing into the pockets of collectors who'll buy one bottle and then disappear into the sunset?
