So you get your Labet, yay, you get to support your friendly neighbourhood wine shop, yay, and maybe even discover a new fave produc

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Natural, textural 2023 was a cooler and wetter year here and as such things feel steely and fresh. It ferments in stainless, really keeping that pure fruited character front and center. It’s razor-sharp and super lithe. The kind of Chenin I could sip on all day long. ABV: 10.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Romorantin Vibe: Mineral Romorantin is my latest obsession. An old Loire variety that has been steadily gaining attention in natural wine circles. I can see why. This is damn good. Floral, nutty, herbal, and intensely mineral. Everything you could want in a white wine. There is so much waiting to unfurl here. Take your time and enjoy the ride. ABV: 12%

Place: Kent, England Grape: 64% Pinot Meunier + 29% Chardonnay + 7% Pinot Noir Vibe: Fun Tastes like spring. Tastes like good times. This is a really lovely bottle. Refreshing, a little frizzante and seemingly impossible to put down. Lots of citrus on show, mainly grapefruit, with some English hedgerow character thrown in too. Just 375 bottles made! An absolute bargain considering the fruit is exceptional, Meunier grown at Ham Street, and the wine is made by Les Caves’ very own Kevin Barbry. ABV: 10.5%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano Vibe: Scintilating One of the discoveries of 2025, shame is there is hardly any. Trebbiano from 2023 was aged in oak, before secondary fermentation in bottle and 6 months spent on the lees. Everything is done by hand, I know this because I personally disgorged and recapped half of our UK allocation. Tart green apples, bitter nuts, fresh lime citrus. They're not looking for toasty richness, rather a driving, gastronomic sparkling. Stoked to have some, get some yourself.

wine: Weingut Peter-Jakob Kühn, Blanc de Blancs 2019
notes: Place: Rheingau, Germany Grape: Pinot Blanc + Auxerrois + Riesling Vibe: Stony Fresh yet creamy, this is primarily Pinot Blanc, given a generous time on the lees. Ripe orchard fruits shine alongside a delicate, fine bead of bubbles. It’s high time we gave Sekt the attention it truly deserves! Sekt is gettin' serious. ABV: 12.5%

10% DISCOUNT AUTO APPLIED AT CHECKOUT :) After spending eight years rubbing shoulders and making wine with none other than Frédéric Cossard, Maxime Crotet returned to his home village of Beaune in 2021 to begin his own journey. A couple of tricky vintages led him to source some négociant fruit, but he is now firmly back with his focus on Burgundy. Crotet leans towards a natural approach in the cellar, using zero additives unless absolutely necessary. Fermentations take place in small tanks before the wines are transferred to small, mostly neutral barrels for eight to ten months. The reds are f

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural , textural From two plots, half in Maranges, half in Remigny from 45 year old vines. Again, a similar vinification in the cellar to all the whites. A natural ferment before time in old oak. Terroir will always trump technique. This is all about minerality and citrus, showing the cool vintage wonderfully. Effortless. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural , textural Bourgogne Blanc has no right tasting this good. With fruit harvested in Pernand-Vergelesse, we fall into the more stone-fruited side of things, and all the better for it. A little almond and oatmeal play a subtle supporting role but never distracting from the drinkability. A steal all things considered. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Aligoté Vibe: Tangy Tangy, tangerine-leaning maceration. The colour is to die for. Copper-hued, almost ramato-esque. Texture to match, with just enough grip. Peach skin in both flavour and phenolics. Finally something skinsy with interest but still utterly drinkable. Bravo, Maxime! ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural , textural Finding a great white Burgundy that won’t break the bank isn’t always easy, but here we are! Especially, when it comes from a small plot worked without a tractor and painstakingly by hand alone. Maxime’s time with Cossard really shines through in this one. You get fresh, lively fruit with real verve, but a bit of time in old oak and some lees stirring gives it a smooth, rounded finish. Chalky and mineral, this punches well above its weight. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Aligoté Vibe: Natural , textural From a single parcel of Aligote planted in the 1940s in the village of Chassey le Camp just southeast of Santenay. It then ferments with native yeasts in larger barrels, with regular battonage throughout fermentation to keep the fine lees in suspension. Aged for 10 months in French oak with minimal sulfur added. With each passing vintage, Maxime seems to be honing his craft at an exceptional rate. This is taut and salivating. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal From 40-year-old vines in 1er cru la Fussiere. Yes, 1er at this price... Are we OK? A clear step up from the regional wines. Aromatically alluring with a heady nose of cranberry, pomegranate and spiced plum. The palate doubles down on this and is silky and persistent. ABV: 12%

wine: Maxime Crotet, Bourgogne Hautes Côtes VV 2024
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal The Hautes Côtes is definitely the place to be, both physically and metaphorically. Surrounded by forests and woodlands, it’s a refreshing detour from the monoculture of the more famous villages. Right from the start, this wine is perfumed and aromatic, and it’s got the structure to show that this is just the beginning. Ethereal Pinot at its very best. ABV: 12%

Place: Alcobaça, Portugal Grape: Castelao +Touriga Nacional Vibe: Juicy I’m really getting into Portuguese wines atm. They have so much depth and intrigue for such a good price. This is much lighter than you’d expect. It’s just a short maceration for a juicier, more jovial take on what could otherwise be something bulky. It needs a little time to open up, but once it does, you’re in for a cherry-laced dream. Would work equally well chilled or not. Dealers choice! ABV: 12.5%

Place: Alcobaça, Portugal Grape: Arinto + Fernao Pires Vibe: Saline I’m really getting into Portuguese whites. They have so much depth and intrigue for such a good price. Salty, refreshing, and with real character. The labels and prices are kind of cute too. Also something that’s rare these days. A new always in the fridge wine? I think so. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Rares Les Pièces comes from a tiny plot called L’Aubière, just 0.5 hectares in size. The east to west facing vineyard was planted in the 1970s on clay rich sands packed with fossils, which are cutely and informatively displayed on the label. This is only the second ever vintage. Fermentation takes place in barrel with indigenous yeasts, no fining or filtration and minimal sulphur. It then sees a decent stretch on the lees in bottle, followed by an even longer rest before disgorgement in November 2024. IFYKYK. ABV 12%

wine: Domaine des Fauvettes, De l'Aube à l'Aube
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Wow From young vines of Pinot Noir planted over pure limestone in Uchizy, facing east at around 300 metres above sea level. The grapes ferment as whole bunches for a month in cuve, left to infuse without pigeage or remontage, before being pressed to large foudres for a year of élevage. 2022 was a warm vintage and, even at this altitude, shows a denser, darker expression, with firm tannins and a touch of wood spice. This will reward a short snooze in the cellar. 2023 is a cracker. Nimble and radiating red fruit and spice wrapped around a mineral c

Place: Tuscany, Italy Grape: Tuscan Field Blend Vibe: Bright From the estate’s OG vineyard on clay and limestone. This comes from less than a hectare co-planted with over a dozen local varieties, from Sangiovese to Malvasia Nera. At its heart stands an ancient olive tree. Never sprayed, and now farmed biodynamically, this is a very special site indeed. Picked and pressed together, a field blend in its purest form. Bottled young for a vibrant, fragrant thing bursting with fresh fruit and herbs. Quite simply one of the most pleasurable bottles I have poured recently. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Tuscany, Italy Grape: Trebbiano, Vermentino and Malvasia Vibe: Textural I still remember the first time I drank this... In a gorgeous little trattoria tucked inside the walled town of Lucca. Good times. Tasting it again recently transported me straight back. Salty and herbal, with a bit of texture from a day on skins, it shows both grip and flesh without sacrificing freshness or drive in this cooling vintage. The Italians really have mastered the art of gastronomic whites. Brb, I'm off to the fishmonger. ABV: 12%
Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal Does it get much better? No, it doesn't. ABV: 13%

wine: Cecile Tremblay, Grand Cru 'Clos de Vougeot' 2023
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal Stupidly good, stupidly limited. Collectors item :) ABV: 14%
Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal One of the best-known Premier Crus of Chambolle. An excellent vintage. Oh, and Cecile Tremblays deft touch. What more could ya want? ABV: 14%

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Juicy Chardo of the highest order. Those in France might well be feeling a little nervous, and rightly so. This is flinty and reductive at first, before it unfurls into apple skin, orange zest and a gentle bready note from the lees. Two winters in barrel have harmonised what was a cracking yet powerful vintage in this neck of the woods. Burgundian comparisons are more than fair, but this also speaks very much of the Rhein. Check it out. 12% ABV

aromas: Red Apple, Peach, Cinnamon, Clove, Slate
notes: Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Juicy The intention here was always to focus on dry wines, but in 2024 some fruit from their famed “red slopes” was pre-harvested to capture the tension they were after in the cellar for the dry wines. From this, they made a one-off, off-dry bottling! 40g residual but far from cloying due to such wicked acid. The red clay slate soils of the Roter Hang again reveal the variety in a completely different light. This felt more powerful, full of juicy peach and red apple, with hints of cinnamon and clove that give big apple pie vibes. Oh, just 24 bo

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Herbal The intention here was always to focus on dry wines, but in 2024 some fruit from their famed “red slopes” was pre-harvested to capture the tension they were after in the cellar for the dry wines. From this, they made a one-off, off-dry bottling! 40g residual but far from cloying due to such wicked acid. The red clay and slate soils of the Roter Hang give the variety a completely different expression. Even the fruit seems to lean into red apple, alongside white florals, chamomile and a touch of celery salt. One of the most distinctive Kab

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Crispy From the southernmost part of the 'Red Slope' sheltered from the wind, matured in small wooden barrels. This is the textural side of Riesling. Round, juicy, with a beautifully soothing structure. 100% in 225L French oak! Flinty and slightly reductive at first, it opens beautifully into a medley of orchard fruit and electrifying minerality. Total 874 produceed. Rares! ABV: 12.5%

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Crispy These new single-site wines highlight the diversity of the complex soil structures in Rheinhessen. This particular vineyard sits on calcareous limestone south of Nierstein , and to me it feels the most linear of the lineup. Taut and tense rather than textured. It may be less flamboyant and overtly fragrant, but the ice-cool palate reveals refreshing layers of wet rock and river water. My personal favourite. ABV: 12%

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Crispy "Entry-level" gear from Kissinger. Entry-level my a**. Almost all the fruit sees stainless so it's very much that classic, crispy Rizza profile on the nose before an ultra clean palate. Lemons, limes, and pretty much any citrus you can think of. Sharp. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Cabernet Franc, Gamay, Grolleau Vibe: Classic A cooler site, late ripening, and with more clay-based soil. He wanted to create something a little fresher, a nod to the past traditions when clairret was the dominant style in Montreuil-Bellay. The label even shows his family on this site way back in 1947! Bit of history right there. Heavily inspired by Pataille's famous rose, this could equally be a Light red or Rose. You’re call really but depth of flavour is no issue here. Juicy fruit, a little herbal and a wickedly mineral core. ABV: 12%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Cabernet Franc Vibe: Classic This clos is tucked behind the walls of the Château de la Durandière, which belongs to Étienne’s family, and is bordered by the neighbouring forest. The vineyard is just one of only 20 hectares in Saumur sitting on Bathonian limestone from the Jurassic period, rather than the more typical tuffeau. It’s an early-ripening, well-draining site with limited vigor and active limestone. Étienne’s goal here is to make the most ethereal, elegant wine possible. Mission accomplished. The Clos Rougeard comparisons are accurate on the level of sheer

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Classic Pretty serious Chenin here. In fact, probably one of the most surprisingly delicious bottles I tasted on my recent trip to the Loire. I had no idea what to expect, but after doing some reading, it’s clear to see this is one producer you’ll want on the radar. Old vines bring depth and richness, while the cool vintage keeps things taut and racy. We're talking a tightrope balance between power and precision. A really beautifully put-together bottle that’s immediately delicious, but also has potential for the cellar. Off-the-charts good for a

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural If I see Dureuil Janthial, I buy Dureuil Janthial. Excellent value all things considered. The secret is well and truly out now, so you'll have to move fast. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural If I see Dureuil Janthial, I buy Dureuil Janthial. Flinty up front, followed by waves of toast and salted nuts. If you like Mersault but don't like the prices, then see here. ABV: 13.5%

wine: Thibaut Tassin, Soirée d'Hiver en Pays Aubois 2022
notes: Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Rares Sourced from Celles-sur-Ource and Essoyes in the Côte des Bar, Aube. A year in oak, then bottled on 7 August 2023 and aged under natural cork until disgorgement on 7 April 2025 with no dosage. Raw and racy from the start, yet it fleshes out beautifully. Even better on day two, the only problem is getting there. ABV 12%

Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Rares New kids on the grower Champagne block, Thibaut and Alizée craft seriously compelling gear from just 1.10 hectares in the Côte des Bar. Organically farmed, vinified in seasoned Burgundian barrels. Very tasty, very terroir-expressive. A cool, refreshing vintage. Just the two bottles up for grabs! ABV 12%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Poulsard Vibe: Lithe Seriously coveted bottling from one of the new up and comers in the Jura, who earned his stripes under a certain Stéphane Tissot. Heard of him? This is w ildy captivating, full of crushed berries, blood oranges and earth, with a touch of funk. '23 is a very classic vintage for these Jura reds, don't miss it. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Poulsard Vibe: Juicy Bright and juicy Poulsard from the latest winery whippin' up a Jurassic frenzy. Silky and soft with that airy texture the grape does so well. This is an excellent vintage for the grape. Serve chilled to be chilled. Reckon this is one of those Poulsards that can take a bit of age... ABV: 13%

Place: Rueda, Spain Grape: Verdejo Vibe: Salty The fruit comes entirely from the Vayuste site and follows the same vinification as the mono-parcel bottling. From there, it spends a year in old Sherry casks adding depth and complexity to an already hedonistic wine. Now subtle oxidative notes weave through those layers of citrus and salt. This feels more sapid, more savoury and more of an attack of raw nuts. Equally as good, equally as limited. The site really shines here. ABV:13.5%

wine: Didier Dagueneau, Les Jardins des Babylone 2015
notes: Place: Jurançon , France Grape: Petit Manseng Vibe: Vibes A wine that only starts to show it's best after 10 or so years, so we're on here. A flood of exotic fruit, mature truffles and enviable length. Still a baby but in great nick now. ABV: 9.5%

wine: Michel Autran, Vouvray Petillant Cap a l'Ouest 2021
notes: Place: Loire Valley, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Textural Michel Autran makes some seriously good Chenin, fizz included. Grapes were picked way back in 2021 but only disgorged in September 2025. We appreciate the dedication to the craft Michel. Chalky and saline, my mouth is watering as I type. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Khashmi, Kakheti, Georgia Grape: Kisi Vibe: Skinsy As trad as Georgian wine gets. Thick skinned Kisi gets a 5 day bath in its own skins in Qvevri. The fruit is all dried up, dried persimmons, dried apricot and almond skins, complexity at its finest. Big tannin, big acid, long finish. Everything about this is turned up to 11. ABV: 14%

Place: Khashmi, Kakheti, Georgia Grape: Saperavi Vibe: Big Saperavi done super well. Often over extracted and way too big, this is NOT one of those wines. 2-3 days on skins gives the wine the tannin it deserves. The nose on this wine blew me away, we're talking white chocolate, black cherries and blueberries. The finish goes on for days too. 14% ABV

Place: Khashmi, Kakheti, Georgia Grape: Kisi, Khikvi, Mtsvane, Rkatisiteli Vibe: Tropical A field blend of grapes I can't pronounce, but if there's one word I can pronounce, it's 'delicious'. A short 2 days on skins then a year in qvevri gives us notes of sweet melon, custard apples, almost something foam banana-y. Interesting AF. One of the most interesting wines I've had in a long time. ABV: 12%

Place: Khashmi, Kakheti, Georgia Grape: Rkatisiteli Vibe: Skinsy Proper 'amber' wine from Georgia but a lot more approchable than most. Rkatisiteli has 7 days of skins and then gets chucked into qvevri for a year to chill out. Super fresh acid but less fruit forward than you'd expect. We're more in the dried fruit, herbal territory, some notes of chamomile too. If your looking for something that'll be a bit more challenging, add this to your cart asap. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Kvareli, Georgia Grape: Kisi + Khikvi Vibe: Easy Super easy Georgian gear. Tannin is kept to a minimum for maximum chug-ability. Grapes are directly pressed into qvevri where ferments and ages for a year. Followed by a 3 month slumber in stainless to settle everything. Tinned pinapples and granny smith apples on both the nose and the palate. Georgian wine of the highest order. ABV: 13%

Place: Kvareli, Georgia Grape: Rkatisiteli + Vardisperi Vibe: Unusual Looks like a rose, drinks like a white? Super interesting stuff here. The Vardisperi used for this wine is a pink skinned mutation, which gives it that beautiful colour. 5-6 months on skins followed by 18 months of elevage, all in qvevri. Super complex on the nose, watermelon rind, bay leaves and rasberries. Amazing minerality on the palate with that classic dried fruit thing we know and love. Yummy. ABV: 13%

wine: Kevin Bouillet, Melon a Queue Rouge 2021
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Spicy Kevin is absolutely killin’ it. This is a thumping rendition of Melon, with spice and sea spray dominating among a plethora of stone fruit. With a little bit of age on it, this sits in a very dangerous drinking window. ABV: 13%

wine: Maison des Saules, Côtes du Jura Chardonnay 'Sous les Grands Prés' 2023
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Accomplished Damn, so stoked to make it a trio from Saules. This is my pick of the bunch. Not only do we have primo terroir from a steep, east-facing slope of pure Lias marls, but we also have 22 months with the wine left undisturbed in barrel. Harmony achieved. I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again, I’m so appreciative of young vignerons doing what’s best for the wine. The accountant might have other ideas, but time, although a costly expense, does wonders for wine. Breathtaking.

Place: Cahors, France Grape: Noual Vibe: Mind-Boggling I have never tasted Noual (assuming you're in the same boat) but I trust Calmette with my life. Ancestral fizz from a variety that they are pretty much single-handedly reviving. It's low in alcohol, but high on flavour. Subtly aromatic, clean and crispy. There's interest but drinkability. Long day at the office? See here for instant refreshment.

Place: Cahors, France Grape: Field Blend Vibe: Mind-Boggling Super unique. A field blend they planted of all their white grapes, mainly the hyper local Noual, macerated for a 3 days to give the wine a bit of texture rather than colour. After fermentation, they chuck the wine in 1000L Alsatian 'Foudre' where it takes a lil 2 year nap. During this time, it forms a little layer of flor. Subtle oxidation combined with yellow fruit and ginger spice. Akin to the finer Savagnins from the Jura. That, along with some incredible acid, do yourself a favour.

Place: Cahors, France Grape: Malbec Vibe: Bold Malbec planted on Kimmeridgian (what you'd find in Chablis) bedrock, which is super rare. It gives the wine a real mineral edge, keeping things focused on florals and spice rather than weight. The iron-rich red clay is so intense you can literally find rusty stones scattered through the vineyard. Fermented in concrete then aged for two years in a single old 1000L foudre. A more structured expression but still unlike any Malbec you've had, cause its actually delicious. Pre-aged too, ur welcome.

Place: Cahors, France Grape: Malbec Vibe: Unexpected Malbec planted on their highest plot (350m), expect freshness and acidity! Fermented in concrete eggs, chucked into oak afterwards to round out the tannin. Floral and spice-laden, which is what we expect from Malbec, but with an added freshness in the form of cherry-leaning fruit. One of those wines that really throws you off track, not at all what you'd expect from a Malbec from southern France.

wine: La Calmette, Serpent à Plumes Blanc 2024
notes: Place: Cahors, France Grape: Noual, Slyvaner, Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Vibe: Fresh Inspired by Maya’s time in Alsace, this blend delivers far more than you’d expect. Noual, one of Cahors’ indigenous white grape varieties, rescued from near extinction, is at the heart of this single vineyard. One of the few in the region to make whites, and one of the only with Noual, theres is no reference point here. Macerate some grapes, direct-press others, then blend until they see fit. Who's gonna tell them they're doing it wrong? Herbal notes alongside a tropical, pineapple thing. Rhône-esque but with mor

wine: Daniel Sage & Jordi Torgue, Fonte des Neiges 2023
notes: Place: Ardeche, France Grape: Merlot Vibe: Vibrant Bonkers and brilliant once again. Merlot isn’t inherently a bad grape. It’s just too often forced into being something it’s not. Here, it’s at its most drinkable. True to the house style, this flirts with volatility without overshadowing the fruit which is all blue and brambly. ABV: 14%

wine: Daniel Sage & Jordi Torgue, La Corne d'Impuissance 2022
notes: Place: Ardeche, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Vibrant Fruit from a friend in the Ardeche. Pure, unadulterated Gamay. a Sage masterclass. Wildly charming as per the house style. Softer, spiced southern fruit with herbal twang. Almost impossible to come across, stop reading, get buying. ABV: 13%

wine: Daniel Sage & Jordi Torgue, Prospérité de l'Entreprise 2022
notes: Place: Ardeche, France Grape: Merlot, Carignan Vibe: Vibrant Was served this blind last year, I was pleasantly surprised to find such a floral and fragrant expression when some one told me the varities. Of course, it had to be Sage. Insane. ABV: 12%

wine: Les Vins du Cabanon, Poudre d`Escampette 2021
notes: Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Carignan, Grenache Vibe: Soulful A soulful bottle from the late, great Alain Castex. Old vines rooted in sandy clay and gravel, vinified partly whole bunch and partly destemmed in concrete tank. A garage wine in the purest sense. This is an incredibly personal wine, what the French might call a vin d’émotion. The fruit is dark and brooding, yet so vibrant and full of life. Hard to put into words. Cellar it to allow the fruit to fully settle into itself. Or, if you’d prefer to honour Alain now, it is best shared and savoured in one sitting. Liquid history. ABV:

wine: Rouges Queues, Santenay Blanc 'Saint Jean de Narosse' 2020
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Saline Tasted this earlier in the week with absolutely no intention of buying more White Burgundy. Oops. It was simply too good to ignore. After being held back for a few years, it’s evolved in bottle into something genuinely otherworldly. Savoury, saline and nutty, it’s shed all its baby fat and is drinking right at its peak. Trust me. This is a producer you’ll want to get acquainted with. ABV:13%

wine: Novice, Le Jus de la Folie 2024 250ml
notes: Place: Grapes from Beaujolais, Vinified in Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Fizzy + Fun Don't want to commit to a whole bottle? Got you sorted. Not only does Yves make some of my favourite wines, he is also kind enough to can a portion of his production for when only a glass is required. This is fresh, fun and frothy. Expect plenty of orchard fruit and a subtle, creamy texture. Train journey's never looked so good. ABV: 12%

Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Classic, Crispy Golden in the glass, this feels like the most tropical and petrol laced of the bunch. It sounds weird, but if you’re accustomed to high grade Riesling, you’ll get the gist. As with all these wines, there’s a lot to unpack, so take your time and enjoy the ride. ABV: 13%

Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Classic, Crispy Delicious right now, all youthful and yeasty, but this feels like a wine built for the ages. The blue slate brings minerality and drive, while also hinting at a more herbal and floral future. Give it a bit of air if you’re impatient (like me) and you’ll see pine needles and sapid, savoury notes start to emerge. ABV: 13%

Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Classic, Crispy Crazy how good this is, especially considering we’re only at the starting point of the range. From 50+ year old vines on grey and blue slate, aged for 10 months on lees in large foudres, everything here is done with real intent. Lean and refreshing, and if any residual remains, it’s completely undetectable. Perfectly balanced and totally effortless. ABV: 13%

Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Classic, Crispy Upper echelon Riesling. Textural and weighty, almost Burgundian in shape, before that piercing Mosel freshness cleans everything up. Drinking dreamily right now, but it could easily live forever. A true phenolic masterclass. ABV: 13%

Place: Penedes, Spain Grape: Xarel-Lo + Moscatel de Alejandria (Muscat) Vibe: Pet-Nat + Friends A thumpin' Pet-Nat that's equal parts classy, equal parts fun. Lucy's managed to achieve perfect harmony here, the citrus and salinity from Xarel-lo meeting faint aromatics from the Muscat. A match made in heaven. Rarely does one see ancestral fizz looking so good at this price. Picnic please. ABV: 11%

wine: Timothee Stroebel, Pour Toi Brut Nature NV
notes: Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Meunier + Pinot Noir + Chardonnay Vibe: Elite More generously textured, a little more oxidative but driven by a great acid line. A sibling to Triptyque in terms of site and soil, but Meunier gives colour and fully dominates the palate. No bad thing. Red apple skin bitters and spice shine above a subtle fizz. With air this becomes something to behold. ABV: 12%

wine: Timothee Stroebel, Triptyque Brut Nature NV
notes: Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Meunier + Pinot Noir + Chardonnay Vibe: Elite The three main Champagne varieties from 2018 and 2019. A blend of the diverse soil types he works with and, as always, aged in large oak. This is the house style in a nutshell. Lightly oxidative, gently savoury, a touch salty with fruit that leans peach and pear. Do not miss this. ABV: 12%
Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Sangiovese + Ciliegiolo Vibe: Pet Nat + Friends Bone dry, bright and crunchy! How good is a fizzy red? Thirst-quenching refreshment taken to whole new heights. ABV: 11.5%

wine: Maison Skyaasen, Bourgogne Côte d'Or Rouge 2024
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural, fresher Most of the fruit comes from within Volnay. Here the light clay-limestone soils help produce elegant wines with supple, silky tannin. Fresh-fruited at first, then slowly evolving through the full Pinot spectrum. Every vintage feels more refined than the last. Here for it. ABV: 12%

wine: Conestabile della Staffa, Gimo Rosso NV
notes: Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Merlot + Aleatico Vibe: Tasty Lighter than you'd expect and something that would suit a little chill, if you're that way inclined. Super juicy and the Aleatico brings in a lovely little floral element. Call your local pizza joint now, this is another no-brainer. ABV: 12%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural, lighter Love Chiroubles, love the Metras fam, love Beaujolais in 2023. This quite literally ticks all the boxes. Jules is now bottling under his own name, and this cuvée comes from an older vine parcel in one of my favourite crus, closer to the “green” side of Beaujolais. This cooler pocket of the region is so steep they have to use a cable-powered plough. Tough. Anyway, the word ethereal comes to mind when drinking this. Clearly, something very special runs in the family blood. ABV: 13%

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Pinot Noir + Gamay Vibe: Fun A delightful blend made from fruit sourced from friends. This is a lovely snapshot of the volcanic joy of the Auvergne, brimming with bright fruit and subtle hints of earth and iron. If you want short-term pleasure, look no further. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Textural I have vivid memories of tasting this at a Salon earlier in the year. After copious amounts of Burgundian Chardonnay, this felt like a real change of pace. There was something so exhilarating about it that it stood out among some seriously impressive peers. “Energy” is a word that gets thrown around a lot, and I’m very guilty of that, but this really encapsulates what I mean. The flavour profile here is fairly traditional for Chardonnay: orchard fruit, creamy texture, and subtle warming spice. However, there’s a tension and drive that ma

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Spicy and Seductive Auvergnat Pinot from a vineyard at 550m above sea level, on complex soils of shale, marl, and limestone. This was a warmer vintage, but we still have loads of volcanic freshness. Iron-rich strawberry fruit with plenty of spice. Schenanun-like in its addictive nature. This is going to age like a beauty. ABV: 13%

Place: Štajerska, Slovenia Grape: Furmint Vibe: Steely Furmint from the ridiculously steep slopes of Slovenian Styria. This vineyard is literally an amphitheatre of terraced vines. It’s insane, look at the label to get an idea. The acidity, as you’d expect from the variety, is off the charts. There’s also a flinty reduction that opens into ripe fruit, pastry, and spice. A lot is going on here, in the best possible sense. Zero adds. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Rhone, France Grape: Muscat , Vibe: Fun The Legendary Eric Texier's son Martin is now doing his own thing down in the Rhone. Tasting this for the first time caught me off guard. Who’d have thought a Muscat-y Pet-Nat could be so refreshing? None of the overtly floral thing here. This was subtle but slicing, thanks to a short time in steel before refermenting in bottle. Apple and elderflower remind me that spring is just around the corner. ABV: 10%

wine: Vin de LaGamba, Blanc de Noir 2021
notes: Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Classy Not just a master of fun fizz, Alanna can also craft refined bubbles just as good as those in Champagne. Seriously, if this were poured for me in Reims, there’s no way I’d guess it was from Rheinhessen. Direct-pressed Pinot aged in barrel, then refermented with juice from the following harvest, before 30 months on lees and disgorged in 2025. Toasty and moreish, with plenty of orchard crunch. Classy yet fun, this can do it all. ABV: 12%

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Pinot Blanc, Riesling Vibe: Classy The pinnacle of Alanna’s fizz. Please don’t be fooled by the tongue-in-cheek label, this is some serious Sekt! Time has rendered a savoury and complex bottling with a finish that seemingly never ends. This is autolytic, creamy, and layered with a Germanic acid line slicing through. Champagne move over. ABV: 11%

Place: Badacsony, Hungary Grape: Kekfrankos Vibe: Natural, Fresh, Fun AKA Blaufrankisch. If you're familiar with Bencze, you’ll know he leans into acidity, minerality, and drinkability. Young vines from three carefully selected clones double down on the house style. Youthful vigour makes this lithe and lifted despite it's blue fruited spicy nature. Can't wait to go on a journey with this vineyard. ABV:11%

wine: Conestabile della Staffa, Gimo Bianco NV
notes: Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Grechetto Vibe: Tasty Ripasso method skinsy, with 2022 juice reinvigorated by 2023 skins. Fruit and spice in all the right places. There's generosity to the aroma and favour, with just enough tannin and acidity to keep things moving nicely. No brainer. ABV: 12%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Grechetto Vibe: Yummy Sublime! Plenty to like here and plenty going on, particularly at the price point. Honeyed, almost golden in the glass, there's a tonne of citrus leaf and mandarin flavour, humming alongside some almond nutty stuff. As with the Trebb, it's salty and refreshing to boot. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano Vibe: Yummy Good old Trebbiano d'Abruzzo on show here, with old vine fruit direct pressed into fibreglass. Classic done the Staffa way, it's floral and faintly honeyed at first, opening up in the glass nicely. There's salinity and freshness too. Just delicious, easy drinking from a wonderful source. ABV: 12%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Aleatico Vibe: Crunchy I tasted this in the Staffa cellars in the evening after picking the same vineyard, and having retasted I can confirm that my initial suspicions were correct, this is a banger. A journey to the Mediterranean via Umbria, with plenty of tapenade and coastal feel allied with a bit of mountain and valley freshness. Sign me up. ABV: 12%

Place: Piedmont, Italy Grape: Nebbiolo Vibe: Classico One of the most ethereal Nebbs I've had the pleasure to taste. Explosive with florals, fruit, and tar. This is singing already, nuanced and approachable. However, this is clearly just the beginning... The upside potential for this is endless..

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano Vibe: Vibey Pecorone means big sheep. Big sheep vibes here. A wine of contrast, luscious and deep on the nose, yet peppery, herbal and lithe on the palate. Trebbiano spent 7 days on the skins so you get some nice tannic presence, but plenty of freshness alongside. A great new addition to the range. ABV: 11%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Ciliegolo Vibe: Bright A new bottling from Gio in 2024, it was originally destined to be the base wine for the Ciliegiozzo fizz, but needs must and we instead have a vibrant, crunchy still red. A short maceration with no stems, this is all about the wild strawberry, watermelon and alpine herbal spicey stuff. I had this in situ with house-cured salumi, a combination I still dream about and can heartily recommend. ABV: 12%

Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Generous The FF range consists of rarities from the Dufour cellar, released every three years. They offer a snapshot of Françoise’s personal drinking preferences. She’s got good taste. Ultra-vinous, lower pressure, and complexity off the charts. Fermented in oak, bottled in October 2011, and disgorged in December 2022 with no dosage. The wine then takes one final rest under cork before being deemed worthy of release in 2025. Fifteen years of patience and graft. Umami-laden and veering into slightly oxy territory. Don’t treat this like any other

Place: Beaujolais , France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural, lighter The iconic Lapierre Morgon really needs no introduction. But this bottling is made without any SO₂. Curious to see what difference a tiny splash of sulphur can make? Grab the pair, take some notes, and let me know which one you prefer. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Domaine Marcel Lapierre, Morgon 'Cuvée Marcel Lapierre' 2024
notes: Place: Beaujolais , France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural, lighter Named after the one and only. Marcel is the top top wine from an estate that only makes top wine. Proper vin de garde, so it gets a bit more barrel time to soften out those edges. It’s obviously delicious right now, but it could really go the distance if you’re that way inclined. Beyond rare. ABV: 14.5%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Textural Tiny production here, even by Manuel's standards with a measly 2 barrels produced. 24 months in old barrel, in a distinctly delicious departure from his house style. ABV: 13%

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: Grillo Vibe: Salty Grillo from the coastal plains of Marsala. Can think of worse places to be a grape. 2/3 is direct pressed to old oak for fermentation, with the remainder macerating on skins for about a week before going into fibreglass. A ripper. Textural in the right areas, moreish in its salinity and pure in its vibrant, sun kissed fruit profile. Drinkability that is unmatched. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: Nero d’Avola, Frappato Vibe: Vibey This is effectively Cerasuolo di Vittoria, the top appellation in these parts, but not labelled as such as they don't bother. If only. Co-ferment of 70% Nero d'Avola and 30% Frappato gets done rapidly, which is good when working with zero adds, before blending and settling in old tonneau and fibreglass. Ultra fragrant and alluring, perfume is no issue with these Kalma wines. There's some fruit weight and palate density, as you'd expect, but it never gets tiring or hard work. Basically a dream. ABV: 12%

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: Frappato, Nero d’Avola, Merlot, Albanello Vibe: Ethereal Tastes and drinks like what and how I'd like to make wine. Everything is picked and dealt with separately, macerating and fermenting as whole bunches before blending. Super light, almost like a darker pink wine in the glass, but flavour and intensity abound. A miraculous and tonic like thing to consume. No adds, no problemo. ABV: 11%

Place: Kent, England Grape: Pinot Meunier Vibe: Flat Champers Deft touch as per, all Meunier for the first time. Dark-toned due to a relatively warm vintage, well warm for England. Picked last for ripeness, de-stemmed and foot-crushed before a three-week maceration. Aged in barrel for 8 months before bottling via gravity with no additions. Something between an English Tavel and what Prévost might produce if he made a Coteaux wine. Maybe? I’m a bit biased when it comes to the wines of Ham Street, but you’d be too if you’ve walked these vines. There is something special about them, no doubt due

Place: Kent, England Grape: Pinot Gris Vibe: Energetic From that cool, wet vintage if you remember that miserable summer a few years back? From a small section of vines rooted in a seam of chalk. Hand de-stemmed and foot-crushed, it’s fermented in stainless steel, with just a short time on skins this time around, giving an even more mineral-driven expression. I really love these wines: full of energy, delicate yet demanding your full attention. Only 240 bottles made,UK rares! ABV: 9.5%

Place: Kent, England Grape: Pinot Gris Vibe: Energetic Whilst preferring to work with her own fruit, small yields can make it hard to say no when a bit of exceptional fruit comes your way. Especially when the quality’s this good. Two parts Gris, one part Noir. De-stemmed with a short maceration before heading to stainless. This Pinot clone differs from Sophie’s; its looser bunches give a more easygoing, joyfully fruited expression. The ultimate blouge. Refreshment in spades, with fine detail running throughout. Without a doubt, some of my favourite wines from the UK, if not the world. ABV: 10%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Pineau d'Aunis Vibe: Classic, richer Unicorn level Robinot. Hailing from an iconic, centurion vineyard we're well and truly in vin de garde territory. Coupled with a blockbuster vintage and we're looking at liquid history. Stupid limited. You simply won't find a better expression of the grape. ABV: 13%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Ploussard Vibe: Mineral Directly pressed Ploussard. Is it a rosé? Not quite sure. Ploussard’s thin skins push this into the lighter, skinsy side of things. Is it delicious? Absolutely. Probably my favourite from Yves to date. All red apple skin bitters, spice, and that signature electric energy. ABV:11.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Cabernet Franc Vibe: Natural Crunchy! How good is Cab Franc? A bit of whole bunch and some destemmed fruit for balance. This vintage carries a touch more weight than some of the more easygoing Bobinet bottlings, yet it maintains that signature high drinkability. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Rueda, Spain Grape: Verdejo Vibe: Hectic Esmerleda makes four single-plot wines, this being the most powerful and intense. This site sits at a higher altitude in a sun-drenched, plateau-shaped with distinctive gravelly soils. Short maceration, vertical press before 6 months on fine lees in 500-litre clay vessels. Everything here is dialled up: concentration, texture, and drive. Yet it retains its aromatic lift, with a chalky, mineral core. Salvating rn. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Rueda, Spain Grape: Verdejo Vibe: Elegant Esmerelda makes four single-plot wines. This is the most elegant of the quartet. Sourced from a slightly lower-altitude site nestled between the river and a forest of pine trees, the vineyard sits on beach-like fine sands formed from ancient marine fossilisation. The winemaking mirrors that of the other plots: short maceration, vertical press, then ageing in 500-litre clay vessels. But here, the tension is remarkable, almost electric. The palate remains creamy, chalky, and it all leads into a finish of sea salt, wild herbs, and citrus peel. This

Place: Rueda, Spain Grape: Verdejo Vibe: Salty The fruit comes entirely from the El Carrascal site and follows the same vinification as the mono-parcel bottling. From there, it spends a year in old Sherry casks adding depth and complexity to an already hedonistic wine. Now subtle oxidative notes weave through those layers of citrus and salt. One of the most compelling, thought-provoking wines I’ve tasted. Just when you think you’ve seen it all, wine reminds you there is always more to discover. It really is the gift that keeps on giving. ABV:13.5%

Place: Rueda, Spain Grape: Verdejo Vibe: Hectic Calling this merely a “village” or “entry-level” wine does a disservice to the exceptional quality on show. A blend of the four sites, it’s the perfect intro to the hectic world of pre-phylloxera Verdejo. Vinified in steel, so it’s a bit fresher and more fragrant. Still full of golden fruit and waxy texture, with plenty of herbs and that signature mineral streak. How things only go up from here is beyond me. A must taste. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Regent + Pinot Gris + Riesling Vibe: Fun Lingonberry laced, frothy red that is about as much fun as you can physically cram into a 750ml bottle. Enough depth if you wanted to have this on the dinner table but with enough freshness that it's sitting straight on the sofa with me. Lambrusco but like better? ABV: 9.5%

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: Frappato Vibe: Juicy Frappato has been a longtime favourite on our shelves. So it’s no surprise that Kalma, alumni of both the Occhipinti and COS cellars, has delivered a sure-fire hit with their. This is the grape at its fragrant best. Wild strawberries, rosehips and an unmistakable Sicilian minerality. Chill it down, and the bottle will be gone in a flash. I know that all too well from experience. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Malbec Vibe: Tasty Ok, you've got me. Yes, Côt is actually Malbec. Fear not, this is actually good! Very good. It's not overworked, over-extracted or over the top. You see in the Loire freshness is the name of the game. They managed to show the grape at its most vibrant. Juicy blackberry fruit, smooth tannin, bright acidity. There is a whole lot to like here. Straight into my midweek rotation. ABV: 13%
Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Fresh but oxy Suitably complex, as you'd expect. 8 years in barrel, no messing. ABV: 15.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Tasty Ouille Chard from 2020 flirting with a bit of mealy oxidation. Lots of yellow stone fruit and plenty of acidity to keep things flowin'. This bottling is a personal favourite, one that I sadly rarely get to drink these days . ABV: 14%

wine: Tony Bornard, Chardonnay 'Au Fil des Générations' 2021
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Iconic A response to a horrendous vintages lost largely to frost. Very limited. Hopefully never again.
Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Tasty Lightly oxy, this is all that saline, marzipan, raw nutty stuff that we keep coming back for. Somebody stop me. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Emilia-Romagna, Italy Grape: Pignoletto + Albana + Trebbiano Vibe: Pét Nat + Friends Crisp, dry and callin' out for a good hunk of salumi. How good is Italian Col Fondo? Hard not to like this with all its crunchy, golden fruit and fine bubbles. Apero time is now. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Meunier Vibe: Classic So into this. 95% Pinot Meunier from 45-year-old vines. Indigenous ferment, 36 months on lees, and all from a perpetual reserve dating back from 2011 to 2020. Unfined, unfiltered, unsulphured too. Just a tiny dosage to add a little weight. After reading all that you probably think this is gonna be spenny. Oh how wrong could you be! This is officially the cheapest Champagne on the shelves. Maybe there is a god after all. ABV: 12.5%

wine: ...Dan's presents: The Full English – An End of Harvest Party
notes: Time for another party I reckon – what u sayin?? To celebrate the end of harvest in England, we're throwing a little soirée and bringing together some of the most exciting names in English wine for a good old piss up – introducing, the Full English. We might not have sausages, but by god have we got bangers. We'll be pouring a range of wines from across this country we call home, along with a few surprise bottles from further afield, and we'll even be joined by some of the winemakers themselves to celebrate the end of the 2025 vintage. Your ticket gets you in the door for *all u can taste* of

Place: Loire, France Grape: Grolleau Vibe: Elite Top Grolleau showing us that the grape can achieve greatness when treated with intention and care in the cellar. Cruchiest of the range with just enough wild barrel spice. There is a little brett that for once actually adds complexity rather than turning things feral. This next to a roaring fire will take some beating. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Cabernet Franc Vibe: Elite The soils here are dark, coal-black and brooding, just like the wine. Wild florals, truffle, and forest floor for days. 24 months in barrique, then 3 in bottle, so we're coming into a sweet spot for optimal autumn drinking. Intoxicating stuff. Sadly, our allocation was just a pair... Be quick. ABV: 13%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Cabernet Franc Vibe: Elite The fresher side of the Franc offering. Don’t mistake that for lightness though as this is from pristine, 70-year-old vines on top Anjou Noir terroir. Serious stuff. Black cherry, a touch of graphite, and lots of herbs. Drinking like an absolute dream. ABV: 13%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Textural and Racy 1.4 hectares of slate and quartz soils! This is serious Chenin. Aromatically powerful, with quince drifting into the tropical territory. We've got a juicy mid-palate and layers of honey and minerality coming through on a finish that seemingly never ends. A touch of oak plays a supporting role without distraction from the fruit, while a bright vein of acidity keeps us comin' back for more. Entering a sweet spot now but with massive upward potential. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot Gris Vibe: Textural Pinot Gris done very very well. Fruit from the south and east side of Schoenenbourg Grand Cru, declassifed. Toffee apples, lemon and dried herbs. Rounded and dense on the palate with softer, but pleasing acidity. A crowd-pleaser, even the in-laws will be happy. ABV: 12%

wine: Hunter McKirdy, Les Champs Des Fleurs 2024
notes: Place: Alsace, France Grape: Riesling Vibe: Stunning 100% Riesling from their last plot to ripen and the first time they’ve made this cuvée. In 2023, they lost most of the fruit and had to blend what was left. Thankfully, they managed to bottle it this year. Red apple skins on the nose with that classic Riesling lemon balm thing. The acid is incredible. Linear, sharp, wakes you up a bit. Absolutely incredible gear. ABV: 12%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Auxerrois Vibe: Precise This absolutely floored me. I never knew this humble grape could reach such lofty heights. Flinty and crystalline on opening, before waves of freshly squeezed lemon and wonderfully woven herbal bitters. The perfect palate cleanser for some of that hearty Alsatian fare. My wallet is in big trouble... ABV: 11.5%

Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Flinty Considering this is just the estate Riesling, they've truly outdone themselves. Painstakingly slow, cool ferments and extended time in barrel have given us a strikingly pure expression of site and grape. There's a smoky, sesame-like reduction, almost Styrian in feel, before the full Riesling spectrum takes centre stage. Think wet stones and slate. Yes, “minerality” is overused… but please, just see here. ABV: 11%

Place: Burgenland, Austria Grape: Austrian Blend Vibe: Tropical Can't go wrong with a Burgenland blend that sees time on skins. Tropical fruit for days! Nothing too crazy on the texture front either. Easy as. ABV: 11%

wine: La Ferme de Sato, 'Pinot Noir' Sur les Nuages 2022
notes: Place: Central Otago, New Zealand Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elite The team at Sato really don’t miss or mess around. This is top-quality Pinot, no two ways about it. There’s an old-world edge that’ll please fans of top-shelf Burgundy, and a price point that will please the wallet. This has all the hallmarks of exceptional vino. Biodynamic farming, low intervention in the cellar, pure class in the glass. ABV: 13%

wine: La Ferme de Sato, Chardonnay 'Le Chant du Vent' 2020
notes: Place: Central Otago, New Zealand Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Amazing One of the better Chardonnays I’ve tasted this year. From the first sip, it just smells expensive. Rich, yet chiselled ya know? This comes from the Mendoza clone AKA Gingin. Probably doesn’t mean much to the average punter, but for the super nerdy, it’s a cool little fact. Think croissant and baked bread, with a savoury depth thanks to a long, slow basket press (the only one in Central Otago, btw). Just a dash of sulphur at bottling. Coming into a real sweet spot... Stock up. ABV: 14.5%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Bright Blewitt Springs and Grenache!!! The formidable duo bringing out another beltin' expression of grape and place. Elegant nose with plenty of herbal character before a generous palate full of juicy, red fruit. Tannins are pure velvet. ABV: 13.7%

Place: Eden Valley, South Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Savoury White pepper spice and savoury fruit dominate here. Silky, long, and never-ending. Originally planted in 1857, and it sits at a cool 390 meters of altitude. This site is special. Remote and rugged, it has produced an equally special wine . ABV: 13.6%

Place: Gundagai, NSW Grape: Big Blend Vibe: Layered and Interesting A special blend of no less than 12 varieties from the 2023 vintage, combining elements from our reds, rosés, and orange wines. Originally born from bottling leftover wine that didn't fit into other batches, now a purposeful blend created from selected wines and lees from across the vintage. A fun, juicy celebration of the year that was. Lucky us. ABV: 12.8%

Place: Gundagai, NSW Grape: Sangiovese, Barbera, and Nero d’Avola Vibe: Highly Chillable A mostly carbonic ferment gives us this lithe and springy chillable red that is screaming out for pizza. It's like an Aussie-Greek take on Beaujolais, which is as good as it sounds. Cranberry and raspberry fruited with a ultra light dusting of tannin to hold it's shape. ABV: 12.8%

Place: Gundagai, NSW Grape: Fiano Vibe: Glutinous Fiano given a long 6 month infusion bath on its skins. The result is all gentle grip and sunny citrus, like mandarins, apricots and orange blossom wrapped up in an easy flow. ABV: 13.4%

Place: Riverland, SA Grape: Zibibbo and Vermentino Vibe: Super Vibey Sunshine in a bottle, but in the least derogatory way possible. A wine to make you dream of warmer places by the sea. Juicy but balanced, there's a lot to like with it's exuberant fruit profile and subtle spice keeping things moreish. ABV: 11%

Place: Riverland, SA Grape: Zibibbo Vibe: Spicy An Australian-Greek homage to the Retsina wines of Greece, just better? An aromatic orange wine infused with Aleppo pine resin. All aboard the spice train here, pepper, ginger and tonic like bitters combine with vibrant Muscat driven fruit. Endless summer vibes. ABV: 10.9%

Place: Gundagai, NSW Grape: Fiano Vibe: Bright and Tasty Kind of macerated, kind of not? This is a take on the traditional white production style of the Med, where a bit of skin contact is normal and they don't mind texture. That, mixed in with plenty of zip gives us this ultimate crisp white/easy skinsy colab full of tropical fruits and pithy grip. You needn't bother to keep the cork, this is a session bottle if we ever saw one.

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Shiraz Vibe: Fun Mauricio started winning awards for Syrah under his other label, Seven Eves, so they figured some of the fruit should head to the Somos range. You are the winner. Just medium, it's perky, spicy and fresh, coupled with ample darker fruits. Super tasty. ABV: 14.7%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Mencia Vibe: Floral A lovely bunchy expression of Mencia that has no right tasting this good. Sweet berries and herbs, if you wanna go looking for them. Effortless consumption. ABV: 12.1%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache, Nero d'Avola Vibe: Smashable This kind of rosé doesn't stand a chance around me, it's got a lifespan of about half an hour once it's open. Unparalleled juicy deliciousness, with strawberries, raspberries and florals bursting out the glass, tempered by citrusy freshness. Make some room in your fridge for this one. ABV: 12.9%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Verdelho, Viognier Vibe: Thirst Quenching Some orange wines are meant to be swirled, contemplated, discussed for hours. And some are just meant to be drunk. Guess which one this is? Half the fruit went to barrel for some quality time on the lees, the other half was left on skins for six months to draw out some tart, gingery spice. The aromatics here are all orange blossom and herbs, while the flavours tend towards mandarins and a slight bitter edge reminiscent of Campari. Proper interesting while still being proper drinkable. Proper good, basically. ABV:

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Fiano, Vedelho and Muscat Vibe: Easy to Like They wanted to make something fresh and fun for summertime drinking. Mission accomplished, with the added bonus that it's actually interesting. ABV: 12.9%

wine: Flavien Nowack, S.A "Brut Sans Année" (base 2021) NV
notes: Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Meunier + Chardonnay Vibe: Elite A star of the new grower Champagne Renaissance! While the rest of the range is tightly allocated, this is a good way to get acquainted with the house style. Fruit comes from Vandières in the Vallée de la Marne, grown on limestone sands over (you guessed it) marne. lavien ages the base wine under cork, something usually reserved for post-second ferment. Most fizz starts life under a crown cap, which doesn’t do much for flavour development, but here the wine is treated with real intention from the start. Chalky, vinous, rich,

Place: Loire, France Grape: Grolleau Vibe: Chillable, lighter The clue’s in the name. This short and sweet maceration of Grolleau brings out the grape’s juiciest, most playful side. Crown capped for convenience, and landed just in time for the summer sun. Go nuts. ABV: 10%

wine: Julie & Toby Bainbridge, Pas de Bourée 2024
notes: Place: Loire, France Grape: Grolleau Gris Vibe: Fresher Direct press Grolleau Gris for a citrus sensation! Young vine energy for a bottle that will be gone in seconds. Just enough florals, just enough fruit, plenty of mineral drive. Don't overthink it, just enjoy it. ABV: 9.5%

A BIG ONE! Alexandre Bain is a name well known in Pouilly-Fumé as one of the leading biodynamic producers in the region, although you won’t see the appellation on the label. Popular with sommeliers and lovers of a ‘cult winemaker’, Alexandre Bain is fanatical about terroir. Each of his single vineyard wines are reflective of the soil type, and are not only fermented differently, but aged differently, to protect the singular identity of that cuvée. We're big fans, and can't wait to welcome Alex to London in October. Spaces for this are limited to 16, so if you like cult wines, get clicking. Not

wine: Giuseppe Mascarello e Figlio, Barolo Monprivato 2007
notes: Place: Piemonte, Italy Grape: Nebbiolo Vibe: Cuddly Mascarello is a name that might be familiar, if you're of the Piemonte persuasion. Here’s a Barolo that, for once, is available right in its sweet spot. Dried roses, tar, sandalwood. Pretty much every textbook Nebbiolo note is on full display. Give it time to evolve. It’s both weightless and lingering on the palate. Go hard or go home. ABV: 14.5%

wine: Domaine de la Loue, Vin de Liquer NV
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Sweet How good is Macvin? Sorry, this isn’t technically Macvin… but like, it kind of is. The sugary, unfermented must from some Savagnin is blended with barrel-aged marc. Then it gets whacked into another barrel for four more years to mellow out. Just wow. Caramelised and candy-like, but with a natural acidity that makes this such a compelling way to end any meal. Rum raisin and salted caramel vibes. Treat yourself. You deserve it. ABV: 18%

wine: Domaine de la Loue, Vin Jaune 2017
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Oxy Fruit from the south-east facing Sous La Roche. Pretty cool lieu-dit! Plenty of unicorns have come from these special soils... this might be another. One large barrel, six years of patience. The result? Dried fruit, salted nuts, and so much spice. Chiseled and salivating. I’m seriously impressed with the '17 yellow wines I’ve tasted. For those who say you can’t taste terroir or vintage in oxidative wines, I implore you to give this a go. Breathtaking. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Domaine de la Loue, La Brute 2023
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Juicy Mineral-driven mille-feuille Pinot. Mille-feuille? Isn’t that a dessert? Yes, but also a cool winemaking trick that’s having a bit of a moment right now. The fruit was macerated for six weeks in alternating layers of destemmed and whole bunches, a bit like the layers in your pudding. In layman’s terms, this brings out a fresher side of the grape and some wonderful aromatics. Delicate tannins, subtle spice, usual suspects. Jura reds in 2023 can do no wrong. ABV: 13%

wine: Domaine de la Loue, Cuvée Raphaelle 2022
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Salty Serious skinsy business. Slowly but surely, I’ve become fully converted to macerations of Savagnin. Those exotic yellow fruits get dialled right up, and the texture goes all lovely and pithy. Marmalade and burnt sugar bitters dance beautifully on the back palate, while a streak of salinity runs straight through. A whisper of VA just lifts everything perfectly. Dangerous on its own, but the gastronomic potential here is next level. ABV: 12%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Trousseau Vibe: Juicy Singing straight out the gate, super stable and so seductive. This is straddling the perfect Trousseau middle ground. It's not too pale yet, nor is it too extracted and muddy. Just perfect. It's so easy to get lost in those pretty florals, but things get better with a silky smooth texture that makes this glide. First Trousseau in quite a while that has sent shivers down my spine. Sheesh. ABV: 12%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural, lighter The final press, this time from a cooler vintage. It strikes a gorgeous balance between structure and freshness. Easily my favourite of the bunch and, of course with my luck, the most limited. Pouring a vibrant ruby, bursting with juicy red fruit and that unmistakable mineral core only Gamay on granite can deliver. ABV: 13%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural, lighter Proper paysan vigneron doing wonders without all the modern gimmicks. Patience is always the final pressing, and as such, the most structured and dense. Whilst the warm vintage brings a brooding expression that really tastes of its granitic roots, this still has that unmistakable Ducroux drinkability. ABV: 13%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural, lighter 2024 was a difficult year. They lost a lot of grapes and, as such, only bottled one wine. As ever though, they've managed to capture the wild beauty of the Beaujolais, even despite the tricky circumstances. Luminous and laden with minerals, this is about as invigorating as it gets. ABV: 12%

Place: Rhône, France Grape: Syrah Vibe: Peppered Perfectly poised between freshness and flavour. Extraction here is all whole bunch and gentle, coaxing out silky-smooth tannins that frame the peppered, herb-leaning fruit beautifully. Aged in amphora to let the wine sing, with no oak to weigh it down. New wave St-Jo is everything I want to drink this autumn. Do the thing. ABV: 12.8%

Place: Rhône, France Grape: Syrah Vibe: Pretty Really into Syrah when it gets a direct press. You get that glorious wild strawberry thing, plus a stunning herbal profile often missing from the paler pinks further south. Add a splash of carbonic Cinsault and suddenly you’ve got raspberries and roses in the mixer. Amphora aging, Hugo’s calling card, brings a gentle, earthy edge that sees us off into the sweetest of sunsets. Darker than most, this is comfortably in the light red zone. ABV: 12.7%

wine: Hugo Vercasson, Face à Pierre Blanche 2023
notes: Place: Rhône, France Grape: Marsanne + Viogner Vibe: Floral + Textured Two varieties that usually get me sweatin’ and not in a good way. But when they’re done right, the result can be something breathtaking. Case in point: this. Textured and round, with all the stone-fruited florals you'd expect. But what really sets it apart is a vibrant acidity and this almost Chenin-esque lanolin note that drives down the palate. Something that’s usually flabby and flamboyant is suddenly utterly drinkable. Can’t get over how good this is. Bravo, Hugo! No surprise he spent time with the master of Rhône white

wine: Julie Balagny, Minouche 2022 FLEURIE MAGIC PACK
notes: Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Elite Minouche was still in barrel at the time of the tragic passing of Julie. Uncertain about the future of the estate, the wine remained untouched until the following July, before being bottled by her longtime right-hand man, Brice Grizonne. Brice has since secured a long lease on Julie’s En Remont parcel in Fleurie and, with the family’s blessing, will continue to make the wines in the same chai and cellar at her home in Romanèche. This Minouche bottling comes from fruit grown in Chadounet’s vineyards in Fleurie, mostly from the lieu-dit La Madon

wine: A Pie de Tierra, El Sucro 2023
notes: Place: Méntrida, Spain Grape: Garnacha Vibe: Savoury Granitic and silty soils bring an expression of Garnacha that really glides across the palate. From the gorgeously pretty pale colour alone, you know this has seen some whole bunch but the nose doubles down with a wonderful herbaceousness. Sheer class. ABV: 13.5%

wine: A Pie de Tierra, Fuerza Bruta 2023
notes: Place: Méntrida, Spain Grape: Garnacha Vibe: Savoury Silly old bush vines again producing an ethereal, elegant expression of both grape and balance. This is savoury and sapid. Really into the modern Spanish winemaking trend where over-extraction and oak are being slowly pulled back. Long may it continue. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Fresh Riesling and good value go hand in hand. Not many noble grape varieties of this quality come in at this kinda price... looking at you, Chardy! What we have here is a tri-village blend that shows a more rounded rendition of the Rheinhessen, thanks to malo taking place to soften the acidity a touch. Bone dry and orchard-fruited, you can't go wrong. ABV: 11%

Place: Monmouthsire, Wales Grape: Triomphe and Chardonnay Vibe: Pet-Nat + Friends Watching this particular bottle evolve over the years has been a real joy with each vintage becoming more refined and elegant. It’s a true testament to the hard work and the unique microclimate of their little corner of Wales. Damson-leaning, with a grapey and grassy profile, you can think of this as Wales’ answer to Lambrusco. Curious? You’ll have to taste it to believe it! ABV:9%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, lighter Originally started by the iconic Marcel, but it’s Marie Lapierre who’s now pushing out pristine yet playful wines from this cellar. Beaujolais Blanc is rarely this good. Cutting and fresh, showing a particularly skilled hand in what's becoming an ever-warming part of France. Direct press, mostly in vats, with just a touch of older wood to soften things slightly. All limes and florals with zero of the often associated 'weight'. A stone’s throw from Burgundy and this will easily give plenty of Bourgogne Blancs a run for their mon

wine: Parched + Indigo Wines present... Ochota Barrels
notes: We are extremely blessed and favoured to be welcoming none other than Australian heavyweight, Amber Ochota of Ochota Barrels, to Dan's for a very special tasting. The wines of Ochota Barrels have been a firm staple on our shelves for years, and for good reason. Founded in 2008 by Amber and the late, great Taras Ochota, Ochota Barrels make beautiful wines with fruit sourced from small, carefully selected vineyards that share their commitment to organic and biodynamic farming practices. The decision to make their own wine back home in the Adelaide Hills came about after Taras and Amber had been

Place: Oregon, USA Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Silky I’ll be cracking into plenty of these in the short term. The fruit is just glorious, and the hint of asphalt and tea in the mix makes it pretty irresistible. The tannins are silky and beautifully woven through. How can you not love Pinot when it’s pulled off like this? Great on its own, but with enough guts to stand up to a meal if needed. ABV: 13%

Place: Oregon, USA Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Sultry Another clever single-site bottling from what many would consider an Oregon Grand Cru. The fruit sits firmly in the red camp. It is nicely ripe but not over the top. There’s a herbal, earthy quality at play; sarsaparilla comes to mind, though I’ve been told that might be a bit too niche. Too late now. ABV: 13%
Place: Oregon, USA Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Textural, Oaked, Classic Clos Electrique channeling Grand Cru vibes stateside. April frost in ’22 means this is even more limited than usual. ABV: 13.4%

Place: Oregon, USA Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Textural, Oaked, Classic Tasty Chard is always welcome around here. Loving this one, as it’s all lime leaf and orange on the nose, with creamy orchard fruit rolling through the midweight palate. The oak is subtle and really well integrated at the moment, just barely showing a hint of vanilla. Crisp enough to sip while you cook, substantial enough to carry you through the meal. If you're into New World Chardy, this one’s your ticket. ABV: 13.4%

Place: Sussex, England Grape: Bacchus, Auxerrois, Chardonnay, Ortega Vibe: Lighter An easy-drinking, smile-inducing English blend. This is the future! Think lemon peel, crisp orchard fruit, and a gentle lift of elderflower. The perfect intro to the carefree house style where pleasure comes first, and nothing’s too serious. Priced to pour. ABV: 10.5%

wine: Joh. Jos. Prüm, Graacher Himmelreich Auslese 'Goldkapsel' 2022
notes: Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Classic, Sweeter Intensely spiced, with that perfect sweet-sour interplay. Just love it when Riesling leans ginger-y and here it’s backed by cloves, smoke, and all the regal swagger you'd expect from golden-capped Prüm. ABV: 7.5%

wine: Joh. Jos. Prüm, Bernkasteler Lay Auslese 'Goldkapsel' 2023
notes: Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Sweet + Succulent Even as a baby, this is already intoxicating. Slightly reductive and smoky for now, but it’s built to go the distance. Rich, yet somehow completely weightless. An aromatic dream with apricots teetering on overripe, tangled with rose petals and wet slate. ABV: 8%

wine: Joh. Jos. Prüm, Zeltinger Sonnenuhr Auslese 2020
notes: Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Sweet + Succulent Tropicana. All those juicy fruits, woven together by that signature minerality. Like a Pavlovian dog, I see the words JJ Prüm and immediately start to salivate. So balanced. So moreish. ABV: 7.5%

wine: F.X. Pichler, Riesling Loibner Loibenberg Smaragd 2010
notes: Place: Wachau, Austria Grape: Riesling Vibe: Classic, textural At the peak of its powers presently, offering up a smorgasbord of exotic fruit aromas and flavours. There's plenty of presence here, but it's elegant as hell. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Modern Meursault Sous la Velle lies at the foot of the Meursault slope, and this modern expression brings more tension than the village’s typically plush style. It still delivers a beautifully ripe core of fruit, just without the excess 'fat'. Worth the splurge. ABV: 13%

wine: Domaine Rougeot, Saint Romain 'La Combe Bazin' 2023
notes: Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Special I’ve always had a soft spot for this lieu-dit, ever since a memorable Cossard bottle from the same site, many moons ago. Maybe it’s the high limestone content, but I always feel that these drink a lil' leaner, always more laser-focused even in warmer vintages like 2022. Racy yet textured. The fruit is cushioned by a thoughtful touch of oak (15% new), giving it a classical feel but very much with a modern pulse. Tiny sulphur addition at bottling. ABV: 13%

wine: Domaine Rougeot, Bourgogne Côte d'Or 'Clos des Six Ouvrées' 2022
notes: Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Delicious From a monopole planted in the heart of Meursault, practically the domaine’s back garden, on clay-limestone soils, with 50-year-old vines. The Diagonal striped bottles are always without any additions. Typing that almost brought a tear to my eye. The tides are finally turning in Burgundy, with even the old guard beginning to embrace regenerative farming and gentle vinification. This one’s already golden-fruited and nutty, a total beaut! ABV: 13%

wine: Domaine de la Touraize, Chardonnay en Flandre 2020
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Saline + Salivating This is so on right now! Thankfully, this landed right in the prime drinking window. Extended time in barrel and now a few extra years cooling off in bottle means the edges have softened beautifully, leaving a saline and seductive drinkin' experience. It’s the salty-sweet interplay between ripe fruit and minerality that sends this over the edge. Salivating, sea-shelly, and just utterly joyful. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Burgenland, Austria Grape: Muscat + Grüner + Welschriesling + Chardonnay + Gewürz Vibe: Juicy A carefree and casual maceration that you'd have to have really poor taste in wine not to enjoy. Seriously, reckon even your Nan would be keen on this. There is just a perfect touch of everything: florals, fruit, minerals, tannin, texture. All in a gentle balance. Nothing shouting over the top, just merging effortlessly for one smooth and seductive Skinsy thing. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Parched + Modal Wines present... Yo El Rey
notes: We're hyped to be joined by Angelo van Dyk, not only our wine trade mate but also the talented winemaker behind Yo El Rey wines. Angelo was born and raised in South Africa, before moving to London to experience everything the UK's wine scene has to offer. A year away to spend time with different winemakers and learn even more turned into seven, during which the decision was made to start making wine back in his home country. Yo El Rey make wine from fruit sourced from small, organic growers around South Africa's Cape Town, with all wines being made in their winery in Stellenbosch in a low inte

Place: Styria, Austria Grape: Sauvignon Blanc + Muskateller Vibe: Aromatic Wonderland Elias's wine feels distinctly Styrian, threading together everything I love from the region, yet at once entirely his own. There's the flinty edge of Werlitsch, the clarity and nerve of Tscheppe, and that wild, generous spirit you find in his parents’ wines. At both La Dive and Karakterre, these were the bottles insiders tipped as must-tastes. They more than delivered, and I’m sure the enviable hype will soon follow. But for now, these releases are quietly singin’ under the radar. A 60/40 split, with the mino

Place: Styria, Austria Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: WOW Elias's wine feels distinctly Styrian, threading together everything I love from the region, yet at once entirely his own. There's the flinty edge of Werlitsch, the clarity and nerve of Tscheppe, and that wild, generous spirit you find in his parents’ wines. At both La Dive and Karakterre, these were the bottles insiders tipped as must-tastes. They more than delivered, and I’m sure the enviable hype will soon follow. But for now, these releases are quietly singin’ under the radar. This plot sits on one of the steepest slopes, with serious

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural Dauvissat hitting its stride. Still has that youthful energy, but it's starting to open up nicely. 2020 was a warm, dry year, and personally, I've found the wines can sometimes feel a bit too plush but here, the heat is handled like a pro. Dauvissat is one of the rare few who has mastered this solar vintage, and this is a beautifully balanced wine. Super tasty. '26 cellar release hehe. ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural A nicely matured bottle from the master of Chablis. Tight, ethereal Chardonnay with incredible drive and poise. Things are slowly beginning to uncoil into a thing of real beauty. ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural Rare as hen's teeth. You haven’t really drunk Chablis until you’ve tasted Dauvissat. Entry level in name only, this is smoking. ABV: 13%

wine: Domaine Vincent Dauvissat, Chablis Grand Cru 'Les Preuses' 2020
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural Elegant, expansive, yet somehow almost weightless. The ’20 brings plenty of power, but we’re still firmly in steely Chablis territory. White flowers, citrus oil, and a salty depth all shine bright thanks to Dauvissat’s signature precision. That Grand Cru pedigree is unmistakable. ABV: 13%

wine: Dan's presents... Not A Pub Quiz
notes: We're not a pub. So this isn't a pub quiz. It is gonna be a proper laugh though. If you've ever wanted to flex about how much you know about wine, and other things that aren't wine, this is the quiz for you. All the usual hallmarks of a pub quiz – drinks, a stupid picture round, some crap chat from your host – but better, because you'll be drinking rly nice wine rather than a lukewarm £7 pint. As well as entering the quiz, your ticket gets you four wines and the chance to win some really fun ⋆⭒˚.⋆ prizes ⋆⭒˚.⋆ (everybody say ooOOOOoOOOOooh). So round up your smartest/booziest friends, brush up

Place: England Grape: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Gamay and Pinot Meunier Vibe: An Actual Good English Wine An ode to the wonderous bottling under the same name from Julien Guillot. It's vibey, and it is probably the best wine I've tasted from these isles in terms of actual drinking pleasure. A co-ferment of C hardonnay, Pinot Noir, Gamay and Pinot Meunier in various guises, formats and states of undress. There's a tension on show, combined with an exotic array of fruits that just has you going again and again and again. ABV: 10.5%
Place: Beaujolais , France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural, lighter Vin de Soif Chez Lapierre n Friends. Iconic. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Trousseau Vibe: Delicate Enticing aromatics are the calling card of Guillot's reds, and the Trousseau doesn't lie. Dry without being hard, succulent without being flabby. It's textbook but in a way that you want to smash. ABV: 12%
Place: Jurançon, France Grape: Petit and Gros Manseng Vibe: Vibey This pack includes 1 x Domaine Lajibe, Marcel 2023 and 2 x Mystery Delicious White Wines! Yummy

Place: Jurançon, France Grape: Petit and Gros Manseng Vibe: Vibey Jurançon, but we could also be up in the Jura. If you know, then you know. A steal considering the absolutely hectic nature of this wine. Also featured in Fresh Foillard and Limited Lajibe: The Latest Biweekly Bottle Drop .

wine: Ben Adams: Enmill Field, Col Fondo NV
notes: Place: England Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Serious Fruit that get's pressed super gently with a Coquard, then straight into old 228L and 400L barrels to ferment and rest on lees, untouched. The second ferment kicked off with a splash of the fresher juice, before being bottled by gravity in September 2024. Tiny quantites! Unfiltered, expressive, and full of character. The fruit here feels like some of the ripest and most profound I’ve seen on home soil. There’s a salty, almost oxidative twang that adds a savoury lift, making this about as close to Champagne-level complexity as you’ll find from méth

Place: England Grape: 60% Pinot Meunier + 40% Pinot Noir Vibe: Fresh An 8-day whole bunch maceration, then pressed into old 228L and 400L barrels. Exceptional fruit, beautifully handled with no additions and bottled by gravity. Ethereal and crunchy, this has to be one of the most precise English reds I've tasted.
