Still baby vines, but they bring such youthful vigour! In wine, we tend to fetishise the complexity of old vines, but there's something to be said for the raw energy of a young crop. Outrageously well-priced considering the exceptional farming here in the UK right through to the delig

Place: Marlborough, New Zealand Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Pretty High-toned red fruit up front, silky texture through the middle, and all umami spice at the back. This is one hell of a journey! A little clonal mix and daily siphoning to keep the cap wet (without heavy extraction) delivers a pitch-perfect expression of Pinot. So pristine, packed with flavour but never overpowering. It just glides. This is something I’d gladly drink all day without ever getting bored. ABV: 13%

Place: Marlborough, New Zealand Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Highly Refreshing Chilled red, yes, but this is so much more than that. Featherweight and ethereal, kind of like how they do it up in the Jura. It’s destemmed, with a very gentle maceration that gives us pomegranate, watermelon, and just a whisper of Pinot’s savoury side. There’s something incredibly moreish about the finish that leaves you instantly craving another sip. Breathtaking and thoughtful once again! ABV: 13%

Place: Marlborough, New Zealand Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Tense Ashleigh’s time in Northern France really shows here, with a tension that nods to her time learning with the Labets. Racy, mineral, compelling. Full malo and a long élevage bring just enough weight to keep everything perfectly poised. The more you drink, the more beautiful nuance you’ll coax out. Another outstanding, spine-tingling expression of grape and place. YAY. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Marlborough, New Zealand Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Highly Refreshing Electrifying Chenin at its absolute best. It kicks off all custard apple-y, then slowly unfurls into a saline, mineral-driven bottle that really speaks of maritime Marlborough. There’s a beautiful, delicate edge to all of Ashleigh’s wines that deserves your full time and attention. A wine that’s both contemplative and hard to put down. This one’s gonna age like a dream. Magical. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Classic, textural Mature Sauvignon Blanc at its finest. That punchy fruit has mellowed into a now mineral-laced bottle full of nutty depth and a touch of lanolin. Everything’s come together beautifully! Absolute steal for something over a decade old too. ABV: 13%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Touriga And Friends Vibe: Slippery Touriga, which does really, really well in Australia, is spiced up with some Shiraz and gently pressed to give us this citrus, tropical fruited laden thirst quencher. 11.5% Abv

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Crunchy One barrel made, so only a couple of hundred bottles in circulation. Make one yours. Louis' ode to his great friend and mentor, Taras Ochota is a selection of his best barrel of Grenache from the deep sands of the McLaren Vale. Worthy. 12.8% Abv

Place: South Australia Grape: Shiraz, Grenache, Carignan, Cinsault Vibe: Lovely Tim plays around here, giving us his take on a classic Southern Rhone blend for all those euro-heads. A blend of techniques here. Whole bunches of Grenache fermented in direct pressed Syrah juice, and vice versa. Carbonic Carignan and Cinsault seasoning. Dark fruited, with a definite herbs de Provence undertone that has one hanging out for the Mistral to blow through. 13% Abv

Place: South Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Deep Morgan is made with a bit of Pommard clone Pinot grown in Ironbank aka it's got some depth and oomph, all whilst maintaining the effortless flow that's synonymous with the Les Fruits wines. Dark fruited, ample savoury spice and a dusting of tannins keeping everything moving in the right direction. Sign me up. 13% Abv

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Pure The Vale and Chenin don't immediately come to mind when talking about great pairings, but perhaps minds will now be altered. Fruit of 50+ year old vines within the lovely Brini Vineyard. Part in tank and part in barrel, Rob is looking to preserve that lovely cut and thrust, balancing it out nicely with an intense range of fruit that'll keep you diving back in for more.

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Racy The Collines Vineyard is up in beautiful Piccadilly, prime Chardo territory. hand picked, chilled fruit is direct pressed, lightly settled and run to old oak for 100% barrel fermentation. This is crystalline! There's purity everywhere you look, sniff and sip. Gentle stone fruits, citric cut and cinnamon spice all collide. It's a ripper. 12.8% Abv

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Cinsault + Nebbiolo Vibe: Refreshing Somewhat of a religious experience, this weighing in at only 10%, our Lord and Saviour Jordan Hein almost turning wine into pure hydration. Half way between pink and light red, it should be a constant fixture in your fridge whilst stocks last. Which they wont. 10% Abv

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Mencia Vibe: Playful + Vibey A great variety, Mencia, and it's cool to see it being planted more outside of it's Northern Spanish homeland. Vamos! Jordan treats this to a carbonic maceration bath ala classic Beaujolais and the result is an extremely easy to imbibe with with tonnes of character if you want but also it's fine if you don't. Serve chilled for a good time. 12.5% Abv

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Chardonnay + Riesling Vibe: Pure Mostly Chardy, with a dash of Rizz added to dial up the freshness to all time levels. It's aromatic and fruit driven and then heads down a savoury, moreish root. Keeen. 12% ABV

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Cracking Good Intentions' first release of their single vineyard range, so we're at the pointy end of their offering. The vineyard is planted at the base of Mount Gambier over volcanic soil, bringing a unique salinity to the wine. Pair that with a touch of Jura-style oxyness, a honeycomb topping and peachy fruit, we're onto a ripper here. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal New labels in 23, me likey. These single site expressions are a pretty serious bunch, a definite step up and savoury side quest for the good folk at Good Intentions. As with the 22 Boxers, this is a delicate, spice driven example that drinks kind of like a Mt Etna and Classic Volnay love child. I'm into it. You'll be too. 12.2% Abv

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Cabernet Franc Vibe: Juicy All about the gentle handling here, with the fruit fermented as whole berries before being pressed off before being entirely dry. What we're left with is an eminently drinkable Cab Franc, lacking none of the trademark leafy character and freshness but with a bit of x-factor. One that'll do really well chilled down. 13.5% Abv

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Shiraz Vibe: Beauty Shiraz from a Coonawarra vineyard. Direct press, straight into steel. Don’t be put off by the colour. This is dry, but juicy offering serious refreshment, all year round. Enough creamy texture to work just as well at the table as it does by the pool. Some volcanic minerality in there too, if you’re in the mood to put your thinkin' cap on. Splash splash. ABV: 12.8%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Classic Technically this is a ' pét-nat' but this is so far removed from the yeasty, cloudy numbers often associated with the style (no shade btw, I love them too). This just feels more finely tuned, sharing more in common with grower champers, with it's flavour profile showcasing apple, wet wool and brioche. A touch of cream and chalk is cut through by a searing vein of acid meaning this is a great choice for a fancy fizz that won't break the bank. No dosage. ABV: 13%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Classic, textural Right up there with the very best pink liquid I've had the pleasure to taste. Something to sip and savour. Wild strawberries, summer meadows, plenty of spice but leaving a lasting impression of salinity. I think this is what they mean when they say 'Gastronomic Rosé. Tasty as. ABV: 14%

Place: Mâconnais, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Elite Chavigne is a 3.3-hectare plot situated at the top of the hillside. From slightly younger vines, averaging 20 years old, this wine is freshest and most vibrant. Partially matured in concrete vats with minimal oak, it offers a more immediate drinking style and is intended to be enjoyed earlier than the domaine’s other cuvées. Good for those impatient, like me. ABV: 13.5%

wine: Domaine Guffens-Heynen, Macon Pierreclos 'Tris de Chavigne' 2023
notes: Place: Mâconnais, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Elite From the first presses of grapes picked over three passes in 12 days focused on the upper part of the vineyard, where Jean-Marie noted the acidity was “remarkable”. He wasn't joking, this might be the best Tri de Chavigne ever made... IMO, Guffens has set a new bar with these 2023 releases. Speechless. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Mâconnais, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Elite Sourced from the climats of Côte and Carmentrant in Fuissé, these are older vines planted on a cool slope. That colder exposure brings tension and lift, offering a sharp counterpoint to the natural richness making this both vivid and built to age. Yum. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Mâconnais, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Elite From the first presses of grapes grown in the Saint-Véran lieu-dits Les Combes, Les Carettes, and a small portion of Clos des Poncetys. Only the first, free-run juice is used before fermented with native yeasts in barrel, with a few rounds of bâtonnage. Jean-Marie describes it as “slightly reductive and downright attractive.” I'm not going to argue there. This is flinty and F***ing delicious. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Kamptal, Austria Grape: Kamptal Red Blend Vibe: Natural, textural IMO Austria is unrivalled when it comes to value. They're damn good at creating beautifully balanced bottles that won't break the bank. Raspberries, cherries, a touch of rosehip, and a hint of bay. Nice on the ice. ABV: 12%

Place: Kamptal, Austria Grape: Grüner Veltliner, Muscat, Riesling, Pinot Blanc Vibe: Natural, textural IMO Austria is unrivalled when it comes to value. They're damn good at creating beautifully balanced bottles that won't break the bank. This has it all: a hint of floral aromatics, a bit of texture, lots of orchard fruit. Stock up for summer. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Woof Things get dialled up at Tribut as we head into the primo land of Chablis. Ripping texture, with plenty of presence and fleshy fruit coupled with a wash of saline acidity that keeps you eyeing off the rest of the bottle. ABV: 13%

Place: Kent, England Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural + Moreish Biodynamically grown Chardonnay, basket-pressed by hand. 31 day carbonic maceration for 31 days, then it's off to terracotta for 10 months. No filtration, no fining, no added sulphur. Techy details aside, this is such a unique take on Chardonnay. It's layered and complex, tropical but with a savoury edge. Makes me crave a Gilda in the summer sun. Actually, it kinda tastes like one too. I mean that as a compliment. This is such an interesting expression, and it's so cool to see the delicious results when a creative approach is taken

Place: Sussex, England Grape: Bacchus, Reichensteiner Vibe: Sunny An energetic Pét-Nat from the talented crew at Titch Hill. Ever wandered through the Sussex countryside on a summer stroll? Yeah, this tastes just like that. Citrus, elderflower, wild hedgerows. Direct-press fruit, zero additions, and lip-smackingly good. ABV:10.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Spicy Maxime found a lovely selection of fruit from a grower in Itterswiller in 22. Fermented as whole bunches for a bit of carbonic action. It's energetic and truly spicy but that is balanced out with decent fruit weight and a plushness of tannin. One for right now.

Place: Southern Rhone, France Grape: Syrah Vibe: Crunchy Sourced from vineyards on the lower slopes of Ventoux, and picked a little earlier to maintain freshness. Syrah given the Burgundian treatment, gently macerated as whole berries before going to old oak. It's bright and fresh yet unmistakably Syrah, showing lovely violet florals and meaty undertones. One for the fridge over summer as you wait for the coals to die down.

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Grenache + Cinsault + Sauvignon Blanc + Colombard Vibe: Hot A lovely blend of direct-pressed and macerated red and white grapes from many of the lovely growers Hannah has sourced from over the years. Sun-kissed and tutti-fruitti with a tropical twang to finish. This is obviously so much fun but still with flesh on her bones. Take this for a solo ride or pair it with pretty much any food. Spice would be extra nice though! This has got me all hot and bothered. ABV: 13.4% Please note these bottles are all hand-painted so the wine received may appear different from t

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural , textural Quite simply outstanding Chardonnay. Meyer lemons and poached pears spring to mind. There's loads of coiled up energy here that make it so multi-faceted and delicious. The freshest of the range, I could spend heaps of time with this bottle and never get bored. ABV: 12%

Place: Tavel, Rhône Grape: Grenache Noir, Cinsault, Clairette, Carignan Vibe: Vibey Life affirming ' rosé'. Probably best not to think of this as having a category, it is that mind bending. Aroma and flavour of a red, texture of a white, grip of a macerated wine. Single-site Tavel? Sign me up. Whole bunch maceration of grapes from the vines planted on complex, fossil-rich soils – a mix of red clay, ancient sand, limestone, and galets. Grapes are pressed before aging for 10 months in cement tanks. Due to the limited quantites, we've decided to share the love to some other producers that deserve

Place: Tavel, Rhône Grape: Grenache noir, Clairette, Cinsault, Carignan, Mourvedre Vibe: Vibey Life affirming ' rosé'. Probably best not to think of this as having a category, it is that mind bending. Aroma and flavour of a red, texture of a white, grip of a macerated wine. Single site Tavel? Sign me up. An 8-day whole bunch maceration of fruit from a single parcel planted on white galets. Grapes are pressed separately and juices blended before aging for 1 year in barrels and cement tanks. Due to the limited quantites, we've decided to share the love to some other producers that deserve just a

Place: Rhône, France Grape: Grenache Vibe: Juicy Vincent's take on rosé but to me this is very much giving lighter red vibes. Cranberry fruited and crushable. This is exactly the tonic you need for a heatwave. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Grolleau Vibe: Serve chilled to be chilled Grolleau handled with a light touch to show off the grape’s pretty side, which personally is the side I want to be on. You could call it a light red or a deep rosé, but what really matters is that this is very tasty. It kicks off with a little spritz, which (in my opinion) only adds to the freshness. Not your thing? A quick decant will sort that out. Then it’s all waves of gorgeous brambly fruit and gentle spice. A seriously long finish despite the playful structure too. ABV: 10.5%

wine: Parched + Ripley Wines present... Rizz Masters
notes: Anyone know how to say "gird your loins" in German??? We have the pleasure of being joined by Ripley Wines, importers of some of our all time fav German wines, for a night of elite German Riesling. Come n drink your way through a specially selected line up of Rieslings from top top top tier producers across Germany, such as Hoffgut Falkenstein, Peter Lauer and more. We'll also have an exclusive selection of new vintages to taste before the hit the shelves later this year. Kinda like the wine equivalent of being invited to a super duper fancy VIP film premier, don't u think?? Limited and exclus

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Natural, textural A crisp younger vine bottling from Oliver Lejeune, a man who knows plenty about Chenin. Trust me, we're in safe hands, especially from the cooling '23 vintage. The lightest of the range with a piercing acidity that makes for thirst-quenching drinking. Far from simple, there is beeswax and minerality on show too. Hydrating. ABV: 13%

wine: Clos de la Coulée de Serrant, Les Vieux Clos 2023
producer: CLOS DE LA COULEE DE SERRANT
notes: Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Textured, Natural Vieux Clos is the last of the Joly triplets. It lacks none of the purity and intensity of its siblings and is somewhat easier on the wallet. Deeply hued colour and the aromas back this up with intense mature fruit. That signature stony minerality keeps everything together. Start here if you're new on you're Joly journey. ABV: 13%

wine: Clos de la Coulée de Serrant, Clos de la Bergerie 2023
producer: CLOS DE LA COULEE DE SERRANT
notes: Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Textured, Natural Exotic and explosive as per the house style. Probably the most instantly appealing of the bunch. Barrel-aged with a wicked streak of minerality running through it. So far, 2023 is proving to be a standout year for the Loire, this being no exception. ABV: 13%

wine: Clos de la Coulée de Serrant, Coulée de Serrant 2023
producer: CLOS DE LA COULEE DE SERRANT
notes: Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Textured, Natural The standout in a seriously strong line-up. It’s powerful yet refined. This manages the balancing act between hedonistic and drinkable. Hard to put into words. The fruit feels almost dried but with a fresh lift, and there is a final note of soothing honey. So intense and layered, you'd be forgiven for thinking this has a touch of sweetness in there. Spoiler: there’s not. Genius and guaranteed to get the table talking. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Gewürztraminer Vibe: Oxy From an old vineyard on granite-rich soil above Dambach, this wine’s been aged under flor in old Alsatian foudres. Basically the Jura Alsatian mashup of my dreams. The aromatics are tamed into a salty, savoury expression that makes cheese a non-negotiable here. You'd think this would be too much, but this has been done with real finesse. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Riesling, Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural, Advanced The folks at Beck-Hartweg are pretty stoked about the incredible terroir they’re working with. Instead of focusing on individual grapes, they’re now blending everything together to give a real snapshot of the site itself. This is one hell of a wine with luscious fruit and aromatic spice to start before taking a salty twist. Liquid rock. ABV: 13%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Juicy A total juice bomb. Bursting with vibrant aromatics and just about every red berry you can think of. There’s a bunch of pretty floral notes in the mix too. Tastes like tearing into a bag of your favorite childhood sweets. Serve chilled, and be chilled. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Paralian, 'Blewitt Springs Hill Vineyard' Cabernet Sauvignon 2022
notes: Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Cabernet Sauvignon Vibe: Broody Cabernet that's actually worth drinking, now that’s not something you'll hear me say every day. This one hits that sweet spot: classic enough to keep the old man happy, but dialed in for the modern palate. Juicy blackberry fruit, a hint of bay leaf, and a flicker of graphite on the finish. It’s super approachable now, but it’s also built to go the distance if you’re into the whole cellaring thing. Medium-bodied perfection. ABV: 13.5%

wine: Paralian, 'Blewitt Springs Hill Vineyard' Shiraz Mataro 2023
notes: Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Shiraz + Mataro Vibe: Delicious A single-site blend that puts the spotlight on the beautiful Blewitt Springs vineyard. The Mataro (the French know it as Mourvèdre) was just too good to ignore, so a barrel selection was made before blending everything post-maturation. We've got top notes of tar and juicy blue fruits before the Mataro takes center stage bringing those savoury, almost meaty flavours. The tannins are silky and well-knit, with a fresh black-fruited acidity that gives the whole thing a delicious, moreish finish. ABV: 14%

Place: Guria, Georgia Grape: Blend Vibe: Lighter, Chillable Saperavi can often be a bit of a brute. Muscular, heavy, extracted. This expression turns that reputation on its head. Light on its feet and almost Pinot-like in its aromatics. Juicy and fun but also something to geek out over if that's your bag. Never thought I'd be asking for my Saperavi chilled, but here we are. ABV: 12%

Place: Gascony, France Grape: Colombard + Ugni Blanc + Gros Manseng Vibe: Zippy Finding decent, respectfully made wine under £20 is tough these days, under £15 feels near impossible. And yet, here we are. Lightly aromatic, steely fresh, and a touch herbal. It’s like someone bottled the first sunshine of spring. ABV: 11%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Pineau D'Aunis Vibe: Wild From a mix of young and old vines across varied soils, this is a delicious entry point into the fragrant world of Pineau d’Aunis. The cooler vintage brings an earthern, savoury expression. Soaring aromatics with plenty of that signature cracked pepper the grape is known for. Juicy enough to enjoy chilled, but complex enough to slow down and savour . This would be so so good with a hunk of peppered salami. ABV: 12%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Natural, textural Renaud makes this from the first pick of all his plots so things are nice and linear. Pale, delicate, and nuanced from the colder year of '23 this is something to get stuck into if you're an acid fiend like me. Drinking like such a dream right now . ABV: 11.5%

Time to bring out the big guns. We have the absolute pleasure of being joined by Charlie Seppelt and Skye Salter, the powerhouse behind Paralian Wines, for one night of Aussie excellence on the Dalston Riviera. Paralian is the long awaited, and much lauded, project of Skye and Charlie, who between them have amassed over 50 vintages around the world at names including Chave, Dublère, Château Giscours and Shaw + Smith. The goal of Paralian is to shine a light on distinguished sites throughout McLaren Vale. The winemaking is traditional and gentle, and the wines bright and modern in style. In the

wine: .... Parched x Winemakers Club: Tenuta di Carleone
notes: Ciao bella! Join us on the 3rd of June for an evening with Sean O'Callaghan of Tenuta di Carleone. Founded in 2012, Tenuta di Carleone can be found in the heart of Tuscany's Chianti Classico region, headed up by winemaking wizard Sean O'Callaghan, a Somerset-born Italian transplant with 25 years' experience working in the Chianti region. Sean set about making wines that were inspired by the history of the region, but with a progressive, modern twist. As well as a boatload of winemaking experience and knowledge, Sean brings a commitment to organic and biodynamic farming practices to the estate,

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elite Bourgogne Rouge but let’s be honest, it’s not really. Certainly not when it comes to quality. Red-fruited and fragrant, with lacy tannins. Giving big 'Chambolle' energy. Linear, with high acidity, so it’ll age beautifully if you’re either forgetful or just nice and patient. But it’s also great to drink now. Everyone wins. Yay! ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elite A nice peek into the house style. Even at the village level, this wine shows impressive depth and longevity. Structured, serious, and unmistakably Chambolle in its elegance. You could keep your hands off this for quite some time and things will be very much rewarding. It really punches above its weight. Classy stuff. ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elite Ghislaine reckons this is the most 'Chambolle' of the '22s. Located in a little dip in the heart of the village, this always shows its elegant side even in warmer vintages. This is really pretty, with all those delicate florals you want. Sadly, just a barrel and a half even in this bountiful year. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elite Barthod’s 0.37-hectare sliver flanking Bonnes-Mares’ southwest corner was upgraded to premier cru status in 1987, and rightly so. Deeper and brooding with a distinctly mineral core. ABV: 13.5%

wine: Ghislaine Barthod, Chambolle-Musigny 1er Cru 'Aux Beaux Bruns'
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elite Point a gun at my head and this is the cuvee I'm drinkin' on my deathbed. Iconic wine from an iconic estate. A lower lying Premier Cru that given time showcases the full flamboyance going on in the cellar. Full and long, this is a wine to save for a special, special occasion. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elite A teeny, tiny parcel where in '21 only one barrel got produced. This lies in the northern sector of Chambolle, flanked by Les Baudes to the north and Les Gruenchers to the south. Black cherries and bay dominate the spicier palate whilst the tannins hint that this is gonna be a beauty after a little snooze in the bottle. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elite The Chatelots vineyard is located closer to the town, where the soils tend to be a little more alluvial. This is often a good thing if you're impatient, as the wines tend to be a little more approachable earlier on. That's not to say you shouldn't pop this away for a few years to mature and express itself. Perfumed, pretty, and fine boned. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Molise, Italy Grape: Montepulciano, Merlot + Cabernet Sauvignon Vibe: Rustic A rustic Italian that is priced to pour. Plums and dark cherries, but this is not overly extracted so still nice and fresh. Somewhat old-school, with a charmingly unpolished nature about it. ABV: 12%

wine: Domaine Nathalie et Gilles Fevre, Chablis Vieilles Vignes 2022
notes: Place: Chablis, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural Head over heels into Chablis since the sun decided to come out. Another classic bottling from a classic estate. Wet stones, crunchy orchard fruit and plenty of lemon lime goodness. Cold but not too cold please. ABV: 13%

wine: De Moor, Vendangeur Masqué Bourgogne Blanc 2024
notes: Place: Chablis, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Chiselled A great way to dive into the De Moor range. A negociant blend of different plots, but always offering value and refreshment in spades. They like to let the juice do its own thing, resting on its lees in used foudre casks without bâtonnage. '24 is a return to a leaner, more refreshing rendition. Zesty but with textural intrigue and plenty of salty goodness. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Gewürztraminer Vibe: Intriguing Again, Gewürztraminer but from alluvial soils and this gets a bit more skin contact than its sibling, Habibi Cheri. A more heady, aromatic take. Think bergamot and rose. On the palate, it leans spicy, almost Szechuan-like, with a gorgeous frame of tea-like tannin wrapping it all together. Intriguing and intellectual. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Gewürztraminer Vibe: Pretty Gewürztraminer gets a lot of hate, and sometimes rightly so. It takes a very skilled hand to bring balance to this easily over-the-top grape. This is a perfect example of how those bold aromatics can shine when treated with care. Sourced from young vines on clay and limestone, it sees a short maceration that brings out notes of orange zest and delicate florals. Tatse like sunshine. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Refreshing Younger vine Pinot from clay, limestone and granite in Ammerschwihr. Fully destemmed, and macerated for two weeks! A cool vintage showing the mineral side of Pinot supported by red berries and just enough earthen funk. Nourshing. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Refreshing Directly pressed Pinot for a wonderfully refreshing pink. A slightly smoky reduction is very much a good thing in my eyes, adding not only a delicious top note but also a sign the wine hasn't seen too much oxygen. Freshness is the name of the game. Tart berries, blood orange and just a whisper of Pinot spice. Clean and crushable. ABV: 12%

wine: .... Parched x Justerini & Brooks: Storm Wines
notes: Join us on the 14th of May for an evening with Hannes Storm of Storm Vineyards. We’re buzzing to welcome one of the most exciting names in South African wine for what’s sure to be a night to remember—or not, depending on whether you stick around for a bottle (or two) after… Former head winemaker at Hamilton Russell, Hannes went solo in 2014 and has been quietly redefining what South African Pinot Noir and Chardonnay can be. Think Burgundy-style elegance with a Southern Hemisphere pulse. Fragrant, precise, full of energy. He’s the only winemaker bottling Pinot from all three sub-regions of the

Place: Loire, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Classic, textural If I'm gonna be drinkin' Sauvignon Blanc, it's gotta be good. This is very good. This leans more into the mineral side of the grape whilst showing that classic acidity, only enhanced by the limestone, and a decent bit of texture. Food friendly but also a candiate for splashin' around. ABV: 14%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Classic, textural Barrel-aged Sauvignon Blanc from vines just north of Sury-en-Vaux. This one hits that sweet spot where texture meets tenstion. It's ripe but still razor-sharp. It is exactly what I want from Sauvignon Blanc. Something that is not easy to achieve. Sensational drinkin' if you're a fan of terroir driven bottles . ABV: 14%

Place: England Grape: Pinot Noir + Pinot Blanc Vibe: One of a kind The press juice from Field Notes 1, aged in barrel for 11 months, then blended with a splash of semi-carbonic Pinot Meunier. Geeky winemaking details aside, this is a definite step up in complexity, while still keeping all the easy-drinking charm of its sibling. The fruit is turned up a notch: think almonds, kirsch, and a more mineral-driven profile. The texture is pure silk, with a subtle, savoury, clay-like edge running through it. Polished, poised, and quietly impressive. ABV: 11%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Cabernet Franc + Pineau d’Aunis Vibe: Natural Another gem from the Robinots, made with Cabernet Franc sourced from a friend down in Touraine. True to the house style, the winemaking remains consistent with their other reds: a two-week whole bunch maceration is done separately before blending. 15 months of elevage renders a light, bright expression framed by soft tannin. That unmistakable white pepper note from Pineau d'Aunis shines through! Energetic. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Chablis, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural Ripe and riping in this vintage. Rich and tension filled atm, so it's a wine that'll benefit from a decant for sure. If you don't have a decanter, you can also just drink it from the bottle. De Moor is always delicious. Juice rests in a mix of barrel and foudre, they're looking for balance in that sense. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Chablis, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Pure As per, an exceptional level of detail on show here. Line and length, shape and guile. Fruit from maturing vineyards, pulling all that classic briney influence up from the soil. A cuvee that'll reward a bit of patience, or a tonne of air in its youth. ABV: 12.5%

wine: De Moor, Chablis 1er Cru 'Vaux de Vey' 2023
notes: Place: Chablis, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural Yet another Chablissien dream from the de Moors. This one always needs a bit of air and/or potentially another year or so in bottle to fully unfurl but my lord, the components are there. A decent stint in wood has lent this some concentration, breadth and expression off the bat, before things sharpen up nicely, spitting you out all covered in salt. Drink. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Chablis, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural Always a blend of sites, a nice snapshot of vintage. We're returing to a more linear thing after a couple of scorchers. There is still intensity and depth as per the house style but typically driving in this iteration. Intensity is off the charts, balanced beautifully by characteristic acid lines. Effortless drinking. I'm half inclined to drink them all myself, but that would be rude. ABV: 12%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Ploussard Vibe: Soulful The first time they've bottled a single-varietal Ploussard. I'm not crying, you're crying. Sourced from several parcels and given a three-week maceration before pressing, then left to rest in vats until spring. A cool vintage, and this hums with Jurassic energy. Fragrant red berries, blood orange bitters, and a whisper of funk. Limited release. ABV: 12%

wine: Joh. Jos. Prüm, Bernkasteler Badstube Riesling Kabinett 2021
notes: Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Sweet + Succulent Bernkasteler gives Rizza a darker profile but still wrapped in florals and herbs. There’s an effortless harmony at play here. Ripe yet razor-sharp. A beautiful tension between sugar, acidity, and mineral drive. Lightly off-dry, steely, and impeccably clean. ABV: 8%

wine: Joh. Jos. Prüm, Wehlener Sonnenuhr Auslese Goldkapsel 2017
notes: Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Sweet + Succulent Golden-foil Prüm means we’re in seriously silly territory. This is next-level stuff. Power, depth, and complexity all cranked way up. Layers upon layers, with an almost overwhelming amount to unpack. It’s cerebral drinking, no doubt, but with that unmistakable Prüm grace holding it all together. ABV: 8%

wine: Joh. Jos. Prüm, Graacher Himmelreich Riesling Kabinett 2021
notes: Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Classic, textural Another banger from Prum. Smoky and just a little savoury. Lasering acidity as per, followed by a beautiful flintiness, spice and lime. Crazy good. ABV: 8%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir + Gamay Vibe: Fun Another belter of a blend. The fruit’s from pretty much all over. Pinot Noir from the Mâconnais and Chorey-les-Beaune, blended with Gamay from Chiroubles and a splash from Auxey-Duresses. Now, for some legal reason I won’t bore you with, only 600 bottles were released separately. Long story short: the Pinot from the Mâconnais is planted on an old abandoned plateau that hadn’t seen vines in 200 years, so it was left out of the AOP borders when the appellation was drawn up. Bureaucracy, eh? The winemaking? Also a bit of a head-scratcher

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir + Chardonnay Vibe: Juicy Now this is a Burgundian blend that knows how to have fun. It’s not trying to be overly fancy, but don’t be fooled, there’s still plenty going on. Drinkability is the name of the game, with crunchy cranberries, tangy rhubarb, and a hit of fresh spring strawberries. These wines are some of my favourites from the region, no one else is doing such thought-provoking, vin de soif-style wines like this. Bravo. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elite Bourgogne Rouge declassified to Vin de France. Lots of Lopez Pinotisty but in a more airy and delicate frame, with a little less maceration than his other reds. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Gamay + Aligoté Vibe: Silly good Gamay from the warmer 2022, softened by Aligoté 2023, then two years of élevage. A Blouge of real depth and complexity. Not just a mere glou-glou, this category can be taken seriously too. All spicy and herbal. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Vibe: Elegant These plots used to be blended but Arnaud has now decided to vinify separately to showcase their unique terroir. The vineyard was abandoned for quite some time, and as such has been chemical-free for a while! A parcel at decent altitude (350m) above the village of Chevrey, east of Nuits. Top of the plateau. Another whole bunch masterclass. ABV: 11%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Gamay + Aligoté Vibe: Blouge Blouge AKA Red and white, co-fermented for maximum drinkin' pleasure. Plenty of class still shines through even if this is just the 'entry point' into the delicate house style. You can go hard on this now whilst the rest of the range matures slowly. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Blanc Vibe: Heady Burgundian macerations don't come much better than this. There's actual grip and texture to be found here but this feels a little lighter than the '23. Refined and honing in with each vintage. The fruit is candied, almost caramel-esque. If you're someone who thinks macerating Burgundy is blasphemous, then let this change your mind/world/life. ABV: 11%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Natural, textural I see new bottlings from Batardière, I buy new bottlings from Batardière. That simple. Younger vines they planted in Rablay on eroded schist soil near their parcel for 'Esprit Libre'. Intensely mineral with plenty of verve in its youth. I'll be cracking into this now whilst the rest of the range is taking a short nap. ABV: 11%

wine: Charlotte Sonjon, Roussette de Savoie L'Innocente 2023
notes: Place: Savoie, France Grape: Altesse Vibe: Magical Picked from a beautiful parcel just in front of her front garden overlooking the lake. This is a truly magical vineyard, with the steep slope teeming with life. Bees, lavender, wild flowers. A beautiful expression of grape and place, full of apricots and elderflower, textured and tense. Barely any made it to our shores, and I plan on doing some serious damage, so get a move on. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Ardèche, France Grape: Semillon Vibe: Lemonade So hydrating, so refreshing. Like an ice-cold lemonade on a hot day but with the added bonus of a humble 9% alcohol. Undisgorged, unsulphured, unpretentious. Large pours only. ABV: 9%

wine: Cecile Tremblay, Nuits St Georges 'Aux Murgers' 1er Cru 2019
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal Very fine and floral for NSG whilst still remaining deep and velvety. Just divine. ABV: 13.5%

wine: .... Parched x Liberty Wines x Langham Present: England's Finest Fizz
notes: OOFT, it's happening! We're bubbling with excitement to bring you our latest tasting event, in collaboration with the legendary Langham Wines and Liberty Wines. These guys are without a doubt Britain’s finest fizz-makers, and we’re beyond lucky to have the incredible chief winemaker, Tommy Grimshaw, join us for the evening. Langham Wines are all about quality, using only estate-grown, hand-harvested fruit for their trad-method bubbles. Each base wine is crafted with indigenous yeasts, extended ageing, and regular bâtonnage in a delightful mix of stainless steel, concrete, and used French barri

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal This comes from a 0.53ha parcel of vines in Jacquines (50-ish years old) and also Aux Communes (40-ish years old). Exceptional depth to the mulberry leaning fruit with real poise. A touch of wood here accentuates rather than masks the fruit. IFYKYK. ABV: 13.5%

wine: Cecile Tremblay, Vosne Romanée Premier Cru 'Les Beaumonts' 2022
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal Detailed, seductive, layered. Tremblay can do no wrong. Rumour has it that this plot actually should be in Echézeaux and that the 2023 will be upgraded. If the rumours are true, then things will be getting even more eye-watering. Get in early! ABV: 13.5%

wine: Cecile Tremblay, Grand Cru 'Echezeaux Du Dessus' 2023
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal Hauntingly beautiful with a spicy nose hinting at liquorice, soy, anise, and a distinct note of wild rose. To get the best out of this, you really ought to be letting things mellow out for at least another 10 years! Yes, it's a long wait but future you will be very happy indeed. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Germany Grape: Domina, Muller Thurgau Vibe: Aromatic + Charming Who would've thought one of my personal highlights of the Loire Salons would have been this? Actually, if you know me (Fionn that is) then it's probably not a huge surprise. Either way Sophie has gone back to Germany to source a bit of fruit from some good pals. Drinks like a rosé of the highest order. Heaps of watermelon and rhubarb, wicked line of acid, perfectly textured. As I type the sun has decided to come out and as such I thought I'd treat myself to see if it's how I remembered. Looks like things have gotten even be

wine: Domaine Cécile Tremblay, Morey St Denis 'Très Girard'
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal From a 0.5-hectare plot of 40-year-old vines positioned just below the Premier Cru of Clos des Sorbets. Typical Morey backbone, fine salinity and nicely plush tannin. Drink from now until forever. Joking, well kind of - you've got at least 10 years! ABV: 13.5%

wine: Maison En Belles Lies, Santenay 'Sous la Roche' 2022
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Delicious This bottle is the most mineral expression from Maison En Belles and I’m here for it. This is all baked fruit with a bit of butter and has me wandering to the local fishmonger as I type. Cellar potential for sure but good to go from the offset. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Delicious Only 1% of Monthélie vineyards are planted with chardonnay! When they are, it’s often in the top spots just like here on a south-east facing slope. The limestone-clay soil renders a salivating wine full of fresh florals and a long clean finish. Lovely stuff. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Refined 100% whole bunch and very gently extracted. Sounds good to me. 60-year-old vines at the bottom of the lieu-dit Les Caillettes that has deep, red clay soils. Sounds even better. This is very much in the mold of the modern Burgundy I like, fine-boned, vibrant, and elegant. I reckon this one's just at the beginning of a long life ahead too. ABV: 12%

Guten Tag! We're so excited to be hosting an evening with Angus Macgregor from Heinrich. Weingut Heinrich, based in Burgenland, were pioneers in the biodynamics movement in Austria. Making the conversion in 2006, they were among the founding members of Respekt, a body seeking to certify biodynamic viticulture. As you might expect, they aim for super low intervention in the winery, and nothing is rushed - the wine takes as long as it needs. They believe this focus on biodynamics is the best way to bring out the true terroir of a place. Sounds good (gut) to me! They make a positive plethora of c

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elegant duh! From a plot in Cheilly-les-Maranges from the upper part of the parcel, an average of 65 year old vines. All about elegance. Silky and smooth, this supplies all the fine red fruit and tea-like spice we’re after. Perfectly balanced and ready to go from the offset. That said, I'll be stashing a few away for a rainy day as the upside potential here is looking great. ABV: 12%

wine: La Mariota, VdF 'Bac de las Coves' Rouge 2022
notes: Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Mourvèdre + Grenache + Carignan Vibe: Juicy Crunchy, juicy, gorgeous bottling. Violet aromatics and sweet fruit that veers from strawberries and plums to blackberries and cherries, countered by an enviable freshness and searing acidity. Put this in the fridge for half an hour and thank me l8r. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Muscat à Petits Grains + Roussanne Vibe: Intriguing In this line of work it's not often you can say a wine is like nothing you've ever tasted before - yet here we are! This is incredibly unique, due probably to the unlikely pairing of Muscat à Petits Grains and Roussanne. Strong petrol-like aromas mingle with elegant florals. Almost like a Riesling, except from the Roussillon? And not made from Riesling? Idk. A bottle for those who want to try something out there but still delicious. ABV: 12%

wine: La Mariota, Côtes Catalanes 'Roc de la Vella' 2023
notes: Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Macabeu + Roussanne Vibe: Sumptuous 90% Macabeu from 75 year old vines, with a dash of Roussanne thrown in too. This is fresh as anything and drinks with an enviable lightness, but still maintains that classic smoky Macabeu vibe underneath all the citrusy fruit. A touch of florals rounds everything out for a supremely interesting white. ABV: 11.5%

wine: La Mariota, Côtes Catalanes 'Bac de las Coves' Blanc 2022
notes: Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Grenache Blanc Vibe: Deep I don't normally jump for the joy at the words 'Grenache Blanc', but as with all things wine, in the right hands it can be unreal. Guess what kind of hands La Mariota has? Beautifully golden in the glass with a sumptuous texture, rounded and salty, this is a wonderfully complex take on the grape. ABV: 13%

Place: Penedes, Spain Grape: Xarel-lo Vibe: Easy Skinsy, Natural Radikon Alumni and all-around legend Lucy is THE winemaker to watch coming out of Spain. This is the free-run juice from centurion Xarel-lo vines and as you'd expect their low-yielding nature brings plenty of saline complexity. This is one of those wines that has it all whilst remaining utterly approachable and fun. Bright citrus, herbal, with rasping acid and a fine frame of tannin. I'm obsessed. ABV: 9.7%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Riesling Vibe: Fun This is the perfect entry point into the masterful mind of Mr Gross. Two weeks of gentle skin contact give us a perfect harmony of fruit and spice. Aromatic yet accessible, I couldn't think of a better snapshot of Alsace. ABV: 13%

wine: La Ferme des 9 Chemins, Les Terrasses Rouge 2024
notes: Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Precise Again volcanic sandstone doing plenty of heavy lifting. As ever though, there is such a delicate and lithe approach here. Purity in spades. Small berry Pinot fruit, whips of smoke and a little of that classic Pinot spice. There is something so drinkable about this. ABV: 11%

wine: La Ferme des 9 Chemins, Le Chemin des Loups 2024
notes: Place: Alsace, France Grape: Sylvaner + Auxerrois + Riesling Vibe: Saline What a lovely trio. Everything directly pressed from volcanic sandstone at a decent altitude for Alsace. The fruit feels dense and juicy, whilst the finish is saline and mineral. A cool vintage, and a really beautiful one, quite emotive. It's not loud, it doesn't shout. It doesn't need to. Delicacy is the name of the game, and all the better for it. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Rustic Pinot from a beautiful plot high in the hills above Dambach-la-Ville surrounded by the forest, a rarity in Alsace where monoculture is king. North facing so even in warm vintages were blessed with plenty of energy. Slightly wild and rustic but most importantly bright and charming. Earthen berries and smoke. Big fan. ABV: 12%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Gewürztraminer Vibe: Natural, Advanced Gewürzt on granite. Despite the warm year, Leo harvested earlier than most to keep a refreshing line of acid seldom found in this variety. A 2-day maceration helps coax out those aromatics without extracting too much grip. This is hazy, citrus-dominant and utterly refreshing. Like Lilt, if you remember that. ABV: 12%

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Syrah, Cinsault Vibe: Juicy Hannah drops new wines twice a year, in winter and spring. This one’s from LAST winter’s release, so consider yourselves lucky! Syrah and Cinsault were treated with a light touch to let the fruit shine. Another collector's item, since this is the last batch with clear bottles (they cost a pretty penny!). When the colour is this stunning, you’ve gotta show it off, right? Super fresh and lively, with wild strawberries, a touch of spice, and all things nice. Throw away the cork, sorry, I mean cap. ABV: 12.7% Please note these bottles are

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Grignolino Vibe: Savoury Grignolino from Piedmont happily vinified down in the Auvergne It nails that herbal, savoury vibe the Italians do so well while keeping a nice core of fruit. I really, really want to see this with some age. I also really, really want to drink this now. Vermouth like complexity. ABV: 14.5% Please note these bottles are all hand-painted so the wine received may appear different from the image.

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Cinsault Vibe: Zippy Light and bright! Young vines from Le Mazel that is foot crushed and gently macerated for about a week. Purple florals and plenty of plums, this is really sanguine and silky. It's good chilled and evolves as it warms up. So damn tasty. ABV: 12% Please note these bottles are all hand-painted so the wine received may appear different from the image.

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Mauzac, Grignolino Vibe: Unique A super classic blend with drinkability front and center. It gets a short maceration, followed by just a splash of Grignolino to smooth things out. This wine is really unlike anything else I’ve tasted (in the best possible way), maybe I need to drink more Mauzac? It’s smoky and herbal, with the fruit leaning into candied orange and rum raisin. It felt so familiar, but I couldn’t quite place it. Then Hannah said it reminded her of hot cross buns... Bingo. You’ll have to taste it to believe it. Very limited. ABV: 12% Please note thes

Place: Gaillac, France Grape: Muscadelle Vibe: Easy Smokey reduction gives way to a riot of stone fruit and sherbet. Tropical tones and a little herbal charm shine through with some time in the glass. I'm always floored by how much freshness Ori manages to coax out from this far south. Magical wine that'll make you smile! ABV: 9.5%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Cool The standout from our Big Beaujolais bash 2024. So vibrant, and effortless with the northwest exposure bringing a cooling nature that is increasingly hard to find around here. Divine fruit, herbal tones, and those classic Fleurie violets. What more do you want from your Bojo? ABV: 12.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural , textural Thrilling Chardonnay from the up-and-coming Mr Mang. Thanks to a west-facing parcel on clay soil this still retains plenty, and I mean plenty, of freshness despite the arid conditions in 2022. The long two-year elevage renders a heady wine with great length and smoky aromatics. Energetic on the palate this will easily go the distance. Sadly I've already smashed through my very limited personal stash. Womp. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural Perfumed and pretty, just how I like my Pinot to be. Incredibly fluid, this is the kind of wine I could and would drink every day if I could. Sadly my liver/wallet simply won't allow it!. Sour red fruit with an earthy core. Again, the upside potential is great here but this is just so hard to resist. V limited. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Maison des Saules, Côtes du Jura Chardonnay 'La Madeleine' 2024
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Promising Only the third vintage from these FRM alumni, and already wildly accomplished. Is there something in the water in the Jura? Whatever it is, pour me a glass of it. And of this. Full-bodied yet fresh, tense and driving. Lemons and apples come bursting to the fore with a background of smoke and lip-smacking sourness. Yeesh. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Maison des Saules, Côtes du Jura Savagnin 'Au Poirier' 2023
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Promising Another banger from this young domaine who are just getting started, not that you'd know that from the wines they're putting out. With a stint at FRM under their belts, they know a thing or two about balance and tension. Fresh and finessed, this is serious Sav from a domaine worth getting into now before everyone else hears about them and they double in price. Don't say I didn't warn u! ABV: 12.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: A+ Another mouth-watering bottling from a somewhat under the radar producer, although I doubt it'll stay that way. Elegant and fresh, this is chock full of white flowers and yellow fruit, citrus peel and tingling acid. Woof. ABV: 12%

wine: .... Parched + Tutto Present... Ar Pe Pe
notes: Time to bring out the big guns! We are beyond excited to be welcoming Isabella from Ar Pe Pe to the Dalston Riviera on the 17th of March. Ar Pe Pe need no introduction, but in case you've been living under a rock, the Perego family are based in Valtellina in Lombardy, and have been since 1860. All work is done by hand in the vineyard, which given the vertiginous angle of the slopes, is no mean feat. This is unbelievable alpine Nebbiolo, aged to chef's kiss perfection, and we can't believe we've got the honour of hosting Isabella for an evening of drinking, eating and chatting about this legend

Place: Badacsony, Hungary Grape: Riesling Vibe: Natural This is defo one for you acid heads. Thyme and lemongrass on the nose whilst the palate is all wet rocks and salt. Searing, and I mean searing acid is tempered by a little time in amphora to round out any harsh edges. Electrifying. ABV: 12%

Place: Badacsony, Hungary Grape: Kadarka + Kék Bakator + Kékfrankos + Hajnos kék Vibe: Natural, Juicy A big ol' blend of Hungarian autochthonous varieties. New word for you too? Well, that is a variety that is local to a specific region. I guess you can consider this a snapshot of what the Hungarian wine of yesteryear might have tasted like, and boy is it good. Cranberries, blood orange, hibiscus, rosehip. One of those wines that is just as complex as it is utterly smashable. Chill it, decant it, down it in one! ABV: 11%

grapes: Chardonnay, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc
notes: Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Chenin Blanc + Sauvignon Blanc + Riesling + Fiano + Chardonnay Vibe: Delish Another wacky blend from Nord-Sud, but I'm here for it, especially at this price tag. Salty and fresh thanks to high-altitude vines, the palate is full of creamy, slightly tangy peach fruit. A proper all-rounder, destined to be a staple in the fridge door. ABV: 12.5%

grapes: Pinot Noir, Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz, Grenache
notes: Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Shiraz + Cabernet Sauvignon + Grenache + Pinot Noir Vibe: Balanced A better red you'd be hard pressed to find at this price. Sometimes such esoteric blends earn a raised eyebrow from me, but if you get them right, they're absolutely banging. Cosy and warming yet still juicy and fresh, all the varietals are bringing their best here to produce a wine that's way more than the sum of its parts. ABV: 13%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Accomplished Maylis doesn’t seem to miss, this fizz included. Tasted in the dark, dimly lit Ackerman caves during La Dive Bouteille, it still shone brightly among the many wines poured, elite Champers included. A Blanc de Blancs packed with racy orchard fruit, a touch of beautiful autolytic character and her hallmark saline finish. This release has also seen an extra year of élevage too. ABV: 11%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Gringet Vibe: One Off Another Gringet bottling where the fruit hails from the late great Belluard’s estate. With fruit as precious as this it seemed only right to give the wine the long, three year eleavge it deserved. Tart tangerines, herbs and hay and a seriously salty twang. As expected this is very limited and once it's gone, it's gone. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano Vibe: Fizzy Fun Spritz treatment is given to some Skin Contact Massale selection grapes. Lots of good wine words that I like. You'll like 'em too. Exepect plenty of citrus and florals pushed along by a fine bead of bubbles. All wine is charcuterie and cheese kinda wine to me but this especially so . ABV: 11.5%

wine: Conestabile della Staffa, Rosso Parte Alta 2023
notes: Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Sangiovese Vibe: Earthern Tomato leaf-laden Sangiovese that deserves of a big ol' plate of pasta. If you're too lazy to cook a takeaway pizza will be more than acceptable. Dark cherries and plums with a pleasing earthiness. Cosy. ABV: 13.5%

wine: Conestabile della Staffa, Rosso due Colli 2024
notes: Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Gamay del Trasimeno AKA Grenache Vibe: Liquid Sunshine Gamay del Trasimeno is apparently what the rest of the world calls Grenache. Gosh, the Italians love to make things confusing. I'll give 'em a pass 'cos the wines are always bloody delicious. Old vines here. Signature plush red fruit meeting Italian herbs and a touch of spice. Drinkability is suitably high and this will give the very best Langhe Rossos a good run for the money. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Sangiovese Vibe: Liquid Sunshine The Italians are the king of rosé. Offering depth and serious flavor that most pale pinks simply don't have. Strawberry fruited with a touch of Sangiovese spice, there's herbal scrub and a little grip that makes the mind wander to days spent in a Trattoria. Carbonara would be an obvious choice, but I reckon you could throw pretty much anything at this and it'd still hold its own. ABV: 12%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Malvasia Vibe: Tonic-like In a word, delicious. IMO the unrivaled skinsy offering at this price point, There's been three months of skin soaking yet this steers clear of cloying and chewy. So much freshness, so much aromatic appeal, so much fun. It's giving big peach iced tea vibes. Steal. ABV: 11%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano Vibe: Wild Radioactive in colour this is about as pleasing as macerations come. Pink grapefruit and orange oil dominate upfront whilst spice and dried florals shine in the finish. There is something about rustic Italian wines that just tick all the boxes for me, price included. ABV: 12%

wine: Conestabile della Staffa, Mosso Rosato NV
notes: Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Sangiovese Vibe: Refreshing Rosato is a word that instantly has me salivating. Lovely redcurrant fruit with that signature herbal twang the Italians do so well. Clean and crisp on the finish means with this on hand it will always be Apero hour. Refreshing as hell. ABV: 11.5%

wine: Conestabile della Staffa, Mosso Bianco NV
notes: Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Grechetto, Malvasia Vibe: Hydrating Easy as you like. We've got all the pithy citrus and crisp green apples on show atop a gentle fizz. What more could you want? Well, some nice almond skin bitters on the back end make this even moreish. Can summer hurry along pls. ABV: 11%
Place: Umbria, Italy EVOO from ancient, UNESCO protected olive trees. Need I go on?

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Vermentino Vibe: Staple Ideal white wine. You need to have one of these in the fridge at all times. In case of emergencies, u know? Ripe citrus and stone fruit meet salty minerality and a sprinkling of fresh herbs, with enough funk and intrigue to appease your nattiest friend. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Sangiovese Vibe: Winner Half freshie, half serious-y, 100% delish. This bottling brings out all the good things about Sangiovese (of which there are many) - juicy red and black fruit, a touch of earth, a hint of leather. A smooth and velvety winter warmer. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Vernaccia Rossa Vibe: Chiller Vin de soif, or vino di sete (I guess?) par excellence, or per excellenza (I guess?). This is simultaneously juicy and light but with a bit of heft. The fruit veers between red and black, full of crunchy strawberries and luscious cherries. Chuck this in the fridge for half an hour and you're laughing. ABV: 13%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Ciliegiolo Vibe: Pet Nat + Friends Pink fizz, name something better. A proper explosion of raspberries and strawberries, juicy and light but flinty and mineral at the same time. With a touch of funk, this is definitely one for the natty-heads. Which is you, right? Right. ABV: 12%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano Vibe: Pet Nat + Friends Apero wine with a tonne of personality. Fruity and funky but above all, gluggable. Zesty citrus peel lends a note of freshness, while apples and apricots bring the fruit side of things. So light you could send the whole bottle without even noticing. U've been warned. ABV: 10.5%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Canaiolo + Ciliegiolo + Gamay Vibe: Delicious A nice little traditionally Umbrian bottling, for a nice little price. Ripe red fruit combine with a slightly green, herbaceous note that keeps things fresh, with a cleansing minerality coming through later on. Yum. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano + Malvasia + Grechetto Vibe: Textured Grapes for this bottling come from the oldest vines on the Tiberi estate, some of which are 150 years old. Sheesh! A quick two day bath on skins has this hovering in that elusive territory between a textured white and an orange wine, but tbh, must we stick a label on it? Stone and tropical fruits co-mingle on the palate with some Mediterranean herbs and searing acid. Punchy and intriguing. ABV: 13%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano + Grechetto + Verdello Vibe: Unique Pistarello loosely translates to 'off-piste' (give or take a nuance or two), which is a decent way of describing this one. A unique mash-up of varieties and flavours, there's juicy mango fruit and orange blossom florals, with a herbal edge that keeps you guessing. Dry and refreshing but still with a bit of oomph in terms of body. Not much like it around, try this if you're easily bored. ABV: 11%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Gamay + Ciliegiolo Vibe: Chiller We're in juice-bomb territory here, just in time for spring (well, almost). Fermentation is done in steel before ageing in fibreglass, so this is elegant, light and fresh. Plums, cherries and a cooling menthol hit make this an ideal candidate for a little chill before you start splashing it about. Is it too early for a BBQ? ABV: 12%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano + Grechetto Vibe: Summery Lip-smacking. The fruit here is ripe and tropical, present but not overpowering. Mangos, pineapples and juicy peaches take centre stage, with a salty finish and a sprinkling of herbs. Far more complex and interesting than the modest price tag might suggest. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Gamay + Ciliegiolo Vibe: Pet Nat + Friends Bottles like this don't stand a chance against me. Supremely drinkable, but that doesn't mean it's lacking in complexity. Red berries and spice marry with a vegetal undertone and cracking acidity to create a lively, smashable, fun bottle. ABV: 11%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano di Toscana Vibe: Pet Nat + Friends Apero hour, anyone? This is the ideal fizzer to start your night off with. 100% Trebbiano di Toscana, hand-harvested and direct pressed. It's bone dry and crisp as a freshly pressed shirt. Refreshment factor = off the charts. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Piedmont, Italy Grape: Nebbiolo Vibe: Sublime When Langhe Nebb is on, it can often drink just as well as many a Barolo. This is on. Another vintage down and things just keep getting better. Chiselled, thought-provoking. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Piedmont, Italy Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Stunner Tense and generous without the shackles of oak weighing her down. This is Primo Chard. A tough but delicious blind there is something a little savoury and herbal on the back end that hints at it's Italian roots. ABV: 13%

Place: Piedmont, Italy Grape: Dolcetto Vibe: Classico Dolcetto purchased from the Veglio's in Diana d'Alba. DOCG territory. Prime fruit. Something to whet the appetite with before diving into the Nebb. Structured, pure fruited and elegant. Raised in stainless and only lightly sulphured for pure pleasure.
Place: Piedmont, Italy Grape: Barbera Vibe: Classico Benchmark. Probably about as good as Barbera gets. ABV: 13%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural, lighter Old vine Gamay on pink granite. Raspberries and roses. Salt and stones. Rustically charming and punching well above its weight, this is a true natural icon. Despite the warmth of 2022, it has no shortage of energy. After a short rest, it’s tasting better than ever and will continue to satisfy the patient for many years to come. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural, lighter Free run juice and as such the most ethereal wine coming from Mr Ducroux’s modest cellar. Bottled young, this shines a striking purple in the glass with a captivating nose of wild berries and spice. Feisty in its freshness this transports you straight to the Lyonnaise bistro of your dreams. Once it’s gone, it’s gone. ABV: 12%
Place: Jura, France Grape: Ploussard Vibe: Delicate The more delicate ying to the Chamade yang. One of each should do the Ploussard trick.
Place: Jura, France Grape: Ploussard Vibe: Pretty One of those wines that disappears from the bottle/glass in record time, but not from the memory. Darker and more seductive than your reg.

Place: Jura, France Grape: Pinot Vibe: Bright Iron-rich and brambly fruited. This is an untamed, widly charming expression of Pinot that is so unique. Fruit comes off a plot planted in the 1950s on grey marl. Blink and you'll miss it.

Place: Ardeche, France Grape: Gamay + Pinot Noir Vibe: Vibrant Here Gamay takes a short and sweet bath in the free run juice from the 'Adam Contre le Beefsteack'. Deeper in colour and with a little more heft than 2022. Still Sage though so expect crunchy, bright fruit with a devilishly moreish lick of acid. Gamay bringing a mineral core, Pinot supporting with it fruit! ABV: 11%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Layered Oof. Enviable hype around these and for good reason. Reflecting the year we've got a ripe, rounded Chardonnay with a lick of flinty reduction and that pleasing Jurassic vein of acidity that I crave. Limited AF. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Slovakia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: High Energy I like Chardonnay. I like fizzy. I like this. A short skin soak extracts lots of tropical and citrus fruit. This starts with the aforementioned aromatics before a creamy palate takes over. This is so well made I'd much rather drink this than quite a fair bit of Champagne. Honestly reckon this might age a treat too. ABV: 11 %

Place: Strekov, Slovakia Grape: Gruner Veltliner Vibe: Textural, Natural Gruner with a little oxidative twist! Sign me up. You get the classic bright citrus and white pepper notes but with a hint of complexity from a smidgen of aging under flor. The crown cap is deceiving but deliberate. Chosen to trap in a small amount of intentional reduction. Decant and marvel at notes of salted nuts, honey and pears. This is both uniquely delicious and utterly approachable. It would definitely slap alongside some festive fare too. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Rhone, France Grape: Syrah Vibe: ELITE Rare as. Not your typical Côte-Rôtie. We've got the typicity we want but this has been handled gently, in a way we don't often see around here, one that I'm very much into. Exceptional farming and a gentle approach in the cellar are still considered somewhat avant-garde on these steep slopes. Thibaud lets the fruit express itself and express itself it does. Crushed rock, pepper, spice and both wild fruit and florals. This has that beautiful Rhone rusticity (a teeny tiny touch of brett?), adding complexity without going into feral territory. There i

wine: Maison des Hauts-Baigneux, Chenin Blanc 'Clos des Brancs' 2022
notes: Place: Loire Valley, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Intense The Chenin vines here have been on the registry since the Middle Ages. Flex much? Warming and powerful thanks to the vineyard's southern exposure, but it never tips into flabby territory - the ripe fruit and almond notes are impeccably counteracted by mouthwatering salinity and freshness. ABV: 12%

Place: Rhone, France Grape: Syrah + Viogner Vibe: Light + Bright Mainly Syrah (50% direct press, 50% whole bunch) with a good fifth being made up of Viogner. They are co-fermented in the increasingly fashionable trompette method for a lithe, lifted red that is dangerously drinkable. Sour cherry and orange peel dominate before a lively floral finish. An utter joy to drink. Load up. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Rhone, France Grape: Viogner Vibe: Citrus + Spice Whole bunch crushed and a two-week maceration before a little snooze in 500L oak and amphora. Expect a heady nose of bergamot and woodsy spice. The palate is nicely mineral with well-integrated tannins and a creamy texture. How Thibaud has managed to make Viogner taste this good I'll never know! Here for it though. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Mornington Peninsula, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Stunning This single vineyard brings out such a savoury expression of Pinot it'll have you firmly in the old world. Yes, we've got ripe cherry fruit but underneath there is so much spice and autumnal goodness. Already developed this is very much a go-er in the short term. ABV: 13%

Place: Mornington Peninsula, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Fresh + Ripe Typically full-flavored new world Chard that is reined in by a more old-world acidity. At once both creamy and zesty this is heavy-handed in the citrus and stone fruit departments. Plenty going on now with plenty more going on if given plenty of time. ABV: 13%

Place: Western Cape, South Africa Grape: Grenache Noir Style: Classic, fragrant Another superb '22 coming off schist soil to gives us a more herbal-leaning expression. Sappy and savoury there is plenty to unpack under the core of plush fruit from the bush vine Grenache. The long umami finish makes this a good candidate for the dinner table. Classy. ABV: 13%

Place: Western Cape, South Africa Grape: Grenache Noir Style: Classic, fragrant These 2022 releases from Momento are singing atm. Juicy yet refined from Grenache is a balance that can be challenging to get right but this exceeds on all fronts. From a plot at higher elevation this is full of wild strawberries, a pleasing acidity and a soft frame of tannin. Hard not to like this. ABV: 13%

Place: Beaujolais , France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Natural but a classic Coming off an old vine plot in the Côte du Py with southwest exposure and a very shallow layer of granitic topsoil. Geeky bits aside, this is probably my favourite 2023 from the whole of the Beaujolais. Reflecting the vintage there is fresher fruit than recent warm years whilst still deep and brooding. A driving minerality, fine tannin, and dense salinity hint at a beautiful life ahead. Makes me crave a rustic meal in Lyon. A true icon. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Umbria, Italy Grape: Trebbiano Spoletino Vibe: Elite Where does one begin when trying to describe the thought-provoking bottles of Paolo Bea? The local clone of Trebianno is trained high above the ground, often wrapping itself around trunks and branches of trees woven into the vineyards. Fruit is harvested late and is macerated on skins for a deeply hued delight. Expect wild herbs and plenty of citrus pith among a whole myriad of other notes that seem to evolve alongside this ever-changing wine. If you're into this sort of wine this is hard to beat. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Kent, England Grape: Pinot Meunier Vibe: Energetic From Jules and Lucy’s first harvest. Meunier, aged in barrel for 10 months before 30 months on the lees. All those English Sparklings winning awards are rarely made with grapes as healthy as we have here. Ham Street go above and beyond in both the vines and the cellar, and you can really taste it. Fizz with actual personality. Aromatically on-point, gorgeously racy and with a moreish mouthfeel. Pour this for me blind and I’d be heading straight to the cult growers of the Val de la Marne. 2.5g/l dosage. No fining, no filtration, no added

Place: Kent, England Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Energetic The last pick of Sophie's Pinot, de-stemmed with just a week of gently soaking on skins. It rested in glass demijohn before being bottled in completely reused glass. Red cherry fruit, a pleasing herbaceousness, and little peppery spice. Delicate but so alive. Barely any made. ABV: 10.7%

Place: Auvergne, France Grape: Viogner + 10% Muscat Vibe: Refreshing The Viognier macerates in the juice of the Muscat for roughly 10 days. This is intensely tropical, all pineapple and papaya at first. Things then flesh out into more stone fruit and savoury herbs. Some nice tannin but nothing chewy or weird. Insanely drinkable, and aptly named. ABV: 10%

Place: Yarra Valley, Australia Grape: Mornington Peninsula Vibe: Sultry 'Sur la Crete' refers to the hillcrest vineyard this site is perched on in Mornington Peninsula, a departure from Dappled's usual Yarra Valley bottlings, and a triumphant one at that. The style here is richer and more powerful than the other Dappled reds, delivering purity of fruit as well as real depth and complexity. The aromas are classic Mornington vibes - Morello cherry, plum, beetroot and earthy forest floor. Classy stuff. ABV: 13%

The doctor will c u now! Heh. The doctor in this case being Manuel Girard, former c onnoisseur of medical devices turned current connoisseur of Gamay. With holdings in Fleurie and Morgon and such esteemed neighbours as Lapierre and Dutraive, Manuel's built himself quite the cracking estate. The scientific nouse is evident in the wines, which are precise, pure and clean as a whistle - complex, brooding Gamays and a truly beautiful Beaujolais Blanc, too often relegated to the realm of the afterthought. We're still gobsmacked we managed to be the first to bring these wines to the UK, which is goo

wine: Jean-Claude Lapalu x  Domaine Belluard Feu Follet Brut Zero 2019
notes: Place: Savoie, France Grape: Gringet Vibe: Vibrant A true one-off. Jean-Claude Lapalu and Dominique Belluard, who we sadly lost in 2021, were very close. After Dominique's tragic passing, Jean-Claude bought some of the 2019 Mont Blanc Brut Zero from the estate to finish aging and disgorgement at his cellar in the Beaujolais. This is a fitting tribute. Textured and hazy as any Pet-Nat should be but with all the class of a more high-end fizz. There is so much to unpack and so much to enjoy. Plenty of pithy citrus, vibrant acidity and long saline finish. Best Pet-Nat I've tried? It's up there. AB

Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Dreamy Sous la Velle is a terroir down the slope in Meursault but still with real freshness and lots of complexity This lieu-dit really offers something so hedonistic that I just adore. A mesmerising wine where you'll never want the bottle to end. ABV: 13%

wine: Pierre-Henri Rougeot, Pommard 'La Rue au Port' 2022
notes: Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Concentrated Concentrated doesn't even come close. This has all the structure and plummy fruit you want from your Pommard whilst also retaining plenty of digestibility. Criminally good. I could think of a lot worse to drink during the upcoming festivities. ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Rich, Textural Lots of that classic Chassagne richness here, especially in this vintage. Everything you want from your Chardonnay has been dialed up. Rip this open and watch this unfurl throughout an evening. A meditative wine. ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Fresh Red fruited and mineral with an almost blood orange quality on the finish. Guessing the freshness here is due to the exposition and this is what I'm going hard for both in the short and long term. ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elegant Powerful yet elegant Pinot from a true master of their craft. Whole clusters see only neutral barrels for the purpose of purity. Round with velvet soft tannin, this is good to go now but will require a little decant to show at its best. Needless to say, the cellar potential here is a scary thought... ABV: 13%

wine: Domaine Marc Colin, Saint Aubin 1er Cru 'En Remilly' 2023
notes: Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural What a beauty. More class and power from Marc Colin, no surprises there. Sweet citrus, white florals, fresh bread and beeswax all come jumping out the glass from the get go, framed by ripping salinity and racy acidity. Wow is a word that comes to mind. ABV: 13.5%

Gross but not gross, if you know what I mean? In a world of macerated wine which often flatters to deceive some producers rise far, far above. On a faithful afternoon in November 2023 we stumbled into the cellar of Domaine Gross in Alsace (exact town name is unspellable). Surrounded by spotless amphora and tasting through a range starting with elite grower Champagne level Cremant, dazzling macerations and tonic like Pinot we were all blown away. When you know you know. We're stoked to welcome Vincent and Julie to London for a few days, culminating in a night at Dan's. Get involved. Here are th

wine: .... Parched + Dan's Present: Domaine de l'Iserand
notes: Bienvenue Jeff et Saida! One of the discoveries of 2024 were the seductive wines from Domaine de l'Iserand. Tucked up in the isolated hamlet of Séchère in Saint Joseph they're painstakingly producing some of the most expressive and approachable Rhone wines we've tasted in a long time. We are proud to represent l'Iserand in the UK and stoked to welcome them to London for a few days. Expect textural whites and sultry reds on a wonderful Tuesday night in February. Here are the details: Dan's - 2- 4 Tottenham Rd, N1 4BZ Tuesday 11th Feb 6.30-8.30pm Tickets £25ea 4 wines + light snacks + good vibes
Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural The master of Chablis. Tight, ethereal Chardonnay with incredible drive and poise. Benchmark. ﻿ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural Rare as hen's teeth. You haven’t really drunk Chablis until you’ve tasted Dauvissat. Entry level in name only, from a plot just above Les Clos. This is smoking from a sunkissed vintage. A steal considering this is one of the greats. ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Energetic Vaillons is very much a place we want to be when drinking in Chablis. This is zesty and refreshing with pears and orange zest leading the charge. Backed up by white flowers, baked bread with a pure saline finish. Drinking like a dream atm but time will only serve this well. I don't blame you for popping the cork now though, it's what I'll be doing. ABV: 12%

wine: Si Tu Sais, Côte de Nuits-Villages 'En Chantemerle' 2022
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural Whew! Another primo bottling from Burgundy's latest up and comers. Patrick and Sara use whole bunches judiciously for fruit purity and juiciness while not seeking a ton of stemminess. The fruit here is ripe, sweet and sharp while the texture is supple and soft. Just... yum. ABV: 14.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural Whoever said 'the best things in life are free' had obviously never been to Burgundy. Some things are worth splurging on, you know? This is elite Chardy from Burgundy's new negoce darlings, squeaky clean, fresh and racy. Stupidly limited, be one of the lucky ones. ABV: 13%

wine: Si Tu Sais, Bourgogne Aligoté 'Les Vris' 2022
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Aligoté Vibe: Natural Hot new talent in Burgundy alert, aka time to re-mortgage the house. Heh. Stunning Aligoté, tense and lively, with sage and sea salt mingling with creamy tropical fruit and sizzling acidity. Sheesh. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Alcobaça, Portugal Grape: Castelão Vibe: Glou glou On the more classic side of Espera's range, the Castelão comes from three different plots, with vine age spanning between 50 and 100 years. The grapes see 10 days of maceration with 20% included as whole bunch, which keeps the end product lithe and lifted. There's a thirst-quenching cherry-cola vibe to this with a touch of minerality and a supple texture. Crying out for the ice bucket. ABV: 12.5%
