Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural This cuvée is more about the broody, sultry side of Pinot. No bad thing. Spicy, earthy and full of juicy dark cherries, it's proper moody and deep, ripe for contemplation and ever-evolving. A beauty. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural There's Pinot and then there's Pinot. Guess which one this is? 'Les Bas Liards' is a flat parcel situated close to the river over deep clay and limestone, so there's no shortage of concentration here. The aromatics are more on the meaty, earthy side, but the fruit is just waiting to burst through as soon as you take a sip. Proper acid and structure tie the whole thing up in a delicious, delicious bow. ABV: 13.5%

wine: Maison Skyaasen, Bourgogne Côte d'Or Blanc
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural Old Meursalt vines here, planted over limestone soil resulting in peak depth and complexity. White and citrus fruits abound, with layers of almond and acacia florals that just keep on coming. Finessed as per all things Skyaasen, this punches way above its humble Côte d'Or designation. I love technicalities, especially when they mean that wine this good is priced this well. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural My god. We're seriously on here, like, seriously. Stunning aromatics from the off, with myriad orchard fruits ranging from apples, pears and peach bursting through. The taste is direct, bold and tangy, with a ridiculously long finish. There's a reason people lose their heads over these wines. ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Aligoté Vibe: Natural, textural Another classique 'entry level' wine from a producer that only does elite things. Works for me! Citrusy and floral after the touch of reduction blows off upon opening, the refinement here just builds and builds the longer you wait, if you can wait at all. Sizzling acidity balances perfectly with the full texture and body. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Rhône, France Grape: Syrah Vibe: Stone Cold Classic, Richer Franck’s flagship wine. Fruit comes from century-old vines and this gives us stunning depth, concentration and complexity. Sensational.

Place: Rhône, France Grape: Syrah Vibe: Stone Cold Classic, Richer A young vine cuvee from the King of Cornas that sees no additions at bottling. Precision and vibrant in a way that you rarely see from top producers in these parts. Ethereal and perfumed. Allocated and strictly limited. Get in quick.

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Natural, textural Robinot Chenin. A finer pair of words I'm yet to find. Rich and sumptuous but as ever, kept in line by Robinot's favoured eye-popping acidity. Nectarine fruit combines with caramel, almond and honey for a pretty transcendent drinking experience. ABV: 12%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Pet Nat + Friends Another sparkling stunner from Robinot's mind palace. Directly pressed and fermented in cuve, then 18 months on lees in bottle before disgorgement. The cool vintage has rendered a crispy, crushable expression. This never disappoints, but this is about as good as it gets from my recent, hazy memory. Crying out for apero hour! ABV: 10%

Place: Yarra Valley, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Gorge Dappled making yet another case for Yarra Pinot, as if the point hadn't already been made. The fruit for this one comes from a couple sites across Gladysdale and Macclesfield, and 25% of it goes in as whole bunches. The attention to detail is what sets this apart, with all berries hand-selected and a gentle 15-20 day maceration for soft extraction that still packs a serious punch. Bright, delicate and pure-fruited, cherries and raspberries sit front and centre, with whispers of smoke and spice in the background. Do I need to say anyt

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Cozy A brooding, moody Pinot that makes for a great bottle to crack open for some ponderous, meandering conversation. Smoky and structured, it's got a real tonic-like vibe thanks to crunchy fruit and herbal backbone. Comforting, but sleek and elegant at the same time. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Racy Tense Chardy crackling with energy. The depth and richness here are matched by sizzling acidity, with zesty citrus and stone fruit marrying together perfectly. Chardonnay with real meat on its bones, the way I like it. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Riesling Vibe: Pure Cracking Rizz from the sunnier side of the world. Proper thirst-quenching stuff, with lime fruit taking centre stage and floral notes bringing up the rear. Racy and mineral, this'll sit nicely next to your lobster bisque or your chippie takeaway, whatever your vibe is. ABV: 12%

Place: Yarra Valley, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Special A cuvee dedicated to Ian Marks, who founded Gembrook along with his wife June, the fruit comes from a combination of the oldest and youngest vines on the estate, symbolising the way Ian's legacy will be carried on. Powerful, structured and complex while still emitting the elegance and brightness this area is known for. Tiny amounts made so get it while you can. ABV: 13%

Place: Yarra Valley, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Brooding Single vineyard Pinot from Yellingbo in the Upper Yarra, planted over grey clam loam, somewhat unusual for the area, but which works wonders. The classic Upper Yarra perfume is there, but it's underscored by a denser, deeper palate and gripper tannins than you might normally expect. Which is no bad thing. The boldness of the structure is matched by the intensity strawberry and cherry fruit, and they all combine for a wine that's way greater than the sum of its parts. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Rheingau, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Electric Bright and brimming with citrus. Racy acidity as per all things Riesling and with a super stony finish. Honestly, can't believe that wine this good is this cheap. The biodynamic farming is an added bonus. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Rheingau, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Off Dry Kabinett, but with half of the sugar you'd usually expect, so you're getting a lean and fresh take. The nose is stunning with floral aromatics before you're met with a herbal, stony palate. The perfect poise between rasping acidity and juicy, sweet fruit. Stunner. ABV: 9.5%

Place: Rheingau, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Stony Mineral, saline Riesling that is cooling in its nature. A little hint of that sun-kissed petrol thing the variety is known for too. Everything is integrated so nicely this just flows effortlessly from bottle to glass to mouth. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Rheingau, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Stony An elevated site with slate soil giving us a racy, driving expression that is tightly coiled in its youth but will develop beautifully with time in bottle. Pithy citrus, cooling herbs and a long finish. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Hunter Valley, Australia Grape: Shiraz Vibe: Elegant Beautifully light take on Shiraz, which is essentially the only way I'll drink it. Angus throws 10% whole bunch into each ferment and focuses on super gentle extraction, which is what keeps this bright and lifted. That said, this isn't just juice - there's structure, grip, and a broody, dark-fruited core. ABV: 12.7%

Place: Hunter Valley, Australia Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Precise Searing, direct, linear Chenin. Name me something better? U can't. Fresh and tart-fruited with a banging acid line, it's light n bright while still maintaining a luscious, creamy texture. Can you say bargain? I can. Bargain. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Hunter Valley, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Crowd-pleasing An argument for judicious use of oak if I ever saw one. Gorgeous cedar and smoke notes coming from the wood ageing mingles with a fresh, mineral-led palate, providing the perfect framework for a bouquet of creamy stone fruit. A proper bold, balanced Chardy. This is one that everyone will like, trust me. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Pinot Noir + Trousseau + Poulsard + Gamay + Hyrbids Vibe: Divine Wow, a Jura blend par excellence right here. Tart currants upfront, followed by all the berry fruit. Cherries, raspberries, strawberries, and so on. There is just enough of that rustic earthiness the region's reds do so well. With a modest ABV this is destined for a nice chill and to be drunk with abandon. Steal. ABV: 11%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Mainly Chardonnay + Savagnin Vibe: Lip Smacking You don't get Jura this good at this price point, until now! From a single plot planted with more than a dozen white grape varieties on the hills above Poligny, however, the Savagnin dominates at first, bringing spiced, yellow fruit. Herbal, grassy notes slowly come to the fore before finishing up smoky and salty. Wow.

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Elite From steep slopes surrounded by woodland in the hills of Fleurie. Perfectly poised now but will age with grace over the coming years. ABV: 14% Please note due to scarcity there is limit of one bottle per customer. Multiple orders will be cancelled. Thank you for your understanding.

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Elite A generous and rustic release from Julie's last vintage. The grapes comes from the south and reflects the vintage with it's deep fruit and plush tannin. Delicious now with some hearty fare they love in these neck of the woods. Also, would do well with some further time to snooze in the bottle. Dealers choice. ABV: 12.5% Please note due to scarcity there is limit of one bottle per customer. Multiple orders will be cancelled. Thank you for your understanding.

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Aligote Vibe: Advanced, Elite Same deal with the other intuition bottles but this time around it's Aligote that gets the extended aging. Rare as, especially here on this sorry little island. Sunk one of these in France and haven't stopped thinking about it since. This is a densely concentrated, brooding expression unlike any other Aligote. Serious stuff. ABV: 15%

Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Special Whew, this is proper. A collab between Sam Guy, an Aussie winemaker, and Staffelter Hof's Jan, who traded off harvests at each other's domaines. Two brains are better than one! The importer received this bottling four years ago but sat on it until now, believing in its crazy potential. And wow, is it singing now. Good things come to those who wait, etc. This is everything that's good about Riesling, dialled up to 200. Biting acidity, tart fruit, pronounced aromatics, complex petrol notes - the whole nine yards. No regrets on buying this one,

Place: Badacsony, Hungary Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural Yes yes yes. I love this expression of Pinot, walking the tightrope between fruit-driven and pleasantly herbaceous. This bottling comes from only the best bunches at the top of the vineyard. So drinkable you'll wonder how the bottle went so fast. I love atypical regions 'cos it means prices are low but quality is high. Where else would you find exceptional Pinot at this price! ABV: 11%

Place: Badacsony, Hungary Grape: Pinot Gris Vibe: Natural + Tasty Oooft! Plenty of that unmistakable Bencze energy. Starting slightly reductive before diving into a whole medley of fruit, florals and minerality. Lemon sherbet and white peaches etched into your memory from the first sip. This feels almost Styrian. The ferment went long and slow, not quite eating all the sugar, so technically 5g of residual is left alongside a little spritz. Probably quite useful to brace all the acidity. It's like a little nod to the Plus Range of Tscheppe. A must taste this summer. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Badacsony, Hungary Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Natural István loves the wines of the Loire Valley, and guess what us too! So much so that he thought he'd plant a little Chenin in Hungary to see what happens. I'm so thankful he did. Directly pressed into old burgundy barrels that he didn't top up for a few months so they aged under flor. They were then blended into larger oak and this time topped up for another year. The slight flor aging is nothing to be scared of, we're not in oxy territory here, it just adds a nice salty component. That is on top of the multi-layered citrus, lanolin, an

Place: Loire, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Taut + Mineral After a day where easily a hundred-plus wines were tasted, this stuck out like a sore thumb. Its energy and freshness left a lasting impression, I can still practically taste this. Sauvignon often leaves a lot to be desired, overt in its aromatics but thin and a bit gross. This couldn't be further away. Crisp, taut, and mineral. New flavours reveal themselves with each sip if you give this a bit of time and air. Pristine exotic fruit, smoked herbs, pops of white flowers, and a steely finish. ABV: 11.8%

wine: .... Parched + Dan's x Tutto Wines: The Wines of Cantina Giardino
notes: That's right, baby! A whole evening dedicated to the wines of Cantina Giardino. Do we spoil you or what? Whilst they won't be in town, we have the next best thing. Fred from Tutto Wines, aka their UK importer, will be on hand to run through these unique, thirst-quenching bottles. In case you're not in the know (and shame on u if u aren't) Cantina Giardino is the inspiring project from Antonio and Daniela De Gruttola. Seeking out old vineyards in high in the hills of Campania, they champion and preserve the region’s native varieties, old vines, and the traditional ways of tending them. One of t

Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Intense Vin Jaune par excellent. Six years' ageing under flor brings out an explosion of nuttiness and curried spice. Crying out for comté, as am I. ABV: 14.8%

wine: Domaine Amélie Guillot, Arbois Rouge Poulsard 2022
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Poulsard Vibe: Delicate Enticing aromatics are the calling card of Guillot's reds, and the Poulsard is a prime example. Crunchy, pepper red fruit aromas combine perfectly with an enviable freshness on the palate. Serious, serious value to be found here. ABV: 12%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Oxy Oxy Savagnin done right, there's nothing better. This spent four years under flor, and the resulting bottling is intensely mineral, with cumin and fenugreek aromatics adding to the experience. Carve up some comté and go to town. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Salivating What's better than some elusive Jura gear? Not much. Thomas cut his teeth with Tissot, before giving Alice Bouvot a hand in her cellar. When not at work, he can be found tending his west-facing vines, a real boon in the days of climate change. Yellow citrus, nutty spice, and notes of honey. Liquid electricity. Savagnin of the highest order. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Margaret River, Australia Grape: Cabernet Sauvignon Vibe: Classic Cabernet isn't our usual thing so when we get one on the shelves it must be pretty good. This is from a cool site, and far from overworked, meaning this is about as elegant as Cabernet gets. Resolved, gentle tannins and lightly framed red fruits with a great lengthy finish. ABV: 13%

Place: Margaret River, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural Fleshy stone fruit and lots of zesty citrus on the nose. The palate is nice 'n' creamy from a bit of careful lees work. Find me someone who doesn't like this. The ultimate people pleaser. ABV: 13%

wine: .... Parched + LC Selections present: Salon de Dan's
notes: About time we threw our own Salon, don't u think? On the 20th of October we'll be having a right knees-up to showcase the direct import portfolio we've been grafting so hard on. For the last two years we've been running all over France and Australia to find the best new talents in wine, and now we're gonna share them with u. We'll even be joined by a few of the winemakers themselves. Blessed much? We'll be running three sessions - trade only from 12-2.45pm, then we open the doors to do gods work in two further sessions, from 3-5.45pm then 6-8.45pm. Your ticket gets you in the door for all u ca

Place: Jura, France Grape: Pinot Noir + Trousseau Vibe: Natural , lighter You'll never guess what this was aged in? This is the elite red offering from Philippe. A pitch-perfect blend of Pinot + Trouseau. Sour cherry fruit, earthen tones, and a mineral core. I simply can't get enough of this Chatillion gear. ABV: 13%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural , lighter Mainly Pinot here so expect plenty of earthen cherries alongside a nicely structured mineral core. These Chatillion wines are the real deal. If you've yet to get acquainted then this should be your starting point. Such a soulful wine that one bottle is never enough. ABV: 12%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Textured + Vibrant Very good Chenin, very good price considering these vines used to belong to a Mr Joly. A long, slow, gentle pressing extracts glorious orchard fruit with a bit of citrus and white flowers mingling around for good measure. Honeyed and mineral just as we've come to expect from these parts too. Add 2 cart, thank me later. ABV: 12.4%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Saline One of those wines that has it all. Salty, acidic, crunchy and nutty. Everything you want your Burgundy to be apart from the fact it is hyper limited. We only got 3 bottles :( Salivating stuff if you’re quick. ABV: 11%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Soulful Chris headed up the the Burgundy office for a certain Kermit Lynch so it's fair to say, he knows what he's doing. A gentle 3-week maceration for some exceptionally sourced fruit off a little southwest-facing slope in the village of Givry, 30km from Beaune. So pure, and ethereal. Good fruit that hasn't been overworked. Typicity to a T. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Juicy Gamay and Granite is hardly a new combination, yet rarely do we see it in the form of something pink. Shame, 'cos this is an absolute banger. I opened this for a glass and stayed for the bottle. So good I literally ran out and bought another to continue the party. Stunning structure with vivid citrus fruit ranging from lime through to grapefruit. Aromatics and acidity are both off the charts. Complexity and drink-ability combine for what is honestly a contender for my wine of the year. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Sylvaner Vibe: Natural, textural, It recently dawned on me that we don't have any straight Sylvaner online and I had to put a stop to that real quick. On recent visits to Alsace, this grape has often been outshining its Riesling counterparts with ease. I'm big into this expression. Orange blossom aromatics but with a herbal, savoury side that is hard to ignore. A tiny bit of phenolic grip keeps you coming back for more, and more, and more. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Parched + Wink Lorch Present: Jura Wine 10 Years On
notes: Join us, and more importantly Wink Lorch, for a later summer afternoon on the Dalston Riviera. We're honoured that Wink Lorch, the definitive voice on all things Jura, is coming to present her latest book Jura Wine Ten Years On, a companion volume to her acclaimed book Jura Wine. Tickets include a talk from Wink with 3 elite glasses of the region's very best, a copy of Jura Wine Ten Years On, and light snacks. After the event, everyone is welcome to join in the festivities where Wink will be sticking around to chat all things Jura and sell/sign her other books. We will continue the party, the

wine: .... Parched, LC Selections + Liberty Wines Present: Pinosity
notes: OOFT, here we go! We're stoked to bring you Pinosity, a tasting of sublime, Godly juice from the Southern Hemisphere (Better Hemisphere). We'll be joined by no less than Paul Lipscombe of Sailor Seeks Horse, one of our own, and the newly crowned Queen of Pinot, Mel Chester of Giant Steps. Many of you will have fond, if hazy, memories of the last time Mel was in town, and combined with the elite level Tassie Pinot of Sailor Seeks, its sure to be a repeat. We'll be further joined on the night by Sal and Jack from Stella's who'll be knocking out tartare in nori. Times! Here are the details: Dan's

Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Macabeu Vibe: Tropical Old vine Macabeu that's been macerated for maximum drinking pleasure. Most of the French wouldn't dare to lift a finger in August. Melissa & Laurent are built different. This was picked on the 5th to ensure plenty of freshness despite the ever-rising temperatures in these parts. This vintage is a cracker. High-toned tropical fruit, fleshy texture and just enough grip. The finish is super salty. One of those wines where one glass is never enough. ABV: 11%

Place: Roussillon, France Grape: Merlot Vibe: Ethereal Merlot from the Roussillon is not something I'd usually be getting excited about so you'll just have to trust me on this one. This is so lithe and ethereal that it's almost hard to believe this is from this deep south. A gentle, four-day maceration coaxes out a pretty side of Merlot I've not seen before. Dark cherry fruit is tamed by tight and fine tannin's and we've got plenty of driving acidity too. The finish is almost chinotto-like. If only all Merlot was made like this. Zero zero. ABV: 12%

wine: Vin de LaGamba, Frauen Power Vol 6 2024
notes: Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Dornfelder+ Pinot Noir + Müller-Thurgau + Riesling Vibe: Fresh as Vol 6 of my favourite fizzing red returns. German Lambrusco vibes. Not only defying categories, but also normal levels of flavour you’d expect from a German pet-nat. Insanely good! Insanely refreshing! Insanely fun. Juicy fruit and plenty of herbal intrigue are carried along by fine little bubbles. One for all occasions. ABV: 10.5%

Place: Kent, England Grape: Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier, Bacchus Vibe: Bright Fizzy, fruity and fun from the English OGs. Wild red fruit backed up with elderflower florals and almonds. Pimm's move over, we have a new ultimate summer refresher. ABV: 10.4%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Savagnin Rose Vibe: Pretty A pink-skinned Savagnin mutation that has been soaked on its skin to extract all the good stuff. The floral, tropical side of Savagnin is really on show here working its magic alongside that pleasing line of acid we all know and love. Peaches, pineapple, and a pretty floral lift. ABV: 13%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Elite Chambolle’s highest and coolest vineyard site thrives in hotter vintages like we had in '18. Coming into a sweet spot now with the tannin heading towards velvet and with a little tertiary charm starting to show it's baby-faced self. That being said, if you can hold onto this for a few more years, you'll reap the rewards. The 2022 too is thriving in the warmer vintage, this will need a little longer to really do its thing but when it does, you'll be in heaven. Collectors item. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Trousseau Vibe: Lifted Jeesh. Another supremely elegant bottling. Raspberries and strawberries this time, with a touch more depth in the form of herbs and a hint of cedar. Pure tonic juice on the palate, this will slip down way too easily. Poised, elegant, but above all, smashable. We've got F all of it too, so jump on this while you can. ABV: 12%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Poulsard Vibe: Juicy This is everything that's good about Poulsard hailing from a vintage that's set to go down in the history books. A proper strawberry bomb, a touch reductive at first but pleasantly so. A little stemminess on the nose that blows away to a lithe palate of wild, sweet fruit and a long, savoury finish. Elegant and lifted but with a whisper of structured backbone too. Undeniably delish. ABV: 12%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Lively Negoce fruit this time, this is a deeper, broodier expression of Gamay than you sometimes find. Fruit swings from red to black, with sweet, spicy cherries and blackberries all in the mix. A hint of cooling menthol brings us home. Gamay this good at this price should be illegal. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Styria, Austria Grape: Zweigelt + Blauer Wildbacher + Blaufränkisch Vibe: Herbal How good is Rosé? Plenty of tart cranberry fruit and a whole heap of herbs mingling alongside some subtle Zweiglt white pepper spice. Plenty of time in old oak softens out any harsh edges, and the result is what might be my favourite pink drink in recent memory. Light on the ABV and high on acidity, this is destined for good times and good weather. ABV:11.5%

Place: Styria, Austria Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural The fact this is considered entry-level by Sepp and Maria is laughable. This is one of those wines that just has it all. Beautiful fruit, minerality, enough aromatic charm, and a searing acidity that carries us into an almost never-ending finish. An honest, and soulful expression of their Styrian terroir. ABV:10.5%

Place: Styria, Austria Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, textural Recently I went on a little jolly to Austria and I have come back head over heels in love with Morillion AKA Chardonnay. Styria in particular with its stupid steep slopes and stony soils makes distinctly mineral examples that has me salivating as I type. This has an addictive energy about it. Here in the UK we are guilty of drinking our wines far too young, thankfully for both you and I, the aging has been conveniently done for us. Sepp is a true master of his craft. Drink this, you'll see why. ABV:13%

wine: Domaine Hubert Lamy, Saint-Aubin 1er Cru 'Les Frionnes' 2021
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Classic, textural An elite producer doing elite things. Frionnes shares the same Kimmeridgian soils as you'll find further north in Chablis. This is evidently clear with plenty of oyster-shell minerality and a wonderfully chiselled structure. Masterful use of oak, 20% new, sees us out nicely. ABV: 13%

Place: Tavel, Rhône Grape: Grenache, Cinsault, Carignan, Clairette Rose Vibe: Vibey Life affirming ' rosé'. Probably best not to think of this as having a category, it is that mind bending. Aroma and flavour of a red, texture of a white, grip of a macerated wine. A remarkable assault of crushed flowers, dried herbs and spices from far away places. An 8-day whole bunch maceration of fruit from a single parcel planted on white galets. Grapes are pressed separately and juices blended before aging for 1 year in barrels and cement tanks. Due to the limited quantites, we've decided to share the love

wine: Etienne Seignovert, Le Murmure De L'Eau 2025
notes: Place: Ardèche, France Grape: Jacquère + Marsanne Vibe: Mineral At first, this is all about citrus and white florals but as it opens up we start to see a more tropical side. Salinity and tension run right throughout. Etienne can do no wrong. This is freshness personified. ABV: 11%

wine: Etienne Seignovert & Thibaud Capellaro, Ombre & Lumière 2023
notes: Place: Ardèche, France Grape: Grenache + Syrah + Viognier Vibe: Fruit bomb When two talented winemakers join forces, you know it's gonna be a winner. This goes above and beyond. A full-on fruit bomb, with the usual cherries and strawberries before leaning into passion-fruit and peach. Juicy body, zippy acidity, and a lovely long finish. Chill this down, drink fast. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Gippsland, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Stunning Another A+ bottling from the king that is Bill Downie, who seems to turn everything he touches to gold. The light-hearted, playful counterpart to the dark n moody Gippsland, there's layers and layers of red fruit, violet florals and orange peel. Yet another belter. ABV: 13%

Place: South Australia Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Mind-changing I normally need to be talked into drinking a Sauvignon, but not this one. It's got the classic florals, for sure, but the fruit is what sets it apart - lemon, grapefruit and guava, with a touch of spice coming from the old oak. Juicy and tangy with gorgeous acidity, there's a brininess on the finish that makes it hard to put the glass down. ABV: 12.5%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Collector's Item The Wait vineyard was planted in the 1940s, so there's a fair bit of concentration going on here. The most structural of their single-site Grenache bottlings, this is dark and earthy, with wintery root vegetables bringing up the rear. One to cellar. Wait is the operative word here, if you can. ABV: 14.3%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: World Class Grenache is where Aphelion all began, so their single plot range is among their best offerings. They've farmed the Brini plot since their first vintage, and its the most rounded and intense wine they make. This is 100% whole bunch that sees a quick spell in French oak. Rich, dark plum fruit unfolds in the mouth with a backbone of earthiness, and the sandy soils bring lifted aromatics full of flowers and spice. One to brood over. ABV: 13.9%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Delicious 85 year old vines, hiya! Suitably concentrated and perfectly ripe, this is silky and luxurious, full of crunchy redcurrants and spice. Only small batches of this wine are made, so count yourself lucky if you get your paws on one. ABV: 13.8%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Juicy Described as 'furiously aromatic' by the winemakers themselves, this is pizza wine if I ever saw it. Light as air and full of juicy, spiced cherry and plum notes, this is crying out for a little chill and a call to Dominos. Or a more primo pizza provider. Whatever u like. ABV: 13%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Mataro Vibe: Fresh Proper pale rosé, also known as the only thing I want to drink when the sun comes peekin out. Floral and lightly spicy, the fruit runs the spectrum from blood orange to grapefruit to cranberry, with a good lick of acid to finish things off. As refreshing as a dip in the lido, if you're that way inclined. ABV: 12.9%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Blanc Vibe: Summery Part aged in French oak and part in stainless, this is a vibrant dream. Lively and fresh with citrus fruit aplenty and a hint of gingery spice, this is food-friendly wine par excellence. Get that lobster on the go. ABV: 12.9%

Place: South Australia Grape: Syrah Vibe: Different Two separate parcels joining forces here - one from Adelaide Hills with 50% whole bunches and one from McLaren Vale done 100% carbonic whole bunch. Two pretty different wines that combine to make something even greater than the sum of their parts. Kalamata olives, blue fruits and graphite come from the former, with the latter bringing florals and herbs. Plenty to see here, and plenty to like. ABV: 12.1%

Place: South Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Punchy Earthy and spicy, this rides along the black-red fruit line with elegance. Rose petals come out if you give it a little time and space, and the palate is rich and supple, yet balanced by zippy acidity. Think summer fruits but with autumn leaves in the background. You know? ABV: 13%

Place: South Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Layered Les Fruits' take on a White Burgs, but with a South Australian price tag. So far so good! There's more flavours in this than you can shake a stick at - clementines, peach and apple on the fruit front, subtle elements of creamy vanilla and a Manuka honey-esque floralness, all hanging out in perfect balance. Sheesh. ABV: 13.4%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Fun Biodynamically farmed Grenache from McLaren Vale, aged in 3rd fill French oak. Supple and spiced Grenache that has such generoisty on the palate, especially for the price. The fruit is ripe and plum-y yet still with a nice bit of crunch. Super versatile, super price, what's not to love? Midweek sorted. ABV: 14.7%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Chill In the words of the winemaker, this is Chardonnay intended ' to be drunk in a DJ booth at 3am'. Is that how the kids are drinking these days? Been a while since I saw 3am. Either way, you can see what he's getting at - this is a fun spin on an old classic. Which is not to say it's not still a proper quality Chardy. Fresh and elegant, with a portion aged in new oak for texture and intrigue, this has white peaches and a nutty edge for all round delicious drinking. ABV: 11.8%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Crunchy A Grenache that actually delivers the oft discussed but rarely accomplished 'pinosity', aka, it drinks like a Pinot. Seriously enticing and fresh, with rose aromatics, peppercorns and blood orange at first, unfolding into sharp raspberry and cherry notes on the palate. Super-fine tannins give this a gorgeous silky texture and a lingering finish. ABV: 13.9%

wine: Artefact #1 Tempranillo, Finca Venta de Don Quijote 2024
notes: Place: Toledo, Spain Grape: Tempranillo Vibe: Mellow A cute label + something that actually tastes good on the inside? A combination that's all too rare nowadays, but these Artefact numbers tick both boxes. An almost brandy-esque opening with boozy, jammy plums and cherries plus a cooling hit of menthol and a solid tannin structure make this a punchy, interesting red that's eminently smashable. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Shiraz Vibe: ~European A Rhone-esque take on Aussie Shiraz. R u intrigued? Dense and highly concentrated, brooding and meaty, with blackcurrant fruit, Mediterranean herbs and violet florals. A touch of spice and coal-like earthiness complete the picture. Tall dark and handsome, you might say. ABV: 13.5%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Pure A real wine of place. Site-specific cinnamon notes top off ripe raspberry and blueberry fruit, with a licorice-like basil element for some herbal intrigue. Punchy acidity and powdery tannins round everything out. Superb Grenache. ABV: 14%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Exotic The lesser spotted actually nice fruity Chardonnay. This went through partial malo, which marries perfectly with the exotic fruit flavours going on. Rich peach fruit and frangipane come together with blossom florals and a touch of smoke, with cooling acidity keeping things fresh. ABV: 13%

Place: Tasmania, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Electric Easily one of Tassie’s best Chardonnays. Combine some seriously good winemakers with an excellent vintage, and this is the cracking result. Elegant, pure and restrained. This is stupid tasty, characterised by slatey minerality, with sharp citrus, rounded stone fruit and a hint of indulgent richness, even on the Island's south side. A whisper of spice finishes things off. Modern, razor-sharp and lip-smacking. ABV: 12.7%

wine: Sailor Seeks Horse, Small Wonder Chardonnay 2022
notes: Place: Tasmania, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Poised Bold, structured, small-batch Chardy. Zesty and crisp, with a distinct freshness despite the wine being aged in 20% new oak. An argument for new oak, never thought I'd be making one of those, but here we are. In skilled hands, most anything can be a good ageing vessel. Truly polished and luxurious, the citrusy notes are balanced by an underlying creaminess and a touch of something almost bready. Like a lemon meringue pie, you might say? ABV: 12.3%

Place: Tasmania, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Sought-After Okay, strap in. Once this wine gets going, it'll just build and build and build. Cherries and currants hold court at first, with orange rind, white pepper and almonds all chiming in too, before layers and layers of complexity unfold on the palate, with an underlying roasted meat thing happening too. Tannins and acid all in balance. Supreme, meticulously made Pinot. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Sailor Seeks Horse, Small Wonder Pinot Noir 2022
notes: Place: Tasmania, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Powerful Another masterful bottling from a masterful producer. Driving, powerful Pinot, with real structure and savouriness. Top that with bright red fruit and a supple silkiness and we're really on here. How good is Pinot? ABV: 12.1%

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Limited After ten years spent painstakingly converting the Boxer's vineyard to biodynamics, Good Intentions' lease is up and the new owner is ripping it all out. Great. So this'll be the last bottling from this vineyard. Lucky for you, we got it over here just in time. Whole bunch fermentation and super gentle handling in the winery means this is elegant, juicy and fruit forward, with sharp acidity coming from the volcanic terroir. Simultaneously floral, herbal and spicy. Can't believe they're never gonna make this wine again. Womp womp.

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Pretty A blend of three vineyards here to show off three distinct soil types - volcanic, limestone and clay. Music to my ears. A soft, plush Pinot with fruit running from strawberry to cherry to blackberry, and a cooling minty edge. Just good Pinot doing good things. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Interesting Negoce fruit here, from two different vineyards to show the diversity of the world's most elite grape (IMO). The grapes from Mount Gambier are grown on flint over limestone for lip-smacking minerality, while the Coonawarra portion brings more flesh, depth and texture. Creamy but balanced with searing acidity, this is yet another side to Chardonnay. Get u a grape that can do it all. ABV: 12%

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Cabernet Sauvignon + Petit Verdot Vibe: Electric Another lighter spin on traditionally deeper grapes! I'm into it. The fruit has just one day on skins to draw out a bit of texture without bringing the hardcore tannins with it, and proximity to the sea means the climate is nice n cool, so the wine is nice n fresh. Geddit? Juicy and full of sour cherries, this is another one that works wonders with a little chill before cracking it open. ABV: 13%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Riesling Vibe: Zippy The epitome of does what it says on the tin. Supremely floral Riesling, kept in check by tons of peppery spice. Puckering acidity and honeyed notes hang out alongside every kind of apple you can think of - fresh, baked, dried, u name it. Proper nectar territory. ABV: 10.4%

Place: Mount Gambier, Australia Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Textural The 2023 release marks the 10th anniversary of Good Intentions Wine Co.’s journey, going back to its roots with 100% skin-fermented Sauvignon Blanc. Vineyards here are spitting distance from the sea (if you can spit a few kilometres), so this is a gorgeously fresh summer orange wine. Intrigue comes from the texture, created by 2-3 weeks' skin contact. The fruit veers towards the tropical, with kiwis, pineapple and banana. Like a boozy fruit salad! ABV: 12%

wine: Worlds Apart, 'Up on the Roof' LDR 2025
grapes: Syrah, Sauvignon Blanc, Grenache, Touriga Nacional
notes: Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Syrah + Grenache + Touriga Nacional + Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Too Easy 'Up on the Roof' is more a serving suggestion than anything else, if you're lucky enough to have rooftop access. Doubtless would work as well in a park, or in your living room. A truly intuitive wine, much tweaking and experimenting went into the blend, with the result being more than the sum of its parts. Bright, crunchy and easygoing. ABV: 12.2%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Gamay Vibe: Savoury A tribute to Louis and Hannah's daughter Zoe and her, you guessed it, blue eyes. 100% whole bunch, this is electric and bright, the savoury backbone balanced by creamy strawberries and lively freshness. With a little spell in the fridge this is refreshment city. ABV: 13.9%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Wild A spinoff of Ochota Barrels' 'Fugazi' Grenache, with a suitably punk rock backstory (google it), this is an explosion of wildflowers and red berries, with nervy acidity and fine boned tannins. A brand spanking new and very welcome addition to the Worlds Apart portfolio. ABV: 13%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal Enviable perfumed aromatics and acid here thanks to the long, cool ripening season. Strawberries and melons dominate the light-as-air palate, with a note of something herbal that builds over time. The finish is long and lifted. Really lovely Pinot with a correspondingly lovely price tag. ABV: 12.2%

Place: Adelaide Hills, Australia Grape: Syrah Vibe: Bright A wine made in tribute to the late, great Taras Ochota, who was Louis' mentor. Elegant yet brooding, this is full of morello cherries and jammy raspberries, while the vineyard's altitude keeps things fresh and 60% whole bunches keeps things light. An excellent wine dedicated to an excellent man. ABV: 13%

wine: Parched, Dan's + LC Selections Present: Riley Harrison (AUS)
notes: Join us, and more importantly Riley Harrison , for a night on the riviera. Riley has been making waves back home for a few years now, so we are delighted to introduce him properly to a thirsty UK public via LC Selections. Riley made the jump from 9-5 grind to winemaking back in 2015 with a single tonne of Grenache (not much), fleshing out over time into what is now a pulsating range of Mediterranean-vibe whites and reds. His are wines of incredible moreish quality as well as depth if you're looking. Kind of ideal, if you ask us. As usual, this will sell out, so don't wait, can't wait, CYA THER

Place: Tenerife, Canary Islands Grape: Listán Blanco Vibe: Incredible I remember the first time I tried this, because I had to drink three other glasses of wine beforehand to muster up the strength to pay the price they were pouring it at by the glass. It was worth every eye-watering penny. The production here is miniscule, due to a small vineyard and an even smaller yield, but that's what makes it so special. Waxy in texture, there's slow-burning citrus fruit at the fore, with waves and waves of flinty smoke right behind it, and a lingering, salty finish. It's so pronounced you can practicall

Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Excellent Outrageously good and gastronomic. Rich, full and lively, this is ripe-fruited and savoury. Toasty and persistent, there's an ocean spray thing going on towards the end that'll send your mind to sunnier climes. Oysters, anyone? ABV: 12.5%

Place: Dão, Portugal Grape: Rufete + Touriga Nacional Vibe: Smashable Primo chilled red material. Fire up the barbie! Very gently extracted for a beautiful light colour and body, there's a cola-bottle-sweet thing happening that made it very hard to put the glass down. The fruit rides the line between red and white, with cherries and peaches both having their say. Proper juice bomb with a hint of paprika spice, just for fun. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Foodie A blend of various expressions and sites of Pinot Noir across the Côte des Bar, with the base wine coming from the 2011 vintage. 70% of the grapes are pressed, 20% vinified and whole bunches and the last 10% is reserve wine from 2010 and 2011, with the final blend ageing for three more years in barrel before tirage. Sheesh, complicated or what? Makes sense then that it translates into a wine of incredible complexity and depth. Roasted quince, bergamot and marzipan mingle on the palate with notes of brioche bringing us home. Foodie Champag

wine: Françoise Martinot, 'Bistrøtage B17' Affinage Prolongé Brut Nature NV
notes: Place: Champagne, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Generous This is the biggest and blousiest of Martinot's range, with serious time on the lees. Finesse personified. Bursting with notes of toast and baking spices, there's a lip-smacking umami note in there too that just makes this wine sing. The fruit swings from lemon to grapefruit to peach to barberry and back again. Vinous and absolutely tonic-like. ABV: 12%

Place: Dão, Portugal Grape: Encruzado + Cerceal + Malvasia Fina + Bical Vibe: Lovely You can't swing a cat in Lisbon without knocking over a cascade of Quinta da Boavista wines. A real favourite in Portugal, they've finally made it over to our shores and we're happy to see 'em. This packs a real punch for the price, with lemon, elderflower and pine needle notes at first followed by rich, ripe fruit on the palate. It never gives in to flabbiness though - this is freshness through and through. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: Catarratto Vibe: Easy A lovely, easygoing, fragrant Sicilian white. Great texture on the palate, almost chalky, with pink grapefruit and green apple coming through strong, and a touch of spicy minerality. A pretty complex white for a very nice price. ABV: 12%

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: Nero d'Avola Vibe: Easy The perfect everyday red with some meat on its bones. Dark fruited, full of roasted cherries and plums and some chocolatey, coffee-like notes underneath, this is a great bargain banger. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Bugey, France Grape: Gamay + Ploussard Vibe: Fruity and Fun This was a standout from a mammoth day of tasting. My colleague, who went the following day concurred. Perhaps due to the pleasing, but restrained, amount of residual sugar providing some much-needed respite for the palette. Insanely high acid cuts any sweetness to shreds and makes this incredibly thirst-quenching. Pair this with something sweet or spicy, and you're laughing. A guilty pleasure wine, that you shouldn't feel so guilty about. Sometimes a touch of sweetness is what you need, no shame in that. ABV: 9%

wine: Domaine de Bellevue, 'Maceration Pinot Gris' VDF 2021
notes: Place: Loire, France Grape: Pinot Gris Vibe: Pithy Is it orange? Is it a rosé? No, it's another macerated Pinot Gris, duh! Always a fun one to whip out whilst doing some blind tasting. Anyway, the wine in question is a beautiful example of the grape on its skin with textbook notes of rose-hip, pithy grapefruit, and baked oranges. Gastronomic, and an extremely fine-tuned take, which comes as no surprise from this rising star whose reputation is gaining stock by the minute. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Muscadet Vibe: Herbal Older vines, plenty of time on the lees and ageing in concrete will have your mind darting over to Burgundy. This is herbal, almost anise-like, and comes off a single site on Gabbro soils. Yup, that's a new one for me too. Essentially, an igneous rock formed underground by ancient volcanoes. For those who didn't study Geography it basically lends the wine a verticality, minerality and mouth-watering tension. Ultimate oyster wine. ABV: 12%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Muscadet Vibe: Oceanic In this part of the world, we were blessed in 2020 with almost perfect growing conditions. A single site expressions off granite soils that lends Muscadet more structure and grip. Expect plenty of texture on top of that signature salty edge that runs throughout all the Bellevue releases. Freshness in spades too. Think it's time for a quick trip to the fishmonger. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Muscadet Vibe: Saline A wickedly salty Muscadet that screams of the sea. Hailing from one of the older plots Jerome works with, this is concentrated yet full of vitality. Without a doubt, the best expression of the grape you'll find. Never thought I'd be paying Burgundy prices for Muscadet but here we have it. Get around this pronto. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chardonnay + Savagnin Vibe: Zesty A blend you'd usually find a little further north that somehow works remarkably well next to the Atlantic. Chardonnay does the heavy lifting in the fruit department whilst Savagnin brings its searing acidity and further enhances the salty twang. I'm a little lost for words. A wine you'll have to taste to believe. The fact this bottle not only works but excels is a real testament to the skilled hand of Jérôme Bretaudeau. ABV: 12.5 %

wine: Artefact #2 Verdejo, Finca Venta de Don Quijote 2024
notes: Place: Toledo, Spain Grape: Verdejo Vibe: Essential The perfect staple white doesn't exi —yes it does, and here it is! Floral and stone-fruited, with a nice creaminess coming from extended lees contact and a lovely waxy texture, you'd be hard pressed to find a better white to occupy a permanent position in your fridge. Go on, find one, I dare u. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Cracking If you put a gun to my head and asked me to pick my favourite Riesling style (can't think of a situation that would require this, but whatever), it'd be Kabinett, and wines like this are the reason why. Peaches n cream on the nose and a beautiful sweetness in the mouth, all kept in check by Riesling's signature ripping acid. This is so, so good. ABV: 7.5%

Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Exciting Two vintages joining forces here for a complex, intriguing bottling. The '20 was done in foudre and the '21 went into new-ish Austrian oak. Tonnes of petrol at the fore followed by rich, ripe fruit and eyewatering acidity, plus some gentle toastiness from the oak that only adds to the overall drinking pleasure. There's even a tiny spritz upon opening. One for those who are easily bored! ABV: 11.5%

Place: Mosel, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Apero I'm such a sucker for bargain Riesling. This is just straightforward, no frills, classic Mosel through and through. There's a touch of sulphur added to this bottling, but this estate is lightyears ahead of most other producers in the region in terms of sustainable farming, so we'll allow it. There's strong petrol and honey aromas right off the bat, with sharp lime fruit and a hint of well integrated sugar. Sign me up. ABV: 10.5%

Place: Savoie, France Grape: Gamay + Pinot Noir Vibe: Deep A deep and brooding expression of two grapes often known for their light n bright nature, so this is a very interesting take. 50/50 Gamay/Pinot, fermented separately as whole bunches, so there's a wonderfully fresh stemmy quality, alongside cherry fruit, smoke and wild herbs. After a couple of swirls round the glass some subtle caramel notes even come to the fore. Wowza. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Savoie, France Grape: Jacquère + Altesse Vibe: Fresh Savoie whites are now firm favourites on my drinking list, and here's another great one. Pleasantly medicinal herbs are the first thing that hit you, and sharp lemon flavours are right behind it. There's a cool floral note of dandelion in there as well, and as with most things (or most good things) Savoie this is so fresh you can practically taste the mountain air. Having seen the vineyards, I can now confirm, this botte is a one way ticket to the alps. ABV: 11.5%

Place: Rheinhessen, Germany Grape: Riesling Vibe: Intriguing A pretty fn cool take on Riesling from a pretty fn cool and experimental winemaker. Macerated but still with plenty of freshness. Zesty and herbal for another fascinating side of the grape. ABV: 10%

wine: Etienne Seignovert, En Attendant La Nuit 2022
notes: Place: Ardèche, France Grape: Syrah Vibe: Pitch Perfect Blue and black fruited but still veering into that lithe style Etienne does so well. A textural dream with already soft, silky tannin that will only get better with time. Hard to resist now though with so much garrigue, olive, and licorice spice already. Aromatic, textured, zippy acid. It doesn't get much better than this. Pitch perfect wine. ABV: 13 %

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Tingling The so called "starter-wine" from Domaine Valma. Starter my ****. The only thing this is starting is an addiction/love affair. Vines are grown on what is essentially their estate vineyard, a short walk from the cellar on a north-ish facing slope that'll do well in this warming climate. There's a crispness on show but also a seriousness which gives a sneak peak into the house style. In 2024 we're treated to a cool vintage, reminiscent of the Beaujolais of old. It ebbs and flows, remaining effortless and intriguing all the while. Ready to ham

wine: Domaine Valma, Fleurie Lieu-Dît 'Les Rangs Tard' 2022
notes: Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Free Flowing Rangs Tard is a section of the Les Labourons that ripens a bit later, and therefore goes into this separate bottling. The average vine age is older too, most planted in the 50's at very high density and the remainder in the early 2000's at slightly lower but still high density. This is anything but dense, it's actually a dream. You do get the concentration and anise dusted aromatic character that shows some vine maturity, but it's imbued with an innate freshness and vitality. Yippee. Great now, will be even greater after a short spell i

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Elite Nice view from up top next to La Madone, going to vineyards like this really give context to a wine, even better being driven up there with a beautiful 30kg dog sitting in your lap. Dreamy. Anyway, the wine. Fruit from a 50 year old vineyard going through anything but a midlife crisis. It's up the top, exposed and windy, giving us smaller berries and enviable complexity. This is spice laden, coming out more and more with air, alongside a lot of scrubby herb and vibrant red fruit. Has a classiness, one of those wines where you can just tell tha

wine: Domaine Valma, Fleurie Lieu-Dît 'La Chapelle des Bois' 2023
notes: Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Elite Another of the iconic Fleurie vineyards on show here. Chapelle des Bois generally gives a wine of structure and strength, and this is no different, albeit with a distinctly seductive edge that keeps you coming back for more, and more. The fruit leans darker, the vineyard being a bit lower down than La Madone, and there’s a bit more obvious depth off the bat. 2023 was a touch cooler than the previous year, bringing real vibrancy. I cannot wait to see how this develops, and also how the guys develop with this plot over time, it being a fairly re

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Grippy 10% of the juice here comes from macerated fruit, and all of the vines are young, vibrant and singing. God there's energy in the glass, allied with plenty of ginger spice and a smoky, savoury undertone. A combination of said spice, plenty of verve and a bitterness on the finish make this one to dive right into. ABV: 13%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Tonic The majority of fruit comes from a small plot immediately outside the cellar in Morgon, spitting distance from the vineyards and cellars of a certain Lapierre. Enviable locale. Earthen, and showing a bit of trademark blood and iron. Drinks very well, in a classic style, a harp back to the years before everything got super ripe. It feels lean and ultra digestible yet generous and expansive all at once. There's precision too, we're onto a winner. ABV: 12%

Place: Beaujolais, France Grape: Gamay Vibe: Fresh As A Daisy Meticulous, is Manuel Girard. Fruit from vines planted within the Champagne Lieu-Dit in Fleurie. Good spot. This is dialled in. Plenty of stem showing but they're ripe and adding shape and spice, pairing nicely with the riper fruit from this warm vintage. My notes from this are glowing, with much mention of seduction, brooding fruit and yummy tannin. Dive in. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Wine 4 Dummies: Euro Edition - All Four Sessions
notes: Wine 4 Dummies is back, baby! And this time we're going all ~European. We're smoking Vogues, talking with our hands and going topless at the beach. Heh. Not so much, but we will be drinking a lot of their wine. Brexit who?

wine: Parched + Dan's present: A Night with Wasted Wine Club
notes: We're pumped to have our warehouse neighbour and all around gr8 guy Angelo from Wasted Wine Club , down with us for the evening, and you should be too. Wasted Wine Club was started to combat waste in the wine industry. Angelo works with small producers who have surplus or excess wine and bottles it for them, puts a jazzy label on it, and sells it on to consumers to make sure every drop of that precious liquid gets to the thirsty people it was designed to reach. But the wine isn't just sloppy seconds - with bottlings from such legends as Intellego and Jolie-Laide, this is proper stuff, and it w

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc + Aligoté + Chardonnay Vibe: Natural, Textural The second vintage of the newest addition to the De Moor family. A bit of a curveball compared to their classic Primo Chard lineup, but no less delicious. You get the full fruit spectrum here: tangerine, fleshy peach, even a hint of something tropical. The palate’s chalky and tense. This makes my mind wander to good dry Jurançon, which makes my mind wander to really good Jura. All delicious things. ABV: 13%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Classy Pretty, elegant and dry rosé - shockingly hard to find these days. Willunga's got u! The red fruit is there, but it's kept in check by citrus and florals. Primo picnic wine, primo aperitivo wine, primo any occasion you feel like wine. ABV: 12.5%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Bright The highest and coolest site in McLaren Vale, so freshness is high on the agenda. Lavender florals are the first point of order, then some aromatic basil comes through strong, backed up with blood orange and red cherries. Thirst quenching, mouthwatering stuff. ABV: 14.5%

Place: McLaren Vale, Australia Grape: Grenache Vibe: Bright Single vineyard, dry-farmed Grenache from 70 year old vines. That's a lot of good words in one sentence. Bright and lifted, we've got red berries to the fore and orange zest and cinammon in the back. Cute integrated tannins 2. This is one to have in the fridge at all times. For emergencies, you know? ABV: 14.5%

wine: Wine 4 Dummies, Euro Edition: Week Three - Italy
notes: Wine 4 Dummies is back, baby! And this time we're going all ~European. We're smoking Vogues, talking with our hands and going topless at the beach. Heh. Not so much, but we will be drinking a lot of their wine. Brexit who? Ciao bella, and all that jazz. This week is all things Italian, minus the pasta and the pizza, unfortch. Plenty to like on the drinking front though. From the plains of the Veneto to the heady heights of Mount Etna, Fionn will be taking you through the intricacies of this incredibly diverse region while you glug four tasting glasses and heckle him with questions. Molto bene.

wine: Wine 4 Dummies, Euro Edition: Week Two - France (part two)
notes: Wine 4 Dummies is back, baby! And this time we're going all ~European. We're smoking Vogues, talking with our hands and going topless at the beach. Heh. Not so much, but we will be drinking a lot of their wine. Brexit who? In week two of all things Français, Robyn's gonna be taking us on a jaunt around the Jura, the Loire and the Rhône, chatting soil, aspect, varietals and various other nerdy things, while you glug four tasting glasses and heckle her with questions. Très bien, I reckon. Here are the details: Location: Dan's, 2-4 Tottenham Road, N1 4BZ Tuesday 13th August 6.30-8pm Tickets £40 4

wine: Jean-François Ganevat, 'J'en veux Encore!!!' Rouge NV
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Pinot Noir + Pinot Gris Vibe: Natural, lighter Bright fruits and lifted aromatics alongside tingly acidity and svelte fruit flavours. Deserves a light chill and air before drinking! ABV: 13%

wine: Daniel Sage & Jordi Torgue, Voix du Periscope 2022
notes: Place: Rhône, France Grape: Viognier Vibe: Hyped It's tough trying to make proper good Viognier but Daniel Sage & Jordi Torgue can do no wrong. Macerated for maximum pleasure. This vintage, is darker in colour but still light and breezy. Chock full of citrus, oriental spice, and all that's nice. Buy on-sight. ABV: 12%

Place: Rhône, France Grape: Grenache Noir + Cinsault + Bourboulenc Vibe: Gastronomic Sweet spices, plenty of red fruit, salivating bitters on the back end. Such a joyful little wine that manages to capture the southern sun but marries it effortlessly with drinkability. A delicious rarity. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Rhône, France Grape: Grenache + Cinsault Vibe: Pure + Pretty Here Grenache brings plush fruit and a little something floral atop a very mineral core. The balance between tannin, depth, and drinkability is quite frankly astonishing. Words can't do this thing of beauty justice. Liquid velvet. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Rhône, France Grape: Bourboulenc, Grenache Blanc Vibe: Rare Always one of my favourite releases of the year, the Grillons wines keep ticking all boxes. This is a ripper. 2/3 was direct pressed to vat for freshness, with the remainder aged in barrel without topping up for some oxy, nutty goodness. Unique, delicious. ﻿ABV: 13.5%

Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Woof Banging Chablis from a producer that needs no introduction. A blend of several parcels, this is chiselling and precise. Lightly floral with hints of citrus peel, this is lively and raring to go, held together with a sizzling core of acidity and ending on a spicy finish. One to drink now or to stick in the cellar. Or drink one now and stick one in the cellar. U do u. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Peggy et Jean-Pascal Buronfosse, Poulsard 'Sous le Monceau'
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Poulsard Vibe: Fresher Wildly aromatic with both smoke and strawberries practically leaping out of the glass. Lip-smacking acidity, a touch of Jurassic funk, and most importantly lots and lots of fun. This is Poulsard par excellence. One of those compelling bottles that's irresistible from the first sip to the very last. ABV: 12%

Place: Sicily, Italy Grape: Catarratto Vibe: Easy A tasty and really clean intro into the world of orange wine. Full of ripe lemon and white florals and a hint of sage, this is proper moreish. ABV: 13%

wine: Peggy et Jean-Pascal Buronfosse, Pinot Noir 2022
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Natural , lighter All about this. It's damn hard beating Pinot done in that ethereal style you find from the Jura. Bursting with crushed red berries, a little hint of earth, and plenty of iron-like minerality driving down your palate. I have a strong feeling that one bottle of this won't be enough... ABV: 12%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Natural , textural It's not often you see such an elegant and expressive wine made in the sous voile style. Rippling acidity cuts through those nutty, sherry-esque notes to reveal a nuanced, emotive wine that deserves a good wedge of Comte and much contemplation. Bravo. ABV: 13%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Riesling + Muscat + Gewürztraminer Vibe: Hedonistic Vincent's top maceration with fruit coming from the Goldert Grand Cru. Muscat brings the florals, Gewürz the spice, Riesling the acid. A beautiful balance. Aromatic, herbal, and full of fruit this is utterly compelling. Singing now, time will only do wonders. ABV: 14.5%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Crunchy I'm positively ecstatic to finally have our hands on this. I vividly remember tasting this from tank last year, and you just knew this was destined for greatness. Whole bunch grapes see a cold and gentle maceration to give us a lithe, ethereal bottle. A cherry bomb with lifted aromatics and silky texture. Pinot this good rarely comes this cheap. Stock up. ABV: 12%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Pinot blanc + Sylvaner + Riesling + Muscat + Gewurz Vibe: Natural Essentially one litre of Edelzwicker, which is one of my favourite wine words. It's fun to say, even more fun to drink! Essentially, a hazy blend of all the Alsatian white varieties. The aromatic grapes bring some elderflower whilst the remaining varieties keep this grounded by pithy citrus and minerals. A slight spritz adds even further drinkability. Bottling this in anything under 1 litre would've been a crime . ABV: 11.5%

Place: Kent, England Grape: Pinot Meunier + Pinot Noir + Chardonnay + Bacchus + Pinot Gris Vibe: Natural + Moreish The new field blend is the lightest iteration yet. This is defo more in the hot pink zone than light red, although it's just as delicious. Great length and with that signature acid line carrying plenty of delicate florals and fruit. This is begging to be drunk with some sunshine. ABV: 10%

Place: Kent, England Grape: Bacchus Vibe: Natural + Moreish Sitting somewhere between white and skinsy, but just a very, very great wine. Ham Street are one of the few producers who tame this grape into something I like. Their ‘22 is still the best example I’ve ever tasted. 2024 is a return, macerated gently to round out those aromatics. Wonderfully floral without being OTT, this is pithy and citrusy, with a hint of hedgerow elderflower and lots of chalk minerals. Only 650 btls produced. Don’t sleep on this. ABV: 10.2%

Place: Bierzo, Spain Grape: Godello Vibe: Intriguing Godello can sometimes be a bit rich for my liking, but the vines here are planted at altitude for some mountain freshness that keeps things beautifully balanced. This has a slightly oxy, sherry-esque vibe that adds proper intrigue to the ripe, fleshy stone fruit and a finish so long I can practically still taste it. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Bierzo, Spain Grape: Menc ía Vibe: Too Easy Veronica's entry level wine, which somehow still comes off 80 year old vines?! Bierzo is just full of them, apparently, which is good news for everyone. This is gorgeous, all sweet brambly fruit offset by capsicum and a hint of smoke and liquorice. Far too easy to drink. 'Dar un quite' is an old bullfighting term Veronica learned from her father, meaning to give a helping hand. Like I'm doing for you, bringing you this wine. Ya welcome. ABV: 13%

Place: Bierzo, Spain Grape: Menc ía + Doña Blanca + Godello + Palomino etc etc Vibe: Light n bright 75% Menc í a with the balance made up of various indigenous white varieties, from 90 year old vineyards that were traditionally co-planted with red and white grapes. That, plus the fact the vineyards are planted at 750m altitude and super gentle extraction in the winery means this is about as fresh a Spanish red as you can find. Seriously, find a fresher one, I'll wait. Super delicate and floral at first then giving way to ripe strawberry fruit, with a touch of menthol and pine chucked in for go

Place: Galicia, Spain Grape: Treixadura + Lado + Agudelo Vibe: Stunnin Iago showing off what he can do with his own vines, this is at the top end of his range. This was aged under a thin layer of flor in a combination of barrels and buried tinajas (IYKYK, if you don't, = amphorae) and is luscious and deep, the flor ageing really bringing out the salinity in the wine. Add some tarragon herbiness, pink grapefruit and rose and you've got yourself a heck of a wine. ABV: 12%

Place: Galicia, Spain Grape: Caino Longo + Caino Terra + Brancellao Vibe: Elegant Some lesser known red varieties in this one, including Galicia's answer to Pinot Noir. With an eleganc 36 e all too often missing from Spanish reds, this is fresh and green on the nose, with tart red fruit and an almost minty note in the mouth. A little wild, but in the best way. ABV: 11%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Riesling Vibe: Natural A hazy, orchard-fruited Riesling packed to the brim with tasty minerals, think river rocks and chalk. Younger vines and energetic, this is truly a remarkable embodiment of the Limestone parcels of Andalu. One of those wines that I could drink with a straw but ponder over for hours. Do as you wish! ABV:12.5%

wine: Parched + Dan's x Indigo Wines: Real Pinot ft. William Downie
notes: Been way too long since we had an Aussie in here. Ha ha. We are jazzed to be bringing you an evening with William Downie, a benchmark Australian Pinot producer and reference point for minimal intervention, site-specific winemaking. With stints at Domaine Fourier and Hubert Lignier in Burgundy and Bass Phillip in Oz under his belt, he already had a heck of a resume when he set up his own project in 2003. These days he focuses on the lesser known Gippsland region, and is fanatical about Aussie soil - it's old, like, really old, and has a ton of nuance that William loves to coax out in his wines.

Place: Provence, France Grape: Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah Vibe: Fuller A powerful wine that needed time, and time we have given it. Just entering the sweet spot and still with a long long life ahead. This manages to capture all the warmth of the southern sun but with the class and freshness from cooler climes. Firmly in the upper echelon. ABV: 13.5%

wine: Giuseppe Mascarello e Figlio, Langhe Nebbiolo 2021
notes: Place: Piemonte, Italy Grape: Nebbiolo Vibe: Cuddly Mascarello is a name that might be familiar, if you're of the Piemonte persuasion. This Nebb is like a hug in a glass. Soft and warming, full of the signature red-fruited nature that's the house style round these parts. Wild strawberries abound, cut through with liquorice and black pepper. Stupid good, and hitting its perfect drinking window right about... now.

Place: Lanzarote, Spain Grape: Malvasía Valcanica, Listán Blanco, Diego Vibe: Sea Spray How good is island life? Like proper island life. Taste this and then come back to me. A blend from all over the island, some right by the water, others up in the hills. It all comes together to give us this tropical citrus fruit laden, saline wonder that drinks immensely well on its own but is also the perfect foil for literally anything. You've been warned. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Roberto Voerzio, Barolo del Comune di La Morra 2018
notes: Place: Piemonte, Italy Grape: Nebbiolo Vibe: Charming, Classic A dream. ABV: 14%

Place: Heathcote, Australia Grape: Nero D'Avola + Moscato Giallo Vibe: Fun This is a pretty mental blend of Nero and Moscato. Nothing to be mad about. In fact, you should be positively pumped for an ethereal take on these often mistreated varieties. Semi-carbo treatment results in a lean wine that is dangerously hard to stop drinking once you've popped the cork. Cherry fruited, herbal, and plenty of those tasty minerals. Light in body, certainly not light on flavor. ABV: 12.5%

Place: Heathcote, Australia Grape: Nero D'Avola + Sangiovese + Lambrusco + Syrah Vibe: Silly but in a good way Momento Mori doing that weird blendy thing again, and again pumping out a wine that sings, when on paper it has no right to. Dark but fresh fruit lies atop a bed of earth and tea. Dane says this is a bit like a Jurassic Pinot, and I'd have to say I agree. How he's managed that I don't know, but I am thankful. ABV: 12.5%

wine: Thomas Batardière, Les Noëls de Montbenault 2024
notes: Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Natural, textural Heaps limited. Fruit from newer plantings, they put cuttings from Huet in this esteemed Anjou vineyard. Thomas, behave! A wine that'll reward patience... just let the vitality take hold.

Place: Etna, Sicily, Italy Grape: Grecanico Dorato + Others Vibe: Soulful This is primarily Grecanico Dorato, an Etna mutation of Grecanico, along with a few other local varieties that not even Sonia is entirely sure of. While the blend may be a bit of a mystery, I can say with confidence that this is one of the tastiest whites I've had in quite some time. Grown at over 1,200 metres, this is both energetic and elegant. Give it time and you'll be amazed at what reveals itself. These 2024s are incredibly refined and classy, seeming to get better with each passing vintage. ABV: 12%

Place: Etna, Sicily, Italy Grape: Field Blend Vibe: Lively Another beautiful blend from Sonia, who has quickly become one of our favourite winemakers on Etna. This is a ridiculously good Rosato from the highest plots she lovingly tends. Freshness is off the charts. A bit of bâtonnage helps soften things, leaving us with a textured wine full of pomegranate, florals, and hints of herbs . ABV: 11.5%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Trousseau Vibe: Bright Trousseau from '19. Smoking, savoury and oh-so drinkable. This would be good if you left it in the cellar and forgot about it. It would also be very good if you gave it a quick decant and then polished off the bottle solo. No judgment here. ABV: 14%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Trousseau Vibe: Bright Trousseau from '20. Perhaps a little more lithe, and lifted than the previous vintage but without losing any finesse or charm. Another belting bottle from Bornard. ABV: 13%

Place: Jura, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Electric Kevin's wines are truly stunning, especially considering they're about half the price that they should be. This one deserves a bit of air and if given so you'll be rewarded with a myriad of fruit that takes you from citrus to orchard. Plenty of rocky minerality, nutty grip, and herbal notes thrown in for good measure. Sadly limited AF. ABV: 13%

wine: Domaine Bohn, Eau de Vie Marc "G" NV 50cl
notes: Place: Alsace, France Grape: Gewürztraminer Vibe: Gorge Marc de Gewurz made in the traditional copper alembic. The perfect tipple to sit alongside your pastries, your sorbets, your fruit salads. ABV: 45%

wine: Julien Frémont, Cidre Cuvée Piterne NV
notes: Place: Normandy, France Vibe: Intense A blend of the '21 and '22 vintages, with the '21 reaching full fermentation in an old Calvados barrel, thus retaining some of those lusicous tannins, before being blended with the still fermenting '22 juice. The result is a cracking mixture of power and bitterness with nervy acidity. A belter. ABV: 9.9%

Place: Normandy, France Vibe: Finessed Named after the forest the trees for this cuvée are planted close to, the Quévrue contains more of Julien's bittersweet apple varieties, and aged for eight months in amphora. Elegant, with silky tannins and an extra long finish, this one slaps parked next to some spicy food. Trust me. ABV: 7%

Place: Normandy, France Vibe: Mineral Flintier soils for these trees, so still chock-full of minerality, and made up of every kind of apple grown on the estate. Dry, delicious and a touch bitter on the finish. Refreshing 2 the max. ABV: 6.2%

Place: Normandy, France Vibe: Mineral The trees for this cider are planted in heavy clay soils, so it's packed with terroir-driven minerality. There's a hint of sweetness but not too much, and a dash of pleasant bitterness at the end, making this a proper thirst-quencher. ABV: 5.5%

Place: Normandy, France Vibe: Smooth Proper elegant Calvados aged in oak for at least three years. Made from organic apples, it's full of juicy, sweet orchard fruit with a hint of vanilla and peppery spice. Yum. ABV: 42%

wine: Domaine Henri Naudin-Ferrand, Bourgogne Hautes-Côtes de Beaune 'Orchis Mascula' 2021
notes: Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Pinot Noir Vibe: Ethereal I think we should all be keeping an eye on the Hautes-Côtes. After seeing a large shift towards respectful farming we're now seeing some pretty stellar wines coming out of this region that was, and still is, a bit overlooked. Although 2021 was a challenging vintage, this is remarkably fresh, floral, and fun in its youth. It strikes the perfect balance between crunchy red fruit and earthy intrigue. Will age with grace too. ABV: 12%

Place: Burgundy , France Grape: Aligoté Vibe: Classy Marc Colin is a man who can do no wrong, and this is a bottle that is not only good for the wallet but good for the soul too. Half raised in tank for vitality, half in foudre to soften things out. Fresh and fruity upfront, a bit herbaceous in the middle before a soft creamy finish. A little age has done this wonders... ABV: 12.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Aligoté Vibe: Natural, textural Old vine Aligoté that is overflowing with energy. Can't believe people used to sleep on this grape. So much going on it's hard to know where to begin. Herbal, citrus-laden, a bit of ocean breeze, a whisper of phenolic grip. Burgundy's over-looked grape has been taken to dizzying new heights. ABV: 12%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Pineau d'Aunis Vibe: Pet Nat + Friends Pink fizz, is there anything more fun? This is direct press Pineau d'Aunis which spends 18 months on the lees before being disgorged by hand, and the result is a delicate, ethereal fizzer full of strawberries and black pepper, propped up by a solid, mineral backbone. Fun or serious? U decide! ABV: 10%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Chenin Blanc Vibe: Electric Another cracker from the magical mind of Robinot. Bistrologie is always buzzing with life but especially here in this cooler vintage. High energy, high acid, highly enjoyable from the get-go. No shame if you don't have the patience to wait for this one but reckon it's gotta a long life ahead. ABV: 11.5%

wine: Les Granges Pâquenesses, Savagnin 'La Pierre Renaissance' 2020
notes: Place: Jura, France Grape: Savagnin Vibe: Rich Serious concentration here thanks to a little extra time in barrel - this is rich and and dense but still balanced by that classic Sav acid line, a touch of bitters and a long, saline finish. Mouthwatering, in the truest sense of the word. ﻿ABV: 13.5%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Exceptional Quintessential Dagueneau, always an iconic bottling and from a particularly cracking year in the Loire. Smoky, tightly wound and powerful as heck, it's all citrus and white fruit flavours, crisp, elegant and saline. Basically unparalleled Sauvignon Blanc. Throw away the cork, you won't be needing it. ABV: 13%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Iconic Pur Sang, aka thoroughbred, tells you most of what you need to know here. Nervy, tense and precise, it's herbal and creamy at first, followed up with hints of macadamia nut, gooseberry, lime and apple. Complex doesn't even begin to describe this. ABV: 13%

Place: Loire, France Grape: Sauvignon Blanc Vibe: Fresh The boldest and fruitiest of all the wines coming out of Dagueneau domaine, this comes from a similar site to the Silex parcel but is a fraction cooler, so the freshness level is dialled way up. Flinty minerality is the core of this wine, with layers of candied citrus and exotic fruit coming through as well. A touch of nuttiness and an intriguing note of peppermint towards the end gives this bottling endless intrigue. ABV: 13.5%

Place: Burgundy, France Grape: Chardonnay Vibe: Energetic Proper pure, intense Petit Chablis! Razor sharp acidity, ripe, pulpy stone fruit and gorgeous saline minerality. Packs a serious punch for the price. One to have in the fridge always. In case of emergencies. ABV: 12%

wine: Les Grangeons de L’Albarine, 'Mondouze le Château' 2022
notes: Place: Ain, France Grape: M ondeuse Vibe: Delightful Grapes here come from vines planted in 2007 from massale selection from the ye olde Mondeuse strain from the legendary Prieuré St-Christophe estate. That's a lot of accolades in one sentence, but in essence it translates to an excellent wine - light and energetic with concentrated black cherries and violet aromatics and a peppery finish. Also, 10%? Is that even alcoholic?! ABV: 10%

Place: Alsace, France Grape: Muscat + Pinot Gris Vibe: Enticing Aromatics dialled up to 100 here, with rose, orange blossom and acacia honey all throwing in their two cents. All that gives way to an ultra-fresh palate full of tangerine and ginger. Helpfully walks the line between complex and accessible, meaning this is a no-brainer for anyone into their orange wines. ABV: 13%

Place: Piemonte, Italy Grape: Barbera Vibe: Plump Barbera doing what it does best, bringing all the lush, juicy fruit. This is a far cry from being a sticky mess. There's a whole lot of herbal charm and a whack of acidity to keep you engaged. I can see myself deleting a bottle of this in no time at all. ABV: 14%

Place: Piemonte, Italy Grape: Nebbiolo Vibe: Charming, Classic Class personified with fragrance and fruit aplenty. A refreshing line of acid carries you gracefully from the pretty rose-filled opening into a long, earth-inflected finish. The respectful use of oak helps to round out those prickly Nebb tannins. Charming. ABV: 14%
