Seductive red fruit, vibrant acidity and beautifully integrated powdery tannins form the backbone of Warwick Estate Trilogy 2016, with freshness and a very long finish. Cabernet Franc 51%, Cabernet Sauvignon 34%, Merlot 15%.

This wine is medium to deep brick red in colour and opens with perfumed fruits, showing blue exotic florals, pomegranate and cranberry, with milk chocolate and liquorice depth. The palate is medium weighted with a fresh, tight acidity carrying through. Stylish, approachable and very drinkable. More from Yalumba Estate

wine: Dona Paula Selecion De Bodega Malbec 2016
notes: Deep violet colour. Aromas of berries, with graphite, black cherries and spices notes. Great concentration, firm tannins, fresh acidity and long finish.

Since it's release this particular vintage of Dow's has been regarded as one of the best bottlings in decades. A powerfully dense wine, solidly based on dry tannins and rich black fruit. Structure, fruit and acidity all come together in a wine that shows immense potential as well as a softer side now. Drink now until 2070.

aromas: Blackberry, Plum, Black Pepper, Espresso, Mocha, Graphite
notes: The palate comes through with interweaving layers of blackberry, deep plum and black currant, alongside delicate nuances of mocha, espresso, graphite and black pepper spice. The mouthfeel is powerful and rich, with depth and structure, full of velvety round tannins and a long, lingering mouth-watering finish. The texture is robust and plentiful, but the intensity is softened by the terroir elements coming through from the well-balanced delicacy and grace that has become synonymous with Stags’ Leap estate wines. Drinks superbly now but demonstrates the opulence and intrigue of the estate, that

“Dark ruby. Subtle and rich aromas of prune, spice and juniper berry leaves. Full-bodied and medium sweet, with big round tannins. Lasts for minutes on the palate. Still very young. It’s lost its youthful toughness, but give a little more time.” Robert Parker, Wine Advocate

wine: Karukera Rhum Blanc Calvados Christian Drouin NV
notes: Premium Rhum from Guadalupe, a white spirit produced from 100% sugar cane.

wine: Westward American Single Malt Stout Cask
notes: A celebration of Oregon’s legendary brewing culture, this whiskey grew out of a longstanding cask-trading tradition among a select group of beer producers in the Northwest. For as long as Westward have been making whiskey, they have traded their freshly-emptied barrels with some of their brewing friends in and around the Northwest, who have in turn “seasoned” them with Stout before returning them again. This Stout Cask Finish begins with Westward American Single Malt, and is then aged for one year in Stout casks. Bottled at 46% ABV

wine: Westward American Single Malt Pinot Noir Cask
notes: A tribute to Oregon’s legendary Willamette Valley wine country, this elegant whiskey is influenced by the region’s premier grape varietal: Pinot Noir. This cask-finished whiskey reflects the vibrance of the Valley’s signature grape while allowing the bold, robust notes of the distilleries whiskey to shine through. This Pinot Noir Cask offering begins with original Westward American Single Malt, which is then finished for up to two years in French Oak wine casks from a handful of award-winning producers in the region. Bottled at 45% ABV

wine: Waterford Single Farm Origin Bannow Island - Edition 1.1
notes: First release Made solely using Overture barley harvested in 2015 by Ed Harpur from his Bannow Island farm in Wexford. The sandy, alluvial soil and seaside location give the barley, and the whisky, a gently maritime air. Soft, rounded and fruity – sweet peach and sharp nectarine. Marshmallow and candy floss develop, along with sharp apple, damp grain and a hint of sea breeze. An air of vanilla floats around, followed by zesty lime peel. wine: Waterford Single Farm Origin Ballykilcavan - Edition 1.1
notes: First release David Walsh-Kemis’s Ballykilcaven farm is ideal for growing grain – sheltered by forest and with a rich clay loam soil. The 2015 harvest of Taberna barley went into making this whisky and won David Waterford’s Top Barley Grower award. Sharp stewed apples and unripe pears to start, with zesty orange and lemon peel following, muddled to release their pungent citrus oils. Farmyard straw, freshly crushed grain and allspice notes develop. Sweet cream and gentle vanilla is quickly swamped by the fruit from the nose – orchards and citrus groves in spades. The nose pops with delicate red berries and a hint of biscuit. On the palate, it’s bright, creamy and juicy, carrying ripe cherry and raspberry fruit with gentle mousse and a soft, scented finish. A perfect aperitif, or lovely with smoked salmon, Thai‑style dishes or light seafood starters.

Double the bubbles, twice the fun! A generous 1.5L magnum of crisp, lively Prosecco with delicate, persistent bubbles. Pale straw in colour with glimmers of green, it opens with aromas of white blossom, ripe pear and a hint of citrus zest. The palate is light, juicy and invigorating, carrying gentle notes of apple and melon, finishing fresh and vibrant. Its vibrant acidity and charming fruit character make it ideal for festive toasts or casual sipping, and it shines alongside fresh seafood, soft cheeses, summer salads, or light pasta dishes. Perfect for celebrations big and small!

Twice the vino, twice the fun. A vivid rosé from Veneto’s volcanic soils, made from 100% Pinot Nero. It shows a bright bouquet of wild strawberries and cherries, flowing into a smooth, harmonious palate with glimpses of raspberry and cherry blossom and a delicate mineral finish. The result feels fresh, elegant and effortlessly drinkable. Light, lively and perfect with seaside-style meals — think grilled fish, fresh salads or light risottos — this magnum is ready to elevate summer evenings (or, let’s be honest, any evening worth celebrating).

wine: Viña Cobos, Bramare Malbec (with Luxury Gift Box)
notes: A superb malbec from a specific vineyard site selected for the quality of their fruit. The wine reflects this attention to detail in the creamy dark cherry puree and macerated plum flavours of this concentrated wine, with a smoky mocha finish. This top of the range malbec comes with a luxury gift box with magnetic closure lined with wood wool.

Under appreciated Beaujolais has lots to enjoy for the modern wine lover. While there are similarities each cru has a distinct personality Regnie might be less well known than Fleurie but it has wine every bit as delicious. This for example is the colour of rubies, smooth like silk and matches vegetarian cuisine brilliantly.

From the home of Primitivo, this delightful white was a bit of a surprise. Intensely fragrant white flower, pineapple and lime while on the palate a hint of mandarin and pear alongside a clean minerality on the finish have made this one of our most popular new wines. A superb wine.
Straw yellow with slight green notes. Intense and complex sweet apple and pear perfume with some soft orange flora. Dry, well structured and a palate that reflects the delicious aroma.

wine: Roosters Throwback Oak Conditioned Vintage Ale 5.3%
notes: A vintage stock ale brewed with Goldings hops and Muscovado sugar, before being fermented and conditioned on oak staves from a barrel previously used to age a batch of Hello, Dimitri? Roosters mighty Bourbon barrel-aged imperial stout. Tawny in colour, Throwback offers up fruity notes along with a balanced level of sweetness and a moderate bitterness on the finish.

wine: Turning Point Disco Midnight Stout 5.1% Can
notes: Disco Midnight is a reimagining of Turning Point's flagship pale as a dry hopped stout. The familiar hop additions of Chinook, Simcoe, and Mosaic performing in tandem with a smooth, roasty malt base.

wine: Turning Point Disco Jester Pale Ale 5.1% Can
notes: You’re in the Court of the Disco King. Turning Point take their US hopped flagship beer, and replace the hops with those grown on these shores? Disco Jester. Hopped with Jester, Harlequin, and UK Chinook.

wine: Turning Point Disco Island Tropical Pale 5.1% Can
notes: Your favourite American hopped pale has been transported to a tropical paradise. All the usual hops (Simcoe, Chinook, Mosaic), plus the addition of fresh pineapple, and Sabro hops for a coconut finish.

wine: Turning Point Sunshine Indoors Mango and Saffron Lassi Pale

wine: Turning Point Stuck In A Metaphor Pale 4.3% Can
notes: A super fruity session pale from the boys and girls at Turning Point. Mosaic and Citra are the hops doing their thing to give this a fruity refreshing moreishness.

Eger is a wine lovers' playground with brilliant regional wines being made throughout the valley and the original home of Bulls Blood. This is a much more modern Kekfrankos wine made only in the finest vintages. There is still plenty of depth, intense black fruits, and warming spice. Crying out for Sunday roast.

Reminds one of Clairet, the dark rose/light red from Bordeaux. This delicious and grown-up rose is a much darker thing than the Provence which is rightly popular. A touch of tannin and a hint of sweet cherry and lashings of crisp cranberry and raspberry summer fruit.

A distinct Bordeaux influence here dark fruit spicy leather aromas and a fine dry tannic structure. But this is Istria not Bordeaux and there's a local grape called Teran in the mix adding some brighter red fruit notes. Start shaking things up a little bit in a very tasty way.
What a bright and refreshing wine. Light and floral with some citrus and a grape fruitiness. A perfect summer picnic wine.

Reminiscent of unoked Chardonnay. This Hungarian grape gives a dry wine with herbaceous and slightly smoky aromas. The palate is fresh and crispy with a slightly creamy honeyed note of baked apple. A fantastic partner for spicy chicken dishes.

The fashion for dry wines in Tokaj has given wine lovers a delicious and exciting selection of very accessible wines. This one has plenty of citrus and minerality for lovers of Sancerre but with an almost Riesling like tang and precision.

Light and easy-drinking, it’s a beer that showcases the floral and citrus fruit aromas of the Cascade hop, grown in the Yakima Valley in Washington State, USA, projected against a back drop of soft Yorkshire water and Golden Promise pale malt.

A Single-Estate Cognac produced exclusively from Camus’ own vineyards in the very heart of the prestigious Borderies Appellation. notes: Available at every 3 Michelin star restaurant in France... There isn't much more that needs to be said. After 10 years in contact with the oak, Armagnac starts to take on the aromas of ageing. Still quite fiery, this Eau-de-Vie will become more complex after a few minutes breathing in your glass.

wine: Turning Point Astral Voyage Session NEIPA 3.4% Can

wine: Champagne Devaux D Rosé Aged 5 Years
notes: Ultra pale luxurious rosé Champagne aged for 5 years before release to optimise flavour in a beautiful way. Delicate red fruit and orchard fruit kiss the palate and then spill over into a delightfully complex finish that is both crisp, evolved and moreish.

wine: Herdade do Peso `Trinca Bolotas` Alentejo Tinto
notes: Classic Alentejo red with plenty of rustic herby black fruit think damson and blackcurrant jam but not so sweet. There's good savoury concentration of flavour that retains freshness and supple smoothness. A wine to spend a bit of time with and perfect with a good steak pie.

This gorgeous Georgian red made from Saperavi is Jamie’s top tip for a big, hearty red. It is complex and swoony with notes of sweet cherry, chocolate and a dash of incense. It’s a seamless wine, both classy and voluptuous, making for fabulous fireside drinking.

wine: Altos Las Hormigas `Colonia Las Liebres` Mendoza Bonarda
notes: Bonarda might not be as well known as Malbec but this juicy cherry red fruitbomb shows a different side to Argentinian wine. With an almost Italian easy drinking style this is a perfect match for homemade pizza and shows a lovely red fruit smoothness.

A superb Malbec from a specific vineyard site selected for the quality of their fruit. The wine reflects this attention to detail in the creamy dark cherry puree and macerated plum flavours of this concentrated wine, with a smoky mocha finish.

Premium Alvarinho from vineyards sheltered from the cooling effect of the Atlantic Ocean. As a result the wine shows a perfect balance between fresh zesty citrus and ripe nectarine and mango tropicality. Ideal with cod fritters and spicy prawn dishes.
Merlot led blend with vibrant cherry and winter berry notes giving it a delightful depth of flavour and plenty of character. Some very clever winemaking has gone into this.

Deep and rich with lively aromas of orange peel, almonds and hazelnuts. The palate is dry and powerful rather than sweet with a vibrant and crisp finish.

At Bethany they use fully ripe Shiraz and Grenache grapes, pressed and allowed to ferment, halfway through the fermentation they add premium quality Australian brandy, then age the wine in large old oak barrels for up to 9 years. The bouquet displays intense raisin and nutty characters and on taste show similar flavours. The lingering finish is rich, quite sweet and full of flavour with a lovely ‘Port like’ quality.

wine: Bethany Old Quarry Fronti NV, Barossa
notes: The fully ripened grapes are harvested and allowed to ferment, halfway through the fermentation premium brandy spirit is added, and the wine is aged in oak casks for up to 6 years. The finished wine is a deep golden, amber colour and displays a rich, fragrant nose of orange marmalade, hints of honey and treacle. The full bodied and lingering velvety palate is deliciously rich and smooth

This delightful food friendly Champagne is perfect with canapes or lobster. The 2015 vintage allows for aromas of white peach, dried fruit and toasted almonds. Its persistent, delicate bubble reflects its finesse while its butter and brioche character indicate its development.
Extremely rare vintage Champagne. Liquid apple strudel springs to mind. No one else you are ever likely to meet will have tried this wine! If you’re into experiencing the unique, this is for you.

Lots of teeny tiny bubbles thanks to extended bottle ageing. Aromas of hazelnuts and spice. Low dosage allows the quality of the Pinot Noir fruit to shine through while keeping a crisp tautness. Nuttiness and pear ripeness add breadth on the tongue before a lingering, fresh and dry aftertaste.
Bright, as you'd expect but with a seam of depth that feels rather rewarding. Bone dry but not short of fruity appeal.
Crisp and delicious with aromatic apple and pear aromas on the nose followed by a crisp palate of succulent fruits. Gently foamy, just off dry and possessing an enticing, bright finish.

Love Prosecco but fancy something a bit drier this is the one for you. This single vintage Italian Sparkler comes from a single vineyard site so the quality is excellent and it is made in the same way as prosecco so it has the same lightness and fruit driven freshness. Durello is a grape that gives wine with more zesty freshness and less cloying sweetness.

An exemplary bit of English winemaking on show here. A flawless Blancs de Noirs, 100% pinot noir in aroma and flavour, 100% British. A rose wine to be nationally proud of that’s very welcome and delicious in the glass. Make the switch from overpriced pink Champagne today!

wine: Bodegas Emilio Moro Ribera del Duero (Organic)
notes: Ribero wines, in our humble opinion, need to express their own identity. They need to smell and taste of Ribero and not get masked by layers of oak or international styling. This one by Bodegas Emilio Moro really works for us. There’s a proper sense of typicity from aroma to finish. Stright out of the textbook! Tastes great with slow-cooked beef or lamb.

We loved this wines little brother so much that we thought we better see what Manzanos could do when they set their mind to it. Boy they didn't disappoint this is a bit special. Graciano might not be that widely planted in Rioja but the fruit for this wine comes from the oldest vines left standing and has an intensity of dark fruit and creamy fullness that few other wines can match. Soft on the palate but packed with flavour this is a terrific wine.
Superior modern expression of Rioja's best known grape Tempranillo but here grown in Carinena. Spicey Savoury and Earthy this is bold enough to match up to chorizo and beef stew or a good steak.
Amazing Value for money version of our favourite Rioja. Graciano is a bit of a speciality for Finca Manzanos and this robust yet aromatic and fruit led Rioja is one of our favourite mid-week tipples.
This is serious stuff black fruit aroma with a bonfire smoky twist. Not as overpowering or dense as you might expect but perfectly balanced with ripe sweet tannins.

One of the great modern wines of South Africa with a simple goal of achieving perfection. Individual parcels of grapes are vinified tasted and rejected until only the finest remain which are then blended to achieve a wine greater than the sum of it's parts. A wine which has elements of Bordeaux in style but is utterly unique and resolutely New World. Pencil shavings, Tobacco leaf and pure dark berry compote only begins to hint at the joys to be found in the glass.

Feteasca Neagra, the grape variety is all but exclusive to Romania. So, what’s it like converted to wine? With vibes of red cherry and black pepper this light to medium bodied isn’t a million miles away from Pinot Noir crossed with Merlot. Well worth a visit!
Paul says... Complex aromas of dark fruit/ tobacco and leather in an all together giving fashion. This is world class wine/ smooth/ brooding and dense with exceptional length.
Lovely warm fruit pudding aromas with hints of soft oakiness lead to a palate of complex dark fruit with a soft yet grippy finish.

Vivid red and black fruit and only a gentle hint of New World “wet dog” feral aromas give this classic a huge sense of drinkability. Showing enough “Pinocity” to appease the experienced wine-drinker and enough juicy appeal to a more casual wine fan who just wants a great tasting Pinot Noir.

This wine from the excellent Fontodi stable is sourced from one of the original and highest sites of Chianti Classico at 600 metres altitude. produces wine of rare fragrance and finesse and well-balanced silky flavour. One of Chianti’s best-kept secrets.
Wonderful Italian character

wine: Amarone della Valpolicella Torre del Falasco
notes: Amarone is always a treat, made from semi dried grapes you can expect a deep and luxurious black cherry and ripe plum with layer on layer of almost chocolate darkness. The best versions are expensive and made in very small quantities this strikes a happy balance of quality and affordability. Thanks to a slight residual sweetness this is a wine that can match up to dark chocolate almost as happily as it will to sticky burnt ends or duck in plum sauce.

wine: Vigneti Canosini Tufarello Nero di Troia
notes: Mature bush vines give excellent ripe fruit allowing the wine to develop a deep ruby red in the glass and an intense, long-lasting perfume. It has great structure and concentrated without being confected fruit on the palate with balanced tannins giving a dry finish.

wine: Salice Salentino Vigneti Del Salento  Zolla
notes: Smooth, supple red from one of our favourite Italian winemakers. Their Primitivo has been a customer favourite for the last few years and this is just as tasty. Earthy rustic autumnal wine for nights in with simple meals and good company.

wine: Valpolicella Ripasso Superiore Torre del Falasco
notes: Aromas of dried cherry and dark plums are followed by hints of mocha and dark chocolate on the nose. A powerful, full-bodied palate opens with a spiced fruit character and supportive tannins. Raisin and candied peel notes come from the 'ripasso' method and are layered with rounded, ripe cherry flavours. The finish is long with added spicy nutmeg notes

While not as full as Barolo this lovely wine boasts many of the same delicate floral notes and intense red summer berry flavour. The wine pours with a deceptive lightness and clarity which belies the depth of flavour. A fantastic bottle.

This Veneto Rosso displays an array of dark fruit flavours in a sumptuous and smooth style. In feel this wine is medium to full-bodied with an almost dark powdery tannin structure that makes for cosy drinking with or without food. There is a nod towards the more famous wine of its region - Amarone, but without the big price tag and normally higher alcohol content. Fans of Baglio U-Passimiento should feel at home with this great wine from Northern Italy.
A generous Italian red in the style of Salice Salento, this is worryingly moreish. Lush, lip-smacking blackberry dominates the palate which is rounded off by a smooth and satisfying aftertaste.

Amarone is always a treat, made from semi dried grapes you can expect a deep and luxurious black cherry and ripe plum with layer on layer of almost chocolate darkness. The best versions are expensive and made in very small quantities this is excellent.

A beautiful and seductive Sicilian red, this Nero d'Avola has both presence of flavour and fullness of body. Expect to find plenty in the way of morello cherry and jammy notes with more than a gentle nod to the Amarone style.

wine: Cantina Diomede Canace Nero di Troia
notes: What we in the trade call a "belter". This is wonderfully dark reddish purple in the glass. Mouth-watering aromas of cocoa, coffee, liquorice and ripe berry fruit are complimented by a velvety palate. Full-bodied and lush with elegant tannins and lingering spice.

One of Italy's greatest wines. Beautiful Sangiovese rose petal, depth and complexity here already. Will surely improve over the next 5 to 10 years. Strikingly pure, with a bit of a punch, that is sure to mellow out in time as the wines tannins soften. Despite this the focus and finesse of Fontodi's wine demonstrates the exceptional winemaking these vineyards have become known for.

From two marvellous estates, this is big, rich and concentrated with dark berry fruit. On the nose there is a hint of cigar box and notes of vanilla. The palate is up front and new world in style. A real Sunday treat bottle!

wine: Primitivo Di Manduria Vigneti Del Salento Zolla
notes: Our customers rave over this Puglian winner. Plush/ swish and ample with wide appeal. Notes of cherry/ chocolate and coffee. VERY modern.

wine: Terres Fideles Cotes du Roussillon Villages (Organic)
notes: This blend of Grenache and Carignan balances big dark fruit flavours with juicy freshness. It’s got great texture, making you feel like it was a bargain, plus, it happens to be organic which for many folk, helps it sit more naturally with the metabolism.

Blended from all thirteen varietals allowed in Chateau Neuf from vineyards exposed to the winds of the Mistral. This world leading wine has defined the Region for decades and will continue to do so. Wildly rugged and effortlessly graceful in equal measure.

Bringing New World sensibilities to the most french of wines pays dividends here. Lots of concentration and leathery spicey dark fruit is lifted by a little cherry freshness. This retains a rustic muscularity making it perfect with chargrilled Rib of Beef.

We tasted this after a series of expensive and mildly disappointing wines from Northern Rhone estates and were wowed by the boldness and balance of this wine while retaining that easy drinking generosity that Rhone wines are famed for. For a very reasonable price this is a confident and comforting wine which could easily become a regular in your wine rack. Brambley and lush on the palate with a hint of tannin and a flavour that lingers this is a proper Rhone ranger... Hi ho silver!!
Santa Macarena Pinot Noir

From very high vineyards in Tupungato this is an excellent and refined Malbec. While it has a freshness and comparative lightness on the palate there are layers of savoury fruit absent in many Malbecs at this price. Sophisticated and satisfying.

One of our Favourite finds of 2023 the Las Estellas Pinot Noir is a delight. Summer berry scented and light in body but with a persistent and intense flavour that recalls expensive Burgundy. Highly recommended!

Australia can do Cabernet that can be light and reminiscent of Bordeaux. This is a little more Aussie rules than Polo however but every but every bit as enjoyable. Dark and powerful Cabernet with tonnes of black winter bramble fruit and a very tight balance. This is well made, smooth and hugely enjoyable.

Plenty to explore in the aroma department. Slightly feral savoury scents are pushed to one side by wave after wave of almost port-like dark fruits. The wine has the depth of prunes in its fruit profile, baked and almost burnt. It's a rather charming beast with a growl that thrills.
Fabulous all rounder Cabernet Sauvignon with lovely depth.

As Australian as a Kangaroo surfing in a billabong while playing a didgeridoo and almost as unexpected. This is utterly lovely yes I know it's a bit too big for it's boots and riper than a four week old camembert but for sheer fruity lip staining joy it's hard to beat. Like all the Killibinbin wines this is potent and lush but the blend of Cab and Shiraz gives a lovely mix of dark and spicy with blackcurranty and herby that is irresistible.

The 2015 vintage was a stellar year for a stellar wine receiving scores of 99-100 from may respected judges. After a few tricky vintages 2015 was particularly fine and allowed excellent fruit to be sourced across Eden Valley and the Adelaide Hills. Intense and perfectly balanced with the potential to develop in the bottle for a great many years.

With 20 years of bottle age, this is in an amazing drinking window. It’s a rare expression of the house’s best vineyards and a worthwhile experience for more serous Aussie wine fans. The vintage was exemplary in Australia and Tahbilk have some of the best old vines down under. Looks great on paper, tastes even better in your big glass!

Merlot is much maligned but when it is good it can be very good. This Argentine wine is everything you could want from a cool climate Merlot soft chocolaty fruity plum and bramble coulis with a savoury edge of tannin keeping it satisfyingly dry. Perfect with rack of lamb.
Aniello 006 Riverside Estate Pinot Noir
Fabulous all rounder Malbec/ with lovely depth.

"Top drop. Very Northern Rhone in style." Striving for perfection and purity, the father/son team at Clarendon Hills demonstrate their commitment to quality and authenticity through handpicked fruit, chosen by taste and smell alone. Picked from a single site, home to some of the oldest vines in the world, each wine displays its own character unique to the patch of dirt on which the grapes were grown. Astralis, meaning "pertaining to the stars", is a truly timeless wine, blending together power and purity. Recognised as one of the top 100 wines of the century, this now 15 year old wine still ma

grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot
notes: A blend of Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Petit Verdot.
Aromas of candied apricots, baked apple and Vanilla are followed by plenty of peach and apricot. The extended skin contact gives a dry tannin structure and long, mineral finish.

We know it's expensive and while there are more sensible ways to spend sixty pounds we would struggle to think of a more enjoyable one. This wine pours with a hint of gold that suggests a well judged use of oak and the aromas are heady with tropical stone fruit and jasmine and acacia flowers on the tongue the wine is rich and complex but in balance and the crisp apple note leaves the palate clean and refreshed. The reputation of Paul Hobbs for finding the best sites to plant his vines is well earned and this wine showcases some wonderful fruit brilliantly. Do you really need another pair of sh
As vibrant and expressive as many a Marlborough but with its own, delightful green pepper aromas. Make the swap today! A perfect partner to fennel, herby salads or goat’s cheese dishes.

From the Basque region of Spain this rebellious wine is a thrillingly electric burst of citrus and apple skins. With a subtle spritz which leaves your palate clean and refreshed it is the perfect wine to serve with sushi or Thai fishcakes.

wine: Vinos Mas Buscados Te Quiero Field Blend (Organic)
notes: What happens when you find a vineyard which has too many different vines to make a viable range of different varietal wines. Usually, you rip up lots of them and gamble on the ones that people are familiar with and we all end up drinking ho-hum wines made in the same way. In this case though the winemaker chose to just harvest the lot of them and make the best wine possible. The result is lively fresh and well balanced with, as you might expect, layers of flavour.

With a mature, almost beguiling palate, this wine is very expressive. Plenty of almost breakfast marmalade notes mix with a smoke tinted finish and plenty of grown-up salinity. If you’re an experienced “winey” you’ll want to take this unique drop for a spin in your big glass!

Time travel for your palate! The most royal of Marlborough Sauvignons made by Kevin Judd who created Cloudy Bay. This delivers everything you could want from Sauvignon Blanc and more. More detail, more finesse, more character and impeccable balance.

A single-vineyard Verdicchio that looks a little chardonnay like but with pronounced acacia and field flower aromas. There’s a lushness over super ripe white plum fruit and nice freshness on a long finish. This wine is particularly good with crayfish risotto and chicken Kiev.

A super fresh and elegant example of the Catarratto grape which will compliment fresh seafood perfectly. This is modern winemaking with a respect for tradition organic grapes Natural winemaking with no filtration to give you a taste of Sicily at home. For lovers of low sulphite wines without the funky flavours this might be perfect.

This wine justifies the whole trendy category of natural orange wine. Startling richness and complexity, really ‘ Winey’ and grown-up, like unpasturised milk, or those French cheeses that kill people. Who knew Catarratto (!) could be so tasty? A must-try wine. Even the baby brother bottling, the single cream version, is brilliant.

Completely delicious Italian white from Lugana often listed as Trebbiano this is actually made from Verdicchio which explains why it is so tasty. Peach perfect and super refreshing this is our favourite new thing for sipping in the sunshine. Try with snacks and dips/ cheese straws or stuffed pasta.

Our top Lugana wine really shows what can be achieved with the right level of care and dedication. Often used for blending here the full peachy fullness of the wine is supported by careful Oak to give a fullness and complexity that rivals Burgundy. The local name for the grape used is Turbiana which used to be known internationally as Trebbiano however it has been revealed to be Verdicchio... no wonder it's so tasty.
Slightly off dry floral fruity Garganega blend with a real touch of class. Lovers of the fruitier style of Sauvignon Blanc could be easily tempted by this.

wine: Bellavista Convento della Santissima Annunciata Curtefranca
notes: This is quite simply one of the best wines we have tasted. A wine capable of changing your mind about Chardonnay for ever.

wine: Val de Loire Vignerons de Valencay Sauvignon Blanc
notes: “It’s all about the soil”, Is anything more like to set of the BS detector than that. However, in this case the high proportion Silex soils in the vineyards that produce the fruit for this excellent wine really are the difference maker. In Sancerre they enliven and add minerality and even in the more mundane vineyards of Tourraine they have a similarly transformative effect. Give it a try we are sure you’ll love it as much as we do.

Aligote is the lesser-known white from Burgundy and struggles to achieve the heights of Chardonnay. With the right winemaker at the helm though wines can rival Chablis for a mineral expression that verges toward smoky. This is a really lovely version that adds fresh apple skin textural weight making it perfect with goat’s cheese tarts.

Super rare example of white Chateauneuf by leading Rhone producer, Beaucastel. This is Roussanne expressed in its most voluptuous and opulent way. Yes, rarity plays a big part in this but it’s a once in a lifetime opportunity to experience this wine.

This great value Valencay is an unoaked blend of 85% Sauvignon Blanc and 15% Chardonnay. Sébastien feels the Chardonnay adds body and texture to the wine and offers a slightly different flavour profile to that of its more famous neighbours, Sancerre and Pouilly-Fume.

Enticing aromas of dried apricot, honey and marmalade, with baked apple and a touch of warm spice. Richly sweet and velvety on the palate, layered with quince and candied citrus. A vibrant freshness keeps it balanced, carrying through to a long finish.

A refined and expressive nose of green apple, white peach, and bright citrus fruits, with floral notes and a distinctive mineral freshness. These elegant aromas equally stand out on the flavoursome palate. A long, rounded, and rewarding finish.

Delicious aromas of ripe apple and pear, lemon curd, and toasted brioche, with a hint of honeyed almonds from extended lees ageing. Elegant effervescence; creamy and mouth-filling, beautifully balanced. A long, zesty, and deeply rewarding finish.

Your nose is met with aromas of strawberries, raspberries, and warm pastry, amid the delightful bubbles. A refreshing, flavoursome palate of red cherries, Victoria plum, and a squeeze of lemon, with a long, vibrant finish.
An enticing nose of wild strawberries, raspberries, cranberries, and red cherries leads to a refreshing palate with zippy citrus zest alongside those lush red berry fruits. An excellent English rosé.
Fresh and vibrant aromas of elderflower and pink grapefruit, which continue on the palate with lively, zesty lime and an elegant mineral edge. A long, refreshing, and satisfying finish.

Layers of red cherries, raspberries, rose and liquorice, with a hint of orange zest. The palate is refreshing and full-bodied, with silky tannins that lift the complex flavours and are supported by an elegant minerality. Marvellous length. Worth decanting. Superb cellar potential.
Ripe blueberries and blackberries on the nose with some spicy notes. That fresh dark berry fruit liberally and gracefully fills your mouth, carried by silky smooth tannins. A luscious long finish.

Vibrant red cherries and raspberries on the nose, and an initially fruit-filled palate that enjoys its sparkling nature with a light mousse and rich texture. Worth serving slightly chilled at the family barbecue or pizza night.

aromas: Pear, Apricot, Lemon, Pineapple, Ginger, Honey
notes: Delicious notes of dried apricot, lemon zest, pineapple, honey, and ginger. These brilliantly fresh citrus and stone fruit flavours are joined by ripe pear and apple, a touch of spice, well-integrated oak, and a vibrant minerality. The finish is long, bright, and expressive.

A fragrant and complex nose of blackcurrants, blackberries, blueberries and raspberries, with hints of mint chocolate and forest floor. The palate is generous with fine tannins lifting the fresh fruit flavours and delicate savoury notes. A luscious long finish.
An aromatic nose of apricot, lychee, Earl Grey tea and marmalade. Invigorating in the mouth, with ripe peach and the gentle grip of citrus peel. A lingering and refreshing finish.

Rich, complex aromas of black cherries, blackberries, dried fig, dark chocolate and warm spices, with a hint of vanilla. Beautifully balanced with layers of fruit and spice lifted by velvety tannins. An expressive and deeply rewarding finish of great length.

A rich and inviting nose of blackberries and plum, dark chocolate, cracked black pepper, and warm spices. Fresh and fruity in the mouth with firm tannins and a lick of liquorice. A long, complex and rewarding finish.
Fruity aromas of red cherries and raspberries, plum and a touch of spice. A light and refreshing palate with soft tannins. A charming, fruit-driven finish makes it a perfect everyday red.

Fresh and expressive aromas of strawberries, raspberries, and redcurrants, with subtle floral notes and a hint of brioche. Those juicy red berry flavours are even brighter on the palate with a fine mousse. Delightfully refreshing with an elegant mineral finish.
Elegant floral aromas with apricot, red apple, and fresh cucumber. Delightfully refreshing, with delicate yet lively bubbles and a gentle, creamy mouthfeel.

Ripe red cherries, cranberries, and apple blossom on the nose with a hint of marzipan. A gorgeous and generous palate of red apples and peach with subtle saline notes. Brilliant bubbles. Complex, refreshing, and perfectly persistent on a long finish.

Initial notes of crisp green apple, ripe pear and peach, and a mineral quality. While still a young vintage, give this wine time in your glass, and you will also be greeted with citrus and stone fruits, along with a hint of oak. Beautifully fresh, rich, and complex.
Remarkably refreshing and crisp, with flavours and aromas of pear drops, lemon zest, juicy apricots and peach, and a subtle creamy texture throughout. Expressive finish.
Super aromatic with lots of lime, green apple and gooseberry with hints of passionfruit and elderflower. Extremely refreshing.
Very fruit forward on the nose and palate. Bright red cherries, juicy cranberries and plums, with hints of blackberry leaf. Soft tannins. Long finish. More please.

A delicate yet lively fizz. Aromas of ripe orchard fruits and crunchy red apple, continuing with refreshing flavour and mouthfeel with added notes of lemon zest and brioche. Delightfully refined and complex with a lovely long finish.

Luscious aromas of honey, pineapple and ripe pear, from Sémillon grapes left to dry out on the vine. On the palate, vibrant acidity keeps the sweetness beautifully in check, leading to a long, tangy finish of marmalade.
Very fresh on the nose and palate. Crunchy wild strawberries, red cherries, and raspberries combine with a saline, mineral character.
Crisp aromas and flavours of white peach, lemon zest and kiwi with a hint of almond. Well-balanced minerality and an elegant, savoury finish.
Vibrant aromas of tropical and citrus fruits with a hint of vanilla. Rich and layered on the palate, with baked apple, brioche and a touch of clove. Elegant and long finish.

Refined aromas of red cherries and raspberries, with notes of orange, leather, and a touch of spice. Elegant yet energetic, with silky, well-integrated tannins. Delightful from the first sip through to a succulent finish.

Ripe red cherries and strawberries with zesty lemon tickle your nose and then deliver with delightful refreshing flavour, adding a hint of brioche and cinnamon to the mix. Another sublime English sparkling wine from Everflyht.

A fresh and lively nose of green apple and pear, citrus zest, and notes of white pepper. The juicy palate has a mineral edge and delicate herbaceous character. Very refreshing with a lingering finish.
Charming aromas of green orchard fruits, lime zest and kiwi, with subtle floral notes. There is a distinct minerality on the palate with layers of vibrant young fruit. A delightful zippy finish.
Highly aromatic with an expressive nose and palate filled with ripe tropical fruit and notes of cinnamon. Beautifully balanced and very refreshing with a hint of sweetness on a gorgeous long finish.

Very expressive, effervescent and inviting. Zesty citrus and ripe orchard fruits, toasted almonds with a touch of salinity. A lovely fine mousse and a lingering finish. ‘Corallian’ is named after the coral-rich limestone of the chalky soils where the Chardonnay vines grow in Dorset.

Vibrant aromas of lemon, lime and apple blossom with toasty notes and a gentle hint of petroleum. A concentrated and complex palate with abundant refreshing citrus fruits and warm toast long into the finish.
Expressive aromas of lime, peach and gooseberries, with notes of elderflower and fresh-cut grass. Bright and zesty on the palate, with tropical fruit and a lovely, refreshing finish.

An inviting nose of black tea, morello cherries, strawberries and liquorice, with hints of cedar and warm spices. Bright and fresh on the palate, with hedgerow blackberries, damson and blackcurrants lifted by well-integrated tannins. A soft, smooth and lingering finish.
A crisp and aromatic nose of green apple and citrus fruits, with delicate floral and herbal notes. An elegant palate filled with flavour. A long and refreshing finish.
Bountiful aromas of fresh plum, blackberries and blueberries, with hints of thyme, cedar and spice. The palate is joined by dark chocolate and has a remarkable freshness. A long, smooth finish.

Abundant aromas of red berries and spices. The fruit becomes more refined on the palate, with cranberries, red cherries, redcurrants, and a touch of cedar, walnut, and vanilla. Delectable flavours and length.
Tempting aromas of raspberries, blueberries, blackcurrants, and dark chocolate with hints of mint, all concentrated on the palate with smooth mouthfeel and a touch of mocha on a lengthy finish.

Cracked black pepper, toasted vanilla and coconut with plum jam, hedgerow blackberries, and ripe blueberries. A brilliant and concentrated full-bodied mouthfeel with a wonderfully long and lingering finish.

Remarkably rich aromas of ripe black cherries, cassis and vanilla, with hints of wild herbs and cedar. These scents also translate to the palate, with concentrated, juicy fruit and smooth tannins. Well-balanced. This wine is easily enjoyable now, or even more so over the next few years.

Beautiful, bright, and juicy wine with enticing fresh flavours and aromas of black cherries, cassis, and hints of cedar. A delicious, rich, full-bodied red. Wonderfully well-balanced, silky smooth tannins, and a lovely long finish. Very enjoyable.
Aromas of fresh blackcurrants, plum, and a touch of spice lead into a silky-smooth palate of raspberries and red cherries. The ripe fruit character carries through to a long, harmonious finish.
The bubbles lift delicate floral aromas, and these notes combine with vanilla and refreshing hints of lychee and green apple on the palate.
Aromas of an Autumn forest floor with added flavours of walnut, smoke, and light citrus. Very refreshing and lightly sparkling.

aromas: Apricot, Lime, Orange Peel, Ginger, Vanilla
notes: Lightly sparkling and very aromatic. Orange peel, apricot, lime, vanilla, sweet tannins and a fresh ginger finish. Fragrance of delicious Darjeeling tea.

Delicate aromas of apricots and nectarines with floral, mineral and smoky notes. A refreshing palate with terrific depth and balance. Give time in your glass for the flavours to flourish, as they reflect the nose with added citrus and hints of salinity. A lovely, long finish.
Ripe black cherries and plum on the nose with gentle spice and herbaceous notes, all mirrored on the palate with a distinct minerality. Complex and refined. Long, juicy finish.
Wild roses, liquorice, and strawberry jam, with hints of mint and spices. Smooth tannins. Bright and well-balanced. Lovely finish.
Amazing aromas and a juicy palate of fresh strawberries and morello cherries with notes of fennel balanced by fine tannins leading to a long finish. Very moreish. And we love the Record Label.
Inviting aromas of juicy strawberries, raspberries and red cherries with hints of vanilla and spices. Very smooth on the palate with an additional minerality. Complex and delightful.
Inviting aromas of black and red cherries, plum, blackberries, and notes of coconut and warm spices. A smooth and generous palate, leading to a fresh, fruity and persistent finish.
An expressive nose and palate of black cherries, blackberries, plum, with a hint of warm spices and vanilla. Fresh and vibrant, framed by firm tannins. Long and lingering on the finish.

Intense and complex aromas with notes of black cherries, blackcurrants, cedar, dark chocolate, and warm spices. A rich palate of ripe plum, fig, dried fruit and balsamic notes lifted by velvety tannins. A deeply satisfying finish.
Honey, quince and dried apricot on the nose, with citrus fruits and floral notes. A deliciously rich, refreshing and complex palate with a lovely long finish.
Aromas of raspberries and morello cherries with hints of spices and smoke. Joined by blackcurrants and blackberries on the palate. Silky smooth tannins. Lingering finish.
Delightful aromas of fresh strawberries and grapefruit, flavours that fill your mouth, along with red cherries and a touch of cinnamon. Lovely mouthfeel, somewhat savoury, very refreshing.
Raspberries with strawberries and cream on the nose and palate. Remarkably soft yet fresh. Serve this light red slightly chilled, and the lovely crunchy red fruits will delight your senses.

aromas: Strawberry, Black Pepper, Vanilla, Thyme, Rosemary, Fennel
notes: The carefully handpicked grapes of the hundred-year-old vines provide an abundance of wild strawberry aromas with cracked black pepper and fennel. Light vanilla, rosemary, thyme, and a hint of orange zest. A rich and elegant palate with fine tannins. Let it breathe to enjoy now. Les Genoux will only get better with age. This is quite literally "The Bee's Knees."

A truly delicious wine from the first sip. Masses of ripe red fruit with floral and spice notes. It is very satisfying on the palate and has good weight with soft integrated tobacco leaf tannins. A lovely long finish. Pour me another glass!

aromas: Plum, Black Pepper, Dark Chocolate, Mocha
notes: A nose laden with plum, mocha and dark chocolate. These aromas evolve as flavours with hints of liquorice and cracked black pepper. Soft, velvety tannins and striking acidity. Remarkable and complex.

A blend of four Chenin Blanc vintages creates a striking aroma of peach and honey. The palate has a mineral core with ripe stone fruit, baked apple and a hint of orange zest and citrus. Delightfully refreshing.

aromas: Black Cherry, Plum, Vanilla, Dark Chocolate
notes: Dark chocolate, plum and black cherry on the nose. Rich dark black fruits fill the mouth with subtle hints of bell pepper, dark chocolate and notes of soft vanilla oak. Long, luscious, spicy finish.

aromas: Pear, White Peach, Peach, Vanilla, Hazelnut
notes: A delicious combination of white peach, pear, citrus, vanilla and hazelnut. Creamy texture and great length.
Rich, rounded fruit flavours of apricot, pear and honey. A slight hint of salt and minerality on the finish.
Luscious black fruits with spice and liquorice fill the mouth. Rich, soft tannins and a great length.
Succulent raspberries and cherries on the nose. Masses of fresh berries on the palate with mighty fine tannins.

wine: Château Petit Roubié Picpoul de Pinet 2024
notes: A hint of sea breeze on the nose combined with citrus, apple skins and herbs. Peach and tropical fruits on the palate offer a refreshing glass.
Bursting with bright crushed raspberries and strawberries with light floral notes. These are joined by refreshing notes of orange blossom, redcurrants, and red cherries on the palate.
A delicious blend of old vine Grenache and Carignan. Hedgerow berries, plum and a pinch of vanilla. Well-rounded depth of flavour with subtle tannins.
An abundance of luscious black fruits, blackberries and blueberries with notes of spice and liquorice that last long in the mouth, underlaid by creamy vanilla oak.
Blackcurrants, morello cherries, and spices provide powerful aromas that continue on the palate. A very smooth and lengthy finish.
Hints of stone fruits on the nose, whilst the palate is full of tropical fruit and dried apricots with notes of vanilla and honey that deliver a deliciously long finish.
A Grower Champagne of rich structure. Delicate and complex aromas of flowers, red berries and a hint of butter. Light fizz with citrus and green apple flavours and a long, refreshing finish.

Instant aromas of red cherries and plum, but allow this wine to breathe, and you will also be greeted with generous notes of cracked black pepper and leather. The fruit is fresh on the palate with a luscious and balanced blend of gentle acidity and rich, soft tannins. Lovely to drink now, and has a few years’ ageing potential.

aromas: Pear, Lemon, Grapefruit, Melon, Flint, Honey
notes: Lemon, grapefruit, and pear aromas are balanced with flint and mineral notes. Ample fresh citrus characters combine with melon and honey, leading to a lingering mineral finish. Perfect for a seafood or spicy vegetarian dish.
A complex nose of candied lemon, orange zest, marmalade and acacia honey. The palate translates the nose perfectly. It is harmonious, creamy and full, and the flavoursome finish goes on and on.
Dark, rich morello cherries and forest fruit flavours leap from the glass. These are combined with sweet spices and soft leather on the palate. A smoky, savoury, firm finish.

aromas: Blackcurrant, Cassis, Plum, Black Pepper, Smoke
notes: Rich cassis and chocolate with a hint of smoke on the nose. Luscious blackcurrant, plum, liquorice, and a pinch of cracked black pepper spice are on the palate. Mouth-filling with a generous length of flavour. A delicious Chilean red.

Your senses will welcome a generous helping of strawberries and cream with red cherries on top and pastries on the side. Superbly soft on the tongue with elegant effervescence and crisp acidity. Marvellous.
Traditional apple crumble with a hint of lemon and red cherries fills your nose and mouth. Brioche and mineral notes. Delightfully dignified and fresh.

Bryan Deleu is an up-and-coming name to know in the Northern Rhône. After studying architecture, working as a hotel maître d', and training at a series of renowned wineries, Bryan purchased a small plot of neglected vineyard land in Saint-Joseph in 2018. After clearing and terracing the land himself, Bryan planted syrah on the region’s granite slopes. Exorde is his flagship. It’s textbook Northern Rhône syrah, meaning savory, smoky, and powerfully aromatic. Tastes like: Blackberry, violets, smoke, cracked pepper. How to drink: Alongside lamb chops, steak, or a winter stew.

wine: Scar of the Sea, SLO Coast Chardonnay 2024
notes: On California’s central coast, fog and cool breezes from the Pacific help produce chardonnay that’s fresh, citrusy, and a bit salty. That’s certainly the case at Scar of the Sea, whose home vineyard - a key source of this wine - is just one mile from the ocean. Mikey and Gina Giugni farm it biodynamically, and age their chardonnay for nearly two years in barrel before bottling. The result is a white wine that’s richly textured without being oaky. Tastes like: Green apple, lemon curd, biscuits, sea spray. How to drink: Chilled with shellfish, roast chicken, or linguine with clams.

The husband-and-wife team of Matt Naumann and Audra Chapman launched Newfound in the Sierra Foothills in 2016. They wanted to explore the potential of making fresh, easy-drinking red wines from Mediterranean grapes in this part of northern California. Gravels is their flagship. An equal blend of grenache and carignan, it showcases the juicy fruit and lifted aromatics of the former, as well as the firm structure and savory notes of carignan. Tastes like: Raspberry, lavender, sage, black pepper. How to drink: Lightly chilled with burgers, grilled sausages, or margherita pizza.

wine: Domaine de la Giraudière, Saumur-Champigny Rouge 'Les Meuniers' 2024

This example of the latter comes from the limestone slopes of Saumur-Champigny. It’s a juicy, medium-bodied red with cab franc’s hallmark earthy, spice-laden aromatics on full display. Tastes like: Blackberry, violets, tobacco leaf, black pepper. How to drink: Lightly chilled with barbecue ribs, pepperoni pizza, or vegetarian lasagna.

wine: Terralibera, Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi Classico Superiore 2025
notes: Gian Mario Bongini left a career in corporate finance to pursue one in winemaking, leaving Milan for the rural region of Le Marche. There, Gian Mario organically farms one grape, verdicchio, on two hillside vineyards a half-hour inland from the Adriatic. This white grape makes forgettable wines in many parts of Italy, but in the small area of Castelli di Jesi, it yields one of Italy’s great light, crisp, coastal whites. Tastes like: Pear, lemon zest, salted almond, jasmine. How to drink: Chilled with grilled shrimp or fried calamari.

wine: Domaine Julien Cruchandeau, Bourgogne Hautes-Côtes de Nuits Rouge 'Les Valancons' 2024
notes: For the last 20 years, Julien Cruchandeau has been at the forefront of bringing high-quality winemaking to less heralded parts of Burgundy. That started in Bouzeron, where he focused on aligoté, with some initial assistance from the legendary Aubert de Villaine of DRC. Julien then moved on to the hills above Nuits-Saint-Georges, which is where he organically farms this pinot noir. It’s robust and earthy, while still showing Julien’s bright, elegant touch in the cellar. Tastes like: Blackberry, baking spices, grilled mushrooms. How to drink: Alongside roast chicken or mushroom risotto.

At Tregole, Sophie Conte crafts wines from the highest-altitude vineyards in all of Chianti Classico. The first-generation winemaker takes advantage of the area’s cool nights and limestone soils to produce a fresh, floral, lithe style of sangiovese. That’s on display in this particularly food-friendly Tuscan red. Tastes like: Red cherry, tomato leaf, violets. How to drink: Lightly chilled with spaghetti pomodoro, pizza, or anything with red sauce.

Pedro Rodriguez farms old vines of local grape varieties, which grow on dramatically steep vineyards in Ribeira Sacra, an area of Galicia in northwestern Spain. While Ribeira Sacra is nearly synonymous with reds made from mencia, Pedro makes this richly textured white wine primarily from the godello grape. High altitude, cool nights, and stainless steel-aging keep the medium-bodied white fresh and smoky. Tastes like: Pear, lemon zest, chamomile, fennel. How to drink: Chilled with scallops, fish tacos, or roast chicken.

Since launching his own label 15 years ago in a cellar in downtown Cape Town, Duncan Savage has established himself as one of the most exciting winemakers in South Africa. His white wine style is all about freshness and bright acidity. For this 100% sauvignon blanc bottling, those traits are amplified even more by windy, high-elevation vineyard sites around the Stellenbosch region outside of Cape Town. Tastes like: Grapefruit, lemon zest, white flowers, sea salt. How to drink: Chilled with oysters, fried seafood, or citrusy salads.

wine: Hope Well, Eola-Amity Hills Chenin Blanc 2025
notes: Mimi Casteel grew up in the vines of the Willamette Valley, as her father Ted Casteel is the founder of famed Oregon winery Bethel Heights. Now, Mimi runs her own project in the Willamette, making natural wines at Hope Well. Mimi is extremely passionate about her land, with organic and biodynamic farming only telling a small part of the story. The result is a range of expressive, site-specific pinot noir and chenin blanc. This example of the latter is a vibrant, salty, super fresh white wine. Only a little more than 1000 bottles were produced in total. Tastes like: Peach, lemon zest, honeysuck

This new release of their flagship red is earthy, peppery, and nuanced, without sacrificing anything in the way of freshness or ‘chillability’.

wine: Forteresse de Berrye, Saumur Blanc 'Les Bourgères' 2023
notes: Forteresse de Berrye is an ancient military fort, which happens to sit on some of the best land for chenin blanc in the Loire Valley. Gilles Colinet saw its potential, and has been reviving both the land and castle since 2019. Bourgères comes from a plot of organic chenin grown in chalky limestone soils, which contribute a crisp, minerally character and notable freshness. Tastes like: Pear, lemon zest, sea salt, jasmine. How to drink: Chilled with soft cheeses or rich seafood dishes like pan-seared scallops.

Jean-Claude Lapalu is one of the great natural winemakers in Beaujolais. Following in the footsteps of Lapierre, Foillard, and Métras, he helped show the wine scene in Paris (and then the world) what Beaujolais was capable of. Based in the area of Brouilly, Jean-Claude has an abundance of old vines, which give his Beaujolais structure and complexity to go along with gamay’s classic bright fruit and floral aromatics. Tastes like: Black cherry, violets, white pepper. How to drink: A versatile chilled red that works with cheese and charcuterie or even grilled fish.

wine: Guiberteau, Saumur Blanc 'Les Moulins - Chai de la Dive' 2024

A protege of Nady Foucault at the legendary Clos Rougeard, Romain ages this organic chenin in stainless steel, which yields a particularly fresh, mineral, vivid white wine. Tastes like: Pear, honeycomb, smoke. How to drink: Chilled with a goat cheese salad or lemony seafood dishes.

It’s fresh, citrusy, and salty today, but also complex and capable of aging.

From the Basque Country on the northern coast of Spain, txakolina is an absolutely ideal warm weather white wine. It’s light, tart, and salty, with the kind of brisk acidity that makes it perfect with fresh seafood or refreshing on its own. Tastes like: Green apple, salty limes, cut grass. How to drink: A perfect brunch wine, or any other time of day with spicy seafood soup.

This sparkling wine is made from a grape called glera, which Bisol sources from lush, green hillsides between the Alps and the Adriatic Sea in northeastern Italy. Dry and refreshing, it’s a crisp, floral, easy-drinking alternative to Cava. Tastes like: Pear, salty lemons, and white flowers. How to drink: Cold on its own, or with anything salty and fried.

Agustí Torello Roca makes our favorite sparkling wines in Spain. He produces this bottling with macabeu and xarel-lo in Penedès. While those are the most common grapes and location for Cava production, Roca crafts this natural sparkler in the ancestral method, resulting in an effervescent pét-nat rosé that’s light and highly refreshing. Tastes like: Wild strawberry, citrus peel, and salt. How to drink: Cold, on its own, or with charcuterie and fried snacks.

wine: Château Peyrassol, Côtes de Provence Rosé 'Cuvée des Commanderie' 2023
notes: Peyrassol has been around for 800 years, so as you might imagine, its wines very much reflect those of the region as a whole. For Provencal rosé, that means light, pale pink, easy-drinking wines made from a blend of cinsault and grenache. Peyrassol’s organic vineyards are a stone’s throw from the Mediterranean coast, giving their rosé notable saltiness and freshness.

Les Baux-de-Provence is a tiny French wine region with just 12 producers. Those domaines, however, carry serious weight in the world of fine wine. Domaine de Trévallon, Domaine Hauvette, and Henri Milan all call Les Baux home. A more recent entrant making waves is Domaine Fontchêne, which is meticulously overseen by Henri Milan’s nephew, René Milan. René makes this juicy, lean, salty rosé from grenache, along with a small portion of cinsault and mourvedre. Tastes like: Strawberry, peach, herbs, and salt. How to drink: Chilled, with grilled fish, salad, or on its own.

wine: Maison A&S, Bourgogne Hautes-Côtes de Beaune Rouge 2023

Starting in the early ‘80s, René-Jean Dard and François Ribo pioneered natural winemaking in the Northern Rhone. Organic farming, zero sulfur, short macerations - it all yields some of the most vibrant and just plain delicious wines in the region. Their whites and reds are nuanced and have the stuffing to age, but the style is for fresh wines that are ready to go upon release. This white wine Crozes-Hermitage is a ripe, richly textured blend of roussanne and marsanne.

Deeply savory yet fresh and airy, this wine showcases Poggio’s classic style. It comes from the same vineyards as their Brunello, but it’s just not aged quite as long, and is ready to drink now.

On the Mediterranean coast of southeastern France, the husband-and-wife team of Guillaume and Karina Lefèvre biodynamically farm local grape varieties, along with wheat fields for bread, barley for beer, olive trees for olive oil, and veggies for, well, veggies. They’re meticulous farmers, and it translates into pure, lifted wines. This grenache-based, pale pink wine is as summer-friendly as any Provence rosé out there.

wine: Podere Le Boncie, Rosso di Toscana 'Le Trame' 2023
notes: If you’re a fan of fresh, elegant Tuscan reds, then know that this is one of our favorites at any price. It comes from Giovanna Morganti, who makes just three wines at her small, high-elevation estate in Chianti Classico. Le Trame is her flagship. It showcases the vibrant, earthy, Burgundian side of sangiovese. Think Le Ragnaie, Monteraponi, or Pergole Torte (just with a far friendlier price tag). Considering how little makes it to the U.S., it’s worth stocking up on whenever you get the chance.

Muscadet is always a light and crisp white wine. Less common is Muscadet that’s also textured, nuanced, and produced naturally. This wine from the husband-and-wife team of Guillaume Lavie and Adèle Lemoine checks all the boxes. The Loire Valley upstart farms biodynamically and bottles without filtration or sulfur, resulting in a pure, exceptionally easy-drinking white wine. Tastes like: Green apple, lemon zest, salted almond. How to drink: Cold with a salad, mussels and french fries, or on its own.

This fresh, crisp white comes from a 5th-generation family producer in the Wachau region of Austria. They farm small plots of gruner veltliner - Austria’s most popular grape - and age it in stainless steel, resulting in a particularly zesty, summer-friendly white wine.

In the Marche region of Italy, between the Apennine Mountains and the Adriatic Sea, Stefano Zoli farms just one grape, verdicchio. From his organic, high-altitude vines, Stefano turns the local grape into a quintessential coastal Italian white. It’s crisp, salty, and tailor-made for oysters and fresh seafood. Tastes like: Pear, lemon zest, salted almond. How to drink: When you want an off-the-beaten-path alternative to Chablis.

wine: Guilhem et Jean-Hugues Goisot, Bourgogne Aligoté 2023
notes: The Goisot family is based in Saint Bris, a small village in the northern reaches of Burgundy just outside of Chablis. There, Jean-Hughes Goisot and his son, Guillaume, biodynamically farm aligoté, hand-harvesting the grapes from the region’s chalky slopes. They age it in stainless steel, producing a classically crisp, refreshing expression of White Burgundy. Tastes like: Green apple, toast, white pepper. How to drink: A light white to have with simply prepared seafood or a salad with goat cheese.

Southeast of Vienna in the Austrian region of Burgenland, Helmut Velich planted vines in 1959. Helmut thought he was planting pinot blanc, but fortunately, the vines turned out to be chardonnay, which were ideal for the area’s limestone soils. His sons, Heinz and Roland, took over in the ‘90s, and have gone on to become highly revered figures in the Austrian wine scene. Heinz makes this chardonnay-based bottling from the estate’s younger vines. It’s a medium-bodied, juicy fruited, aromatic white wine. Tastes like: Pineapple, lemon curd, thyme, honeysuckle. How to drink: Chilled but not too col

This marks just the second-ever vintage from Martin Damm, a Danish wine importer who bought vineyards on the dramatically steep slopes of Ribeira Sacra in 2017. Martin previously worked extensively in Burgundy, and he’s now applying those sensibilities for expressive, vineyard-specific wines in northwestern Spain. This deep, peppery, savory red is made from garnacha tintorera, also known as alicante bouschet, which Martin ages in used barrels from Burgundy.

Aurélien Chatagnier is part of a new generation of Northern Rhône producers making fresh, transparent, immediately approachable red wines. Aurélien, who previously worked at Domaine Jamet in Côte-Rôtie, set up shop near Saint-Joseph in 2002. ‘Le Crêt Louison’ is a single-vineyard, 100% syrah that showcases his vibrant, peppery style. Tastes like: Plum, violets, olive tapenade, cracked pepper. How to drink: Lightly chilled with lamb chops, duck, or winter stews.

Beaujolais gets no better than Lapierre. Largely responsible for both Beaujolais and natural wine breaking into the global wine mainstream, Lapierre epitomizes the savory side of gamay. This new release of their flagship bottling is earthy, peppery, and bright - the perfect chilled red.

wine: Mani di Luna, Umbria Trebbiano 'Il Baratto' 2024
notes: Mani di Luna was launched in 2012 by three long-time friends in the hills of central Italy. Along with olives and cherries, they biodynamically farm a range of local grape varieties to make vibrant natural wines. Primarily from trebbiano, this medium-bodied white wine is ripe-fruited, salty, and crisp. Tastes like: Nectarine, orange zest, honeysuckle, salted almond. How to drink: Chilled alongside pasta with seafood, grilled fish, or salty appetizers.

Stéphane Tissot is an icon in the Jura. Their organic, biodynamic chardonnay is similar to White Burgundy, but a little more salty and savory. This single-vineyard bottling represents the top of the Jura's quality hierarchy. Tastes like: Ripe pears, roasted hazelnut, and ocean breeze. Tissot is a benchmark in the Jura for a wide range of wines. This is perhaps the most unusual. Chardonnay Rose is a very rare, pink grape variety that Tissot makes in miniscule quantities. It yields a white wine that’s floral, toasty, and herbal - it’s unlike any other wine out there, from the Jura or otherwise. Tastes like: Citrus zest, fennel, acacia, brioche. How to drink: Chilled with herb and spice-heavy dishes like falafel.

Dureuil-Janthial is one of the rare addresses that’s equally sought-after by casual Burgundy fans and the most serious collectors. The reason is simple: Vincent Dureuil's wines continue to represent some of the best value in all of Burgundy. This red comes from a single vineyard in Dureuil-Janthial’s hometown of Rully. A touch of gamay is blended with the pinot noir, resulting in a bright-fruited, earthy, chillable red wine.

Chave doesn’t have a sprawling range - you can count all of the domaine bottlings on one hand. And the 500 year-old family estate has very few peers in terms of wine-world prestige. That’s what makes Chave’s Saint-Joseph such an unlikely source of value. Yet year after year, it’s one of the smartest buys in the Northern Rhône. It’s also delicious right away, offering the chance to enjoy style-defining Rhône syrah without the classic wait.

Stéphane Tissot is the first name people associate with the Jura. That’s due to the fact that he’s a benchmark for local styles and grape varieties, a torchbearer for the natural wine movement, and a source of wines that has brought the Jura into the global wine discourse. Their wines are on the right side of natural, meaning they are a little bit wild but still delicious. This chardonnay is salty and savory, and tastes more like White Burgundy than most Jura whites. Pair this with comté cheese for optimal results.

notes: Chevillon’s Premier Crus are better than the Grand Crus of many producers. Their ‘19 'Les Perrières' illustrates that perfectly. Robert Chevillon is a reference point producer for Red Burgundy. The wines possess a very rare combination of collectibility and value. Synonymous with Nuits-Saint-Georges, Chevillon has old-vine plots in the village’s very best vineyards. 'Les Perrières' is one of those vineyards, yielding a wine that’s elegant and deeply concentrated, particularly from a classically-styled vintage like 2019.

Fresh. Biodynamic. Immediately enjoyable. These aren’t the first words we typically associate with Bordeaux. Not far from the borders of both Slovenia and Hungary, Christoph Neumeister makes some of Austria’s most singular white wines. David Trousselle is located in the generally unknown village of Orches in Burgundy. You’d go a long way towards grasping the nuances and potential of the Jura by tasting through the wines of Stéphane Tissot. He was a torchbearer for both the natural wine movement and the Jura as a whole, and over the past quarter-century, his wines have helped each break into the global mainstream. Stéphane crafts a wide range of styles, including this regional specialty made from savagnin. Château Chalon denotes a wine style called ‘Vin Jaune’. The savagnin grapes are aged oxidatively like Sherry for years in barrel before bottling. Unlike Sherry, however, the resulting wine isn’t fortified.

Morgon produces the most Burgundy-like wines in Beaujolais. That’s especially true when at the hands of a producer like Lapierre. notes: The young José Joaquín Ballesteros makes wines in a southern Spanish village best known for its clay amphora tanks. In fact, José Joaquín comes from a line of grape growers on his dad’s side, and amphorae producers on his mom’s. At Llámalo (pronounced "yah-mah-low"), he organically farms local grape varieties like cencibel, moravia, and bobal to make this smooth, aromatic red wine. Aged in amphora and bottled unfiltered, only 500 cases are produced each year. Tastes like: Blueberry, violets, smoke. How to drink: Enjoy with paella, winter stews, or all kinds of BBQ.

It’s run by Bárbara Requejo Frutos, who previously worked at Château Haut-Brion in Bordeaux and Pierre Peters in Champagne. Back in Spain, she organically farms just one grape variety: garnacha (grenache). Bright, herbal, and floral, ‘Los Arroyuelos’ is a perfect window into Bárbara’s elegant style. Tastes like: Raspberry, lavender, thyme, black pepper. How to drink: Lightly chilled with just about anything on the grill.

At Guímaro, Pedro Rodriguez is making some of the most exciting wines in Spain today. The family producer farms old vines of local grape varieties, which grow on dramatically steep vineyards in Ribeira Sacra, an area of Galicia in northwestern Spain. Pedro makes this richly textured white wine from godello. High altitude, cool nights, and stainless steel-aging keep it the midweight white tasting fresh and mineral Tastes like: Pear, lemon zest, chamomile, fennel. This white grape makes forgettable wines in many parts of Italy, but in the small area of Castelli di Jesi, it yields one of Italy’s great, crisp coastal whites. Tastes like: Ripe peach, salted almond, jasmine. How to drink: As a unique alternative to Chablis, or anytime there are oysters on the table.

Gruner veltliner is Austria’s most common grape, and it runs the stylistic gamut from light and easy to dense and opulent. Our favorite versions, however, are somewhere in between. Lithe and pure yet intensely mineral and full of energy. Barbara Öhlzelt epitomizes this take on the grape. Old vines and barrel aging yield a gruner with texture and depth over a lightweight frame. Tastes like: Ripe pear, white pepper, chives, salt. How to drink: Cold with sushi, grilled fish, or roasted veggies.

Liguria doesn’t have the reputation of coastal Italian wine regions like Campania, Sicily, Tuscany, Sardinia, and so on. The small area south of Piedmont is better known for plenty of other things - the beaches of the Riviera, Monet paintings, Cinque Terre, and pesto. With all that said, we tried this Ligurian vermentino recently, and it’s absolutely worth a shot. It’s made by Fabio Lambruschi, who is still helped in the vineyard by his 93 year-old father Ottaviano, on a dramatic hillside overlooking the Mediterranean Sea. While some vermentino can be waxy, oaky, or bitter, this is different.

Jacquère is the most planted grape in the Savoie, a region better known for skiing and fondue than high-quality wine. But in the hands of David Dupasquier, the fifth-generation to run his family winery, you’ll see exactly what this alpine grape is capable of. It’s crisp, minerally, and highly refreshing, an ideal alternative to Muscadet or Chablis. Tastes like: Lemon zest, toast, sea salt, smoke. How to drink: Cold with crudo, oysters, or soft cheeses.

If you’re not familiar, Envínate is arguably the most exciting producer in Spain. And if you are, then know that these wines are as good as any reds they’ve ever released. They’re all made naturally in the remote (absolutely gorgeous) region of Ribeira Sacra in Galicia. These are savory, spicy red wines that are wildly undervalued considering the quality. More savory than the 'Viñas de Aldea' and less weighty than their single-parcel wines, this small-production bottling is fresh, earthy, and highly versatile with food.

Morgon produces some of the most savory, deep, full-bodied wines in Beaujolais. The area’s granite-rich soils, which the young Quentin Harel farms organically, yields a particularly grippy, concentrated expression of gamay. Tastes like: Ripe plum, violet, fresh-tilled soil. How to drink: Slightly chilled with burgers, pizza, or BBQ chicken.

Located west of Beaujolais and south of the Loire, Tricot takes advantage of volcanic soils and old vines to make vibrant, highly enjoyable wines. 'Les Petites Fleurs' is made entirely from gamay, and tastes like a particularly deep and peppery version of Beaujolais.

T his crisp white comes from the German region of Franken, where Stefan Vetter is making truly electric natural wines. 'Sandstein' is one of Vetter's Premier Cru bottlings, and showcases the delicate, almost ethereal quality that his wines achieve.

Tissot is a benchmark in the Jura for a wide range of wines. This is perhaps the most unusual. Chardonnay Rose is a very rare, pink grape variety that Tissot makes in miniscule quantities. It yields a white wine that’s floral, toasty, and herbal - it’s unlike any other wine out there, from the Jura or otherwise. Tastes like: Citrus zest, fennel, acacia, brioche. How to drink: Chilled with herb and spice-heavy dishes like falafel.

This is the flagship white wine from arguably the most important producer in the Jura: Stéphane Tissot. Salty and toasty yet crisp and detailed, ‘Patchwork’ always serves as a clear reminder that the Jura is just an hour’s drive east from the heart of the Cote de Beaune. Tastes like: Ripe pear, sea salt, roasted hazelnuts. How to drink: Not too cold anytime you want an alternative to salty, textured White Burgundy.

notes: 700 miles from the Spanish mainland off the coast of Morocco, the Canary Islands are home to some of the most distinctive, just plain delicious white wines in all of Spain. While the volcanic island of Tenerife has become a natural wine hotspot in recent years, Borja Pérez Gonzalez’s family has been making wine here for the last century. Borja makes this salty, savory white from old vines of the local grape, listan blanco. Tastes like: Peach, smoke, sea salt, lemon curd. How to drink: Chilled with all types of seafood.

wine: Rubén Díaz Viticultor, Cebreros Doré Chasselas 2022
notes: Skin-contact chasselas from the mountains of central Spain. It sounds… strange. But in the hands of Rubén Díaz, the result is a delicate orange wine that’s more mineral-driven and refreshing than funky. Díaz has been a quality pioneer of Gredos, the rugged area west of Madrid, for the last 20 years. He only makes 200 cases of this chasselas, a high-acid grape variety typically reserved for the alpine slopes of Switzerland. Tastes like: Apricot, orange zest, sea salt. How to drink: Cold with curry, falafel, or a big cheese board.

On dramatically steep vineyards in Ribeira Sacra in northwestern Spain, Pedro Rodriguez hand-crafts bright red wines from the local grape, mencía. The region’s high altitude and cool nights allow the grapes to retain a ton of freshness, yielding vibrant, spicy red wines. Tastes like: Blackberry, nutmeg, smoke. How to drink: Lightly chilled with tacos al pastor or lean cuts of red meat.

A volcanic island chain 700 miles from mainland Spain, the Canary Islands are remote. This red wine illustrates that better than any other. It comes from a range of indigenous grapes, which grow untrained (wildly on the ground) on a steep slope on vines upwards of 200 years old. The result? A peppery, mineral-driven red that’s the most concentrated wine in Envínate's lineup.

Taganan is made from a whole host of red grape varieties native to the Canary Islands. Some of them remain unidentified, but all of them share a proximity to the Atlantic. Together, they yield a wine that's juicy, savory, and smoky – a perfect year-round red. Tastes like: Blackberries, black pepper, crackling fire. How to drink: Alongside roasted or grilled meats.

This bright red is a relatively new bottling from Envínate. On the Canary Islands, Roberto Santana hand-harvests very old vines of local grape varieties to craft a lithe, floral, slightly wild red wine. Enjoy it lightly chilled.

If you’re ever unsure what we mean when we call a white wine ‘salty’, ‘smoky’, or ‘savory’, this bottle is it. Envínate makes it from 100-year-old listan blanco vines a couple thousand feet above the Atlantic on the Canary Island of Tenerife.

Barbera doesn’t get better than this. Not only is it made by one of the world’s greatest red winemakers, but it comes from a vineyard that yields the most collectible wines in all of Italy. While barbera is generally regarded as a solid pizza wine, this is a more serious proposition. Extended aging, a legendary vineyard, and Roberto Conterno’s classic winemaking yield a bright red with structure and depth typically reserved for the region’s best nebbiolo.

An hour’s drive east of our favorite white winemakers in Italy, Marko Fon hunts down old and abandoned vineyards in Slovenia. Using only local grape varieties, he makes textured, salty white wines that are a bit cloudy and totally distinct. This malvasia, which he ferments on the skins for a short time to add depth and aromatics, is an ideal window into Marko’s house style. Tastes like: Apricot, sage, chamomile, sea salt. How to drink: Chilled with cheese and charcuterie, or pretty much anything from the ocean.

Few, if any, German winemakers crafted Kabinett - a delicate, ethereal, slightly off-dry style of riesling - as well as than the late Daniel Vollenweider. This is an seriously well-made wine from one of the Mosel's unsung stars.

Vollenweider is an insider’s estate in the Mosel region of Germany. Following in the footsteps of the late Daniel Vollenweider, Moritz Hoffman is making exceptional old-vine riesling. Tart, herbal, and smoky, 'Felsenfest' showcases Moritz’s preternatural feel for dry wines.

This remarkably complex dry riesling comes from the husband-and-wife team of Konstantin Weiser and Alexandra Künstler. In the Mosel region of Germany, they make fresh, focused white wines that punch well above their weight for the price. None more so than this deeply textured riesling from the lithe, pure 2022 vintage.

Konstantin Weiser and Alexandra Künstler make this bone-dry sparkling wine with old-vine riesling using the same method as Champagne. It's a lithe, refreshing, limited-release bubbly from one of the most exciting producers in the Mosel today.
