With more than 500 years of winemaking on the hill of Hermitage, the Chave family is the reference point of the Rhône Valley. Jean-Louis Chave, the 16th generation to run the winery, makes Chave Sélection from a series of vineyards that he has acquired or replanted over the past few decades. ‘Mon Coeur’ is a savory, dark-fruited red made with syrah and grenache from vineyards near Chateauneuf-du-Pape in the Southern Rhone. Tastes like: Blackberry, olives, pepper, beef jerky. How to drink: Alongside bolognese, burgers, or lamb chops.

A volcanic island chain 700 miles from mainland Spain, the Canary Islands are remote. This red wine illustrates that better than any other. It comes from a range of indigenous grapes, which grow untrained (wildly on the ground) on a super steep slope on vines up to 300 years old. The result? A peppery, minerally red that’s the most concentrated wine in the lineup.

wine: Dominio del Challao, Rioja 'Angelita del Challao' 2020
notes: In the Spanish village of Labastida, Manu Michelini makes Rioja focused on freshness and aromatics rather than richness and oak. This biodynamic, tempranillo-dominant blend showcases that perfectly. It’s hearty and warming, a winter-friendly red packed into a compact frame. Tastes like: Strawberry, roses, black pepper, leather. How to drink: Ideal with lamb chops, bbq ribs, or even vegetarian lasagna.

wine: Domaine des Bérioles, Val de Loire Tressalier 'Trésaille' 2022
notes: Tressallier is an exceptionally rare white grape variety found almost exclusively in the remote Loire village of Saint-Pourçain. It sounds esoteric, and it is, but the flavors will be familiar to any fan of Chablis or Muscadet. Citrusy, mineral-driven, and refreshing, this is a crisp white tailor-made for fresh seafood. Tastes like: Lemon zest, roasted hazelnuts, sea salt. How to drink: Cold with oysters, summer rolls, or any salad with goat cheese.

wine: Quinta de Santiago, 'Vinha do Chapim' Alvarinho 2021
notes: Vinho Verde gets a bad rap. Well, actually, that’s not right. Most of it isn’t very good. The wines of Joana Santiago are notable exceptions. On her family’s farm, surrounded by olive trees and nearly 100 varieties of fruits, she farms albarino (called alvarinho in Portugal) a stone’s throw from the Spanish border. It’s citrusy and refreshing, with depth and intensity rarely found in albarino. Tastes like: Lemon zest, peach, sea salt, chamomile. How to drink: Cold with oysters, fish tacos, or salty snacks.

wine: Château Falfas, Côtes de Bourg 'Les Demoiselles de Falfas' 2022

Château Chalon denotes a wine style called ‘Vin Jaune’, which is a Jura specialty. It’s made with savagnin grapes, which are aged oxidatively like Sherry for years in barrel before bottling. Unlike Sherry, however, the resulting wine isn’t fortified. It’s nutty, richly aromatic, and dry.

Since Gautier Desvignes joined his father, Eric, at their family winery in the Burgundian village of Givry, the domaine’s wines have gone to a whole new level. With organic farming and no added sulfur, less oak and longer aging, their reds have become more vibrant, expressive, and just plain tasty. They only produce 1000 cases of this Red Burgundy each year, which is plush and aromatic, ready to enjoy today. Tastes like: Red cherry, dried roses, mushroom. How to drink: With pan-seared duck, delicate cuts of red meat, or any pasta with mushrooms.

In Catalonia inland from Spain’s Mediterranean coast, Josep Grau organically farms local grape varieties to make bright red wines. As is common in neighboring Priorat, the main grapes in this red are grenache and carignan. The former contributes juicy red fruit, while the latter adds structure and herbal, savory notes. Tastes like: Strawberry, balsamic, lavender. How to drink: An ideal wine to have with pizza or all-things BBQ.

His Champagne is made with zero additives, and he plants different types of trees around his land to enrich the soil, all in an effort to let the vineyards do the talking. Those vineyards, some of the only sand-based ones in Champagne, produce wines with as much texture, nuance, and elegance as any from the big-name growers that tend to dominate today’s conversations. ‘L’Arbre’ is the Cullier family’s most prized vineyard. The 100% pinot meunier bottling is rich but not oaky

While Sancerre is the best known source of sauvignon blanc in the Loire Valley, some of the region’s most exciting producers and best-value whites are located in the nearby village of Quincy. This bright, mineral, herbaceous sauvignon blanc from Vincent Siret illustrates that perfectly. Tastes like: Grapefruit, acacia, basil, smoke. How to drink: Cold alongside sushi, summer rolls, or any salad with goat cheese.

While the Côte Roannaise is technically part of the Loire, it should really be compared to Beaujolais. For example, not only is Domaine Sérol a 30-minute drive from Morgon, but it makes bright, chillable red wines from gamay. Stéphane Sérol - the family’s 5th generation to run the domaine - makes this organic bottling from a relatively warm vineyard site, which yields a concentrated yet lifted red that reminds us of our favorite Beaujoalis. Tastes like: Strawberry, cracked pepper, violets. How to drink: Lightly chilled with roast chicken, BBQ, or cheese and charcuterie.

This wine epitomizes the best of the Jura. It’s crafted by the region’s seminal winemaker using a local grape variety, savagnin, which is farmed biodynamically and bottled naturally. It’s savory and toasty yet salty and crisp in a way that’s unique to Jura whites. Production is ‘boutique’, like ‘one barrel per year’ boutique, and yet the wine still punches above its weight for the price. All that is to say, snag as much as you can.

Rosso di Montalcino from Cerbaiona should be measured against Brunello from the majority of the region’s producers. One of the greatest estates in Tuscany, Cerbaiona makes this wine using the same vineyards and attention to detail as their $300 Brunello, but with less oak and cellar aging. The result is a red wine that’s lighter and fresher, ready to be enjoyed young. The Rosso is also a lot scarcer than their Brunello, meaning it tends to disappear almost immediately upon release.

Amélie Berthaut minimizes the use of oak to produce a style of Red Burgundy that’s savory, smooth, and nuanced. While far rarer, her textured, earthy White Burgundy is very much worth seeking out as well.

Name a marquee wine region, and Pedro Parra has likely consulted for its best producers. From Roulot and Liger Belair to Marco Marengo and Comando G. But his eponymous project isn't based in Burgundy or Barolo. It's located 500 km south of Santiago in Chile. There in his hometown of Concepción, Pedro is the force behind a winemaking movement you could call the ‘New Chile’. Pedro has a passion for terroir (he literally has his PhD in the field), and he focuses it on the isolated granite soils of southern Chile. Using native grape varieties, he produces fresh, exceptionally drinkable red wines.

While his domaine has grown in both size and notoriety since he started it in his early 20’s, his Petit Chablis bottling has been there through it all. Pure, bright, and mineral-driven, this is a good window into Christophe’s house style. Tastes like: Peach, lemon zest, salted almonds. How to drink: Perfect with oysters, but it’s also great with sushi and all types of fresh seafood.

'La Chêne Marchand' has everything you look for in classic Sancerre - crisp minerality, citrus fruit, bright acidity - along with elegance and complexity that punch above the price-point.

wine: Lucien Crochet, Sancerre 'La Croix du Roy' 2021

Gilles organically farms some of the best vineyards in the region to make white wines that are fresh and precise. This bottling has more richness and power than most Sancerre, but its salty, citrusy flavors keep it vibrant and refreshing.

In the town of Saumur, Romain Guiberteau farms top plots of cabernet franc to make some of the region’s best red and rosé wines. Like his mentor, Nady Foucault of Clos Rougeard, Romain farms organically, producing deeply savory yet elegant wines. His rosé is crisp and floral, with enough structure and herbal notes to pair perfectly with a margherita pizza. Tastes like: Strawberry, sea salt, sage, bell pepper. How to drink: Chilled alongside a caprese salad, margherita pizza, or any other dish involving fresh basil.

Between the volcanic soils, high altitudes, and constant sea breezes, Mount Etna is a unique place to make wine. Nobody masters the conditions better than Girolamo Russo. Now run by Girolamo’s son, Giuseppe, the benchmark Etna winery makes this rosé with the local nerello mascalese grape. It’s refreshing and easy-drinking, with herbal, smoky flavors that make it highly versatile with food. Tastes like: Strawberry, lemon zest, oregano, sea salt. How to drink: Chilled alongside antipasti like anchovies and caponata with crostini.

How to drink: Not too cold alongside pan-seared scallops, roast chicken, or pasta in a white sauce.

Gros Nore is located five minutes down the road from the legendary Domaine Tempier in Bandol. And like Tempier, Gros Nore makes collectible rosé that's s avory and food-friendly yet bright and finessed.

Terrebrune uses the same blend as Tempier - mourvédre, grenache, and cinsault - to make a similarly crisp, herbaceous, age-worthy rosé. Located in Bandol, a Provencal fishing village on the Mediterranean, the wine has a salty character that makes it particularly refreshing in the summer.

Responsible for spurring France’s natural wine movement in the ‘80s, Marcel Lapierre carries as much weight as any producer in Beaujolais. Their ‘Morgon’ remains a benchmark for the region, and this new addition to their lineup is essentially a brighter, more accessible version of that. Tastes like: Tart cherry, black pepper, and roses. Their salmon-pink, pinot noir rosé has delicate floral and herbal notes, along with bright fruit and minerality. Tastes like: Strawberry, grapefruit zest, roses, smoke. How to drink: Cold at a summer picnic, or anytime you’d rather be on the beach.

After a run of hot and sunny vintages, 2021 was a relatively cool one in Beaujolais, yielding bright and vibrant wines. Even in tough years, Château Thivin - the best producer in the Côte de Brouilly - is able to produce balanced wines. But in a vintage like 2021, Thivin turned out an exceptionally fresh red with all of the depth and mineral-intensity that this hill-top cru in Beaujolais is known for. Tastes like: Raspberry, smoke, mushrooms, roses. How to drink: Lightly chilled with burgers and grilled portobello mushrooms.

Chiroubles is at the highest elevation of any ‘Cru’ in Beaujolais, which leads to particularly light and fresh wines. In Chiroubles, Camille Mélinand organically farms a steep slope of old vines to make this bright red. If you’re looking for an ideal chilled red, this is it. Tastes like: Raspberry, black pepper, roses. How to drink: Chilled with burgers and BBQ or on its own.

wine: Domaine de la Prébende, Beaujolais Rosé 2021

Tastes like: Strawberry, roses, smoke. How to drink: Cold with charcuterie and bright salads, ideally outside on a summer afternoon.

When it comes to Northern Rhône syrah, Crozes-Hermitage doesn’t carry the reputation of Hermitage. In fairness, no place does. But in the right hands, its wines can offer better value for the price. For proof, take this bottling from Charles Tardy and his son, François. From a single, organically-farmed vineyard a ten-minute drive from the famed hill of Hermitage, the family-run winery makes this syrah that’s dense, silky, and deeply savory. Tastes like: Blueberry, thyme, black olive, leather. How to Drink: Decant and enjoy with lamb chops or your slow-cooked meat of choice.

This unfiltered blend of riesling, chardonnay, and gewürztraminer is floral and powerfully aromatic, yet crisp and vibrant. It’s dry and low alcohol, meaning exceptionally easy-drinking. notes: Savoie has always been a source of easy-drinking white wines, but in the last decade, it’s also become home to some of France’s most singular reds. This biodynamic mondeuse from Nicolas Ferrand is one of them. Nicolas’s steep vineyards, which are plowed by horse, receive lots of sunshine, giving the wine surprising depth and richness despite its relatively low alcohol and lean frame. Tastes like: Black cherry, violets, thyme, black pepper. How to Drink: Lightly chilled with burgers, pepperoni pizza, or a cheese and charcuterie board.

Massimo Clerico, whose family winemaking roots in Piedmont go back to the 1700s, makes this deeply savory nebbiolo a 90-minute drive north of Barolo. But taste it blind, and Barolo is exactly where you’ll assume it’s from. Made using traditional methods in exceptionally small quantities, the ‘Lessona Riserva’ consistently ranks among the best values in all of Italian wine. That’s especially true of a hallmark vintage like 2013. Tastes like: Black cherry, dried roses, mushrooms, licorice. How to drink: Decant for an hour before pairing with braised meats or mushroom agnolotti.

Laura Lorenzo is making some of the most exciting wines in Galicia today. From small, organically farmed vineyards, she crafts the kind of vibrant yet savory Spanish reds that will appeal to fans of Envínate, Raúl Pérez, and Comando G. Her ‘Azos da Vila’ is a field blend of local grapes from very old vines. It’s bright, rustic, and ideal for outdoor barbecues. Tastes like: Blackberry, black olive, charred wood, cracked black pepper. How to drink: Ideal with most things fresh off the grill, especially pork chops or peppery flank steak.

Because the perception of Muscadet is still tied to simple (and cheap) whites, the prices of Bretaudeau’s wines lag way behind their quality. These single-vineyard Muscadets are crisp, clean, and textured. wine: Bérêche & Fils, Brut Réserve Magnum (2019 base)
notes: Brut Réserve is a blend of the three classic Champagne grapes – pinot noir, chardonnay, and pinot meunier – and vintages spanning the decade. It’s subtly nutty, very dry, and full of the citrus and savory flavors only achieved by the best producers. If we got more, this would be on our daily rotation of drinks: water, coffee, more coffee, Bérêche.

Aligoté is often treated as chardonnay’s simpler, less noteworthy white wine counterpart in Burgundy. But the fact is, some wineries have been making aligoté for ages, coaxing texture and complexity out of the lean white grape. Bitouzet-Prieur is one such producer. The classic Burgundy estate uses old-vine aligoté from just outside Meursault to make a crisp, structured wine. Tastes like: Yellow apple, smoke, biscuits. How to drink: Chilled alongside soft cheeses or any type of fresh seafood.

The Fontana family has been making wine in Monforte d’Alba for 200 years. Currently run by the wonderful Mario Fontana, the winery releases classically-styled Barolo that requires time to age, as well as this barbera meant to be enjoyed young. While it’s fresh and accessible, Mario’s old vines and traditional winemaking yield a barbera with plenty of depth and finesse. Tastes like: Strawberry, violet, anise. How to drink: Enjoy with charcuterie, roasted mushrooms, or chicken parm.

Italy is home to countless white grape varieties, most of which only grow in a single region or village. Those esoteric grapes, however, yield some of the best values in all of white wine. Take this crisp white from Diletta Tonello as proof. On steep, volcanic hillsides near Verona, Diletta uses a grape called durella to make a razor sharp, mineral-driven wine. Tastes like: Green apple, smoke, sea breeze. How to drink: Chilled with fresh seafood, ideally oysters.

The Cornu family has lived in the Burgundian town of Echevronne since the thirteenth century, and you’ll find their winery there today. They make this Red Burgundy from old-vine pinot noir grown at high elevation, which leads to a fresh, earthy wine. Yields were quite low in 2021, but the Burgundy that did get produced is classic. This is a prime example. Tastes like: Blackberry, mushroom, rhubarb. How to drink: Alongside herb-roasted chicken or ravioli with parmesan cream sauce.

Las Jaras 2-Pack $110 While Las Jaras has a celebrity co-founder in Eric Wareheim, this California-based natural producer is truly passionate about quality winemaking. An hour’s drive east of our favorite white winemakers in Italy, Marko Fon hunts down old and abandoned vineyards in Slovenia. Using only local grape varieties, he makes textured, salty white wines that are a bit cloudy and totally distinct. This malvasia, which he ferments on the skins for a short time to add depth and aromatics, is an ideal window into Marko’s house style. Tastes like: Apricot, sage, chamomile, sea salt. How to drink: Chilled with cheese and charcuterie, or pretty much anything from the ocean.

F resh and lively on the palate, with plump, juicy tannins providing just enough grip and plenty of lush flavors, from rose-water charm to overripe mandarins and mango chutney to clean apple-orchard fruit and rhubarb. Notes of cinnamon and ginger come through on a memorable finish. A serious and impressive skin-contac

Sourced from the iron-rich calcareous soils of the celebrated Villero cru, on the outskirts of the village of Castiglione Falletto, Nebbiolo fruit from 65-year-old vines sees a full 40 days of maceration during alcoholic fermentation before transferring to large Salvanonian casks for 36 months before bottling. The 2018, simply, gorgeous, capturing the intensity of this site married to a super-classic expression of Nebbiolo. Sage, menthol, licorice, spice, tobacco, and incense are woven throughout a core dark red and blue fruit.

Onto the lighter side of things, here, Grignolino – the ultimate Piemontese 'chillable red' – gets the serious Rinaldi treatment while still maintaining the variety's innate levity. Crushed flowers, spice, and sweet, red-toned fruit are all nicely lifted, with added elemetns of singed orange rind, Angostura bitters and menthol. The palate is fine, fresh, light and taut with a cool finish that binds everything into perfect harmony. Served with a light chill, this will make for a serious warm weather red.

wine: Orsi San Vito Posca Bianca NV
notes: The Posca Bianca is a still take on Pignoletto (with a bit of Alionza, Albana and Malvasia), crafted in a style Federico dubs vino perpetuo . Drawn from a multi-vintage, solera-style tank that includes every vintage back to 2010, each bottling continues a never-ending blend. Combining the waxy and herbal characters of mature Pignoletto with the bright fruit and floral freshness of younger vintages, the Posca rolls out elderberry, white peach and gooseberry, kept in check by the grape’s trademark salty, nutty backbone. A trattoria-style wine of real intrigue — easy to drink, anything but simple

wine: Vino di Anna Sfuso di Anna Rosso 2022
notes: A bright, easy-going Etna red that wears its name with a wink— ‘sfuso’ may mean ‘bulk wine,’ or the kind you fill your own jug with down at the local cantina, but there’s nothing commonplace about it. Mostly old, bush-vine Nerello Mascalese with a scattering of Nerello Cappuccio, Grenache, and local whites, it’s fermented partly in clay qvevri and aged in chestnut barrels. Things are never boring chez Vino di Anna, as the final blend pulls from the estate’s 2022 field blend, enlivened with a splash of Palmento Rosso and just a dash Jeudi 15 Rosato for lift. Only the second bottling of this cuvee after the launch of this label in 2021, ‘Jeudi 15’ is a blend of organically grown Carricante, Catarratto, and Grecanico from high-elevation northern vineyards. It’s bright and saline, with ripe lemon and pineapple cutting through a taut, mineral frame. Dry, with a fleshy mid-palate full of yellow peach, citrus zest, and wildflowers, it finishes with a tropical lift and electric acidity.

A striking Etna red drawn from two vineyards on opposite sides of the winery, one ancient, one young, both alive with volcanic intensity. Half comes from Vigna Jules, a 90-year-old bush-vine parcel farmed biodynamically, its deep silty soils yielding dark cherry, plum, and spice with brooding depth and fine, firm tannins. The other half, from Vigna Gaspard, an amphitheater of terraces planted in 2014 from massale selections, brings lift and crunch —wild strawberry, blueberry, and orange blossom flashing through volcanic earth. Charged with volcanic verve, this vintage comes from a cooler year, giving it tighter lines and sharper edges. A blend of organically farmed, native Sicilian varieties gathered from four distinct corners of the island (Grillo from Marsala, Cataratto from Alcamo, etc.), each parcel is fermented on its own before being united at Anna and Eric’s cellar high on Etna’s northern slopes. The nose opens with white flowers and citrus oil; the palate with lemon zest, grapefruit pith, and sea-spray salinity. This is a wine that is at once dangerously drinkable and wildly iconoclastic, yet leveled with vi

The Palmento Rosso – a nod to their 300-year-old traditional Etnean wine building – is true to style: while light and fresh, it has the pronounced fruit intensity of a great Etna red, full of cherries, brambly wild raspberry, macerated strawberries, blood orange. There are floral notes, along with a distinctive minerality indicative of the volcanic terroir. Acidity is well-defined and balanced, the finish is persistent and refreshing. Nerello Mascalese makes up 90% of this blend, along with small percentages of Nerello Cappuccio, Grecanico, Carricante, and Minnella Bianca; as old-school as it

Bianco 'G' is Vino di Anna's flagship white wine, the 'G' here standing for Grecanico (known as Garganega up north in the Veneto) from 60+-year-old vines, and a small portion of Carricante (grape varieties that proved resistant to downy mildew, which decimated Etna’s vineyards of Nerello Mascalese in 2023.) The Grecancio is macerated on the skins for four days and matured in stainless steel; the rest is whole bunch, direct pressed and aged in chestnut barrels before blending all together. aromas: Pear, White Peach, Peach, Apricot, Nectarine, Lemon, Honeysuckle, Smoke, Limestone, Almond
notes: It's time to get to know Vitovska, an indigenous grape of Friuli and Slovenia (which were, of course, one and the same), whose profile is inextricably linked to its environment. Grown in the Carso district of Italy near Trieste, between mountains (the Alps) and sea (the Adriatic), it’s a variety that marries the identities of these climatic forces effortlessly. It’s an extreme and strongly territorial grape, for which there are no similar varieties throughout the Mediterranean; in the past it was often vinified to blend with other cultivars, especially Malvasia Istriana, but increasingly now i

Meaning 'cluster,' Togliana's 'L’Arsin' is a classically-styled Carema, made from 100% Nebbiolo from the various small estate owned parcels. The fermentation is carried out with native yeasts in stainless steel tanks. Aging takes place in large French oak casks (1,000L) for 15 months, plus in stainless steel for 2 months before release. A classic alpine Nebbiolo, juicy, vibrant and loaded with small berry aromas, followed by wild herbs and forest floor. Fine tannins and the typical mineral backbone of Carema close on the finish. 2000 bottles made. Carema, nestled at the foothills of the Alps n

An unassuming but spot-on introduction to Valtellina Nebbiolo, and to the new wave of the Balgera winery. 20% is 2019 unoaked Nebbiolo, 80% is 2016 Nebbiolo aged in large cask, all subject to shorter macerations. A juicy, and bright mountain red (not unsuited for a light chill!), loaded with wild strawberries, faded red flowers, thyme and freshly ripe blackberries. Silky and smooth tannins give this great structure and keep it super easy-going.

Legendary Mauro Franchino and his nephew Alberto Raviciotti farm a scant three hectares practicing sustainable viticulture. They select only their best Nebbiolo to make their wines in their tiny winery in the center of Gattinara. On a typical year, they use only 50% of their crop, while the remaining 50% is sold to other producers. Nestled in the pre-Alpi hills north of Novara and Vercelli, Gattinara has for centuries been known for austere, age-worthy Nebbiolo, locally known as Spanna, Gattinara’s reputation pre-dates even Barolo and Barbaresco, but the cultivation of vines here was progressi

Made from 100% Marzemino grown in Trentino’s La Rua vineyard, this is a faithful expression of one of northern Italy’s most characterful native grapes —delicate, fragrant, and effortlessly drinkable. Violets, red cherries, and wild raspberries rise from the glass with vivid clarity, accented by a faint note of spice and crushed stone. The palate is bright and supple, carrying flavors of fresh plum, sour cherry, and red currant, balanced by lively acidity and just a whisper of fine-grained tannins. Fermented and aged in stainless steel, the wine retains a pure, aromatic brightness, and is light

wine: Torre dei Beati Giocheremo con i Fiori Pecorino d'Abruzzo 2023
notes: “We are playing with flowers” is the perfect title for a wine that smells of elderflowers and beeswax, and has a remarkable amount of both texture and tart typical Pecorino acidity on the palate.

wine: Fattoria Coroncino Il Bacco Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi Classico 2022

wine: Borgo Maragliano Francesco Galliano Alta Langa Brut Blanc De Blanc 2021
notes: Fresh and classic, this wine opens with delicate notes of green apple, citrus blossom, and a hint of freshly baked bread. Light and effortless, the flavors are crisp and clean, carried by fine bubbles and bright acidity. An easy, enjoyable sip that showcases its understated charm with refreshing precision.

wine: Divella Gussago Rose de Saignee Dosaggio Zero 2019
notes: *ALL WINES WILL BE AVAILABLE FOR PICK UP OR SHIPPING AS OF NOVEMBER 18th* Derived from the very early, gentle pressings of Pinot Noir grapes, with the freely running juice 'bled' from the tanks after only a day of maceration, then aged in used barriques. 54 months sure lie. Uninhibited by any addition of dosage and hemmed together with a soft touch of tannin and marked salinity, on the palate it is sleek and fine, with pronounced freshness and a creamy bubble. Reeling with wild strawberries, red flowers, custard and dry pastry, this is a sparkling wine of substance and elegance.

wine: Divella Gussago Blanc de Blancs Dosaggio Zero 2021 Magnum 1.5L
notes: *ALL WINES WILL BE AVAILABLE FOR PICK UP OR SHIPPING AS OF NOVEMBER 25th* The flagship wine and a dazzler, one to convert you to Franciacorta (and Alessandra!) once and for all. 100% Chardonnay, Alessandra harvests the grapes in one pass and employs a soft, slow hand pressing of the grapes with the manual wood basket press, resulting in a very light maceration. With only 1g/L of residual sugar present in the bottle, and a whopping 33 months on the lees, the wine is racy and full on the palate, with big bursts of green apple, lemon zest, pear, and brioche. Precise, long, and all about mineral-d

100% Barbera (estate fruit from Cellario’s own biodynamic vineyards). 10 days skin maceration gives it good extraction but still keeps it juicy and fresh. Aging is in cement. “Quantobasta” means “just enough”, meaning you can have as little or as much as you want - the perfect amount!

aromas: Cranberry, Star Anise, Smoke, Flint, Thyme, Graphite
notes: Nestled between Etna's Passopisciaro and Solicchiata, sourced from 80 year old vines, emerges an elegant 100% Nerello Mascalese by Rocca Coeli. Aromatics of smoke, flint, dark currant, rose and Mediterranean scrub gives way to layers of morello cherry, cranberry, star anise, thyme and graphite on the palate. Packed with elegance and mineral tension along with fine tannins and crisp acidity this Etna Rosso pairs well with oily fish like sardines, tuna, and swordfish, as well as heavier, meaty dishes.

wine: Podere Il Saliceto Bi Fri Frizzante 2024
notes: 80% Trebbiano di Modena, 20% Sauvignon, ‘Bi Fri' stands for Bianco Frizzante , but also 'Be Free' - and who are we to argue with this light, lively, and lip-smacking offering? Direct press juice with natural primary fermentation in stainless steel, and secondary fermentation in bottle with must from original harvest. Minimal added sulfur and no filtering or fining. White flowers, grapefruit and citrus pith, and tomato leaf dominate an über-fresh and vivacious mouthful of rustic Emilia fizz. A killer wine perfect for any sunny occasion.

wine: Erpacrife Nebbiolo Metodo Classico Dossage Zero 2019
notes: Tags: classical, light, metodo classico, metodoclassico, Nebbiolo, piedmont, Piemonte, Sparkling, sparkling/frizzante, White

“Mofete” which means “it’s erupting” in Sicilian dialect is an Etna Rosso comprised of 80% Nerello Mascalese and 20% Nerello Cappuccio from various estate vineyards in Passopisciaro. Each plot is fermented separately with native yeasts in stainless steel. A selection of the resulting batches is then assembled and aged 50% in stainless steel, 50% in 50HL Slavonian neutral oak. Juicy, wild berry aromas are wrapped in the signature mineral notes typical of volcanic soils. Grilled, smoked herbs close a delicious finish.

wine: Roeno Collezione di Famiglia Riesling Renano 2018
notes: There are less than 450 acres of Rhine Riesling planted in Italy, and the majority are located in Trentino and Alto Adige thanks to the strong influence of German and Austrian winemaking. Roeno’s Riesling vineyards are located on the slopes of Mount Baldo, which stands between Garda Lake and the Adige Valley. “Collezione di Famiglia” is made only in the best vintages from a strict selection of the best grapes. Roeno draws from the influence of Germany and Austria to craft a marvelous example, bright and tight like a violin string, and yet exuding opulent notes of petrol and ripe orchard and tr

Bright acidity, great minerality, superb freshness, light tannins — what else could you want in a late summer wine? Weingut Pranzegg is a small 3.5 hectare family estate nestled in the surrounding mountain foothills of the town of Bozen in Südtirol (AKA Alto Adige), just 50 km south of the Austrian border. The winery has been in the hands of the Gojer family for three generations. Martin took over the estate in 2008 and started the conversion to biodynamic farming straight away; he also stopped selling to the local cooperatives, a bold move in an area where 90% of all grapes are bottled by coo

Not your mom's Pinot Grigio! An brilliant and unexpected take on the varietal. High elevation grapes are picked over the course of several passes in the vineyard for optimal quality and ripeness. Whole bunch maceration over a couple of weeks results in a deep amber/dark rose color, stunning aromatics and a pluck on the palate that leaves us smiling each and every time.

Pinot Blanc needs certain things to truly thrive: complex soils, perfect sun exposure and a good breeze. Dornach, sitting at an elevation of 350 meters, in the idyllic Alto Adige region, is perfectly positioned to grow world class Pinot Blanc, and the farm’s embrace of the natural world and deft touch in the cellar creates a wine with intense, crystalline personality and passion. This cuvee blends Chardonnay (40%) for lovely added texture and complexity.

A stunner, Dornach's vins de soif (thirst wine) is an alpine Pinot Noir that bursts with pleasure and personality. It’s elegant and lovely but don’t let the almost translucent hue fool you -- this is serious wine from a top estate full of pure fresh fruit. Fresh picked strawberries, rhubarb and love.

A new cuvée from mountain maestro and dedicated biodynamic vigeron Martin Gojer just arrived; 'Elysion' is 100% Pinot Bianco (aka Weissburgunder in these German-speaking parts) and marries the natural weight and siftness of the variety with zippy notes of lemongrass and wild herbs. Fleshy stone fruit and a mineral spine add depth.

Four generations of the Pichler family live in the same small stone farmhouse home, farm the same vines their family has been tending to almost a millennium, and produce organically farmed, classic examples of Südtirol Schiava, Lagrein, and a small amount of French varieties. Located in Eppan, in the heart of the Südtirol – Italy's only Deutsche speaking region – the architecture, cuisine, and culture in this area is Austrian, and the region's reds have less in common with the powerful, sanguine, tannic reds of Tuscany or Piedmont that define Italy in the minds of many wine lovers, than the th

100% biodynamically-farmed Müller-Thurgau from super high elevation – 720 meters! Elegant and easy drinking, with a golden yellow hue and refreshing palate of bright, spicy fruit, and tight minerality. Incredibly aromatic, as a delightful blend of apple and wildflower create an intriguing and unforgettable Alpine experience. Textured with layers of flavors that show orchard fruit in all its glory while notes of yeast and vibrant acidity keep the wine fresh.

Another wonder from ‘Fizz Wizzard’ Matteo Furlani - dry, juicy and absolutely delicious. A field blend of native Dolomiti grapes Marzemino, Turca, and Negrara, full of spice, earth and red forest fruits throughout. Wild strawberry, crushed white peppercorn, and a distinctively herbaceous, bell peppery streak are buoyed by tiny, tight fizz and mineral drive. Fresh and bright as a summer’s morning in the mountains of Trentino! The grapes were pressed slowly with a vertical press (torchio) without being crushed or destemmed. As always, very serious for the appellation, with pure cherry, bark and walnut character as well as a hint of dark chocolate. Medium-bodied, firm and focused, with integrated tannins and a long and flavorful finish. The fruit is generous and primary, and the wine ends with mildly chalky tannins.

wine: Domini Del Leone Prosecco Brut NV
notes: A Prosecco from Veneto's oldest organic producer. Unlike the filtered, tank-fermented proseccos that are common today, it follows the older col fondo tradition, a nod to the way frizzante wines were made in many areas of Italy before modern methods took over. F ruit-forward notes of green apple and fresh-cut pear meet salty undertones from the distinctive Caranto soil.

wine: Fratelli Alessandria Barolo San Lorenzo di Verduno 2021
aromas: Blood Orange, Orange Peel, Rose Petal, White Pepper, Chalk, Slate, Saline, Mint
notes: Vittore Alessandria's 2021 Barolos are hugely promising. The Sarn Lorenzo is a wine of translucence, elegance, and finesse. Bright acids cut through a core of red and purple fruit, chalk, slate, crushed stone, and white pepper. Rose petal, blood orange peel, and mint resonate on the high-toned, intensely saline finish.

wine: Fasoli Gino La Corte Del Pozzo Bardolino 2024

Gianluigi Lano is an understated, stoic man who works a small certified organic farmstead in San Rocco Seno d’Elvio, Barbaresco. His wines are complex and classically styled, but always offer plenty of truffle/floral intrigue to compliment the instantly gratifying dark fruit. There is no modern technology in the cellar. The most impactful "technique" is that Gianluigi refuses to release wines until they're truly ready to drink. Almost monolithic in its stature and presence, the 'Dinavolo' is Giulio's most serious bottling, hailing from a selection of the best bunches, from the oldest vines on the property. Malvasia, Ortrugo, and Marsanne dominate the blend with the addition of 25% 'unknown varietals;' the Dinavolo offers a dense and brawny profile highlighted by apricot skin, marmalade, white balsamic, candied citrus pith, and bay leaf all woven through unashamedly full and luscious mouthfeel drawn from a number of month spent on skins. A wine that demands time, air, temperature and a big beautiful hunk of porchetta.

Don Fausto Spumante is a sparkling wine made from Malvasia and Chardonnay. Very aromatic nose with typical floral and fruity hints of Malvasia to which are added hazelnuts, sage, butter, and mineral from aging on the lees. Fresh and creamy mouthfeel with savory finish and nice structure.

wine: Il Roccolo di Monticelli Monticelli Rosso 2022
notes: A blend of Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella, Molinara, and Oseleta from limestone soil, this is Valpolicella at its more lithe and playful end. Grapes see a whopping 90-day maceration but you'd never guess it here - no signs of over-extraction, just bright, justly restrained red fruit. It then ages 8 months further in steel. A lighter-styled red, with echoes of the Loire Valley, Silvia's rosso is delicate in body with aromas of white pepper and geranium alongside notes of cherry and raspberry. Fresh and juicy, yet still refined, the high acidity and hint of bitter spice round out a energetic, re

wine: Il Roccolo di Monticelli Obelix Bianco 2023
notes: Only the grapes of the oldest vines of Garganega are used for this cuvee and are carefully harvested from select bunches. After spontaneous fermentation, with some whole cluster maceration, the wine is aged for several months in terracotta amphora. This is pure, old-world wine making; no clarification, filtration or addition of sulfur. What results is a bright, light orange wine bursting with citrus notes and a touch of flinty herbaceousness. You might even consider pairing it with Obelix’s favorite dish: wild boar!

Marco’s ‘Tufaliccio’ Rosso is one of those seemingly humble wines that possesses that rare ‘transportational’ quality. wine: Berucci Mola da Piedi Cesanese del Piglio 2019
notes: Aged in one single 300L clay amphorae, this is as as pristine, unadorned and manicured expression of Cesanese as you will find. Fruit is sourced from one small vineyard of very old vines, accessible only by foot; once picked it is foot-trodden and fermented in open-tops wooden vats. Delicate, dried purple flowers, perfectly ripe plummy fruit and a sense of… life that seems to evade comprehension. While this is the pinnacle of Maria's production, in her own words, this is not a wine intended to age. This is sheer vibrancy, soil, and sunshine, held in glass and crafted with the intention of bein

A new addition – for us! – to the Mattioli's seemingly inexhaustible lineup, 'Buscaia' is a tale of two Malvasias: a direct-press white wine obtained from two different strains of the variety, the traditional strain with a tight bunch and thick skin, and the “Candia” strain with a loose bunch, and a large and delicate grape. Both are harvested at the beginning of October and are vinified through spontaneous fermentation in stainless steel tanks; no sulfur is added at any point. In typical Malvasia fashion, the nose leans fresh and floral, though, less expectedly, towards lavender and spicy, al

aromas: Blackberry, Raspberry, Black Cherry, Sour Cherry, Violet, Black Pepper, Cinnamon
notes: 100% Ciliegiolo from 15-50 years old vines; spontaneous fermentation with wild yeasts on the skins for 6 days in cement vats, then aged in steel all winter, and bottled during the waning moon in early March. Red-violet in color, with aromas of black cherry, sour cherry, black pepper, a shake of cinnamon, a trace of wild violets and warm terracotta. Blackberry, raspberry, red currant, and balsamic notes are met with bright acidity and good tannins. Plush, pure, and bright, and very suited for a light chill.

Even in a sometimes "challenging" vintage in Tuscany, Veronica's Chianti DOCG s a wave of dark and red cherry fruit, pleasantly chewy, and endlessly refreshing on the palate, with haunting blue flowers and tobacco on the nose and a flavor architecture perfectly framed by dusty tannins. Veronica recently revived the property's century-old underground concrete fermenters, which helps author this wine's irresistible freshness and vivid fruit. The end result is everything we want from a Chianti vino da tavola.

Fongoli's 2016 Fracanton Montefalco Sagrantino is a wine of remarkable precision and depth. It exhibits the varietal's hallmark intensity—robust tannins, concentrated layers of dark cherry and plum, and mineral undertones that reflect the limestone-rich soils of Umbria. This vintage demonstrates excellent structure and aging capacity, making it particularly suited for cellaring or pairing with substantial dishes such as braised meats and aged charcuterie.

Born on the volcanic slopes of Mount Somma—the ancient inner cone of Vesuvius—this captivating white from Cantine Olivella channels the raw energy of Campania’s landscape. Crafted entirely from Catalanesca, a grape once relegated to table fruit, Katà has shed its humble origins to emerge as a wine of precision and place. Fragrant notes of lemon zest, crisp pear, and wild herbs rise from the glass, underpinned by a briny whisper of sea spray and a streak of volcanic minerality. wine: Durin Riviera Ligure di Ponente Vermentino 2023

Aromas of ripe citrus and honey, mint, and a touch of sea salt dominate this medium-bodied, textured, refined Campanian white. Since the end of the nineteenth century, the Troisi family has championed the wines of Irpina, a historic vine-growing area in northern Campania. Vadiaperti’s high-altitude vineyards and pure volcanic soils combine for southern Italian white wines of impeccable finesse, freshness and character.

Made from the little-known Grignolino grape, this light red wine is made for drinking not meditation. That is, however, not to say that great care was not taken in the making of this little gem: hand harvested organic grapes are spontaneously fermented, sulfur additions are kept to an absolute minimum and neither fining nor filtration are employed. Cranberry-hued, translucent, and just a shade or two darker than rosé (the skin of Grignolino contains little pigment), E Grino! is the paragon of a light-drinking red and surprisingly versatile for even chillier climes. wine: Poderi Cellario Il Baffone Bianco Frizzante 2023
notes: A surprising blend of Moscato and Nascetta, a rare native Piemontese variety with skins excellent for maceration. This rustic pet-nat sees 5 days of skin contact for a little extra structure. The result is charmingly cloudy and pleasantly floral, with notes of delicate apricot, hay, and pear. It's a touch tropical and eminently quaffable.

Bellifolli is a new project by Valle dell’Acate. Although the winery has been the property of the Jacono family for six generations and has focused on traditional wine styles using native grapes, they wanted to add a line of fresh and lively wines which are still marvelously Sicilian. Bellifolli synthesizes the character and the contrasts of Sicily and the Sicilians: the beauty and the moments of folly, the light and the shade, the sea in turmoil and the warm sirocco breeze.

wine: Massetti Francesco Trebbiano Colli Aprutini Mezzo Pieno 2022
notes: The main rules at Azienda Agricola Francesco are no to chemistry and yes to biodiversity. Working exclusively with Trebbiano and Montepulciano, and in tiny amounts, Francesco's wines are natively fermented and see zero chemical or physical interventions. Rich yellow-gold in color, with strong notes of orchard fruit – golden pear, spiced apples – his Trebbiano is intense and persistent in the mouth with a strong streak of sea-air minerality (Digging through the rows of trees you can still find the remains of shells where once there was an ancient sea). It is here that the Carpineti family have for generations now tended to a patchwork of grape vines, today led by current-day patriarch Marco Caprinetti, who has guided the estate forward since taking the reins in 1986. wine: LeLarge Pugeot La Cote des Glaises Champagne 2019
notes: 100% Chardonnay from a single plot in Coteaux Champenois with a smidge of extended skin contact (a slooow pressing), lending an herbaceous undertone to the tart fruit and minerality, alongside a concentrated, savory edge: preserved lemon, rich & unctuous oxidative notes, caramelized aromatics. Eight months oak aging brings out a bit of baking spices and a more serious weight and texture still met by lasting acidity. Made with zero sulfur and via natural fermentation, t he characteristics of this are unmistakably Chardonnay, just seen through a very distinct lens.

wine: Romeo del Castello Etna Rosso Allegracore 2019
notes: This Nerello Mascalese/Cappuccio blend begins with a delicate whisper of powdered sugar before diving headlong into a vivid medley of wild herbs, tangy cherries, tangerine zest, and a trace of crushed volcanic stone. The texture is supple, almost plush, yet remains lifted and precise, as vibrant red berries glide across a spine of energetic acidity. The finish is long and gently framed, leaving behind an impression of steeped black tea and lingering rose petals.

Vitovska is an indigenous grape that tastes inextricably linked to its environment. The grapes, grown in the Carso near Trieste, between the Alps and the Adriatic, marry the identities of these climatic forces effortlessly. One sip brings to mind the pure, breezy whites we love from other Alpine regions like Savoie and Alto Adige, as well as the warm, salty air you can taste in Mediterranean whites from Corsica and Sardegna. A house with records dating back to 1791 and an official start in 1830, Italo Pietrantonj is as old as it gets for wineries from Abruzzo (literally the oldest). Eight winemaking generations deep in the town of Vittorita, Pietrantonj is rich with family heritage and tradition. Now the winery is run by two sisters, Roberta and Alice, whose great-great-great-grandfather Niccolo was the first certified winemaker in the Abruzzo region, gaining a diploma from the Royal School of Conegliano Veneto in 1889. Just over 60 hectares of estate vineyards high up in the rolling hills of the Apinine Mountains

wine: Giuseppe Cipolla Passofonduto Le Robbe Rosso 2022
notes: Warmly integrated with soft black tea-like tannins, black licorice, citrus zest and an almost pottery-like, earthen tone that just feels Sicilian, the Passofonduto is balanced with bright, earthy plum, and a host of savory, mineral aromas and flavors. This wine may emerge in the coming years as one of Sicily's truly great, standard-bearing wines!

'In Chino' is made according to an old recipe from the Langhe region of Piemonte featuring Cinchona root (Cinchona Officinalis), Cinchona calisaya bark, quassia, and a special blend of herbs and spices. Intense, bitter and honey notes with hints of toasted clove, eucalyptus, cinnamon and coriander open on the nose. These flavors evolve on the palate into a yin-and-yang of bitter and sweet that coats the tongue; rhubarb, date, sultana, cloves, five spice and orange bitters are all present and there is a lovely, warm mouth-feel. An incredibly long, intense finish that is both dry and sweet.

We have stocked Drusian Prosecco since day one. A customer favorite, due to its versatility, price and flavor profile, this is a dry, delicately fruity and crisp Prosecco that is perfect for any occasion, whether mixing for cocktails or simply as an aperitif. Creamy and rich, this delivers a distant softness. The mouthfeel is enhanced by flavors of peach, citrus and honey.

Talk about fresh as a daisy and firing on all cylinders! Derived entirely from the local specialty in Nerello Mascalese, the fruit sees a feather-light pressing before being transferred to concrete tanks for fermentation and aging. Equal parts vibrant, delicate and punchy; über-pretty cherry, raspberry, rose petal, cassis and sweet herbs bursting on the nose and palate, with a distinct core of savory, flinty minerality that harks to the wine’s volcanic home.

Nino’s Vermentino comes from 30-year-old vines planted over clay and limestone amongst his olive groves — a hymn to the territory and to the ancient tradition of Dolceacqua, with its hilly, terraced soils and air charged with saltiness. It spends four days on skins and is aged in old casks. A traditionsl Mediterranean white, in that the use of skins and a little oxygen provide depth, grip, and savory complexity. A beautiful shade of gold in the glass , this is all aromatic herbs, sea spray, and citrus fruits — it begs for sunshine, and a nice piece of fish.

aromas: Strawberry, Red Cherry, Red Apple, Rose Petal, Black Pepper, Sandalwood
notes: Tight, tart, and wonderfully evocative of northern Italy. The Antoniotti's low-intervention, very clean winemaking has resulted in a fresh young wine redolent of red cherry, rose petal, dusty sandalwood spice, a hint of black pepper, and slightly under-ripe strawberry. Mostly Nebbiolo, with Croatina and Vespolina, just about the same blend as their Bramaterra bottling, but in a more accessible style. Vibrant, pure, and delicate with subtle red apple skin-like tannin. A strong contender for your new house red!

wine: Casale della Ioria Campo Novo Cesanese 2020
notes: The ‘Campo Novo’ is a vibrant yet remarkably complex version of the classic Cesanese grape that comes from the hilly land of Ciociaria in Lazio. The estate’s younger vines (15 years old) are harvested and spend about 15 days on the skins in steel fermenting with its own natural pied de cuve (meaning fermentation is jumpstarted by wild yeasts from the vineyard); it remains in steel on fine lees for one year before bottling. wine: Il Carpino Vis Uvae Pinot Grigio 2013

Cave Gargantua is the story of Laurent Cuneaz and his family who are based in Gressan. Named after the giant mountain depression formed from glacial debris known as Gargantua, Laurent developed his passion for vineyards and wine from his grandfather on those slopes. Their connection to their land is deep. Laurent and his brother André are renting some new vineyards in Morgex, too, known for its white variety, Prié. The Rucantu vineyard was planted some 50 years ago by Aris's grandfather. It sees 5-7 days of skin contact before transferring to old barriques and being treated to regular battonage during its 12 months of elevage, lending structure and weight to the finished wine. Powerful and persistent, though strung tightly with an undeniable sense of tension, the Rucantu doles out Mediterranean brush, pine resin, orange peel, honey, saffron and kerosene, with a palate that skews marine, fresh, rustic and textural with a finish of sweet spices and dried fruit.

A wine that seems to take you on a metaphorical beach walk, the fruit for the Crescendo hails from a younger Pigato vineyard located at the end of the Riviera di Ponente, dangling 200 meters above the Mediterranean below. As with the Rebosso, the Crescendo sees no skin maceration, transferred directly into tanks for a few months of development. Salty, subtle, beguiling, the wine oscillates between something crystalline and delicate to something delightfully chewy. aromas: Raspberry, Red Cherry, Blood Orange, Black Pepper, Mint

The Ripasso method means that dried grapes from the estate's Amarone production are added to the wine for a secondary fermentation, bolstering the structure and depth of the final product. While Le Piane's celebrated name comes from the reputation of its red wines, the ultra-rare 'Bianko' makes a strong case for Keunzli's white wine-making chops. Only produced in in favorable vintages, fruit here is drawn from a tiny parcel of Erbaluce, an oft-overlooked white grape native to the Alto Piemonte. The wine sees 6 months on lees in an array of vessels - cement, amphora and acacia barrels. Elegant and texture, the wine is driven by a waxy, honeyed stone fruit character that seems never ending.

Canus’ 2022 Ribolla Gialla offers a super fresh and classically wrapped interpretation of a variety that is often more widely seen and celebrated on the Slovenian side of the border (and even deeper into eastern Europe.) A brisk and focused nose of lime, bosc pear, white flowers, chalky mineral, and crushed stone dazzles, as the palate delivers dimensions and persistence that seem to far outweigh the wine’s modest price tag. The gorgeously oily/nutty roundness one would expect from Ribolla is here, wedged into place by plum skin, yellow orchard fruit, acacia and more of that distinct pear char

wine: Edi Kante Spumante Dossagio Zero NV
notes: A blend of Chardonnay and Malvasia Istriana, Edi’s metodao classico is aged for 12 months in old barrels, then one year in bottle before disgorgement, and bottled with zero dosage. It is dry, chalky, and just the right combination of fleshy and lean. Sharply focused, with sweet apple offset by stone and lime, a chiseled bead of fine bubbles casts a wash of salty minerals across the palate. Wickedly fresh and mouthwatering through the end, leaving a savory sensation with hints of rose, this absolutely gives some entry-level Champagnes a run for their money.

wine: Edi Kante Rose Spumante Dosaggio Zero NV
notes: This pure Pinot Noir made in the Champagne method and aged in the Kante cellars is a delicate flower—very pretty, aromatic, and racy. There are very few sparkling rosatos of this quality in Italia.

The 2019 Sangiovese Romagna Predappio Pre opens in the glass with a bouquet of dusty roses, crushed rocks, sour cherry and animal musk. This is finessed and silky in feel. Brilliant ripe red fruits and inner florals cascade across a crunchy core of saline-minerality. It finishes lightly structured, echoing licorice and autumnal spice notes as residual acids maintain a lovely freshness. The balance and purity here are something to behold.

With so much attention on Sangiovese from Tuscany, its often goes unmentioned that it is the most widely planted grape in Italy, which means that other regions are making great wines with Sangiovese. Neighboring Emiglia-Romagna is one such region and Villa Papiano is a shining example of the regional expression. Winemaker Francesco Bordini comes from wine royalty, his father Remigio a widely respected enologist. His approach is local and agriculturally focused, achieving full organic status in 2009 and continuing towards full biodynamic status to this day. Calling its holdings “the vineyards a

Federico Scarzello is the third generation to make wine at his family’s estate in Barolo, taking over in 2001. Since then he has gone from strength to strength, and has been tipped as one of Barolo’s rising stars for his respect for traditional winemaking combined with an utter dedication to quality. Long macerations, very large casks, and very minimal intervention in the cellar are the hallmarks of this winery. Scarzello has prided itself on its independence and its individuality, and Federico’s Langhe Nebbiolo is an exceedingly pretty style (Langhe Nebbiolo is typically a lighter, fresher, a

Frank's 'Grand Vin' hails from 100-year-old, ungrafted Nerello Mascalese vines in their Barbabecchi vineyard; at 910 meters asl it's the highest in the region, and, planted around 1910 and North-North East exposed, it captures the first and cool morning sun rays. 'Magma' is produced only in great vintages when they can achieve phenolic ripeness and is known for its pure expression of the variety and vineyard.

wine: Alberto Lot Filari Margherita Amber Bianco 2022
notes: Giulia and Alberto decided to work with Bronner explicitly because as a PIWI variety (crosses of American and Asian wild grapevines with European grape varieties), it is resistant to fungal diseases, meaning no pesticides need to be used in the vineyards; this makes it all the more straightforward for them to fulfill their commitment to maintaining the health and history of their soil. The Munjebel Rosso is Frank's 'Grand Vin' or 'Classico' – his idea of what an authentic Northern Valley Etna wine should be. 100% Nerello Mascalese, it’s an ever-evolving blend of fruit from Frank's many parcels (including those used for his cru bottlings), and a wine that feels far more traditionally bent when compared to the raw and naked energy of Suscaru. 100% Nero d’Avola on the low-intervention end; what can be heavy and overblown typically in the grape is still rich here but with a real freshness and balance. Vinified in concrete tanks, which captures the freshness of the fruit , it ages for 8 months in the tank and 3 months in the bottle. Sour black cherry, red currant, and wild herbs lend vibrancy to the peppery, earthy, and smokier tones in the wine. Bright acidity and some bold but well-integrated tannins make this an excellent wine at an exceptional cost.

Comprised entirely of the exceedingly rare Trebbiano di Spagna, from a vineyard Max rescued from near-destruction. Unlike the other wines described heretofore, this is a still wine, aged in ceramic vessels after pressing. ‘Funambol’ comes from the name of the acrobat that walks the tightrope — what an accurate picture of the precision of this, rich with candied ginger, orange zest, and yellow peach aromatics. Max sees the rich, glycerin, mouth-filling element as a signature of Trebbiano di Spagna; we say its flickering freshness balances a technicolor, bee pollen, and sweet spice-laden palate

wine: Denis Montanar Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso Scodovacca 2016
aromas: Black Cherry, Plum, Violet, Licorice, Cocoa, Tobacco
notes: A Friulian native grape par excellence , from 25-year-old vineyards. Violet, black cherry, and plum meet aromatic tobacco, cardamom, licorice, and cocoa on the nose. Explosive on the palate – Denis’ 35-day whole cluster maceration amps up Refosco’s inherent qualities – with layers of concentrated black fruit, rich, savory earth, plenty of prickly acidity, and tannins made supple but very much still holding everything together. Aged in steel for nearly 4 years on fine lees, this is bold, fresh, and very Friuli.

The 2020 wafts up with a sweet-and-sour bouquet as spiced orange and tropical citrus combine with masses of black raspberry and a dusting of violet candies. This is vividly fruit-focused, with wild acidity that excites the palate as crunchy woodland berry fruits cascade beneath an air of blue- and purple-toned inner florals. It closes with a coating of mouthwatering primary concentration and a sensation of liquid stone, all contrasted by crisp minerality. The Porcaria is built on power yet elegant to the extreme.

Sourced from contrada Monte Colla at 780 to 800 meters in elevation, Frank refers to this as his 'Hermitage' of Etna, as it comes from vines planted in 1946 to an extremely steep and terraced vineyard, which is exposed to sun and wind and sits directly north of Etna's smouldering peak. 100% Nerello Mascalese, the 2020 MC opens with dark floral tones and a mix of dusty roses, ash and dried black cherries. Silky and serene, this stands out for its vibrant red berry fruits and hints of sour citrus, becoming quite spicy toward the close.

Foglia Tonda (meaning 'round leaf' in Italian) is another rare, ancient local Tuscan variety, dating back to the early Renaissance, saved and brought back to new life by the Morettis. From old vines lovingly cultivated according to biodynamic principles, it ferments spontaneously, then ages in wood and steel with no added SO2. Intense and of unforgettable personality: marasca cherries, pickled capers, spring flowers, and willow essence.

100% Canaiolo – one of the few mono-varietal bottlings to be found in the region – from old clones, planted over clay, silt and sand. Achingly soft, bright and lifted, the wine reels with high-toned red fruit and endless layers of violets, both dried and fresh (seriously, this thing is purple flowers galore!). The artist formerly known as 'Contadino' Rosso, Frank's entry-level red wine is a bucket of fun times. Vivid, wild floral tones mix with notes of Campari and tart red berries, underlined by flinty, smoky minerality. There’s a reason Frank’s wines have achieved über-cult status...

wine: Alberto Lot Fior de Lot Frizzante Bianco 2022

wine: Cascina degli Ulivi Ivag Gavi Bianco 2021
notes: After consistently running afoul of the Gavi DOCG for his raw and unadorned expressions of Cortese, in 2015 Stefano withdrew this wine from the classification, instead choosing to label it as Ivag (Gavi backwards), an indication of his thoughts on the consorzio's conventionally-leaning stipulations. Pulled from 3 parcels of Cortese spread throughout the property and aged for a year in large botti, the Ivag is golden, fleshy, electric and raw: salted meyer lemon, citrus oil, sea salt, little white blossoms. In other words, this is Gavi in all its unadorned and punch-drunk glory.

Named in homage to Stefano's beloved Maremma sheep dog, the Filagnotti Bianco is one of a few truly mesmerizing, single-vineyard expressions of Cortese from the estate, pulled from a parcel of 60 year old vines overlooking the nearby village of Tassarolo. Aged for a few brief months in acacia barrels, the Filagnotti displays the mesmerizing density possible when working with old-vine fruit. What feels like gamma rays compressed into liquid form, the Filagnotti takes everything the Ivag does well and does it even better. Cortese sourced from one of the highest points in all of the Gavi region, the Montemarino leans into the more savory and spice laden side of Cortese. Pulled from another parcel of 60+ year old vines, subjected to 3 days of skin maceration and aged in large acacia botti, the Montemarino offers something more fleshy and textural than its siblings. A wine that only seems to fully reveal itself after an hour or so of aeration, a patient consumer is lead down a path of golden bosc pear, kumquat, and damson plum with tight lines and a salty bristle discecting throughout.

wine: Cascina degli Ulivi Le Mat du Raisin Rosso 2021
notes: A wicked blend of equal parts Barbera and Dolcetto from prized 60-year-old vines. This wine matures for 1 year on its lees in oak barrels and is bottled unfined and unfiltered. Fresh blackberries, raisiny plums, and tart cherries form the backbone of fruit, as moderate tannins underpin mild acidity through a very dry finish. The Bellotti reds always smack of the earth, with dark chocolate and herbs countering the soft, sour-juicy fruit.

Having fostered a culture of polyculturalism and biodynamic farming practices since taking charge of his family’s vines in 1985, Stefano set about focusing his energies on the revival of ‘true’ Cortese wines, though he continued to foster a small parcel of pre-phylloxera Dolcetto vines that remained. You'd be forgiven in thinking while consuming the ‘Nibio’ that you were staring deep into a glass old Nebbiolo here; uncompromising and meditative, the Nibio is 100% Dolcetto - drawn from the same vines mentioned above. 70% Carricante, 30% Catarratto, the ripping Etna Bianco from Graci is loaded with pithy citrus and chiseled yellow stone fruits. Don't get me wrong, the incisive mineral delivery is very much there, front and center though Alberto's interpretation offers more in terms of mouthfeel and texture than most of his peers, lacing notes of white peach, honey and anise into a wine that punches well above its weight.

Drawn from a jigsaw puzzle of tiny parcels strewn across the property, the Maggiorina is dominated by Nebbiolo (40%), Croatina (40%) and Vespolina (5%) but contains upwards of another 9 varietals, both white and red. Well worth rotating into your 'everyday' drinker line up

Brand new from the estate, Freisa is a cousin to Nebbiolo and can be made in a brighter, berry-laden style (the name comes from the Latin for strawberry ), or turn to darker, deeper tones and show off the serious structure that is certainly a family trait. Ripe tannins fill the mouth and sweep across the palate, enticing one to go back to the glass almost a little too quickly...

The 2019 Barolo classico is dark, ample, and super expressive, showing juicy and perfectly ripe red fruits, with succulent dark cherry, plum, leather, rose petal and spice, all nicely amplified. The 2018 is bright and effusive, as wines from this cru tend to be; the Rinaldis' offers fine depth and tons of site characters, both of which were hard to achieve in this vintage. Crushed flowers, spice, new leather and macerated cherry are some of the aromatic notes that soar from the glass.

A wine of pure pleasure.

Crushed flowers, spice, and sweet, red-toned fruit are all nicely lifted, with added elemetns of singed orange rind, Angostura bitters and menthol. The palate is fine, fresh, light and taut with a cool finish that binds everything into perfect harmony. Served with a light chill, this will make for a serious warm weather red.

With white floral notes, burnt citrus, melon, dried apricot, and sun-baked herbs, great texture, and a mineral-saline finish that goes on and on. Grab a big bottle and dream of spring!

The Ronc dai Luchis winery is located in Faedis, a town northeast of Udine at the base of the eastern hills of Friuli. It is a small, family business and the Refosco di Faedis vines (also known as Refosco Nostrano) are approximately 80 years old. Refosco is a variety know for its high acidity, but which two years in oak casks has greatly helped tamed here, rounding out to maintain lift and vibrancy. Medium-bodied, tart and tangy but smooth, with violets, rose hips, and berries, with a woodsy/smokey undertone.

Marco Pecorari's San Lurins estate – the name of their region, San Lorenzo Isontino, in local dialect – produces only two wines: a traditional-method sparkling Malvasia Istriana from the family’s 50-year-old vineyards, and this pet-nat style Ribolla Gialla from their only new planting. A lightly sparkling wine with a salty and mineral profile – one that perfectly recalls the surprisingly nearby Adriatic Sea – coupled with Ribolla Gialla hallmark citrus and thyme notes. Crisp, clean, and dry – the ultimate aperitif!

This hits all the Nebbiolo high-note: crushed rose petals, licorice, red berries, orange peel, spice and hints of warm terracotta, all decidedly lithe and airy in tone but never without purpose. This wonderfully vibrant wine is a blend of Trebbiano, Malvasia Toscana, and Ansonica from young vines in Bolsena that spent just three days on the skins before nine months in vats. Old-school Prosecco right here, fermented in bottle with its spent yeast left in place ( col fondo = sur lie ), lending texture, warmth, and a gentle cloudiness to this very pretty bottle of extra brut bubbles. The Padovani sisters of Fonterenza have around 4.2 contiguous hectares in the hills near Poggio San Polo, the southeastern part of the Montalcino zone. Their Brunello comes from a mere hectare's worth of fruit from their prized 'Vigna del Bosco' parcel, a site they planted themselves in 2000. (It's is surrounded entirely by the woods, or 'bosco.') Their Brunello spends six years in a 2500L botte and is a concentrated, complex wine: riserva-level in character and beyond riserva in its aging process.

Vittorio makes minuscule amounts of this rustic, still red wine, a collection of Lambrusco, Malbo Gentile, and those ever-present mystery grapes, hand harvested, destemmed, and fermented dry in fiberglass containers before getting racked to old barrels for aging. ‘Sassoscuro’ is packed with red plum, strawberry, kirsch, blackberry, and other fruits-of-the-forest but has a wonderfully leafy, savory undertone of dark, fresh forest floor, supported by moderate tannins and a mineral-rich earthiness. A rosato that reads more like a light red, it’s full of tart cranberry, raspberry compote, and sweet herbs, with tiny tongue-pricking bubbles. 'Ripa di Sopravento' is crafted from two hyper-local sub-clone of Trebbiano (plus three ‘mystery grapes’ interplanted amongst them), grapes are de-stemmed, followed by a direct press. The wine ferments in fiberglass containers and after a racking off the lees with 10g of residual sugar left in the must, the wine is bottled, where it then re-ferments to create its crisp, creamy bubbles. One of the most sought-after Lambruscos we carry – yes, it's amazing, but mainly because Vittorio only sends over a shipment every 2 or 3 years! Spontaneous fermentation, 6 days skin maceration, then aged in fiberglass tanks; like all wines in the lineup, no added sulfur and no filtering or fining. 100% Trebbiano d’Abruzzo with 8 days of skin contact; aged in fiberglass. Like a generator in a bottle, this light, bright orange wine keeps on giving. On the nose, cara cara orange juice and white flowers; on the palate, it’s vibrant and zesty, with notes of passion fruit, hibiscus, orange rind, and almonds, great acidity and a dry finish. Will quench the thirst of any skin-contact aficionado while also convincing the uninitiated to jump on board the orange bandwagon.

Enzo’s Primatraccia Bianco feels like a day at the beach in liquid format: a refreshing dunk in an ocean of briney, sun-drenched, and smile inducing grape juice. 100% Trebbiano grown along Enzo’s calcareous hillsides, the wine undergoes spontaneous fermentations in steel tanks with a few days macerating on skins before being transferred to clay amphora (as seen on the label) for 6-8 months of development, bottled without any filtration of sulphur. A head-turning and joy-inducing turn on the Sangiovese grape. Non-existent are the dusty tannins and more brooding fruit often associated with traditional renditions of the grape; instead this is a gentle and sexy beast - wrapped in a powdery soft, velvet texture we find oodles of ripe and candied cherry and raspberry fruit projected through a prism of high-toned dried rose petal aromatics. Fermented and aged in fiberglass with the slightest dash of SO2. Serve ever so slightly chilled.

Mint, lavender and fennel lead on the nose, while sweet, juicy persimmon and crisp pomegranate provide the backdrop on the palate. The youthful density of the ripe primary fruit contrasts with salty minerality and lively acidity, leaving a cascading and crisp impression on the palate. Siro's Sassella reveals another, darker-noted level of fruit and spice on the palate, with five-spice and brambly berries, tart red currant, caramelized sugar, and bresaola, wrapped around an inner, red floral sweetness. Fine, pin-prick-like tannins continue this dynamic, creating an interplay between luscious and pleasingly bitter/drying, leading to a lip-smacking, savory finish. A Nebbiolo that displays Burgundian richness and elegance and the lacy finesse of much bigger name Piemontese producers, this one's ready to go between now and the next 5 years.

Born from a trip to Alsace, where Corrado was inspired by the idea of expressing terroir and season not through a single variety wine but by mixing different grapes from the same soil, the 'Metccio' also nods to the traditions of the Marche; until the mid-90s, mixing different grapes from a vineyard site was the norm, vinifying by single varietal only a very recent phenomena born from enology and marketing. A co-fermentation of white grapes and red grapes spontaneously fermented, Corrado knocked this one out of the park – a joyful, moreish melange marked by red berries, touches of tropical ton

A blend of Trebbiano, Malvasia and Verdicchio from three parcels of vines young and old. The grapes were fermented on the skins for three weeks before being pressed off to concrete vats for a year of rest. A vibrant, sunshiny shade of amber, this is heady with ripe citrus, earth and spice, while tea-like tannins frame flavors of apricot, minerals and bitter herbs.

Sourced from two plots of Verdicchio that both lie within the borders of the classic Castelli di Jesi growing zone - one up in the mountains, the other neighboring the cantina - the Terre Silvate is fermented and aged in old concrete vats and while the majority is given a direct press, around twenty percent sits on skins for a few days, lending a little flesh and grip. Open and expressive in its youth, it pairs stone fruits, brine and a pleasant, almond-like bitterness to great effect.

From the singular contrada of Crasà, the 2018 Rosso 'Alberello' hails from a parcel of century-old (plus!), pre-phylloxera vines planted in the ancient bush vine (i.e. alberello) format. This corner of Etna is home to softer, more ashen volcanic soils, the resulting wines offering an extreme aromatic punch as a result. Intensely floral and perfumed, the wine reels with dried rose, powdered cocoa, dark cherry skin and raspberry candies straddled across a palate that is at once precise, complex, rich, lithe, persistent... we could go on and on.

wine: Lassaigne Le Cotet Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut NV

It’s a powerful chardonnay Champagne, the chalkiness mellowed with flavors of fresh almonds, scents of dried flowers and gingerbread spice. Like all of Lassaigne’s wines, it’s made without added yeast and with only a slight addition of sulfur at the press (none after).

We're #blessed to have snagged one of the few 6-packs of this juicy, large-format slugger to have made it to the west coast. 2 liters (yes, 2 whole liters) of bright and easy Veneto sunshine in a big ol' bottle, the Vino da Tavola is a laid back amalgamation of Merlot, Refosco, Cab Franc and Raboso, perfectly primed as the ultimate party favor. Unabashedly easy going and fresh, this will make for a killer bottle to share with friends al fresco.

A 10 day maceration on skins lends the '450' a deeply golden hue and more textural weight than its compatriots. With first fermentation in steel, second fermentation in bottle - basically an un-disgorged Champagne for orange wine aficionados.From vines planted in the early 1950s, the 450 leans heavily into the citrus skin/oil side of things capturing zesty pink grapefruit, Cara Cara orange and tangerine in a web of dusty stone and white orchid. L ow in alcohol but the most structured of their wines, though never sacrificing a hallmark saline freshness.

The story of Le Sincette lies right in the producer’s colorful labels. Splashes of purple for grapes, green for olive groves, a big dollop of blue denoting the nearby shores of Lake Garda, along with drawings of the plants and animals that grow there alongside the vines. Having purchased the property in the late 1970s, the Brunori family have spent the last 4 decades bringing light to some of Lombardia’s lesser known vinous stars such as Marzemino, Rebo, and, most importantly for them, Groppello. wine: Podere Veneri Vecchio BellaCiao Agostinella Bianco 2020
notes: Raffaello Annichiarico has been producing in the province of Benevento since 1999. His wines have a very precise idea at their base: to create an ecosystem in synergy between man and nature. A deeply amber wine, with lots of white flowers, citrus and pulpy fruit notes, mineral, herbaceous overtones and some serious but never astringent tannic bite.

wine: Poderi Veneri Vecchio Oh Oh Camajo Rosso 2021

An elegant red that is based on 90% Nerello Mascalese and 10% Nerello Cappuccio that mostly come from 80-100 year-old vines in Solicchiata. Almost rosé-like in hue, it is utterly true to a varietal character that is based on delicacy rather than intensity. wine: Mazzoni Colline Novaresi Vespolina Il Ricetto 2020

Vibrant and easy-drinking, 'Il Ricetto' doles out tart red cherry, wild strawberry, and white pepper alongside brisk acidity and lithe tannins.

The 'wonder child' in Dario's stable and arguably the benchmark grape of Oslavia, Princic's Ribolla spends 30 days on skins before aging in combination of old acacia and chestnut barrels. Deeply golden and silkily textured, the palate is chock with salty apricot skin, orange liqueur, lemon verbena, rosewater and creme caramel, the fruit stealthily unfolding in the mouth to reveal a wine deceptively supple in body, though there is plenty of underlying backbone by way of acid and fine tannins that promise a long life for this stunner. Dario's spiced and savory 'Jakot' is from 60-year-old Friulano vines - 'Jakot' being the winking, local nomenclature for native Tocai ('Tokaj') Friulano. 22 days of on-skin maceration followed by 24-30 months of aging in Slovenian oak barrels culminate in an amber wine of undeniable richness and outstanding length. A sulfur-free sparkling rosé from the Gambellara subregion of Veneto. Made from local red grape Corvina with Garganega must, ‘Confondo' is a play on Col Fondo, meaning "on the lees", which give the wine its lovely hazy character. Everything is done by hand in the production here, and the result is fruity and clean, with red currant and apple skin, strawberry and lemon, and a tart and tangy dry finish to cut any sweetness. A no brainer for sunny days!

The Parasiliti's baseline Etna Rosso contains fruit from vines averaging 80 years of age, spread across the contradas of Crasa and Calderara. Dominated by Mascalese with a small percentage of Nerello Cappuccio and Mirello Rossa, fermentation occurs in botte grande before transferring to cement in an effort to retain tension and verve. Tightly wound red berries, red cherry and cherry stone cushion a core of flinty woodsmoke, singed orange and wild herbs, emerging from a palate that is as lengthy as it is pure and juicy.

This wine may emerge in the coming years as one of Sicily's truly great, standard-bearing wines!

This 2016 is only the second edition of this magical but unfortunately rare bottling. This is a complex and meticulous blend of all the house's cuvées in the most difficult years. It is a mix of 80% Chardonnay and 20% Pinot Noir, 100% vinified in used Leflaive barrels. Its fine bubbles release an appealing nose featuring aromas of sweet-ripe citrus fruits, peach and red berries backed with notes of roasted nuts and some baked apple. A very complex palate in the mouth showing citrus spice and profound minerality with a lot of tension as well as great length and grace.

Some say the tiny wine region of Molise is Italy’s last hidden gem. Tucked away on the southern cusp of the high Apennines, the land here rolls from the steep slopes of interior Abruzzo to the southern plains of Puglia. Wine exports to the US are few and far between, but we managed to score a real gem here! Comprised of 50% Tintilla (a local varietal), 25% Falanghina and 25% Trebbiano Toscano the Tagada is a super sour, tart, and lively red. With fresh acidity and a youthful finish, this chillable, low ABV wine is supremely sluggable with notes of cranberry, kaffir lime, and orange peel.

The Libero sees 12 months in old oak tonneaux. Its freshness and precision galore on offer here, with Sangiovese fruit so defined that it almost feels three dimensional in the mouth: sweet red and black cherry and blackberry hover beneath lifted aromatics of violet and underbrush with a sweetly savory, almost tarry note adding some really meditative complexity.

Offering endless white flowers-lime blossom, daisy, viburnum jasmine-followed by golden apple, basil and lime. Taut, vertical and savory, the Ambaraba is testament to how well bottle-fermented wines develop over the course of a few years, snapping shut with a finish of moreish yellow citrus and rock salt.
A striking rosato made of Barbera. Off-dry and slightly frizzante; think raspberry soda, cherry, and lavender on a raft of subtle bubbles.

Orange peel, apricot, wild sage, and hints of candied fruit abound, carried on intense tannins well balanced by searing acidity. Not for the faint of heart but absolutely delicious when given a little time, air, and an open mind (a hunk of prosciutto wouldn't hurt either).

5ha vineyard near the sea, opposite the Aeolian Islands. The sun, the heat and the cool sea breeze wrap around this wine like a gentle hug. Grapes are grown organically with biodynamic treatments. Tones of violets, red currant, and sun-warmed blueberry, with moderate tannins.
