Equal parts Trebbiano, Malvasia and Bombino aged in stainless and without skin contact; an honest and straightforward nod to the Frascati wines of old, that retains an elegance and precision that transcends first impressions. Golden apples, lemon pith and smoky earth laced with pocks of ginger, geranium and spearmint.

Dominated by the southern Lazio specialty in Cesanese (though Daniele claims it different to the more celebrated clone in nearby Piglio) with smaller percentages of Sangiovese and Montepulciano. Wild blackberry, blackberry leaf and a smidge of balsamic highlight this classically styled red, wrapped neatly in velvety tannins over a mid-weight frame.

100% Montepulciano, with an intense, deep bouquet filled with red fruit, pepper and a whiff of smoke. On the palate it’s medium-bodied, balanced, with crisp acidity, a hint of tannins and a grippy, savory finish. “This wine is produced thanks to the land rich in stones and its exposure, to the sun, to the sea breeze, and to the meticulous work of man.” — Vincezo Di Meo. A lightly sparkling wine derived of 100% Malvasia, made according to ancestral method and with a salty and mineral profile, one that perfectly reminds the surprisingly nearby Adriatic Sea. The first and only (for the moment) wine made by Marco Pecorari, a young artisan from Friuli, who works with old-school methods. This wine ferments spontaneously in bottle without being disgorged. Gastronomic and rustic; to drink with fish dishes, or with your best friend.

Friulano is the grape that made Friuli famous, and this expression is truly stunning. Bright golden yellow in the glass with familiar hints of apple and pear carried by an otherwise outspoken nose and palate, you won't be forgetting this wine any time soon...

Not your typical Montepulciano as this undergoes carbonic maceration, lending an immediately appealing nose – scents of pickled cherry and strawberry jam, whiffs of smoke, flint, and undergrowth. Juicy and bright, with lightly chewy tannins and electric acidity, this is a lighter red wine, though there’s a touch of ferrous minerality lending extra character. Wild in style and wildly delicious.

Barely sulfured for maximum honesty. Offering a dynamic push-pull between ripe fruit and more tangy, salt-tinged notes: ainier cherry, yellow nectarine, and cantaloupe meet citrus zest, bitter almond, and scrubby aromatic herbs. 90% Spergola (hence the name “Gola”, which cleverly means "throat" or "gulp" in Italian), 7% Malvasia di Candia, 3% Uva Termarina with variable proportions depending on vintage. Spontaneous fermentation with 3 days skin maceration; aged in tank; re-fermentation in bottle; no disgorgement, fining or filtration, and no added sulfur. Wild aromatics, ginger and honey with amazing texture. Just a glass of sunshine.

Trebbiano Toscano, Trebbiano Spoletino, and a small amount of Grechetto, tended to organically and with little-intervention - a lively, mineral, and fresh expression of Umbria. On the nose, candied lemon, yellow apple, honeysuckle and jasmine - breath deeper and you can sense the cool breeze off nearby Lake Trasimeno. The palate showcases golden-fruit met with a zippy, signature salinity.

A gently sparkling wine from the classic local grape, Lambrusco di Sorbara. That’s all that’s classic about it however - as a short maceration on skins leads to a bone dry, rosato -style Sorbara, all tart strawberries, cherries, and herbs. Fermentations all happen in stainless steel before a secondary fermentation in bottle is fired with a little must from original harvest. Minimal sulfur added at bottling and no filtering or fining. There’s the potential you might wanna bathe in this stuff, and given the volumes in which people purchase this wine, we suspect some maybe do.

Canus’ 2019 Ribolla Gialla offers a super fresh and classically wrapped interpretation of a variety that is often more widely seen and celebrated on the Slovenian side of the border (and even deeper into eastern Europe.) A brisk and focused nose of lime, bosc pear, white flowers, chalky mineral, and crushed stone dazzles, as the palate delivers dimensions and persistence that seem to far outweigh the wine’s modest price tag. The Malvasia by Il Carpino is a well-structured and full-bodied orange wine, vinified like red wine: with long maceration, and aged in oak. It has rich and intense scents of dried fruit, honey, and ripe yellow fruit; on the palate, it's warm and full-bodied, smooth, and complex.

wine: La Cappucina Faren Colline Novaresi Nebbiolo
notes: Raffaella’s ‘Faren’ bottling sees a super classical and somewhat matured rendition of Alto Piemonte Nebbiolo; something structurally softer and more rounded than you’d traditionally find in the more ‘classical’ corners of the Langhe to the south, and, in this instance, packed with boatloads of brooding red fruit and plenty of darker, alluring savory tones. "It is our daring tour in pursuit of the grapes with greater acidity and freshness," says the crew of Argricola Forestieri. Mainly Sangiovese, it comes from co-fermentation with a small amount of white grapes. Short macerations and aging in concrete. A wine without unnecessary frills from the mountainous Maremma: bing cherries, violets, wild herbs.

60% Nero Buono from Guyot-trained vines on volcanic soil, 40% Malvasia and Trebbiano, from Pergola-trained vines. The white and red grapes are fermented separately in fiberglass and then blended before bottling for a wine of great freshness and surprising acidity with a crunchy tannin structure that lengthens and complete the drink. There is everything you need: red fruit and minerality, body, acidity and balsamic hints.

A subtle skin-contact wine made of Malvasia and Trebbiano. Clementine and chamomile backed by slight, supple tannins and a crisp, dry finish. 'Corragio' means ‘courage’ and this wine speaks of the will of Leonardo and his family to take the plunge into making natural wines that are free from flavor-fixing additives, preservatives, and synthetic chemicals.

Intensely aromatic, starting with peach and citrus peel, sage, mint and white flowers that evolve into more savory, earth-rich notes of chamomile, chestnut, honey, leather, carob, and salt. wine: Sebastian Van de Sype Ancestrale Lambrusco 2020
notes: Sebastian's Ancestrale has a deep ruby ​​red color and a nose with full of beautiful black fruit, cherries, forest fruits, fresh grass, and violets. A bit rustic but what charm and character! A farmhouse wine in the most noble sense of the word.

Based around the Fogarina grape - a sub-varietal thought to be extinct in the Emilia-Romagna region but resuscitated by the Alberici family, now the only ones who cultivate it - this is a completely fresh take on Lambrusco, frisky with tart currant notes and a vegetal undercurrent in juxtaposition to purple berry ripeness. Dangerously fun, low ABV (10 percent), and a small victory for biodiversity to boot!

wine: La Ca Nova Bric Mentin Montefico Barbaresco 2018
notes: Still one the best values in Piemonte, hands down, and it's hard to ignore the praise heaped upon Barbaresco estate La Ca'Nova. Their 2018 Barbaresco Montefico Vigna Bric Mentina is fabulous. Most producers would dream of making a wine like this in a strong vintage, much less one that presented so many challenges. Rose petal, lavender, spice and blue/purplish fruit open first. The 2018 is relatively soft and supple, but that is not a bad thing for a wine from Montefico, where the Barbarescos are often searing in intensity. The 2018 finishes with real weight and intensity.

Purchased in 1980, the Falletto estate is comprised of 13 hectares (32acres) in the commune of Serralunga d’Alba. Considered by Bruno Giacosa as the best area for producing elegant and long-lived Barolos, the Falletto vineyard is southwest facing on steep slopes of calcareaous clay soils in an amphitheater shape. The Falletto wines are austere, elegant and complex on the nose, with excellent structure and suave tannins. The 2017 vintage will be a year to remember for the challenges that growers faced from Mother Nature, namely hot weather and very little rain. Surprisingly, the wines produced

Asili represents one of the most important single vineyards of Barbaresco. Bruno Giacosa purchased vineyards in Asili in the 1980s, which now total 2.5 hectares There’s impeccable transparency and freshness to this Barbaresco on the nose, which introduces bright rose petals, lifted orange peel, crushed stones and sour cherries. The stoney tannins trace intricate detail on the medium-to full-bodied palate, highlighting the racy acidity, brambly undertones and a beautiful array of wild berries. Yes, there’s power and depth of flavor, but this is all about grace and beauty. Drink from 2024. The 2

Setting themselves apart even further, They insist that great wine can come only from fully ripe grapes, something the majority of producers here seem unwilling or unable to achieve, relying on sugar instead and making highly technical wines. Everything kicked off in 2008, but it was in 2010 when the first wine, "Notti Stellate" Etna Rosso was bottled from the first vineyard located in Contrada Galfina in Linguaglossa. Two weeks on the skins for good old Favorita, the Piemonte white variety so close to Vermentino that the two are considered identical (so a non-maritime Vermentino if you will, with the signature of a more continental terroir and climate.) The skin of Favorita grapes is on the thicker side, influencing its marked tannic structure here without ever being too powerful or intrusive. Saline notes, dynamite acidity, and fruit, fruit, and fruit are the main takeaways here, wonderfully aromatic and rounded to perfection, it's full of caramelized orange with a little citrus peach and floral honey blos

A wine that is at once both Italian at heart and French in execution – this is distinctly Barbera just through JYP’s lens. The vines, around 40 years old, grow on gray and white marl soils cultivated biodynamically. These are old vines with low yields, grown biodynmically on gray and white marl soils, harvested by hand slightly under-ripe to counterbalance the richness of the grape variety. It undergoes carbonic maceration without punching down for 4 weeks, on indigenous yeasts, then ages for at least a year in 900 liter sandstone amphoras, which enhances the tension and minerality of the wine

Lisa and Silvia grow a minuscule amount of red grapes, including just enough for this uber-cheerful 100% Ciliegiolo bottle. Fruit sees 6 days skin maceration and spontaneous fermentation before being aged in old barrique for 7 months before bottling. Ciliegiolo makes the quintessential chillable red – full of ripe, red, lush fruit and fresh herbs. No different here, with an added Twizzler-tang and subtly smoky bite from those volcanic soils.

Comprised entirely of Procanico that sees just under a month on skins maceration in anfora before gentle pressing, followed by aging also in anfora for 5 months, then another 6 months in steel (with some still on skins). A wine that ranges widely, in a good way – intensely aromatic recalling tropical fruit, yellow flowers, sage, and mineral notes, but ultimately decidedly gastronomic and savory, with the local Trebbiano clone giving back all the tuffaceous-soil gifts of Lake Bolsena's volcanic origins. Only 500 bottle produced.

100% Roscetto, a third of which sees 15 days skin maceration and one year of aging in stainless steel on fine lees before bottling. The result is a wine that smells of apricot, honey, and fresh almond, but remains lithe and fresh at each sip – a smidge of residual sugar and sensational length makes for an exceedingly elegant orange wine. Poggio Bbaranello is the only producer making 100% Roscetto with skin maceration, due to vines being very low yielding. As such, production is super small – less than 300 bottles!

wine: JM Seleque Le Quintette Extra Brut NV
notes: Jean-Marc is without doubt one of the bright young stars of the region, yet his wines continue to fly under the radar. His only Blanc de Blancs, the 'Le Quintette' is a blend of five Chardonnay vineyards planted between 1950 and 1985. The low dosage style works well in bringing out the wine's inner tension and vivid, precise varietal notes – citrus oil, fresh bread, nougat, dried white flowers and crisp orchard fruit. Tightly wound, energetic, with racy acidity and chalky, structuring dry extract, concluding with a long, saline finish.

A rosé for the summer to drink cold or for the winter months at room temp. Made from 100% Nero d’Avola and harvested early with respect to the sugar and phenolic ripeness. Aged in steel for 5 months. A supremely refreshing wine with a dark pink color that resembles fresh pressed strawberries. Flavors of bright red fruits (we think of strawberries) and herbs (basil) with just a touch of creaminess to round out the acidity. A serious thirst quencher.

Forever our darling in the Margo line up! A super versatile and plush rosato, the fruit emanating from an early season pass of Carlo's prized Sangiovese plot. Leafy, just-picked strawberries, confit cherry tomato and pomegranate, ensconced in a mouthful of pithy magenta grape juice. Definitely darker in color than your average rose, it's a wine that still always seems to speak of sunnier days on the horizon, while packing plenty of rounder and spicier winter feels.

Always lifted, high-toned and very alive, the 2020 rendition of the Margo Rosso seems to have taken on an added dimension of structure and seriousness this season. Bing cherries and cola zing one way, violets and lavender sway the other, all of them guided into place by an intense herbal quality and firm tannins. Sees 6 months raising in old barrels.

Earthy aromas of smoke, iron, and crushed black stones mix with dark cherry and cassis on the nose. On the palate, the flavors are framed by ripe, firm tannins, with bursts of earthy red plum and blackberry/raspberry fruit.

The I Cacciagalli estate focuses on natural wines, some of which are made in clay amphorae (with long skin macerations, and fermentations with ambient yeasts). This expression, the 2017 Phos, shows pretty elegance and tightness that is further underscored by the naturally high tannins of the Aglianico grape. This wine opens a window onto the grape in its most naked state. This is a rare perspective on a variety that is often plied with extra oak and aging time. Sourced from an 80 year old, alberello-trained parcel affectionately known is Pirao from within the contrada of Prezzemolo, the wine undergoes native fermentation in larger botti before being transferred to smaller barrels (250-500L) for 2 years of development in the cellar. Giovanni's Nebbiolo Prachiosso sees a traditional maceration and an aging of 20 months, between oak barrel and bottle. Intense ruby red in color, this Nebbiooo has a fine and elegant nose with hints of rose and notes of raspberry, strawberry and spices. On the palate, it is expressively warm and enveloping, with delicate tannins.

wine: Aia delle Monache Giusto un Litro Rosso NV
notes: Vittorio and Michele are just as adventurous as they are dedicated to respecting local history. No better example than this, a shorter maceration and earlier harvested, fresh expression of what are typically more intense grapes. Comprised of 70% Pallagrello Nero and 30% Casavecchia, grapes are harvested earlier, maintaining higher acidity. Notes of red grapefruit, orange blossom, and fresh plum jump out on the nose, with a distinct streak of chewy red fruit from the Pallagrello and earthy, spicy notes from the Casavecchia. Surprisingly easy-drinking, and the perfect size for it.

wine: Jacques Lassaigne Vignes de Montgueux Extra Brut NV
notes: Emmanuel Lassaigne's most broadly appealing offering – a real journeyman on our shelves. 100% Chardonnay sourced from 9 different sites in Montgueux – an island of Chardonnay-appropriate limestone in the otherwise Pinot Noir-rich Aube – aged in a mix of new & old barrels for 12 to 24 months. Bright citrus aromatics with leafy, herbal notes, rolling into a palate vibrantly alive with more succulent citrus and melon. It's a richer Blanc de Blancs that maintains plenty of acidity and cut. A wonderful match to oysters, seafood and shellfish – and of course, by itself.

Martirio Pet Nat 2024 is a natural wine crafted by El Regreso , in the La Mancha region in Spain . This sparkling Pet Nat wine is made with Marisancho and Moscatel grapes. Manually disgorged after 12 months lees aging in the bottle. No added sulphites We have not yet tried this fizz, but hear it has strong citrussy and tropical aspects keeping it fun and fresh!

Garnatxa Rosada is a natural wine crafted by La Rural , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This 10% Rosé wine is made with 100% Grenache grapes. We have not yet tried this rose wine but hear it has notes of grapefruit, strawberries and subtle dried-herb notes. Fresh and vibrant, with bright acidity, a mineral edge and a clean, refreshing finish. 100% Grenache (known locally as Garnaxta Negre) from 5-year-old vines around Santes Creus, Alt Camp, planted at 317 metres altitude on lime-clay soils. The grapes are destemmed and macerated in stainless steel for 6 hours, then gently pressed before go

Sumoll 2023 is a natural wine crafted by La Rural , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This light, 12.5% red wine is made with Sumoll grapes, which are grown on old vines planted at around 422 metres altitude on lime-clay soils with east–west exposure. We have not yet tried this wine but hear it has a mineralic edge with some fleshy red fruit bursts.

Ull De Llebre 2024 is a natural wine crafted by La Rural , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This red wine is made with Ull De Llebre grapes, otherwise known as Tempranillo. There is also a cheeky little 10% of Grenache slipped into the blend here to add a little soft spice. Expect pops of dark cherrys, liquorice, blackcurrants, black olive and mild violets blackcurrant, dark cherry, liquorice, black olive and subtle violet notes, with a savoury finish. Claret 2023 is a natural wine crafted by La Rural , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This red wine is made with 80% Macabeu , 10% Sumoll and 10% Ull De Llebre grapes, otherwise known as Tempranillo. The Catalan vines here are aged between 6 and 35 years, planted around Santes Creus at roughly 316–408 metres altitude on lime-clay soils with river stones. The grapes undergo 6 days of skin contact before gentle pressing, followed by controlled fermentation in stainless steel. The wine is then aged in stainless steel. No added sulphites to our knowledge

1l Yellow 2025 is a one litre bottle of natural wine crafted by La Rural , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This mild yet also somewhat wild white wine is made with a Catalan blend of Macabeu , Xarel Lo and Moscatell grapes. Expect a wild nose followed by some tropical touches. A playful, but adventerous and raw one that has a bit of funk

Malvasia de Sitges 2024 is a natural wine crafted by La Rural , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This mildly orange wine is made with 100% Malvasia grapes, as the name suggests and features no added sulphites. This wine features a nice, mild reduction and good acidity for the grape. Stone fruits dominate with touches of herbs and wet pebble minerality. Less invasive on aromatics than some other Malvasia wines, but still with a good twang on the finish for an easy drinking sipper! Here in their Malvasia de Sitges 2024, the grapes are sourced from young vines around Santes Creus, Alt Camp in C

Moscatell D'Alexandria 2024 is a natural wine crafted by La Rural , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This vibrant and aromatic white wine is made with 100% Moscatel grapes, known in Italy as Zibibbo or in France as Muscat d'Alexandrie. Its a floral grape, often used for sweet wines in the conventional wine world, but here in the natural wine scene is often made dry, like this, where to perfumed aromatics really breathe a burst of life to the nose.

Macabeu 2023 is a natural wine crafted by La Rural , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This light 11% white wine with no added sulphites is made with Macabeu grapes, and features a mild smokey reduction, giving it a mystical wild character. Its certainly an adventure, with a little funk too! Otherwise pops of yellow apples, lime, cinnamon, smoke and ash. Pretty cool for those who like things wild!

Cava Rose Brut Nature 2023 is a natural wine crafted by Azimut , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This sparkling wine is made with Grenache , Monastrell and Xarel Lo grapes. Expect this slight more raw Cava to feature pops of toasted spice alongside red berries and raspberry hints. This fizz is Brut Nature, so with no added sugar dosage. Only a small addition of sulphites at bottling is added.

Cava Brut Nature 2023 is a natural wine crafted by Azimut , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This sparkling wine is made with Macabeu , Xarel Lo and Parellada grapes. Expect pops of green apple, bruised pear and soft tropical fruit coming through, with a crisp and energetic perlage that keeps it vibrant, fresh and perky. It's got a little wildness and a little punk rock attitude

Negre 2020 is a natural wine crafted by Azimut , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This 12% medium bodied red wine is made with a rich Catalan blend of Tempranillo knowen as Ull De Llebre ,as well as Monastrell , Grenache and Caraignan grapes. Expect pops of blackberry, red cherry, and dark forest fruit. Nice acidity, a rustic touch and savoury, Spanish finish that makes it suitable for grilled meats and hearty stews. Aged in concrete tanks and with a little SO2 addition at bottling

Brisat 2023 is a easy going, fresh and vibrant natural wine crafted by Azimut , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This orange wine is made with a Catalan blend of Parellada , Sumoll Blanc , Grenache Blanc and Moscatell grapes. We find this wine to be EXCELLENT VALUE for a light and non-fussy orange wine. The Moscatell (Zibibbo) give it an aromatic edge. The other grapes bring a nice amount of flavour along too, for example bursts of peach, apricot, vanilla, tangerine and a soft herbal edge. There is the softest tannic grip, which gives it a little complexity whilst still being a chuggable eas

Blanc 2023 is a natural wine crafted by Azimut , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This crisp, easy going white wine is made with a Catalan blend of Macabeu , Grenache Blanc , Xarel Lo and Moscatell grapes. Good value for the price point this Azimut Blanc. Fresh and crisp, offering soft touches of pear, elderflower and peaches with a mild salty touch.

Costabosco 2024 is a natural wine crafted by La Stoppa , in the Emilia Romagna region in Italy . This orange wine is made with Malvasia di Candia Aromatica grapes and is similar in style to the current (delicious) Ageno 2022, however this one is a touch lighter and more approachable without aging. La Stoppa is one of those estates that has quietly shaped what natural wine looks like in Emilia-Romagna. Riostoppa 2019 is a natural wine crafted by La Stoppa , in the Emilia Romagna region in Italy . This red wine is made with classic French Bordeaux varieties Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon grapes, which were planted in the region a long time ago as was the fashion then. Here... La Stoppa put their take on it, and this remains a strong red wine at 14.5%.

wine: Entre Vinyes - Oniric Gravetat Zero Pet Nat
notes: Oniric Gravetat Zero Pet Nat is a natural wine crafted by Entre Vinyes , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This super light, 9% alc Pet Nat wine is made with 100% Xarel-lo grapes AND WE LOVE IT! Nicely salty, mineralic and with a pop of pear and lemon sherbert tingling on your palate, this wine is everything a zingy and fresh white pet nat should be!
Rosato is a natural wine crafted by Sette , in the Piedmont region in Italy . 100% Barbera from 15-year-old vines, with a very pale nice colour. We expect good things from this!

Mary of Modena is a natural wine crafted by Il Farneto , in the Emilia-Romagna region in Italy . This sparkling wine is made with a blend of mostly white and but a TOUCH of red grapes too: 60% Spergola, 38% Chardonnay and 2% Termarina grapes (quite a rare one, which is red). We hear this 11.5% fizz to be light and with citrussy undertones, not too fruity with citrus, flowers and cotton candy memories coming through under a nice mineralic edge.

Riz 2024 is a natural wine crafted by Viniverso , in the Friuli Venezia Giulia region in Italy . This white wine is made with Pinot Grigio grapes, made here as a white wine rather than orange as the grape and region often do. Expect a VERY classic profile and mouthfeel here, despite still being low intervention and a low budget pricepoint. We hear it has notes of pear, apple and a touch of white pepper. Fresh and uncomplicated classic fun.

Sclopit is a natural wine crafted by Viniverso , in the Friuli Venezia Giulia region in Italy . This red wine is made with 50% Schioppettino and 50% Pinot Noir grapes, and is light at 12.5% but still with Italian soul. Expect bursts of cherry, forest fruits and a little spicey touch

Svol is a natural wine crafted by Viniverso , in the Friuli Venezia Giulia region in Italy . This light, fresh and crisp white wine is made with 100% Sauvignon Blanc grapes, which comes armed with a green, flinty and aromatic profile. Aged in concrete tanks for freshness, we expect this wine to pair brilliantly with shellfish or seafood on warm evenings

Bianco Testalonga is a natural wine crafted by Antonio Perrino who makes wine under the name Testalonga (not to be confused with the South African producer of the same name). He tends to steep vineyards in the Liguria region in Italy . This white wine is made with Vermentino grapes, which see 5 days skin contact before 18 months in old oak barrels to age.

Rossese di Dolceacqua is a natural wine crafted by Antonio Perrino , making wine under the name Testalonga . He is based in the Liguria region in Italy . This red wine is made with Rossese grapes, which is quite a rare grape - there are just 80 hectares planted in total! A challenging grape to master, here Antonio grows 2 hectares of the 80 total on steep vineyard terraces. He also does not add any sulphites in production.

Viaria is a natural wine crafted by Il Mortellito , in the south eastern corner of Sicily, in Italy . This white wine is made with Moscato di Noto grapes, which is a native Sicilian varietal of Muscat (there are many different ones!). Here there is just a short maceration on the skins, so expect this wine to be more white than orange, as the grape is often made like. Aged in stainless steel tanks for freshness, expect ripe stone fruit, lemon rind and salty aspects too with a mild floral touch.

Pinot Draga 2017 is a natural wine crafted by Kmetija Stekar , in the Brda region in Slovenia . This is right on the border of Italy, where the winery farms 5 hectares of vines. This serious, structured and complex orange wine is made with Pinot Grigio grapes, which undergo 20 days of skin-contact maceration before seeing 36 months of aging in Acacia barrels. No added sulphites. Expect depth, tannin, complexity and energy.

Cala Iancu is a natural wine crafted by Il Mortellito , in the south eastern corner of Sicily, in Italy . This white wine is made with Sicilian grapes 90% Grillo and 10% Catarratto grapes, and we hear it is VERY fresh, and very Italian - dolce vita in a glass some would say. Aged in stainless steel tanks to achieve this, we expect this wine to deliver a lot of nice summery vibes and great value too!

Cala Niuru is a natural wine crafted by Il Mortellito , based in the south eastern part of the Sicily, in Italy . This medium-bodied, fresh red wine is made with mostly Frappato and a little Nero d'Avola grapes, which are all grown on Alberello bush vines. This plush and fruity red wine sees 4 days skin contact. Aged in stainless steel tank to maintain freshness, we hear it has notes of cherries, raspberries and a hint of liquorice. Ideal for a weeknight pasta or casual weekend bbq.

Monocromo #1 (Passerina del Frusinata) 2022 is a natural wine crafted by Macciocca , in the Lazio region in Italy . This serious white wine is made with Passerina del Frusinate and Malvasia grapes, cultivated in the region of Civitella. This 11.5% wine is aged in cement tanks as well as stainless steel. To our knowledge, this wine does not have any added sulphites but this needs verification.

wine: La Via del Colle  - Lopi Rosa
notes: Lopi Rosa is a natural wine crafted by La Via del Colle in the Emilia-Romagna region in Italy . This rosé wine is made with a blend of S angiovese and Syrah grapes, and despite the rich colour, we hear this wine delivers a lot of light freshness that the colour and grapes might not lead you to expect.

Sar-Do-Né or SAR DO NÉ i s a natural wine crafted by Santa Colomba , in the Veneto region in Italy . This white wine is made with Chardonnay grapes, hence the play on the word in the name in a Venetian accent and sardines hehe. Aged in stainless steel tanks, expect freshness and light mineralic flickers here, very different to a more rounded, barrel aged Chardonnay and quite light in alcohol too.

El Griso is a natural wine crafted by Santa Colomba , in the Veneto region in Italy . This orange wine is made with Pinot Grigio grapes (often referred to as a Ramato in Italy when making orange with with Pinot Grigio). The grapes are grown on clay and calcerous soils in the hills of Colli Berici . We have not yet tried this wine but hear it has fresh acidity with dominant orange zest notes, and light tannins.

Jankot 2020 is a natural wine crafted by Kmetija Stekar , in the Brda region in Slovenia. Located right on the border of Italy, this orange wine is made with Tokaj grapes.. which are not allowed to be called as such such to EU law. Tokaj or Tokaji is both a region famous for sweet wines in Hungary (made mainly with Furmint grapes), but also a wine grape, now not allowed to be labelled as such which is called Tojai or Tokaj (for Tokaj Friulano), made famous in the Friuli region of Italy and nearby Slovenia. Malvasia 2020 is a natural wine crafted by Kmetija Stekar , in the Brda region in Slovenia . This is right on the border of Italy, where the winery farms 5 hectares of vines. This serious, structured and complex orange wine is made with Malvasia grapes, which spend 14 days macerating on their skins before seeing 14 months aging in old acacia barrels. No added sulphites. Expect a floral, aromatic profile with depth and complexity, alongside tannins and vibrant energy

Pinot Draga 2018 is a natural wine crafted by Kmetija Stekar , in the Brda region in Slovenia . This is right on the border of Italy, where the winery farms 5 hectares of vines. This serious, structured and complex orange wine is made with Pinot Grigio grapes, which undergo 20 days of skin-contact maceration before seeing 36 months of aging in Acacia barrels. No added sulphites. Expect depth, tannin, complexity and energy.

Elisir 2022 is a natural wine crafted by Calabretta , in the Sicily region in Italy . This red wine from Mount Etna is made with Nerello Mascalese and a small amount of Nerello Cappuccio grapes. We have not tried this vintage yet but hear it has notes of r ed cherry, raspberry, minerals, concentrated fruit, smoke and some tart red fruit. Expect a more classic touch to this 14% wine, in addition to a bold structure and tannic weight. It is very hard to find low intervention Etna wines at this lower pricepoint, so we are excited to try it soon!

Vinu I Casa Macerato 2023 is a natural wine crafted by Nasciri , in the Calabria region in Italy . This vibrant coloured orange wine is made with Greco Bianco grapes which undergo 5 days of skin contact and 8 months aging on lees. We have not yet tried this vintage, but hear it has a lovely floral touch, which aromas of honey and acacia. We expect a bit of wildness here too based on other wines from the producer we have tried!

DoReMi Wine 'Rkatsiteli Mtsvane 2023' is an incredible wine that blew us all away with it's complexity and drinkabilty, the age on it is just right for its tannic structure and balance. Expect huge bursts of both dried apricot AND fresh apricot alongside notes of cinnamon, vanilla and mint. As for the winemaking, here there has been 6 months on skins in Qvevri Amphora. With all Georgian wines, do not serve chilled, and allow to breathe for best results. These wines are stable and should hold a good few days once open, improving greatly with time. Mtsvane Amber 2024 is a natural wine crafted by Doremi , in the Kakheti region in Eastern Georgia . This orange wine features 6 months on the skins in traditional Georgian Qvevri Amphora and is made with 100% Mtsvane grapes. We hear this wine has a nutty aspect running alongside vibrant herbal undertones and grippy tannins. Don't serve chilled.

We discovered this new Brand Bros orange wine at our pals bar 'Le Regret' in London and immediately requested it -so are now thrilled to have Orange Pur online and in stores now. Featuring a big mix of 7 grapes, fermented on the skins for 3 weeks, expect a very (actual) orange like flavour , almost like an Adult Fanta! wine: Jean Marc Dreyer - Pinot Gris Origin 2023 (One Per Order)
notes: Pinot Gris Origin 2023 (One Per Order) is a natural wine crafted by Jean Marc Dreyer , in the Alsace region in France . This orange wine is made with Pinot Gris grapes, which are macerated for around 20 days on the skins. Hard to find, aged holistically and will age beautifully too. No additions of sulphites, as with all Jean-Marc Dreyer wines.

Whilst similar to Homok, Dio has a slightly creamier, saltier edge. Truly delicious! Wet rocks, citrus zest, salt and vanilla. Perspektive Weiss N.V by Koppitsch is a natural wine made in Burgenland with Weissburgunder and a tiny splash of Chardonnay grapes, which features vibrant acidity and a salty approach. This is one of the more complex Koppitsch wines, and really is very good indeed! Mild bitter and vegetal touches lift its presence, making ideal for summery afternoon and Asian food or salads. This new edition released in 2026 is a non-vintage wine, so we expect a blend of the 2024 and 2025. This wine will age remarkably well too, from our experience having tried older vintages like 2015!

Oooh! WE LOVE HOMOK by Koppitsch, a wonderful winery from Burgenland, Austria! Homok 2025 is made of Grüner Veltliner, Weissburgunder and Sauvignon Blanc. Expect Salt, Citrus, Banana and Tropical aromas on the nose which then meets a zingy and refreshing, citrus filled, saline and mineral rich mouthfeel here. Homok is one of those wines that is both gluggable on a warm afternoon but also has that zingy, acidic salty bite on the finish - plus it's incredible value! Watch our Koppitsch documentary HERE

Brutal 2023 is a rare natural wine crafted by Vinyes Tortuga , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This orange wine with just 750 bottles made is created with Carinyena Blanca , Garnacha Blanca and Garnacha Roja (Grenache Gris) grapes. Both the owners of Vinyes Tortuga actually are no stranger to making Brutal wines, having worked with one of the founders Joan Ramón Escoda. Some of the vines in their own offering are 90 years old The mix of grapes are destemmed by hand and then macerated on the skins for a week before theaging in steel tanks for fresness. We hear its salty and a little spicy.

wine: Sepp & Maria Muster - Rosé Vom Opok 2022
notes: Rosé Vom Opok 2022 by Sepp & Maria Muster is a natural wine made in Styria with Blauer Zweigelt , Blauer Wildbacher and Blaufränkisch grapes. We are yet to try this vintage, but the previous vintage was a remarkable wine with lots of character! Earthy notes alongside macerated strawberries, white pepper, cranberry, lime. Gorgeous colour too. Complex and one to really sit with and think about - as this is an example of truly excellent winemaking.

Kisi 2024 is a natural wine crafted by Gelovani Cellar , in the Kakheti region in Georgia . Made from Kisi grapes, this amber wine undergoes seven months of skin maceration, allowing the wine to develop its deep color, structure and layered character typical of traditional Kakhetian skin-contact wines. rich and inviting, with aromas of ripe peach , dried apricot and hints of citrus , complemented by subtle earthy and nutty notes. Otskhanuri Sapere 2019 is a natural wine crafted by Nanua Wines , in the Imereti region in Georgia . This red wine is made with Otskhanuri Sapere grapes. Proxy E is a non-alcoholic proxy wine crafted by Bouche , in the Berlin region in Germany . This non alcoholic alternative to wine is made with white tea, refined with fermented honey and sage and silverberry. The honey brings a delicate, hovering sweetness, sage adds herbal depth and silverberry delivers a fine, mineral finish. Fresh, layered and with fine effervescence. An alcohol-free sparkling wine alternative with its own character.

This very light red wine is made with Poulsard grapes, and at 11.5% alcohol we expect Poulsard Pinte Bien to go down as easy as possible, with that slightly more classic edge Domaine de la Pinte offer, with a little more sulphur use than some others in the region.

Steinmergel 2022 is a natural wine crafted by new wine producer Kleines Gut , in the Württemberg region in Germany . This white wine is made with 1/3 Kerner and 2/3 Riesling grapes, and is the entry level wine for Kleines Gut. 10mg/l sulphur added at bottling. Meant to be fruity and mineralic at the same time.

Spätburgunder 2022 is a natural wine crafted by Kleines Gut , in the Württemberg region in Germany . This red wine is made with Pinot Noir grapes, which are grown on very small plots of vines aged between 20 and 50 years old, that Kleines Gut actually call "Gardens" due to their small scale. This Spätburgunder 2022 is aged in old barrique barrels for 12 months, after 10 days of whole cluster fermentation. It's limited to 1073 bottles.

Schwabenmagnum is a natural red "table wine" crafted by Kleines Gut , in the Württemberg region in Germany . This red wine is made with Blaufränkisch aka Lemberger in Germany and Trollinger grapes, both with not the best reputation in Germany and so this is the idea for the table wine in a litre bottle of Schwabenmagnum. Schwabenmagnum is limited to 808 bottles and is aged with equal splits of grapes in Amphora... so a bit more care taken than your average table wine! 25mg/l suphur added at bottling.

Lemberger "Großer Stein" 2022 is a natural wine crafted by Kleines Gut , in the Württemberg region in Germany . This red wine with 30 mg/l sulphur at bottling is made with Blaufränkisch grapes (aka Lemberger) and was limited to 616 bottles. We hear this one needs a little breathing room, so ideally put in a carafe for 20-30 minutes before drinking.

Munjebel Rosso 2021 is a natural wine (although less so than previous years) crafted by Frank Cornelissen , on Mount Etna in the Sicily region in Italy . This red wine is made with 100% Nerello Mascalese grapes, and this is the entry level of his more serious wines before reaching the Cru level. Munjebel is a wine that has gone through a lot of evolution over the past decade, with Frank Cornelissen now opting for a less zero-zero approach and taking on use of sulphur and some filtration for his preferred style. wine: Feral - No. 1 White Szechuan Pepper & Hops
notes: Feral are a group of botanists, fermentation experts, and chefs creating uniquely flavoured alcohol free alternatives out of the Italian Dolomites by fermenting and macerating beets, herbs, spices and wild fruit. From the maker: A still alternative that is anything but quiet in terms of taste. Fermented white beetroot combined with hops and Szechuan pepper makes a tasty trio to remember. Richly fragrant, with pronounced citrus notes and a tickling spiciness, velvety and spicy.

SALMONIDO by Barranco Oscuro is a red wine made in Granada with Pinot Noir grapes, which are not so common to see in Spain. Barranco Oscuro is a natural wine project by father Manuel Valenzuela and son Lorenzo Valenzuela. The vinyard is situated in the south of Spain, Granada on top of a set of mountains called ""Sierra Nevada"", 1300 meters above the sea level, where climate conditions are extremely special. Very fruity, but not sweet. Like all good things, this wine needs time to breathe, allowing its rich, berry-laden aromas to fully unfold.

Kisi 2024 is a natural wine crafted by Iberieli , in the western Kakheti region in Georgia . She farms a recovered old family vineyard using a lunar-calendar approach without synthetic chemistry. The wine ferments naturally and ages in stainless steel before bottling. Tasting Notes: We have not yet tried this vintage of O'Belix by Il Roccolo, but we hear it has notes of pale cherry, dried herbs, almond and a light perfumed

wine: Max Dexheimer - Schmuck Pet Nat Rosé
notes: Max Dexheimer's 'Schmuck Pet Nat' is a natural wine made from Pinot Noir in Rheinhessen, is full of Sour Cherry & Fizzy Sweet notes. Really yummy 10% fizz! Whilst Dexheimer has his Schmuck... there is also the Nice Guy, which is perhaps the opposite and a play on words!
Nice Guy Rosé by Dexheimer is a natural wine made in Rheinhessen, Germany with Blauer Portugieser , Silvaner and Pinot Noir grapes.

Collo Tortonesi by I Carpini is a natural white wine made in the North of Italy, in Piedmont with Timorasso grapes. Simple, very clean white wine. Mineral touches, mildly floral with hint of vanilla. Some mild sulphur use but for this price no complaints

Kékburgundi 2022 by Franz Weninger is a natural red wine made in Burgenland with Pinot Noir grapes, which are called Kékburgundi in Hungarian where this wine is harvested (but vinified in Austria's Burgenland)
Hubertus Purus by Rudolf Trossen is a premium, no-added sulphur Riesling wine from the famous Mosel valley. This crisp white wine is vinified on two slate plots and aged in old German Foudre.

wine: Eschenhof Holzer - The Natural Orange 1 litre
notes: The Natural Orange by Eschenhofer Holzer, from Wagram in Austria is a natural wine surprisingly impressive for an easy, very affordable orange in 1 litre milk bottle! Made with Grüner Veltliner, this gives off an interesting nose of mint, wet grass and clementine. Easy breezy in mouthfeel, mild and good value considering its a whole litre.

Massale 2019 by Opi d'aqui is a natural wine made in Languedoc with three different types of Grenache; Grenache Gris , Grenache and Grenache Blanc grapes. This makes it a red white blend, and with an unusual chartacter.

wine: Manuel Pineau - Le Jardin de la Hyonnière Folle blanche 2021
notes: Le Jardin de la Hyonnière Folle blanche 2021 by Manuel Pineau is a natural wine made in Loire with Picpoule grapes.

wine: Manuel Pineau - Le Jardin de la Hyonnière Melon 2021
notes: Le Jardin de la Hyonnière Melon 2021 by Manuel Pineau is a natural wine made in Loire with Melon de bourgogne grapes.

Presto by Ab Initio is a natural white wine made with the creamy and equally refreshing Melon du Bourgogne, Chardonnay and Folle-blanche ( Piquepoul). Decant this one for best results to let the meadow flower aromas develop. We found it absolutely singing on the second day actually! Ab Initio is a Loire wine project involving winemaker Emmanuel Roblin as well as Fred and Claire Niger from esteemed Domaine de l’Ecu. Bottles are limited in quantity and despite being new and relatively unknown there is strong interest from winelovers!

wine: Christopher Barth - Rot vom Grun Nr 4
notes: Rot vom Grun nr 4 by is a natural wine made in Rheinhessen with Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir grapes, so this is a red white blend, hence the name. The wines from Christopher Barth are generally excellent value, light and refreshing. Production details of Rot vom Grun Nr 4: Rot vom Grun Nr 4 is made by Christopher Barth in the Rheinhessen region of Germany. The blend mixes Pinot Gris (Grauburgunder) and Pinot Noir, hence the name (a red-white blend). Christopher's natural wines are known for being light and easy-drinking. Tasting Notes: We have not yet tried this vintage of Rot vom Grun Nr 4 by Ch

Riesling 2020 by Max Dexheimer is a natural white wine made in Rheinhessen with 100% Riesling grapes, as the name suggests. This wine spends time on the lees, actually spending 18 months in the barrel

wine: Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques - Vin Dzi (ONE PER ORDER)
notes: Vin Dzi by Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques is a wine made in Jura with Savagnin grapes. This wine varies vintage to vintage but we find it to be an interesting take on Savagnin, perhaps more on the easier drinking, gluggable style than classic. WATCH OUR DOCUMENTARY ON THEM HERE

wine: Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques - Méli Mélo (one per order)
notes: Méli Mélo is a red/white field blend wine from Jura's Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques, featuring Savagnin, Ploussard, Trousseau and Chardonnay. Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques often focus on blends, as most of their vineyards are mixed varietals. This wine has a bright tartness to it. Being a big blend, its really quite unique for a Jura wine and thus should be drunk with this in mind. Wild and herbacious. Very fine, gentle sandy tannins. Serve very cold and enjoy One per order due to low production. WATCH OUR DOCUMENTARY ON THEM HERE

wine: Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques - Pif (one per order)
notes: Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques are small scale natural wine producers, who make natural wine without any sulphur in the Jura region of France. This Pif wine is a big red field blend, with great energy on the palate. WATCH OUR DOCUMENTARY ON THEM HERE
Max Dexheimer 'Pet Nat Weiss' is a sparkling wine made from Gelber Muskateller, Gewürtztraminer, Kerner, Müller-Thurgau, Silvaner. Super refreshing!

PIRI Naturel wines are made by young up-and-coming female producer Christine Pieroth, who is developing quite a buzz in Germany! This is her Pinot Noir, and it's both super juicy and elegant, very tasty indeed with a big depth of flavour and some earthy touches too. Quite cool!!!
Natural Wine producer Gregory White makes 'La Famille (1 Liter)' using grapes of Chenanson, which are grown in the Languedoc region of France.

Elle Aime by L'Octavin is a a natural wine, made with a blend of domain grapes of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. This red/white blend from Jura is zippy and fresh, and featuring high acid! Watch our L'Octavin documentary here

Weissburgunder by Wasenhaus is a wonderful wine, by the highly sought-after winery from Baden, widely recognised amongst critics as being one of the most exciting low intervention producers in Germany. Having gained extensive experience in Burgundy, Christoph Wolber & Alexander Götze bring a unique Burgundian touch to German fine wines. VERY LIMITED. STRICTLY ONE PER ORDER

Franz Weninger's 'Rozsa Petsovits' is a beautiful dark rosé / light red made with Pinot Noir, Syrah, Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt... and it tastes Wunderbar! This wine has excellent value & excellent acidity. Great vibrations and bright energy. Expect vibrant dark cherry mingling with a touch of wood, hint of vanilla and herbs. Dark rosé but could act like a red. Interesting fact about Rosza Petsovits Rozsa Petsovits is really great value! And interestingly, the wine is named after Franz's grandmother, who was born in 1921 in Horitschon, then part of Hungary. This rosé is just as multicultural a

A Glimmer of Hops by Franz Weninger is a unique wine, as it is infused with Hops. Franz Weninger says: Around the fence of one of our orchards, wild hops settled down a few years ago. None of our beer brewer friends wanted to work with this wild hops. Therefore, we decided to process it ourselves: The fresh, uncooked hops was added to the wine during fermentation and remained with it for several weeks in the amphora. Since the wine was directly pressed Blaufränkisch, tannin and fruit on the palate of the Glimmer of Hops are attributed to the hops.

The Weninger Steiner site in Sopron is located in the south-western corner of Lake Neusiedl, on a slight slope to the east. In the Sopron annals, this vineyard was classified in 1680 as the best and most expensive vineyard in western Hungary (today's Burgenland). The gneiss and mica slate that comes to the surface makes the soil permeable, therefore dry and hot. Fourth Furmint vintage from the Steiner site. The barren soil of the site seems ideal for this strain. Unlike on the lime, it gets a slightly more mature, golden aroma here.
Tasty budget natural red from Austria's Weninger!

grapes: Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc, Blaufränkisch, Zweigelt
notes: Ponzichter from Franz Weninger is an excellent value red , taken from vineyards in both Austria AND Hungary, as he has plots in both countries. The grapes are a combination of Blaufränkisch, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Noir and Zweigelt. The name actually comes from the German minority who used to grow wine there, and grew vegetables inbetween the vines, which the Hungarians mocked them for, calling them Ponzichter. This juicy, light wine is for lovers of Claus Preisinger’s Puszta Libre, as it shares some resemblance. Bright cherry and earthy hits with a touch of spice, all in tasty glouglou format

Blaufränkisch Hoch 2024 by Weninger is a natural wine made in Burgenland, and he Hochäcker site is one of the oldest vineyards in Horitschon. Its stoneless, hard, loamy subsoil is interspersed with iron. This makes it a traditional soil for Blaufränkisch. The vines are 40 years old. Franz Weninger states that this has notes of "Red berry fruit, fine forest berries, delicate hints of cherries, spices and tobacco. Freshly structured on the palate. A complex wine, but not opulent. Dense and extremely close-meshed, therefore easy to store."

Brand - Holy Chapel is a white wine made from Pinot Blanc (Weissburgunder) in the Pfalz region of Germany. This elegant yet raw and wild white wine is taken from a single vineyard plot, which really showcases their terroir and winemaking skill. We love it. So precise, so minerally and so balanced. Lengthy finish with clear malolactic vibes from long lees aging. A perfect Pinot Blanc (Weissburgunder) !!!

wine: Tenuta Vincenzo Nardone & Cantina Giardino - FxF
notes: Tenuta Vincenzo Nardone "FxF" is a lovely and aromatic orange wine from Campania, made of Fiano and Falaghnina grapes, which were actually made by both Tenuta Vincenzo Nardone and other Campanian winery Cantina Giardino, each vinifying their grapes and then blended together before bottling.

l'Americana 2020 by Tenuta Vincenzo Nardone is a bitter, tangy orange wine made in Campania, Italy with Greco grapes. The wine is made with carbonic maceration, and sees no additions of sulphites. Expect a little tannic grip and stone fruit touches dominant in the flavour profile.

Lafrea by Poderi Cellario is a fun, easy going natural wine made in the Langhe, a sub region of Piedmonte, Italy. La Favorita uses the grape Favorita, an old native grape variety of the Langa and Roero regions, well-adapted to poor, preferably sandy, soils. It was so named because it was once said to be a favored grape, particularly favored by King Vittorio Emanuele II. A straw-yellow wine, its bouquet is fruity and floral: hay, fresh flowers, and banana; on the palate, it is fresh and smooth, easy and unfussy

Nino Barraco 'Fior di Rosso' is made with Nero d’Avola, grown from the west coast of Sicily, Marsala to be precise. This has lovely touches of black cherry, eucalyptus and pepper on the nose and features a tasty prune and mild sour apple twang on the palate. Nice to have it at 12%, tasty stuff.
Rosato MAGNUM by Cantina Giardino is a red wine made in Campania with the regional Aglianico grapes.

Du Bicer Rosé (33cl) by Ferretti is a natural wine made in Emilia-Romagna with Lambrusco , Maestri and Salamino grapes. Du Bicer is a fun and cheerful Italian Pet Nat 'to go', ideal for times when one glass is enough or you fancy bringing something on the train to somewhere :)

Il Baffone, meaning "the moustache" by Podere Cellario is a sparkling pet nat wine from Veneto, Italy made using grapes of both Favorita and Moscato Bianco. These are quite aromatic grapes, so we expect bright floral tones and a herbacious quality to this Venetian pet nat!

Gaia 2019* by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Fiano grapes. Gaia is a high acidic white with fresh aromatics and soft skin contact, with notes of apricot, cream popcorn, flowers and herbs.
Paski 2019* by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Coda di Volpe grapes.
Volpe Rosa 2019* by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Coda di Volpe grapes.
Pinot Nero 2019 by Bressan is a classic, quite collectable wine made in Friuli with Pinot Noir grapes, known in Italy as Pinot Nero. Expect rustic charm and a rich Italian soul ideal for aging

Chora Rosso by L'acino, is a lovely Italian red made from Magliocco grapes, soft and rounded with a tingly tannic structure, yet still light. This wine comes from the very hot region of Sourthern region of Calabria, where there is not much Natural Wine made, to be fair. Perfect with pizza and pasta. Production Details: Chora Rosso is a red wine from L'Acino in Emilia-Romagna made from a blend of local red grapes. Fermentation happens with native yeasts for an extended period on the skins — typically 4 to 6 weeks. The wine then ages in large wooden vessels, building complexity and texture witho

E´ Rosato (1 Liter) by Poderi Cellario is a natural wine made in Piedmont with Nebbiolo and Dolcetto grapes. Poderi Cellario state this is a Rosé wine produced from the bloodletting of two important vineyards. It remains on the skins for about a day, allowing it to ferment with its own yeasts. This wine is aged in cement vats; it is unclarified and unfiltered. On the nose, it releases red fruits and spices; the palate is fresh with a lovely tannin finish.

Bianco Anfora MAGNUM by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Coda di Volpe , Falanghina and Fiano grapes. This Cantina Giardino wine, does not have any added Sulphites, like all their wines.

SIVI by Kemtijia Stekar is a delicious orange wine made from Pinot Grigio, in Slovenia. For those unaware, Pinot Grigio (aka Pinot Gris or Grauburgunder) is a pink skinned grape, which when macerated like an orange wine turns a beautiful and unique blush colour. Expect delightful notes of concentrated apricots, peaches and plums alongside a herbacious touch and vanilla cream finish. DELICIOUS! Watch a video review at the Colloseum here! Production Details: Located in the Brda region of Slovenia, Kmetija Stekar works with 5 hectares of vineyards. Sivi is a Pinot Grigio made as an orange wine th

E´ Orange (1 Liter) by Poderi Cellario is a natural wine made in Piedmont with Nascetta , Moscato Bianco and Incrocio Manzoni grapes. WOW! Talk about drinkability! This orange glouglou is just like breakfast juice, it's that damn gluggable. Watch out, dangerously easy drinking!!! Slightly aromatic and with a hint of honey on the finish. Little “body lotion” fun, clementines and citrus vibes. Remember to shake! As some vintages are less orange than this photographed vintage suggests

Drogone 2018 by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Aglianico grapes, and no added sulphur. 2010 vintage: Earthy, complex, and with a clearly-aged flavour profile featuring notes of leather, plum & tobacco. This won't be for everyone but damn it sure kicks a punch for those who want this sort of wine. We enjoyed its complexity very much, but keep it for the right moment...

Derthona 2022 by Ricci is a natural wine made in Piedmont with Timorasso grapes. This rich, white wine ages for 12 months in used, 700 litre acacia wood barrels. Flavourwise it is creamy, full bodied and with low acidity, featuring a lovely minty note, alongside subtle flavours of melon and vanilla. Production Details: Derthona is a wine from the Piedmont region made from Barbera. The grapes are fermented with natural yeasts for approximately 30 days on the skins. Ageing takes place in large wooden barrels, allowing the wine to develop complexity whilst retaining the freshness and fruit charac
Dhyana 2021 by Valdibella is a simple natural Rosé wine made in Sicily with Perricone grapes made for fun afternoons. Expect red berries, hints of watermelon and vanilla

Zibibbo 2023 by Nino Barraco is a natural wine made in the Western part of Sicily next to Marsala. Here aromatic Zibibbo grapes, which are also known as Muscat d'Alexandria or Moscatel in other European countries, give of a large presence alongside a salty aspect with the vines being close to the sea. Expect big floral elements and extensive aromatics Production Details: Zibibbo is made from Grillo grapes grown in Marsala's hot, clay-limestone soils. Nino Barraco harvests ripe fruit and ferments with natural yeasts without added sulfites. The wine ages briefly in stainless steel, preserving th

Catarratto 2022 by Nino Barraco is a natural wine made in Sicily with the regional, often minerally and citrusy Catarratto grapes. Here the vines grow just a few hundred metres from the sea on volcanic soils giving a lot of tension and vibrancy to the wine.

Benedic 2020 by Monastero Trappiste Vitorchiano is a natural red wine made in Lazio with Sangiovese and Ciliegiolo grapes. The wine is made by Italian nuns, guided by natural winemaker Giampiero Bea. Tasting notes of Benedic 2020 from American wine importer Rosenthal: "The sisters produce a scant amount of red wine: a charming blend of equal parts Sangiovese and Ciliegiolo called “Benedic.” Despite a two-week maceration, “Benedic” is typically a beautifully pale, translucent wine. Registering just 11% alcohol, its color is calm, soft, and almost coppery—one can sense its gentle nature just fro

Coenobium Ruscum 2024 by Monastero Trappiste Vitorchiano is a natural wine made in Lazio with 45% Trebbiano , 35% Malvasia and 20% Verdicchio grapes. This white wine is grown and vinified by nuns in a monastary! This orange wine will have floral touches, nice aromatics and a slight tannic grip About Monastero Trappiste Vitorchiano - natural wines made by nuns! Amid Lazio’s volcanic tufa soils, the Cistercian Trappist nuns of Vitorchiano treat winemaking as a form of liturgy. Guided by Giampiero Bea, they hand-tend decades-old vines, ferment with wild yeasts and bottle without frills. The resul

Croci 'Valtolla' is a delightful, crunchy red blend of 60% Barbera and 40% Bonarda aka Croatina from Croci - perfect with cheeseboards or hearty pasta dishes! The grapes are macerated for 25-30 days on the skins and aged in cement vats. Croci states that Val Tolla was the ancient name for the middle Arda Valley, where vines have been cultivated since Roman times. It is made from Barbera and Bonarda (Croatina) grapes, traditionally grown on our hills. The fully ripe grapes are hand-picked into small crates and vinified by macerating on the skins for approximately thirty days. The rustic wine ex

Campedello by Croci is an unusual orange pet nat, with a cork. Bready, a bit meaty, grassy and tangy. Not for everyone, but very unique and interesting. A love it or hate it wine... For the grapes, here we have Malvasia di Candia 60%, Trebbiano e Ortrugo 35%, Sauvignon and Marsanne 5% which spend 7 days macerating on the skins. This Campedello wine which is a Colli Piacentini DOC spends 12 months in bottle before release, and is sparkling but not by a huge amount

wine: Podere Cipolla - Rosa Dei Venti Lambrusco
notes: Rosa Dei Venti Lambrusco by Podere Cipolla is a sparkling Lambrusco wine, made in Emilia-Romagna with Lambrusco Grasparossa and Malbo Gentile grapes. Absolutely delightful.

aromas: Raspberry, Sour Cherry, Mushroom, Limestone, Saline
notes: Saseti 2023 by Monte Dall´Ora is a natural wine made in Veneto with Corvina , Corvinone , Rondinella and Molinara Y Oseleta grapes. Perched on the limestone terraces of Castelrotto in the heart of Valpolicella Classica, Monte Dall’Ora farms its 25- to 70-year-old pergola-trained vines biodynamically, letting the “saseti” (“little stones”) in the soil shape the wine’s mineral pulse. Corvina and Corvinone dominate the field blend, rounded out by Rondinella, Molinara and the heirloom Oseleta, all harvested by hand from southeast-facing slopes between 70 – 200 m high. The 2023 was fermented sponta

Camporenzo 2020 by Monte Dall´Ora is a 13% natural red wine made in Veneto, Italy with 50% Corvina, 20% Corvinone, 20% Rondinella, 10% Molinara grapes. This wine ages for 10 months in 25-hl botti (wooden barrels made of Slovenian oak). After bottling, it ages for at least two years in the bottle before release. Expect a full body and smooth velvety finish Production Details: Camporenzo is a Valpolicella Superiore from a specific vineyard site. The blend of Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella, and Oseleta reflects the terroir of the vineyard. Fermentation happens in stainless steel, followed by agei

Mongarda make high-quality Prosecco using the Charmant method (as well as Col Fondo, the ancient Pet Nat style). They farm 12 hectares and often do single vineyard plots in their bottlings, like the Extra Dry Valdobbiadene. The Vineyards here look beautiful and on well-exposed plots in the hills. This is a beautiful Prosecco using the traditional Glera grape - classic and clean yet still natural in feeling Production Details: This Prosecco from the Veneto region is made using the charmat method. Fermentation takes place in stainless steel pressure tanks, where the secondary fermentation create

Bolle Bandite by Gatti is a natural wine made in Veneto with Glera grapes. Working on a farm surrounded by animals, the wines of Carolina Gatti are rustic and approachable and at a good price too. Bolle Bandita is the name of her most well known wine, a Col Fondo Pet Nat featuring the Glera grape... so technically an old-school Prosecco. Except, it cannot be called Prosecco as not the legal style, so the name means "forbidden bubbles"...

É Rosso (1 Liter) by Poderi Cellario is a natural wine made in Piedmont with Barbera grapes. E Rosso is ideal as a table wine for BBQ or Pizza nights, and this is exactly what it was designed for, in a fun one litre bottle.

Cinino by La Segreta is a vibrant coloured Rosè wine made in Umbria, Italy with 100% Sangiovese grapes. The vines are grown on limestone and no added sulphites are used. Agri Segretum ( La Segreta) is located on 80 hectacres of olives, forest and plains in Collazzone, Umbria in Central Italy. 7.5 hectares of sunny southwest facing land Production Details: Cinino is a young wine from La Segreta in Sicily, made from indigenous grapes. The fruit ferments with natural yeasts in stainless steel or concrete, preserving freshness and acidity. The wine spends minimal time ageing, emphasising the prima

wine: La Via del Colle - Ambaradan Bianco 2020
notes: Ambaradan Bianco 2020 by La Via del Colle is a wine made in Emilia Romagna with Albana , Trebbiano and Pagadebit grapes.
Trebbiano by Casale is a traditional yet natural wine, is made in Tuscany with Trebbiano grapes.

Scirocco 2021 by La Via del Colle is an orange wine made in Emilia-Romagna, Italy with Pagadebit grapes. This wine is macerated on the skins for 15 days and aged for 6 months in Amphora, with no added sulphur. Expect some tannic grip here, making it ideal for food
Origine Rosso by Conti is a natural wine made in Piedmonte in the north of Italy with Nebbiolo and Vespolina grapes.
Giramondo by L'Acino is a white wine made in Calabria, Italy with aromatic Malvasia grapes.

Ego 2019 by Bressan is a cult, rare wine made in Friuli with Schioppettino and Cabernet Franc grapes. Whilst much of Friuli is focused on skin-contact amber wines, Bressan is known for his big reds. This wine will feature some peppery notes from the Cabernet Franc and bold, forest fruit touches from the Schioppettino. Production Details: Ego is a red wine from Bressan in Friuli-Venezia Giulia made from a blend of indigenous red grapes. Fermentation lasts 30 to 35 days on the skins with native yeasts. The wine then ages for an extended period in mixed wooden vessels — oak, chestnut, and wild pe
No3 2019 by Bressan is a natural wine made in Friuli with Pinot Noir , Cabernet Sauvignon and Schioppettino grapes. Expect this to be rustic, big, bold and full of Italian soul. This is a rare find.

Ognostro Bianco is a well-rounded italian white from Campania using the Fiano grape, with a slight touch of skin-contact. Expect notes of apricot, almonds, mint, bitter orange with white pepper tingling on the top of your palate. A tasty food wine where the alcohol is present in the taste but in an enjoyable way. About Marco Tinessa Marco Tinessa is a natural wine producer from the Campania region in Italy , although he actually used to be a banker in Milan - so quite the different life! Having received support from his mentor Frank Cornelissen, he decided to take on some land to preserve and

Bianco Frizzante by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania, Italy with Coda di Volpe , Falanghina and Fiano grapes. It's not common to see a sparkling wine from Cantina Giardino. This one is rather tasty with a slight 'twang' to it, as we recall.

Amico Frizz by Castello Di Stefanago is a natural wine made in Lombardia with Riesling grapes, which is not a common find in Lombardia. Production details of Amico Frizz: Amico Frizz comes from Castello di Stefanago in the Oltrepò Pavese hills of Lombardia, run by brothers Antonio and Giacomo Baruffaldi. The Castello has stood since the 11th century and the family farms 20 hectares of vines across small scattered plots within a 135-hectare estate. The Riesling here is made by the ancestral method with refermentation in bottle, and bottled under crown cap with no added sulphur. Tasting Notes: W
Tu Tu by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Fiano grapes. Tu Tu is an easy going, very drinkable wine served in a litre bottle, for extra fun!

Cantina Giardino 'Rosso Magnum' is made with Aglianico grapes, and is usually an assemblage of vintages making it a Non-Vintage wine. Long maceration on the skins, no added sulphur and a nice drinkability make the Cantina Giadino magnum a good fit for a BBQ or dinner party.

El Matt by Ricci is a more classic styled, red natural wine, with elegance and Italian charm. El Matt is made using 100% Croatina grapes from Piedmonte, more specifically the T ortonese area. This rich and deep 15% red wine is in steel in order to enhance freshness. This rustic red has big fruit notes of pomegante and cherry with a hint of earth, and finalising with a finish of light licorice. This one is big at 15% and for tannin lovers

Renosu Bianco by Dettori is a natural wine made in Sardinia, Italy with Vermentino and the aromatic Moscato Giallo grapes. Dettori state their Renosu Bianco is " an intensely aromatic wine, straight forward and uncomplicated, pure pleasure in a wineglass. Enjoy chilled. Renosu, which in our local language mean sandy, is not new, but traditional here: marrying together complex acidity with the intense sweetness is a pleasurable custom. Renosu Bianco expresses a singular coppery golden colour, crystalline and bright. The nose presents fine and fragrant scents of ripe pear, nectarine, white flowe

Renosu Rosso by Dettori is a natural wine made in Sardinia, Italy with Grenache (Cannelou), Monica and Pascale grapes. This is a nicely extracted wine, very fruit forward with a touch of mild residual sugar, which works well. Here a slight earthy, mushroom taste that works well. Dettori state that "Renosu Rosso is our everyday red wine—-fragrant, simple, natural, the red wine to uncork with friends, for a wine glass brimming with pleasure. Renosu, which means sandy in our language, was born from the idea of the traditional custom, for everyday wines, of combining wines of different red grapes.

This is the formally known Vignamare from Nino Barraco, who is based close to Marsala in Sicily. This refreshing and saline white wine is now called Biancammare. The Grillo vines roots reach right to the sea, and many vintages offer a strong sense of salinity, hence the name. Expect classical finesse alongside saline touches and a nice natural energy. Sicily in a glass! Production Details: Biancammare is a Grillo from Marsala in Sicily. The vineyard soils are clay and limestone. Nino Barraco practices organic methods in the vineyard and natural winemaking in the cellar. The wine ferments witho
Rosammare 2022 by Nino Barraco is a natural wine made in the Marsala region of Sicily with Nero D’Avola grapes, which are harvested earlier giving this wine some tannic, dark fruity character.

Nero D´Avola 2022 by Nino Barraco is a natural wine made in the Marsala region of Sicily with red Nero D’Avola grapes, typical to the island. This wine is known to features notes of Mullberry and Cocoa.

Nino Barraco is one of the pioneers of natural wine in Sicily, but rather than other local superstars in Etna or Alcamo, he is more lonesome over in Marsala. A region famed for fortified wine production.. of which a HUGE portion made is actually only used as cooking wine! We visited the estate before we had fully set up MORE Natural Wine, and we impressed to see some vineyards have roots reaching literally into the sea! Some may argue this gives the wines a salinity, whilst others will argue in the name of science that this is technically impossible to get flavours delivered from root to grape

Ognostro by Marco Tinessa is a natural wine made in Campania with Aglianico grapes. Aglianico is a special grape usually found in Campania Italy, and this Ognostro is rather special indeed, as less bitter than most expressions of it. Perhaps this is as the wine is aged in clay pots, rather than oak. There are touches of balsamic going on here which make Ognostro interesting. Production Details: Ognostro is an Aglianico from Campania in southern Italy. The vineyard contains vines ranging from 30 to 90 years old. Fermentation takes place in mixed vessels: fiberglass, amphorae, and concrete. This

wine: Al Di La´ Del Fiume - Fricandó
notes: Fricandó by Al Di La Del Fiume is a natural wine made in Emilia-Romagna with Albana and Elbling grapes. This was actually one of the first Orange wines we tried. Complex, tangy, herbal and structured with some tannic grip.
Molin 2016 by Villa Persani is a natural wine made in Trentino-Alto-Adige with Manzoni and Müller-Thurgau grapes. Expect strong minerality, saltiness and mountain freshness

Meet "The Cock," a lively duo of Grüner Veltliner and Riesling. Grüner brings the pepper , while Riesling delivers a punch of crisp, mouthwatering acidity . Leaving the vines unpruned produces tiny, concentrated grapes that—alongside extended skin contact—give this wine its delightfully rustic feel and textured tannins. On the palate, clementine , lemon , and lime mingle with fragrant notes of vermouth and rosemary .

Traditionally foot-stomped, macerated on the skins for two weeks, and aged for two full years in oak barriques, it’s an elegant orange wine with mild earthy and rustic nuances. Up front, you'll catch some white pepper , clementine and green tea followed by rich notes of vanilla , rum , and apricot .

Floris is another wonderful white in Quantum's selection. It's not your usual Grüner Veltliner , this one has a character of its own. It is herbal and fruity , it has great complexity and a cool reductive touch . Yellow apple , pear , some pineapple , thyme and caramel aromas.
