Pacina created this wine to celebrate the Etruscan God of wine, Pachna . This special wine is not produced every year and few bottles were made. The 100% Sangiovese is what you would expect it to be, earthy and powerful plus a natural kick. Definitely complex with blueberries and violets aromas, a real gem. It comes in two beautiful labels, one is designed by Giovanna’s mother and the other by their friend’s daughter!

This golden dessert wine from Georg Schmelzer is meade from Welschriesling grapes. The Trockenbeerauslese is the highest quality type of sweet wine production in Austria and consists in a very late late harvest, hand picked grapes and a small fine production. This nectar has aromas of vanilla and honey in the nose. In the mouth a playful balance between sweetness and acidity with a long fruity finish .

La Sorpresa from Pacina is literally a sweet Tuscan surprise! Made from 50% Trebbiano Toscano and 50% Malvasia del Chianti and aged in small chestnut barrels for 5 years, it’s the perfect choice if you’d like to finish up an amazing meal with some quality vin santo . Thick syrupy consistency plus some caramel and coffee aromas. Yum!

The powerful Redition from Georg Schmelzer unites 3 different grape varieties (Zweigelt, Roesler, Cabernet Sauvignon) and 4 vintages. Fruity notes of blackberries , cherry and cassis harmonize well with the earthy, bite-y tannins . Enjoy this fantastic wine with food or leave it to mature in the cellar to see how develops in a couple of months or years!

Rich, savoury and full of character, it challenges the conventional idea of what dry sake should taste like. The successor to Heavy Pétting, Piggy Pop is bright ruby red in colour with aromas of fresh cherries and raspberry liquorice. The palate explodes with cherries, black plum and light spice. Bone-dry with mouth filling bubbles and a good lick of zippy acidity.

Deliciously fresh and reminds us of a sparkling tropical fruit juice. Aromas of white peach and juicy clementines. Astro Bunny is a blend of Fiano (43%), Malvasia Bianca (32%), Nero d’Avola (13%), Prieto Picudo (7%), Montepulciano (5%).

The 2025 Masseria Cuturi Tumà Primitivo begins with a fruity bouquet with fresh notes of blackberry and sweet spices. The palate reveals notes of black fruit and sweet licorice, finishing fresh and juicy.

Ruby red colour with intense aromas of red fruit and black cherry jam, light notes of cocoa and toasted oak complete the bouquet. The palate is warm, fairly tannic but soft on the finish. If you enjoy a California red, you might really like this wine!

Shochu made from chestnuts. Chestnuts make up an unusually high 50% of the raw ingredients, alongside barley, rice and rice koji. The palate is smooth and rounded, with gentle richness and a lingering chestnut character. Bone-dry cloudy sake! This is where rice becomes part of the drinking experience. Akishika Shuzō farms much of its own organic rice in Osaka, maintaining unusually close control over its sake from the rice field through brewing. Akishika’s Aragoshi Nigori is thick, textured and almost snowy with rice, but beneath its milky appearance is a sake with serious acidity and a distinctly dry finish. First produced in 1923, Buon Padre has been a Viberti flagship for over a century. It brings together Nebbiolo from ten sites across the Barolo appellation, including Bricco delle Viole, Ravera and Perno to create a wine that reflects the broader character of Barolo. Following fermentation, the wine spends 36 months in large, untoasted, steamed Slavonian oak vats, allowing its tannins to develop without the pronounced oak flavours. The warm 2022 vintage delivers generous red and dark cherry fruit, wild raspberry, rosehip and violet, with notes of liquorice, sweet spice and tobacco. Full-bodied

Longaví is a collaboration between Chilean winemaker Julio Bouchon and South African winemaker David Nieuwoudt, two friends united by a shared interest in Chile's diverse vineyard landscapes. Their Gran Reserva Cabernet Sauvignon comes from the Andean foothills of the Maule Valley, where the influence of altitude helps preserve freshness in this generous, full-bodied red. Aged for approximately 12 to 14 months in French oak, it offers ripe blackcurrant, dark cherry and subtle herbal and floral notes. Juicy, robust, and structured, with rounded tannins and a smooth, lingering finish.

Jasper Wickens is part of a new generation of Swartland winemakers exploring the region's old vineyards and the possibilities of minimal intervention winemaking. Oranje Blanje is his take on orange wine, combining the freshness of Chenin Blanc with the texture and structure of extended skin contact. Early-harvested Chenin Blanc undergoes spontaneous fermentation on skins for 22 days. Grenache Blanc contributes additional texture. Followed by 10 months ageing in neutral oak. Juicy cherry, raspberry and fresh plum meet hints of violet, black pepper and almond. Medium-bodied and supple, with bright acidity and gentle tannins.

Dr. Bürklin-Wolf's Estate Riesling is a dry (trocken) wine made from a blend of biodynamic vineyards. Fermented in a mix of stainless steel and old oak casks, it offers fresh aromas of apple, lemon, and a hint of florals. The palate is crisp and refreshing, with bright acidity and fine minerality.

Pinot Grigio finds one of its purest expressions in Northeastern Italy, and Friuli’s Alpine–Adriatic microclimate brings out its full intensity. Venchiarezza crafts a Pinot Grigio that resists the simple and the neutral, opting instead for a style that is full, textural and genuinely terroir driven. Grapes are harvested fully ripe and gently pressed, with part of the must fermented in second-pass small wooden barrels for added depth. Old-vine, South African Chenin Blanc sings in the care of Jasper Wickens. Notes of ripe white peaches, quince, and citrus zest with an herbal touch. Complex and layered with a long finish.

Pale pink in the glass, it opens with raspberry, strawberry and citrus alongside melon and subtle floral notes. This is a blend of Zweigelt and Blauer Portugieser with a touch of Cabernet Sauvignon grown on loam, loess and sandstone soils. The grapes are fermented whole cluster with native yeasts, then aged for around nine months in stainless steel and old wooden barrels. Bottled unfined and unfiltered with minimal sulphur.

The French would call this a 'gouleyant' wine, meaning that it is gluggable or smashable.

100% Sauvignon Blanc. 3 weeks of skin-contact results in a wine that's nearly the colour of a tangerine! Notes of sea buckthorn, passionfruit and hints of grassy-spice.

After a few weeks on skins it becomes floral and fun on the nose with hints of honeysuckle and apricot, and plenty of crisp acidity on the palate.

A gentle interplay of fruit richness and natural lift makes this both characterful and highly drinkable.

100% Tempranillo from the Ribera del Duero. Intense bouquet of cherries, raspberries, blueberries and elderberries and a slight sweetness from the ripening of the grape. Its brief ageing in oak adds hints of vanilla, chocolate and caramel to the fruit. On the palate, all its flavours are pronounced but balanced by smooth tannins and pleasant acidity: red fruit and creamy notes of the oak, but there are also hints of scrubland herbs and liquorice, which adds excellent complexity to the wine as a whole.

A lively, fruit-forward Rioja made from 80% Tempranillo, 10% Garnacha, and 10% Mazuela, harvested in 2023. Fermented with native yeasts in stainless steel to preserve its bright cherry-red color and vibrant red fruit flavors, it has a smooth, medium-bodied palate with balanced acidity. Crafted with minimal intervention, this youthful Rioja reflects the Espinosa family's commitment to sustainable viticulture. Best enjoyed slightly chilled alongside tapas, grilled meats, or traditional Spanish dishes.

Lucette is beautiful, cheerful, and full of beans! Her smile is contagious, solar. Her thirst for life will catapult you to the heart of the party. Lucette is a blend of Roussane, Terret, Vermentino and a discrete drop of Muscat. A light, thirst-quenching, fresh aromatic white wine to crack open in all circumstances.

This crisp, aromatic white blends 40% Albanello and 60% Zibibbo, both native to Sicily. Light straw yellow, SP68 Bianco offers aromas of ripe peaches, orange blossoms, and Mediterranean herbs. Medium-bodied with bright acidity, it delivers flavours of apricots, blood oranges, and honey, finishing dry and lush.

Fresh and youthful, SP68 Rosso is a 70/30 blend of Frappato and Nero d’Avola from 15-year-old vines, named after the road to the winery. Frappato brings floral lift and crunch, while Nero d’Avola adds depth and spice. The palate is vibrant and silky with fine tannins, savory mineral tension and a long, refreshing finish. A perfect pizza wine!

Hand harvested and naturally fermented, it shows notes of lemon peel, pear, white flowers and gentle minerality. Fresh, clean, a perfect crisp fresh white wine to accompany any occasion.

The palate is equally appealing, delivering a juicy and supple texture with moderate acidity and fine, delicate tannins. The palate emphasizes red berries complemented by light spices which add complexity and lead to a persistent, gourmet finish.

notes: An incredible single-site Burgundy that we love. An elegant, round and leesy Chardonnay made from the Mâcon-La Roche-Vineuse appellation of Burgundy, France. The palate is generally fresh and well-balanced, featuring a mineral freshness that is complemented by a hint of spice. The wine's style makes it versatile for food pairings. Try it with fish dishes, white meats, cheeses like Munster, or risotto with mushrooms.

The 2022 vintage brought high temperatures and low rainfall, resulting in small, concentrated berries with exceptional fruit intensity. Deep ruby with violet hues, it opens with aromas of blackberry, plum, and wild strawberry in liqueur. The palate is vibrant and silky, with juicy red fruit and fine tannins carrying through to a fresh, lingering finish. La Gemella refers to Maria Viberti, Claudio’s mother, who is herself a twin. This Barbera d’Alba is crafted to reflect a classic style: bold yet balanced, expressive yet elegant. La Gemella 2023 is a textbook example of what the Langhe can offer at excellent value: Barbera with structure, elegance and clarity. Not overdone, not flamboyant.

wine: Mount Edward Big TED Pinot Noir 2024 2L Cask
notes: Pinot Noir is perhaps the grape closest to the Mount Edward team’s heart. A range of de-stemmed, 25% whole bunch and 100% whole bunch fruit is open fermented and hand plunged before resting in French oak for 11 months. This is a beautifully perfumed example, berries of a darker complexion mingle with a little spice and dried herbs. On the palate we are talking power and class, silky and lush. Get it while we’ve got it. FYI this works out to be $31.35 a bottle, now thats the kinda steel we are looking for!

wine: Worlds Apart Wines Up On The Roof 2026
notes: Peramangk and Kaurna Country. We started with a parcel of cool climate syrah from Kangarilla on the McLaren Vale/Adelaide Hills border, kept it on skins for a day or so, then pressed it (so kind of a heavy rosé), and fermented it dry in tank. To this, we added some McLaren Vale grenache and some touriga Rosé, some Adelaide Hills pinot and gamay and a splash of orange wine (made from gewurztraminer). The goal of all the painstaking blending being to make a light red that is both refreshing, but also has structure. Tannin and acidity playing together to make a wine that makes your mouth water an

wine: Worlds Apart Wines In the Flowers Riesling 2026
notes: Peramangk Country Grown by Chris Alderton at his ruggedly beautiful Pendee Farm, outside of Springton at the Southern end of Eden Valley. Soil is Clay-loam with quartz riddled gravel. These vines were planted in 1969 and are grown without irrigation or synthetic chemicals. Green-tinged straw in color. This vintage shows vibrant floral character on the nose, with dried herbs and an intense palate of grapefruit and wisps of lemon, lime and white pepper. - Worlds Apart

wine: Worlds Apart Wines Everlasting Happiness Rose 2025
notes: Kaurna Country This is from McLaren Vale and a blend of touriga nacional and shiraz. It sees heaps of lees stirring and hangs out in old oak. Good drink. Right off the bat it welcomes with crispness, perfume and fresh watermelon juice. Everlasting Summer more like it!

As usual this rosé is made from several separate components, and this year is a blend of grenache noir, merlot, muscat à petits grains, and muscat d’alexandrie. These four grape varieties are ones that thrive on the soils and climate in this area. The main component is the grenache noir, which is from the Rivesaltes vineyards, as is the Merlot. The muscat is from Espira-de-l’Agly. Each variety had a short maceration but was vinified separately, partly because the picking window extends over 10 days. It is light, fresh and highly aromatic. - Living Wines, Importer

This year’s Otium is an infusion of grenache noir, (90% of the wine) picked from 80 year old selection massale vines planted by Laurent’s grandfather in Espira d’Agly. Laurent says it’s an old variety of grenache with nowhere near as strong a colour as newer clones and very little tannin, which allows the complexities the soil offers to be better expressed. It was infused for 11 days with grenache gris from the Fourques vineyard the previously Alain Castex farmed and aging was in a concrete tank which fittingly belonged to Castex. It is pink and we possibly should have it as a rosé. The pinkne

Idoine, as usual, is 100% Merlot. It comes from 30 year old vines in Rivesaltes planted by Laurent’s father on quite heavy clay soils. His meticulous pruning in this vineyard, and then strict disbudding each spring is, Laurent thinks, contributing to more maturity each year, and it’s visible in the glass. Although it’s juicy, there is plenty of structure as well. Whole bunches were macerated for a few days and it was aged in a mix of fibreglass and barrels. “It’s our gamay” according to Laurent. And, because it’s not as dark as last year’s vintage, it’s another one of our new ‘dark, light red’

The wine is made from approximately 70 year old macabeu vines growing on clay and rolled pebbles of limestone in Espira-de-l’Agly. The vines were planted by Laurent’s grandfather but they purchased the vineyard from a subsequent owner a few years ago, at the time without knowing who had planted them. It is a mix of approximately 50/50 directly-pressed and macerated juice. But the short 5 day maceration was not with the purpose of making an orange wine. Laurent feels thar this period of maceration helps the finished wine to express some of the soil’s complexities and also is insurance for a goo

wine: 78 Degrees Distillery The Italian Australian Bitter Orange
notes: The orange bitter uses native Australian botanicals, riberries, thyme, lime and quandong, alongside traditional European botanicals. It is the perfect balance between Campari and Aperol. Best served in a Spritz or Negroni.

Wiradjuri Country. Sangiovese grown in Mudgee. Raspberry and cola with an effortless dry finish, serve chilled for maximum fun drinking. A parcel of these grapes were harvested earlier for direct press rosato style and then the remaining grapes when picked a little fuller in ripeness and fermented with native yeast in an open top fermenter. Gentle plunges only then pressed from skins within 7 days. The two parcels were then blended together resulting in a lighter style wine that is aromatic and crunchy. … and yes this wine is absolutely named after Rizzo from Grease - Samantha May
Tags: Australia, Ephemera, Pinot Noir, Victoria, Yarra Valley

grapes: Pinot Noir, Syrah, Shiraz, Pinot Gris
notes: Creative flair has always been the metier of Konpira Maru and here they blend five different varieties from five vineyards to create a super blend (like the 1980s space explorers who combined in the TV series of the same name). It’s quietly complex, very juicy, easy drinking in style and generally a lot of fun. It’s all sloshy textured but with crunchy, red berry fruit and sweet/floral detail. It feels more juice than wine in some respects, and fittingly comes with incredible drinkability.

Wurundjeri Country This riesling, pinot gris and gewurztraminer field blend is from the Merkel Vineyard that straddles the ridge (~550m above sea level) running up to Mount Bellevue on a forgotten outpost of Whitlands. Tropical acid! Dried apple, pineapple, a bit of paw paw and some sharp apricot. Then throw in some electric acidity, not sour acid, yummy, saliva inducing acid. Literally impossible to drink a bottle in more than 20 minutes(by yourself) excepting some sort of epic tantric mind control. - Konpira Maru

Kaurna Country Dry on the tongue, but it's a very wet wine. A visceral medley of passion, indulgence and spaghetti alle vongole. Nebbiolo and Sangiovese from the Barossa, plus a little Sangiovese from the Hills, gently made under the sultry supervision of Monica Bellucci. - Giovanni Armani Giorgio

Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Country A blend of cabernet sauvignon and pinot noir, which would likely have the toffs reeling due to the 'crossing of the streams' of Bordeaux and Burgundy's finest red varieties, but no issue for the playful, avant garde of Bobar. This is a lighter weight red, not transparent, but swishy and red fruited, lashed with truffle and dried, Italian herb notes, a squish of blood orange to close. Chillable as. Drink without a chill, fine also. Go forth.

Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Country A blend of chardonnay, sauvignon blanc and viognier to produce a textural, salty white wine! Here's what the winemakers say: A fresh, textured and saline white, extremely versatile for food pairing and downright delicious. Beurre Bosc pear, white flowers, fleshy white and yellow nectarine, marzipan and wet stone. A blend of varieties, and a blend of techniques. The Chardonnay was direct pressed and barrel fermented, the Sauvignon Blanc given a short amount of skin contact before pressing and barrel fermentation, and the Viognier carbonic macerated for 7 days befo

Peramangk Country Everyone's favourite cosmic cat is back outta the bag! Living legend James Erskine's shiraz/grenache blend is a perennial favourite, and this year's release is no exception. The best of both varieties: big, bold red fruit and peppery spice joining forces in a slurpy, juicy red with crunchy texture that's primed for a light chill. As always, no sulphur...but lots of deliciousness!

Kaurna Country and Peramangk Country Who doesn't love Danby? James Erskine's carbonic grenache is back in full force in 2024. Light, bright, skippy as all get-out and full of energy. Fruit-forward, packed with r aspberries and christmas spices , but balanced with a good dose of rocky minerality. Chill it right down and drink it right up!

The world's best Bloody Mary mix, made from scratch in our very out back yard ... well Redfern. Makes 3 small / 2 medium or 1 maxi-Mary, just add your favourite white spirit. We like a liberal splash of Poor Tom's Sydney Gin in ours. A cause AND a cure. May as well get 2 !

A lively and refreshing attack, driven by perfectly balanced acidity. Fresh fruit flavors mingle harmoniously with herbal infusions like basil and chamomile, offering a subtle and soothing complexity. Fine bubbles add a sparkling and festive touch, while the delicate bitterness on the finish prolongs the sensation of freshness. A refined and healthy alter

Its composition showcases refined, natural aromas: woody and aromatic notes of juniper, pine, and bay leaf, balanced by a slight bitterness from gentian and yarrow. With 50% less sugar than Antidote and a beautiful golden hue, L'Antilope offers a healthy and sophisticated alternative. The Antelope is elegance in all its simplicity, to be enjoyed at any time! Its composition highlights notes of bitter orange, enhanced by Sichuan pepper and supported by a herbaceous and floral base of verbena and yarrow.
